## Session 159 (2026-07-27) — proved by full source read that RT64's 15th crash class (`loadDrawState` zero-sample assert) cannot be caused by any guest-supplied tile field, landed an always-on guard+log+clamp at the site instead of chasing a guest-side instrument that the proof rules out; soak's crash was neither the 15th class nor `composeNpcOrientationMatrix` but a brand-new, 21st crash class inside `drawSubtitleText`, reached earlier in the menu flow than any prior soak in this family

### What s159 did

1. Per NEXT.md's step 1, traced every write path to `dstCallTile.sampleWidth`/
   `sampleHeight` in `RT64::State::loadDrawState` (`lib/rt64/src/hle/
   rt64_state.cpp:441-747`) end to end, instead of guessing where to
   instrument:
   - The only initial write (`:595-596`) is `min(tileWidth, maskWidth)` /
     `min(tileHeight, maskHeight)`. `tileWidth`/`tileHeight` are always
     `std::max(computed, 1)` when clamped, or `0xFFFF` when wrapping — never
     less than 1 by construction (`:591-592`). `maskWidth`/`maskHeight` are
     `0xFFFF` when `tile.masks`/`maskt == 0`, else `1 << tile.masks` — and
     `tile.masks`/`maskt` are `uint8_t` (`lib/rt64/src/common/
     rt64_load_types.h:20-21`) written from exactly one call site
     (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_rdp.cpp:611`, `RDP::setTile`), fed by
     `DisplayList::p1(pos, 4)` (`lib/rt64/src/gbi/rt64_gbi.cpp:37-39`,
     `(w1 >> pos) & 0xF`) at the sole call site
     (`lib/rt64/src/gbi/rt64_gbi_rdp.cpp:60-61`) — **structurally bounded to
     0-15 regardless of what garbage is in the guest DL word `w1`**, so
     `1 << tile.masks` is at most `1 << 15 = 32768`, never 0, never UB.
   - The 3 subsequent writers (`ROGUESQ_FLATTEN_RGBA16`/`_I4`/`_CI4`,
     `:661-744`) are all default-OFF debug probes (per CURRENT-TRUTH's
     "Default-OFF" list) and were not armed this soak.
   - The one writer in between (`ROGUESQ_FIX_SAMPLE_BOUNDS`, default ON,
     `:598-659`) explicitly does `dstCallTile.sampleWidth =
     std::max(wantW, 1)` (`:655-656`) — clamped, cannot zero.
   - Conclusion: **no combination of guest-supplied `LoadTile` fields
     (masks, maskt, cms, cmt, uls, ult, lrs, lrt) can make this formula
     compute 0** under the code's own type/masking invariants. This is a
     proof from the merged source, not a hypothesis — closing NEXT.md's
     framed question definitively in the "RT64-side, out of scope for the
     guest-guard approach" direction, without needing to build a
     guest-dispatch instrument that a genuine zero was never going to reach
     anyway.
2. Landed a guard at the assert site itself (`rt64_state.cpp:746-780`)
   instead: if `sampleWidth`/`sampleHeight` are still 0 despite the proof
   above, log every raw tile field (`masks`/`maskt`/`cms`/`cmt`/`uls`/`ult`/
   `lrs`/`lrt`) plus an independently-recomputed-from-scratch width/height,
   then clamp to 1 and continue instead of aborting. The recompute is the
   actual discriminator for a future hit: if it's also 0, this session's
   proof has a gap; if it's non-zero, `dstCallTile` was corrupted (or its
   backing `std::vector` reallocated out from under the held reference —
   `dstCallTile` is `auto &drawData.callTiles[callTileIndex]`, taken once at
   `:543` and written across 200+ lines) between the correct write at `:595`
   and this read at `:747`, which would be an RT64-internal concurrency bug,
   not guest data. `lib/` change — ran `./submodule-patches/export.sh` and
   committed the refreshed `rt64.patch` in this same session (hard rule).
3. `cmake --build` (cwd `build/`, `DEVELOPER_DIR=...Xcode.app...`) — exit 0,
   only pre-existing imgui `-Wnontrivial-memcall` warnings, no new ones.
4. Soaked (`scratch/agent/run_zerosample1.sh`, same full battery as s158's
   `run_composeguard7.sh`, no new env var needed since the guard is
   always-on). **Died far earlier in the menu flow than any prior soak in
   this family**: driver log shows the title→1024 phase transition at
   45.0s, two scheduled `start` key presses both completed (screenshots
   exist for both), then the process died during the subsequent 12s
   "wait for SELECT YOUR CRAFT stable" window — **before ever reaching
   SELECT YOUR CRAFT, the war room, or hangar-flight this run**. No further
   `[phase]` transition past `vi_width=1024` was ever logged. `[compose-npc]`
   entry diagnostic: **0** this run (function never even reached, unlike
   s158's 508/508) — confirms the death genuinely predates the whole
   post-leave/hangar-tick window this family usually crashes in.

### The actual crash

Signal 10 (Bus error), backtrace: `drawSubtitleText+34664` ←
`setupCameraMatrices+27984` ← `static_5_800B47D0+99260` ←
`menuOverlayInit+4472` ← `mainGameLoop` ← `mainBootstrapWorker` ← thread
entry. Confirmed via `scratch/agent/machoparse.py build/RogueSquadron64Recomp
drawSubtitleText` that `drawSubtitleText` really is a 37300-byte function

### What this rules out / establishes

## Session 160 (2026-07-27) — full source read of `drawSubtitleText` (the 21st crash class) found and guarded a genuine unguarded-pointer-deref site matching the family's classic shape; soak was the first fully crash-free run in the entire family since s88 (single data point, guard itself unvalidated 0/0)

### What s160 did

1. Located `drawSubtitleText` in the regenerated tree: guest address
   `0x800159B4` (`symbol_files/main_overlay.txt:1666`), found in
   `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:15603-18922`. Read the **entire**
   function body end to end (confirmed the real epilogue at the closing
   `return;`/`0x80016C3C`/`0x80016C40`, so no code was left unread — the
   function's guest-instruction span is only ~4.8 KB despite a 37300-byte
   *host*-compiled size, which is why the crash's host-offset (+34664) could
   not be mapped proportionally to a guest address without a disassembler
   that isn't on the allowlist; a full read was the only reliable option).
2. Found this function is **atypically well-guarded** compared to the rest
   of the family: nearly every guest-controlled array/string index has a
   real MIPS bounds-check branch (`sltu`/loop-limit compare) translated
   ahead of it, matching legitimate original Factor 5 code rather than the
   "no check at all" shape the other 20 classes shared. Two candidates were
   weighed and one ruled out before landing a guard:
   - An unbounded "count consecutive 0xFFFF sentinels" loop
     (`0x800161A4`-`0x800161B4`) reads a caller-populated glyph-index array
     with no length bound — a real latent OOB-read risk, but weaker
     evidence it's reachable with malformed data in practice, and correctly
     terminates in-loop rather than crashing under any data seen so far.
     Not guarded this session (documented, not force-fit).
   - A per-call-site table-write for a kerning/DL cache
     (`0x800166FC`-`0x80016738`), indexed by two persistent global counters
     with no visible modulo. Traced both counters' only reset sites
     (`grep` for `MEM_W(0X7C00,`/`MEM_W(-0X5B58,` writes of literal `0`
     across all `funcs_*.c`) to `frameStartReset` and
     `initRenderStateArrays` — **both reset every frame**, which refutes
     the "grows unbounded across many frames" theory that would have made
     this the leading candidate. Not guarded (checked, not assumed, per
     rule 5 — boring explanation first).
3. Found the genuine match: a per-string-position glyph-pointer cache read
   from a fixed table (`0x8011....-0x1758`, 4-byte stride,
   `ctx->r16 = MEM_W(charIndex*4 + table_base, 0X0)`) is dereferenced twice
   (`MEM_HU(ctx->r16, 0X6)` then `MEM_HU(ctx->r16, 0X4)`, computing glyph
   advance/kerning) **before** the function's own null check on the same
   value (`beq $s0, $zero, ...`) — which exists a dozen-plus lines later in
   the same block but only guards a separate linked-list-walk loop, not
   this earlier pair of reads. If the cache entry for a given position is
   unpopulated (0 — e.g. an unsupported/never-cached glyph), this
   dereferences guest address `0x6`/`0x4` — unmapped, SIGBUS. Occurs twice,
   structurally identical, once per branch of a runtime alignment switch
   (`0x80016328`/`$s2`-loop and its mirror `0x80016790`/`$a2`-loop) — same
   "value read from a fixed table, immediately dereferenced, no check"
   shape as every other class in this family, just one level more

the non-idempotency trap NEXT.md warns about) — caught it immediately via
`grep -c` on the new patch's marker string (2 hits instead of 1), and fixed
it properly (delete `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_*.c` → `make_elf.py` →
`regen_n64recomp.sh` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` exactly once, reverified 1 hit)
before building. Flagging so a future session doesn't have to rediscover
that the "don't re-run fixup twice" rule has zero tolerance — even a
same-session accidental re-run duplicates every patch in the touched file.

### Source-read finding: neither of NEXT.md's two hypotheses as literally worded is what the code does

`cinematicLoopBody` (0x800A5D80, `funcs_27.c:106840`) calls `static_6_800AF550`
(real body `funcs_44.c:6187`) every frame; that function accumulates
elapsed time against a **fixed `.rodata` float literal** (0x800A5D70) — a
pure per-frame timer, not a poll on any DMA/asset-done flag. Crossing the
threshold sends control to `L_800A64BC`
(`funcs_27.c:107336-107340`), the cutscene's own teardown path:
`bufferArbiterProducerScanWait` (0x8000BF60) → `cinematicDeactivator` →
`waitForAnyAudioSlot` (0x800668B0) → `cinematicShutdownAudioAndAssets`.
Read `waitForAnyAudioSlot`'s actual body (`funcs_15.c:6896`) directly (not
inferred from the name): it's

```
L_800668C0:
    tickMusyXIfActive(rdram, ctx);      // first iteration only, outside the label
L_800668C0:
    anyAudioSlotActive(rdram, ctx);
    if ((r2 & 0xFF) == 0) goto L_800668C0;
```

— i.e. `while (!anyAudioSlotActive()) { }` with **no iteration cap and no
yield inside the loop**, calling `tickMusyXIfActive` only once before
entering, contrary to my first-pass reading (corrected on the 2nd read —
`tickMusyXIfActive` runs once before the label, not every iteration; the
loop body itself only calls `anyAudioSlotActive`). Read `anyAudioSlotActive`
(`funcs_23.c:8806`) too: its final return is
`v0 = ((s1 & 0xFF) < 1) ? 1 : 0` where `s1` is an OR-accumulation of
`isAudioSlotActive()` across up to `MEM_BU(0x1AD0, 0x80140000)` channels —
so it returns **1 when NO channel is active, 0 when at least one is** — the
function name is inverted relative to its own logic; `waitForAnyAudioSlot`
is actually a **drain-wait**: spin until every audio voice slot reports
idle. **This is a 3rd, previously un-named mechanism** (not H-DMA's
asset-flag poll, not H-INPUT's skip-button poll): if any voice never
signals idle (e.g. a stuck/looping channel, possibly from the same
DMA/asset-corruption family that's dogged this project since s85), this
spin loop never returns, and cinematicLoopBody never proceeds to whatever
submits the next display list — while the loop's neighbor,
`tickMusyXIfActive`, keeps the audio-ucode task counter moving, which is
exactly the s160/s161 log signature (`[lle task]` ticking forever while
`fs` is frozen). Also found by the same read: `selectPostCrawlCraft`
(0x800CB9BC) has exactly one caller, a menu_overlay mission-setup function
unreached from `cinematicLoopBody` — ruling out the "does craft-select
happen twice" alternate framing NEXT.md's Q4 raised. Full agent report
available in this session's transcript; not re-derived here to keep this
entry a summary.

### Instrument landed (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, not `lib/` — same convention as every prior guard/log in this family)

`ROGUESQ_LOG_AUDIO_DRAIN=1`, three-site patch on `waitForAnyAudioSlot`
(`funcs_15.c`, file-scoped): entry log (call index + active-channel count +
return address), a heartbeat every 2000 loop iterations via a new
file-scope `static long g_audio_drain_iters` global (proves runaway
spinning without flooding the log), and an exit log with the total
iteration count for that call. 4 call sites exist for this function
(`funcs_27/29/32/39.c`) so ordinary menu/cutscene teardown calls earlier in
a soak give a same-run positive control for "this function normally
returns fast" against whatever call is stuck at the actual stall. Full
delete-all regen + fixup (exactly once, verified) + `cmake --build`, clean
(pre-existing warning classes only, no new errors).

as `audiodrain2`, testing the same two live hypotheses for the s162

never returns; H-INPUT: a late `start`/`a` press at hold+95/100s clears

~92s stall window at all," per the budget s163 set after attempt 1 died

crash (s132/s133-135).

### Result: died at hold-iter 2 (even earlier than attempt 1's hold-iter 6), CRASH: 1, NOT `emitAllocatedDLCommand`

The crash backtrace:

```
[CRASH] caught signal 10 (Bus error: 10)
3   rs_malloc + 492
4   rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList + 224
5   static_5_800AAD9C + 5192
6   static_5_800C6854 + 628
7   menuOverlayInit + 3512
8   mainGameLoop + 2400
9   mainBootstrapWorker + 2032
```

`static_5_800AAD9C` is the known dispatcher (NEXT.md: "closed s157," not
itself a bug site) — the actual fault is inside `rs_malloc`, the guest
heap allocator itself, not in an unguarded guest-code pointer deref one
frame up. **This is a genuinely new crash class — grepped both
`docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` and this file for `rs_malloc`/
`rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` combined with SIGBUS/crash; no prior
occurrence.** The family's highest catalogued class going into this
session was the 21st (`drawSubtitleText`, s159/s160) — this is the
**22nd**.

### Source read: `rs_malloc` is a real free-list-walking allocator, not a stub — the fault site is very plausibly a corrupted free-list node, not a bad argument

Read both functions directly from `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/` (not a
symbol-file comment):

- `rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` (`funcs_14.c:8544`) calls
  `rs_malloc(rdram, ctx)` as the very first thing it does, with fixed
  `a0=0x400` (1024 bytes), `a1=0` (flags) — confirmed by the already-armed
  `[rs-malloc]` log line immediately preceding the crash (see below): this
  is not a corrupted-argument crash, the call inputs are sane and
  identical to 14 immediately-prior successful calls this same run.
- `rs_malloc` (`funcs_0.c:2745`) is a genuine heap allocator: after
  `ensureHeapInitialized` and an `osRecvMesg` lock/unlock pair, it walks a
  linked free list starting at `L_80001BB0`/`L_80001BC4` — for each node,
  loads a `flags` halfword (`MEM_HU(a0, 0)`), a `size` word
  (`MEM_W(a0, 0x4)`), and on a "not the last node" flag, advances
  `a0 = a0 + size + 0x10` to the next node (`L_80001BF4`/`L_80001C00`). A
  free-list node whose `size` field is corrupted (garbage) would make this
  walk jump to an unmapped address, and the walk's own next-iteration load
  (`MEM_HU`) would SIGBUS exactly like the observed crash — a plausible,
  concrete mechanism, not yet confirmed by a live node dump.

### `[rs-malloc]` log (already armed this run, free data) shows the crashing call broke a 14-for-14 streak, ruling out "always fails on this input"

```
[rs-malloc] ptr=0x801CD7D0 size=1024 flags=0x0 caller_ra=0x00000000   (×14, lines 64213–64448)
[CRASH] caught signal 10 ...                                          (line 64474, no matching log line for the crashing call)
```

Same `ptr`/`size`/`flags` on every one of the 14 prior calls this run
(`rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` runs once per hangar-tick frame,
allocates+presumably frees the same 1024-byte block each time — a churn
pattern, not a one-shot init) — and the crashing call has **no** log
line, meaning it faulted inside the free-list walk *before* reaching the
log write at the function's return, consistent with the walk-jumps-off-
into-unmapped-memory mechanism above. `caller_ra=0x00000000` on every
line is the already-established (s92) **routine** artifact, not evidence
by itself — noted only for completeness.

### What this establishes / rules out

- **Not a recurrence of `emitAllocatedDLCommand`/s132.** Different
  function, different call chain, different signal-adjacent frame
  entirely. NEXT.md's "if it dies to any other, different crash" branch
  applies: catalogued as new (22nd), this counts as the 2nd of the 3
  allowed soak attempts.
- **Not an argument-corruption crash** — the call's own inputs
  (`size=1024 flags=0`) are fixed and identical to 14 successful calls
  moments earlier in the same run. This narrows the mechanism to
  *allocator-internal state* (free-list metadata) rather than a bad
  pointer handed in from the caller — a different flavor from every prior
  guest-code "unguarded `table[idx]` deref" class in this family (9th
  through 21st).
- **Fits, but does not yet confirm, the long-running "shared heap
  corruption" thread** raised at s85 and chased through the DMA-ring/
  `voice+0x34` investigation (s91–s114): a free-list node's `size` field
  going bad between allocator calls is the same shape of bug (a fixed
  struct offset getting stomped by something unrelated) as `voice+0x34`,
  `ring_slot+0x4`, and the OSThread-context corruption chased earlier —
  just landing in the allocator's own bookkeeping this time instead of a
  MusyX voice struct. Not proven to be the *same* corruption source; only
  noted as a strong pattern match worth testing directly before treating
  it as a 3rd independent bug.
- **Zero new data on H-AUDIO-DRAIN/H-INPUT** — same outcome as attempt 1;
  the process still hasn't survived long enough to reach the ~92s stall
  window. Both hypotheses remain untested.
- The pre-cutscene hangar-tick window (`menuOverlayInit` → ... →
  `runHangarSelectionFrame`/`rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` etc.) is, if
  anything, **less stable** than when last soaked — this run died at
  hold-iter 2 vs. attempt 1's hold-iter 6, to a brand-new class in both
  cases. Continuing to blind-soak the exact same recipe a 3rd time has a
  visibly declining chance of reaching the target window; per rule 8 the
  higher-value move is to characterize this new crash (or the shared-
  corruption hypothesis directly) before spending the 3rd attempt.

Instead, the process died **at task #267, 1.7s into VI width 640** —

```
[CRASH] caught signal 11 (Segmentation fault: 11)
3   waitForAnyAudioSlot + 76

5   mainGameLoop + 1532
6   mainBootstrapWorker + 2032
```

## Session 166 (2026-07-27) — source-read found and guarded a concrete unguarded-pointer deref matching the 23rd class's family shape; validating soak was the cleanest ever recorded for this env block, but the guard itself got no positive control, so attribution is unresolved — the confound hypothesis is well supported either way

### Work unit

Per `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` step 1: read `waitForAnyAudioSlot`'s two
direct callees before writing anything. `tickMusyXIfActive`
(`funcs_23.c:6785`) is all-callee (`factor5MutexAcquire`/
`tickActiveSongs`/`tickAndReap3DAudioVoices`/`stopAllSynthVoices`/
`factor5MutexRelease`), no raw `MEM_*` deref of its own — ruled out.
`anyAudioSlotActive` (`funcs_23.c:8806`) loops `isAudioSlotActive` per
channel index `0..chCount-1` off a **fresh** `MEM_BU(0x80141AD0)` re-read
each iteration — no deref itself, ruled out as the direct site but not as
the source of a bad index. One level deeper, `isAudioSlotActive`
(`funcs_24.c:5788`) is the real site: loads a base pointer from the fixed
global slot at `0x801496F8` (`lw $v0, -0x6908($v0)` off `lui $v0,0x8015`),
computes `base + a0*136` (the `sll/addu/sll` idiom for `×17×8`), and does
`lbu $v0, 0x0($v1)` with **zero null-check on the base pointer** —
textbook match for this family's dominant shape (12th/14th/16th/21st
classes: fixed-global table pointer, indexed, dereferenced with no
null/range check). Also checked `rs_free` (`funcs_0.c:3093`,
`waitForAnyAudioSlot`'s other global-pointer-sourced callee, called twice
near its exit) — it already null-checks its argument at entry
(`beq $s0, $zero, L_80001F78`), ruled out as a candidate.

Could not disassemble the crash's native `+76`-byte offset to confirm
this is the *exact* faulting instruction — `nm`/`otool`/`lldb` are not on
the Bash allowlist (`scratch/agent/machoparse.py` only reads Mach-O
symbols, not disassembly) — so this is a strong, concrete, family-shape
match, not a byte-for-byte proven root cause. `isAudioSlotActive` is
frameless (no `$sp` adjustment, no callee-saved spills), so per NEXT.md
step 2's judgment call ("only do this if the source-read genuinely
identifies a concrete site"), landed a guard the same way as every prior
site in this family (s99's fixed lesson: truncate the `ctx->rN` value
through `U32()` before comparing against the `0x80000000`–`0x80800000`
valid-RDRAM-pointer bound) — but as a bare early `return;` with
`ctx->r2 = 0` (safe "not active" default) instead of a `goto`, since there
is no existing epilogue label to jump to and none of the ABI-restore
concerns every previous guard's `goto` had to reason about apply here.
Guest addresses `0x80092110`/`0x80092114` confirmed unique across the
whole `RecompiledFuncs/` tree (not just `funcs_24.c`) via grep before
writing the patch — same belt-and-suspenders check s100's collision
taught. Full regen (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py`,
patched x1, clean report, no duplication) → `cmake --build`, exit 0, only
pre-existing-class warnings.

### Result: 0 crashes across the entire 120s hold + full input sequence — the cleanest run ever recorded for this env block, but the new guard never fired (0/0, no positive control)

Ran `scratch/agent/run_audioslotguard1.sh` — identical env block to
s165's `run_audiodrain3.sh` (all ~35 loggers kept, nothing dropped) plus
`ROGUESQ_LOG_AUDIO_SLOT_ACTIVE_GUARD=1` for the new guard. Result: the
process **never crashed**. It reached VI width 1024 (title) at 44.8s,
drove through the full `STICK_SCHEDULE` (including the `95:start`
leave-key press), held the entire 120s window, and was still alive at
wall=163s when the driver killed it — every one of the 23 known crash
classes fired 0 times, every existing guard's log tag is absent from the
run (`grep`ed the full 1.6M-line log for any `-guard` tag: none), and
`[rs-malloc-walk]` fired 1,581,316 times as a clean positive control on
the logging pipeline itself.

The new `[audio-slot-active-guard]` tag **never fired** — no positive
control. `[audio-drain-enter]` (the pre-existing s163 instrument) fired
only 4 times total, all `chCount=121`, all resolving without a heartbeat
(i.e. `anyAudioSlotActive` found an active slot on its first or near-first
pass every time) — `waitForAnyAudioSlot` was barely exercised this run,
consistent with the guarded base pointer simply never being invalid this
time, not with the guard skipping a would-be crash.

The run did reproduce the **already-known** s162 post-leave
graphics-task-submission stall (`[vi-fs-decision] stalled=1 pairs=0`
continuous from mid-run, `rdpFs` plateaued at 3719 — inside the
3297–3784 range every prior crash-free/stall run has plateaued at), so
this is not a new frontier past that stall, but it **is** a 3rd
independent instance of a fully crash-free run through the entire known
23-class gauntlet (after s160/s161), now reproduced under a **much
heavier** instrumentation load (35+ loggers plus the new guard) and
driving further (4709 `[lle task]` entries vs. s165's 267) than any prior
soak in the `audiodrain`/`hangar-tick` lineage.

### What this does and doesn't prove

**Does not prove**: that the `isAudioSlotActive` guard fixed the 23rd
crash class — the guard never fired, so there is no evidence it was ever
on the crash's actual path this run. The candidate remains plausible but
unvalidated.

**Does support**: NEXT.md step 3's confound hypothesis, and more strongly
than the originally planned experiment would have — the plan was to drop
~35 env vars and see if boot still died early; instead this run **kept**
all ~35 vars, added a 36th, and still ran the entire gauntlet crash-free.
A rebuild that changes nothing about the actual bug (the guard is
dead code this run) still produced a completely different outcome than
s165's `audiodrain3` (which died at task #267 under the same-ish
instrumentation load, before this session's rebuild). This is now a
**3rd** instance of "a rebuild/relink changes which bug wins a timing
race" in this project's history (after s93's `ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME`
confound and s160→s161's own corroboration pattern), reinforcing the
shared-corruption/race framing from s85–s114 over a "23rd class is a
deterministic new frontier" framing. **Do not treat "23rd class blocks
earliest" as settled** — treat it as one data point in a family that
clearly has run-to-run/build-to-build variance independent of any single
guard.

s166 landed a guard on `isAudioSlotActive` (a concrete unguarded
base-pointer deref matching the family's dominant shape) as a candidate
fix for the 23rd crash class, but the validating soak's guard never

**Ran it.** `scratch/agent/run_audioslotguard1.sh`, unmodified, same
binary (`build/RogueSquadron64Recomp`, mtime 23:05, unchanged from the
s166 run — confirmed via `find -newer` across the whole tree between the
two driver-log timestamps: nothing else was rebuilt either). Outcome:
**it crashed.** Died at hold-iter 96 (task #7452, `lle tasks: 7452`,
`fs max: 4163`), later into the hold than several past deaths but well
before the full 120s + grace window completed cleanly the way s166's run
did.

**Not the 23rd class.** `grep -c "audio-slot-active-guard"` on the new
run's log: 0 — the guard did not fire, 2nd straight null (0/0 across
both soaks now). The crash backtrace is a SIGBUS (signal 10) with a
completely different call chain:

```
rs_free (funcs_0.c:3093)
  <- freeManifestSegmentAssets (funcs_1.c:3728)
  <- menuOverlayInit
  <- mainGameLoop
  <- mainBootstrapWorker
```

Confirmed via `grep -n "freeManifestSegmentAssets" PORTING-STATE.md
docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` returning zero hits before this session — this
exact call chain has never been catalogued. It is the **24th** distinct
crash class (23 is the highest number in use going into this session).

**Source-read the mechanism (no rebuild needed, both functions already
in `RecompiledFuncs/`).** `freeManifestSegmentAssets` walks a fixed
4-entry manifest table at guest `0x8011A80` (stride `0x50`); for each
entry it reads a pointer-sized field at offset `+0x40`
(`ctx->r4 = MEM_W(ctx->r16, 0X40)`, `funcs_1.c:3819-3820`) and passes it
straight to `rs_free` with no validation — the same "read a field off a
fixed-address table, dereference/pass it unguarded" shape as every prior
class in this family (s99, s100, s101, etc.). `rs_free` itself does
guard against a literal null pointer at entry (`funcs_0.c:3109-3110`,
`beq $s0, $zero, L_80001F78` skips the whole body), so the crash is not
a simple null deref — the table field held a *non-null, invalid*
pointer, and the SIGBUS actually happens inside `rs_free`'s free-list
walk logic (the region right after the `osRecvMesg`/list-header read at
`funcs_0.c:3131-3136`, guest base `0x8011` `-0xE8`/`-0x120` — i.e. the
same `0x8010Fxxx`-ish free-list-header neighborhood implicated in s164's
`rs_malloc` walk SIGBUS). Plausible reading: this is another surface of
the same shared free-list-corruption mechanism s164/s165 were chasing in
`rs_malloc`, now showing up on the `rs_free` side — not yet proven,
no instrument landed for it this session.

**More load-bearing than the crash-class taxonomy: the rebuild-confound
question.** s93 and the s160→s161 pair both showed "a rebuild happened,
and the crash that won the race changed" — consistent with, but not
proof of, "rebuilds specifically are what perturbs the race." This
session is a cleaner test: **the exact same binary, run twice in a row
with nothing rebuilt in between**, went crash-free then crashed on a
brand-new class. That single fact refutes "only rebuilds can cause this"
as a complete explanation — the nondeterminism is present run-to-run
even holding the binary perfectly fixed. It doesn't overturn s93 (which
remains a real, separately-confirmed instance of a rebuild changing
outcomes), but it means future soak planning should not treat "avoid
rebuilding between comparison runs" as sufficient to get a stable
before/after signal.

**Attribution scorecard after 2 runs of this exact recipe:**
- `isAudioSlotActive` guard: 0/0 both runs — unvalidated, demoted from
  "candidate fix" to "harmless parked guard," same posture as several
  other guards in this family (s99–s101, s128, s160) that never got a
  positive control.
- 23rd crash class (`waitForAnyAudioSlot`): did not recur either run —
  0/2, informative null, not a refutation (rule: a null needs a
  same-run positive control to mean anything, and this family's controls
  are about *other* logs, not this specific site).
- 24th crash class (`rs_free` ← `freeManifestSegmentAssets`): 1/2, new
  this session.

Per NEXT.md's own stopping rule ("2 data points is enough to act on...
a 3rd identical run without new information would just be burning a
soak"), this closes the `run_audioslotguard1.sh` recipe. Do not re-run

## Session 169 (2026-07-28) — source-read located and guarded all 3 unguarded free-list-pop derefs inside `reserveAndEmitDLEntry`; 2 soaks show 0/2 recurrence of the 14th-class crash that killed s168 (best-ever crash-free hold on record), but neither the new guards nor s109's guard ever fired, and the 2nd soak crashed anyway to an unrelated, previously-uncatalogued runtime-scheduler SIGSEGV

### Work unit

Per `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` step 1: source-read `reserveAndEmitDLEntry`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_3.c`, guest `0x8000CB88`-`0x8000CE90`)
past the s109 guard's coverage, looking for the same "unguarded pointer
or table-lookup result, then immediate dereference" shape as the rest of
this crash family (9th-12th, 14th's first deref all fit it).

### Source-read result

The function calls `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry()` — an internal free-list
pop — **three separate times** (labels `after_0`/`after_1`/`after_2` in
the recompiled C, guest `0x8000CBC8`/`0x8000CCC4`/`0x8000CDD0`). Each call
site already null-checks the returned pointer (`if (rX == 0) goto
<skip-label>;`, skipping the deref block when the free list was empty)
but **never range-checks a non-null return** before dereferencing it —
the identical "lookup result dereferenced without validating it's a
plausible RDRAM pointer" shape as the rest of the family, just one level
removed from s109's guard (which only covers the incoming *argument*
pointer, `ctx->r16`, not these three internal pop results). This matches
s168's own offset hint (native crash at `reserveAndEmitDLEntry + 4608`,
"not near the top"): the first occurrence (`0x8000CBDC`, ~21 guest
instructions in) is close to the top, but the second (`0x8000CCD8`, ~84
instructions in) and third (`0x8000CDE4`, ~151 instructions in, plus its
chained continuation through `0x8000CE68`/`0x8000CE70` near the function's
very end at ~184/230 instructions) both clear a "skip the first 30-40
instructions" bar and land progressively later in the function body,
consistent with a deep-offset native fault.

### Fix landed

`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`: three new guard patches, one per pop
site, following the s99-s101/s109 convention exactly (`U32()` truncation,
`0x80000000`-`0x80800000` RDRAM range check) — but reusing each site's
**own existing null-check skip label** (`L_8000CC18` / `L_8000CD14` /
`L_8000CE20`) instead of adding new labels, since the null-check already
proved that label is safe to jump to when there's no valid node to use.
Shared log gate `ROGUESQ_LOG_DLENTRY_POP_GUARD=1`, `site=0/1/2` field
distinguishes which one fired. Regenerated via
`tools/agent/regen_n64recomp.sh` (fixup-script-only change, no
`make_elf.py` needed) then `fixup_game_funcs.py` once
(`scratch/agent/s169_fixup.log`: `site=0`/`site=1`/`site=2` each patched
`x1`, no duplication, plus the pre-existing s109 patches also `x1` each —
confirms `fixup_game_funcs.py`'s per-run non-idempotence from s102 wasn't
re-triggered). `cmake --build` clean, exit 0, only pre-existing-class
format warnings.

s168's `run_rsfreewalk1.sh` plus `ROGUESQ_LOG_DLENTRY_POP_GUARD=1`)

present), `thr-resume bad=1: 0`, `missing-func: 0`, `UnhandledJump: 0`.
This is the **best crash-free result on record for this env block**,
surpassing s166's previous best (4709 tasks, first-ever full-hold

### Soak 2 (same script, same tag, re-run to test reproducibility —
same rationale as s167's re-run of s166's finding)

Crashed at **hold-iter 6** (wall=5s into the hold, before the earliest
`STICK_SCHEDULE` entry at 10s) — pop-guards and s109 guard again **0**
fires each, and critically **not the 14th class at all**: a SIGSEGV
(signal 11) with a completely different stack, entirely inside the
runtime scheduler, no guest code involved:

```
idle_thread_handle -> pause_self -> check_running_queue -> swap_to_thread
-> resume_thread_and_wait -> wait_for_resumed
-> moodycamel::LightweightSemaphore::tryWait
-> std::__atomic_base<long>::load -> SIGSEGV
```

This is the **same broad idle-thread scheduler path** as s70's SIGBUS
(`idle_thread_handle -> pause_self -> check_running_queue ->
swap_to_thread -> resume_thread_and_wait -> resume_thread ->
LightweightSemaphore::signal -> fetch_add -> Bus error`) — same call
chain down through `swap_to_thread`, but a **different leaf function**
(`tryWait`/`load` vs `signal`/`fetch_add`) and a **different signal**
(11 vs 10). Grepped this file for `tryWait` and `__atomic_base.*load`:
zero prior hits — this specific leaf/signal combination is not
previously catalogued under any class number. Given it's runtime
(`ultramodern`) code, not a guest-recompiled function, it doesn't fit
this session's guarded-deref numbering scheme; it reads as another
manifestation of the same shared thread-context-corruption family raised
at s85 and touched again at s70/s72/s83-s86 (`thr-resume bad=1` fired 0
this run, so that specific gate didn't catch whatever corrupted the
context this time either). **Not root-caused this session** — out of
scope for this work unit, flagged for a future one.

that killed s168's run** (`reserveAndEmitDLEntry`, either via the s109
site or any of the 3 newly-guarded pop sites). That's a genuine
improvement over s168 (which died to this exact crash at hold-iter 3).
But because **none of the guards ever produced a positive control across
either run**, this can't be distinguished from the established confound
(same or rebuilt binary, run-to-run timing nondeterminism changes which
bug wins the race first — s93, s160/161, s167) — it's equally consistent
with "the guards happen to cover the real fault and it's fixed" and with
"this build's binary layout just didn't hit that specific fault site
either time, for reasons unrelated to the new guards." Unlike s166 (whose
single soak gave no reproducibility check at all), this session got a
second data point via immediate re-run, and that second run **did**
crash — just to something else. The pop-guards are real, correctly
targeted (same convention as the validated 9th-12th/s109 guards), and
harmless (0/0 negative control, no regression signal) — keep them armed.
Whether they're *the* fix for the 14th class's deeper site remains
unconfirmed; a 3rd soak (per rule 8's 3-attempt budget) is the natural
next test, but was not run this session (budget spent on the
reproducibility check + this write-up instead).

### The FIRE-spacing check that complicates the stall-clear-adjacency hypothesis

Before treating `decisionsSinceFire=22`/`24` as any kind of signal, checked
what "normal" spacing between `[vi-fs-decision]` FIRE events looks like in
the window where these 2 crashes actually happened (`grep "vi-fs-decision.*FIRE"`
on the tail of each log). In both logs, FIRE events (`reason=swap` and
`reason=stalled` both present) recur roughly **every 8–61 decisions**
throughout this **active** early-post-leave window — nothing like the
"~90% stuck in `stalled=1 pairs=0`" signature s170 found in the *deep,
late-run* stall region. A `decisionsSinceFire` of 22–24 is therefore
**unremarkable, near-average spacing for this window**, not evidence of
proximity to anything — the two data points gathered this session **do not
support H1** the way s170's single post-hoc read (crash following the stall's

subsequent node in the list) was **never guarded at all**, at any of the 5
sites. This is the exact same shape already fixed elsewhere in this project
(submitSceneNodeRender's GUARD2/GUARD3 pair, s131; emitAllocatedDLCommand,
s133) — a head-deref guard alone only protects a list of length 0-1; any
list with 2+ live entries walks through the completely unprotected loop.

stayed 0/0 across every soak since s157 despite `frameStartReset`-attributed
crashes continuing to recur against exactly the class it's supposed to
cover: the guard was watching the wrong dereference.

initial-deref site to the existing `_heapwalker_guard_sites` table, and
added a new loop-back guard section (`ROGUESQ_LOG_HEAPWALKER_GUARD3`,

## Session 173 (2026-07-28) — landed and validated the `rs_malloc` walk-loop deref guard per NEXT.md, but its 2 soaks show it isn't the dominant early-crash site this run — instead recurred a **new, still-unguarded** SIGSEGV in the `waitForAnyAudioSlot` call chain, deeper than s166's own guard on the same chain

### What ran

Read the free-list walk loop in full first (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/
funcs_0.c` ~2860-3020, guest `L_80001BB0`-`L_80001C04`) to trace its actual
exit/termination condition before guarding anything, per NEXT.md's own
instruction. Confirmed: the walk's loop-back deref at `0x80001BF4`
(`MEM_HU(next, 0x10)`, `next = node + size` computed the line before) is
followed by a branch on bit `0x8` of the dereferenced flags halfword — if
set, the code falls through to `L_80001C04` (list search ends, `ctx->r4`
left unchanged); if clear, it advances `ctx->r4 = next+0x10` and loops back
to `L_80001BC4`. `ctx->r3` (the dereferenced value itself) is never read
again after that one branch, so bailing straight to `L_80001C04` without
setting it is behaviorally identical to the real "bit was set" exit — no
new termination path invented, matching the rest of this family's guard
idiom (same `0x80000000u`/`0x80800000u` bounds check, `goto` the loop's own
natural exit label).

Landed the guard (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, file-scoped to
`funcs_0.c`, new env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_MALLOC_WALK_GUARD`) right between
the existing s165 walk-log and the risky deref, following the same
comment-plus-patch-function convention as every prior guard. Full regen
(`N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py`, redirected to a log, verified exactly
x1, no duplication) -> clean rebuild (exit 0, only the pre-existing warning
classes).

  `MTLCompilerFSCache::addElement` -> ... -> `_dispatch_workloop_worker_

### What ran

Source-read `processSceneNode` (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:13759-
14861`) and its self-call site directly (not delegated), per NEXT.md's own
instruction and rule 6:

- The function walks a singly-linked sibling list rooted at mutable global
  `0x80112B20` (funcs_4.c:15037-15038/15051-15052), advanced each iteration
  by dereferencing the current node's own "next" field at offset 0
  (`ctx->r3 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0)`, funcs_4.c:15055-15056) — and calls
  **itself** once per sibling (funcs_4.c:15044) to recursively render that
  sibling's own subtree. This is a real, guest-intentional scene-graph tree
  walk, not this family's usual fixed-table-lookup-then-deref shape.
- Confirmed no depth bound exists anywhere: the `a3` argument threaded
  through the recursive call (`ctx->r7`) is immediately clobbered for
  unrelated local float-to-fixed arithmetic at funcs_4.c:13922-13940 (not a
  depth counter), and no local/static counter exists in the function at
  all. This matches the crash's own signature better than a single-deref
  bug would: both catalogued occurrences (s172 soak 1, s174) died deep
  inside the function's own native code (native PC +8148 bytes past the
  function start) rather than at any one identifiable dereference — the
  shape of a native C-stack overflow from unbounded recursion, not a bad
  pointer dereference.
- Confirmed the function's control flow funnels every return path (the
  sole `return;` at the end, plus every internal early-exit `goto`) through
  one real epilogue label, `L_80015528` (restores `$s0-$s3`/`$ra`, pops
  `$sp` by `0x30`) — confirmed unique within `funcs_4.c` via grep, as was
  the 3-line prologue anchor used for the entry-side patch (the naive
  1-line anchor collided with an unrelated function elsewhere in the same
  file, so the entry patch anchors on 3 lines instead, following s100's
  own collision lesson).

Landed a recursion-depth cap (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, file-scoped
`funcs_4.c`, new env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_DEPTH_GUARD`): a `static
int` counter (deliberately declared at the function's top-level scope, not
wrapped in its own `{ }` like every other guard in this file, so the same
counter is visible at both the entry-increment site and the far-away
epilogue-decrement site within the same function body) increments at
function entry and decrements once at the shared epilogue, so it tracks
true recursion depth 1:1 regardless of which internal path returns. On
tripping past 128, sets the return value (`ctx->r2`/`$v0`) to 0 before
bailing to the epilogue — the caller's own sibling-loop condition
(funcs_4.c:15053-15070) reads this value and stops issuing further sibling
calls when it's false, so tripping the cap also cleanly halts the runaway
branch rather than leaving the parent looping on a return value from a
call that never ran. Full regen (`N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py`,
redirected to a log, verified both new patch lines exactly x1 each, no
duplication) -> clean rebuild (exit 0, only pre-existing warning classes).

## Session 177 (2026-07-28) — offline log analysis narrowed the stall's own "stalled" field to a wall-clock artifact (not the real threshold) and found a candidate shared internal ceiling instead; landed and soaked a targeted `waitForPostSwapAck` producer-side instrument; this run's soak did not reproduce the stall, recurring instead to the s84 `frameStartReset` SIGBUS (2nd occurrence, softening its "fluke" label) with the new instrument showing a clean negative control

### What ran

Per NEXT.md's step 1 (offline log re-analysis, no rebuild): dispatched a background agent to grep the two s176 stall logs (`scenenodedepthguard1`/`2`) for the field values at each run's last real `[vi-fs-decision]` transition before the stall became permanent, looking for a shared threshold.

In parallel, source-read the RT64-side decision logic (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp` ~2828-2934) and the guest-side per-frame producer chain (`runHangarSelectionFrame` -> `waitForPrevFrameDone` -> `waitForPostSwapAck`, `funcs_40.c`/`funcs_3.c`/`funcs_5.c`) before writing any new instrument, per rule 6.

### Result 1: the "stalled" field is wall-clock-defined, not a hidden counter threshold — NEXT.md's framing needed correcting before instrumenting further

Source read of `rt64_state.cpp:2841-2843` shows `stalled` is computed directly from `std::chrono::steady_clock` — `(now - g_rs64LastAdvance) > 100.0ms` — not from any guest tick or resource count. NEXT.md's s176 framing ("most plausibly tick-count or resource-count based") was an unverified guess; it's refuted at the source level. The real open question was never "what value does `stalled` cross" (it's just elapsed wall time) — it's "why does the pending workload's `fbPairCount` (the `pairs` field) stay 0 indefinitely once stalled," i.e. why the guest stops registering new framebuffer pairs at all.

### Result 2 (background agent, offline grep, both prior runs' existing logs — no rebuild): a candidate shared internal ceiling, not a wall-clock/tick threshold

At each run's last `stalled=0` line: `rdpFs`/`skSeen`/`skNoTrig` cluster in a narrow band (~3175-3802) in **both** runs despite run 1 running 87% longer in wall-clock time before its onset (141.8s vs 75.8s) than run 2. If these counters were wall-clock- or tick-scaled, they should differ by roughly that same 87% — instead they're within 5-8% of each other. (`skPair0` is the one field that actually is wall-clock-scaled, ~50x apart, and should be discounted as a threshold candidate.) This is a single-source (one background-agent pass over 2 runs) but well-reasoned candidate: some fixed-size resource (buffer/queue-slot/semaphore count in the ~3500-3800 range) may be exhausted at roughly the same *operation count* regardless of which scene the process is in, rather than the stall being purely wall-clock/tick-gated. Not yet confirmed by a 3rd data point.

### Result 3: landed and soaked a targeted producer-side instrument (`ROGUESQ_LOG_SWAP_ACK_WAIT`) — this soak did not reproduce the stall, so it did not test the hypothesis end-to-end, but it did produce a clean negative control on the instrument itself

Source trace: `runHangarSelectionFrame` (`static_5_800AAD9C`, `funcs_40.c:5464`) calls `waitForPrevFrameDone` (`funcs_3.c:8231`) as the very first thing in its per-frame body, before any animation/camera/`submitGfxFrame` work; `waitForPrevFrameDone` calls `waitForPostSwapAck` (`funcs_5.c:6013`), which — only when two guest flags (0x8011A8C9 and 0x8011A8C8) are both set — loops on `osRecvMesg_recomp` waiting for a swap-ack message before returning. This is the only point in the per-frame producer where it can block before producing new framebuffer pairs, making it the natural target for "does the producer stop being invoked, or does it get stuck once invoked" (NEXT.md's own step-2 framing).

Landed `fixup_game_funcs.py` patches (funcs_5.c): entry counter + pre-recv/post-recv logging around the `osRecvMesg_recomp` call, gated `ROGUESQ_LOG_SWAP_ACK_WAIT`. Regenerated via `N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py` (applied exactly once, confirmed via grep on the fixup log: `funcs_5.c: waitForPostSwapAck entry diagnostic patched x1` / `... pre/post-recv diagnostic patched x1`) -> `cmake --build` (exit 0, only pre-existing SDL2-version linker warnings).

One soak (`swapackwait1`, same env block as `scenenodedepthguard2` plus the new flag): the graphics-task-submission stall **did not recur this run** — instead the process crashed (`CRASH: 2`, one `[CRASH]` block) to **a recurrence of the s84 `frameStartReset` SIGBUS** (backtrace: `frameStartReset` (x2, see below) <- `static_5_800C9BF0` <- `menuOverlayInit` <- `mainGameLoop`), at wall ~146.5s, origin `0x006A2900` width 640 (the same post-leave cutscene window s162/s176-run-1 identified) — i.e. this run got further than either s176 stall run (`rdpFs` reached 4125 vs. 3563-3746 at the other runs' stall onsets) before dying to an unrelated bug first. The backtrace shows `frameStartReset + 532` twice in a row; source-checked (`funcs_3.c:7969` onward) confirms **zero self-calls** in the function body, so this is very likely the same kind of stack-unwind duplication artifact already established for `advancePlayerAnimationPhase` in s87/88, not true recursion.

The new instrument itself behaved exactly as designed and gives a genuine (if narrow) negative control: 7391 `enter` events, 10033 `pre-recv`/10033 `post-recv` (perfectly matched — every single blocking wait this run completed and returned; the higher pre/post-recv count vs. enter count is expected, since the function's own loop can iterate more than once per call when the second flag stays set). The last 3 calls before the crash (`call=7388/7389/7390`) all show clean enter/pre-recv/post-recv triples, with the crash landing immediately after `call=7390 post-recv` — i.e. `waitForPostSwapAck` was not blocked and was not in-flight at the moment of the crash. **This is a negative control on "the producer is parked in this specific wait" for THIS run's failure mode only** — it says nothing about the original graphics-task-submission stall, since that stall did not occur this run to be tested against.

### Rules out / narrows

- Refutes NEXT.md's literal "tick-count or resource-count threshold explains the `stalled` field" framing — `stalled` is wall-clock by construction, confirmed at the source, not a threshold of any kind.
- Does not refute (nor confirm) the underlying `waitForPostSwapAck`-blocks-forever hypothesis for the graphics-task-submission stall specifically — no data point yet, since this soak crashed via a different, already-catalogued bug before ever reaching a stalled state.
- Weakens s85's "frameStartReset was a fluke" framing: that call was made after only 2 non-recurrences following the single s84 occurrence; this session adds a 2nd real occurrence (3rd total data point, now 2/3 sessions where the crash-family gauntlet reached this same site), suggesting it is at least occasionally recurring rather than a one-off, though still far rarer than the family's most-recurring classes.

### Landed (this session)

- `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`: `waitForPostSwapAck` entry + pre/post-recv diagnostic (`ROGUESQ_LOG_SWAP_ACK_WAIT`), `N64Recomp` sibling checkout (uncommitted, same posture as flagged since s90 — see Housekeeping).
- `scratch/agent/run_swapackwait1.sh` (copy of `run_scenenodedepthguard2.sh`, tag renamed, one flag added) — gitignored, not tracked.
- This repo's tracked files: `scratch/agent/NEXT.md`, `docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md`, this entry.

### Next

1. **Re-run the same `swapackwait1` recipe** (or extend `STICK_SCHEDULE` to try to reach a 3rd data point) specifically to catch the instrument DURING an actual graphics-task-submission stall — this session's soak crashed via an unrelated bug before ever reaching that state, so the instrument is armed and validated but still untested against its actual target. Watch for: last log line is `pre-recv` with no matching `post-recv` and no further `enter` ever (confirms blocked-forever-in-`osRecvMesg`), vs. `enter`/`pre-recv`/`post-recv` continuing to cycle normally throughout the stall window (refutes this mechanism, points back at the RT64-side gate logic per NEXT.md's original outcome-2 branch).
2. If the shared-ceiling candidate (Result 2, ~3500-3800 on `rdpFs`/`skSeen`/`skNoTrig`) survives a 3rd occurrence at a similar value, that becomes the priority lead over the producer-side instrument — it would give a concrete reproduction target (drive the counter to ~3500-3800) instead of waiting on wall-clock.
3. `tickSongSequence`'s 2 unguarded list walks (funcs_25.c:5018-5046, 5050-5077, found s174, not guarded) — still open, still lower priority.
4. `submitSceneNodeRender+16780` (s171) — still open, still lowest priority of the characterized-but-unfixed leads.

### Result 3: the swap-ack-wait instrument refutes BOTH of NEXT.md's anticipated outcomes — a 3rd, more specific mechanism instead

Neither of s177's two hypothesized outcomes happened:
- **Not** "blocked forever inside `osRecvMesg_recomp`" — every `[swap-ack-wait]` call this run completed cleanly: 5768 `enter` events, 9447 `pre-recv`, 9447 `post-recv` (perfectly matched, zero orphans), and the very last call (`call=5767`) shows a complete `enter`/`pre-recv`/`post-recv` triple with nothing dangling.
- **Not** "keeps cycling normally throughout the stall window" either — `[swap-ack-wait]` simply **stops appearing in the log at all** after `call=5767` (line ~64,036,414), for the remaining ~9.5M lines of the run (log ends at line 73,542,139) until the process was killed. The per-frame producer chain (`runHangarSelectionFrame` -> `waitForPrevFrameDone` -> `waitForPostSwapAck`) was never invoked again, not stuck mid-call.

This closely correlates with graphics task submission itself: the last `[lle task]` entry (RSP graphics-task submission — literally what "graphics-task-submission stall" names) is at line 64,761,412, and the driver summary's `lle tasks: 5767` count matches `[swap-ack-wait]`'s last call number almost exactly. Both stop within ~700K log lines of each other, both far short of the log's end — i.e. **graphics-task submission genuinely halts** (not merely "this one wait call never returns"), and it halts at essentially the same point the calling per-frame loop stops iterating.

The process is not a full hang, though: `[rs-malloc]` continues logging until line 67,300,546 (further than graphics/swap-ack-wait but still short of the end), and `[rs-free-walk]` dominates the log's final ~2 MB, still firing at the moment of the kill — a **staggered subsystem shutdown**, not a simultaneous freeze. Matches the pre-existing CURRENT-TRUTH characterization ("process alive... heap allocation keep running to the end of the log") only partially: heap *free-walking* runs to the very end this session, but heap *allocation* (`rs-malloc`) and graphics-task submission both stop well before the end, a nuance not previously documented.

`UnhandledJump: 873` this run — checked directly (not assumed): 867/873 matched lines decode as `Unhandled jump target 0x0231|0x17F0 in microcode factor5_ucode`, the already-documented benign RSP-microcode-fallback pattern, not a guest-CPU regression (the remaining ~6 are truncated duplicates of the same two lines at a log-rotation boundary, not new patterns).

### Rules out / narrows

- **Refutes** "the producer is blocked forever inside `osRecvMesg_recomp`" (s177's outcome-1 hypothesis) — clean, fully-matched enter/pre-recv/post-recv counts through the last call, no orphaned wait.
- **Refutes** "the producer keeps cycling normally throughout the stall" (s177's outcome-2 hypothesis, would have pointed at the RT64-side gate logic alone) — the producer stops being invoked at all, well before the stall's own tail end.
- **Reframes the root-cause direction**: the bug is not inside `waitForPostSwapAck`/`osRecvMesg_recomp` itself — it's upstream, in whatever schedules/loops `runHangarSelectionFrame` (its caller, or the guest OS thread executing it). That loop or thread stops iterating/being resumed at almost exactly the point graphics-task submission stops, which is a new, more specific, and more answerable question than "does this one wait call return."
- **Promotes** the s176/177 shared-ceiling candidate (`rdpFs`/`skSeen`/`skNoTrig` ~3175-3802) from single-source to a 3-occurrence-confirmed pattern.
- Partially corrects the pre-existing CURRENT-TRUTH stall characterization: heap *allocation* and graphics-task submission both stop before the log's end this run, only heap *free-walking* runs to the very end — "audio ucode and heap allocation keep running to the end of the log" (s162 wording) does not hold uniformly across all subsystems in this occurrence.

## Session 180 (2026-07-28) — 3rd `schedcaller` attempt reproduced the sustained graphics-task-submission stall crash-free for the first time, and found a source-confirmed, tightly-timed root-cause mechanism: the s84 UAF guard silently drops the scheduler's "next thread" turn instead of retrying or waking its caller

Per rule 8 this was the 3rd (and last allowed) attempt at the `schedcaller`-shape soak (s177 1st miss, s179 2nd miss, both to `frameStartReset`). Copied `run_schedcaller1.sh` verbatim to `run_schedcaller2.sh` (only the tag string changed) and reran.

**Outcome: full success on both axes.** Driver summary: `CRASH: 0`, `hold done wall=137s`, `done wall=161s`, process still alive at the end (driver killed it) — the **first fully crash-free soak to ever reach the target stall state**, previously the two outcomes had been mutually exclusive (s88's one crash-free run never reached the ~90-115s post-leave window this stall lives in; every run that reached it before now died to something else first). `fs max: 3747`, inside the s176-179 `~3175-3802` candidate-ceiling band (5th data point).

**The stall is genuinely sustained, not a blip.** `stalled=1 pairs=0` fired 301 times total; the tail of the run (`[vi-fs-decision]` decisions **#8000 through #16256**, the last line in the log) is one unbroken run of `stalled=1 pairs=0` with `rdpFs` frozen at exactly 3747 throughout — over 8000 consecutive stalled decisions, not isolated blips like s179's 43. `[lle task]`/`[runner] task` submission stopped for good at task `#4780`.

**Discriminating result for NEXT.md's own question.** `[hangar-loop]`'s last firing is `n=538` at run.log line 3489078; the very next lines are `[swap-ack-wait] call=4781 enter/pre-recv/post-recv` (lines 3489079-3489082) — a clean, fully-matched call, no orphan. Neither instrument fires even once more anywhere in the remaining ~400k lines of log (confirmed by full-file `grep -c`: 539 total `[hangar-loop]` lines, 19764 total `[swap-ack-wait]` lines, both accounted for by their last-seen line numbers). This is NEXT.md's first bullet outcome exactly: **the outer polling loop itself stops iterating** (it does not keep running while its callee silently skips the wait) — pointing at the guest OS thread executing it (thread id 3, confirmed again this run — 2nd confirmation that one consistent thread owns this loop) simply never being resumed/scheduled again.

**Root mechanism found, source-confirmed, single-run positive control.** Between `[swap-ack-wait] call=4781 post-recv` and the stall's onset, exactly one `[thr-resume-skip]` line fires in the entire run (`ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME` was 0 all run per s93's confound finding, so this is the always-on cheap-atomic path, not the verbose log):
```
[runner] task #4780 exit=1 dl_ptr=0x80751908 tris=578 texrects=0 fillrects=0 syncs=0 cimg=2 depth=2
[thr-resume-skip] tag=run_next id=0 ctx=0x0 live=0 bad_total=1
[vi-fs-decision] #7967 FIRE reason=stalled ...
[vi-fs-decision] #7968 SKIP reason=no-trigger ... stalled=0
[vi] update_screen #8000 ...
[vi-fs-decision] #8000 SKIP reason=pair=0 ... stalled=1 pairs=0   <- sustained from here to EOF
```
This is only the 2nd positive control the s84 gate has ever gotten (1st was s88, `bad_total=1`, process survived unaffected) — but this time it's tightly correlated with the stall onset rather than incidental. Read the gate's own source (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/threads.cpp:198-258`, `resume_thread_tagged`) to understand the mechanism rather than guessing from the log line alone:
- `run_next_thread` (line 264-272) pops the front of `running_queue` and calls `resume_thread_tagged(to_run, "run_next")`.
- If `to_run`'s context is `bad` (null, or not in the live-context set — the exact s83/s70-72 UAF signature), `resume_thread_tagged` prints `[thr-resume-skip]` and **returns without signalling anything** (line 216-220) — it does **not** retry with the next queue entry, and does **not** wake whichever thread called into the scheduler expecting a handoff.
- `run_next_thread_and_wait` (line 274-278, called from `osStopThread` and — critically — `mesgqueue.cpp`'s `do_recv`/`do_send` blocking paths at lines 105/143, which is what the guest `osRecvMesg`/`osSendMesg` blocking loop compiles down to) works by popping the next thread, then **waiting on its own context to be resumed** (`wait_for_resumed(cur_context)`). Nothing else in this call chain will ever signal that context if the popped thread was silently dropped by the guard above.

**This fully explains the observed stall mechanically, not just correlatively:** thread 3 (the hangar-loop thread) reaches `waitForPostSwapAck`'s underlying `osRecvMesg`, finds the swap-ack queue empty, inserts itself into `blocked_on_recv`, and calls `run_next_thread_and_wait` to yield — which pops thread **id 0** off the running queue to hand off execution. Thread 0's context is bad (already UAF'd/torn-down, same corruption family as s70-s94), so the s84 guard correctly refuses to signal it (avoiding the SIGBUS this run — hence `CRASH: 0`) but returns having done nothing else. Thread 3's own context is never signalled back, so it blocks forever in `wait_for_resumed`. If thread 0 was also the thread that would eventually have serviced the swap-ack message queue (i.e. would have called `do_send` on it), the deadlock is permanent and total: nobody is left to either wake thread 3 directly or produce the message it's waiting on. **This reframes the multi-session "graphics-task-submission stall" as very likely a direct, known side effect of the s84 crash-avoidance gate**: the gate trades a SIGBUS crash for a silent, permanent scheduler stall by dropping the "next" thread's turn instead of recovering from it. Not yet a 2nd independent confirmation (rule 4) — this is one run, one firing — but the timing (`[thr-resume-skip]` immediately followed by the stall's onset, with zero other candidate events in between) and the source-level mechanism (a proven silent-drop-with-no-retry, not a hand-wavy correlation) make this the strongest lead this investigation has produced since it began at s176.

**Not yet established, flagged for next session:** what guest thread **id 0** actually is (name/role/priority) — needs a source read of thread-creation call sites (`osCreateThread` call sites with their `id`/`pri` arguments), not a rebuild. Likely candidate given the message-queue mechanism above: whichever thread is expected to send the per-frame swap-ack message that `waitForPostSwapAck` waits on. Confirming this would be the natural 2nd independent line of evidence before this enters the "current truth" summary as more than a strong single-run lead.

**Stability/control summary this run:** `missing-func: 0`, `UnhandledJump: 0`, `ost-wb SKIP_OOB: 10` (routine), `thr-resume bad=1: 0` (this reports only the verbose-log path's own counter, which was off — the always-on cheap-atomic path is what actually fired, see above; do not read this field as contradicting the finding). No other crash-guard family fired; no `[CRASH]` block at all this run.

Soak artifacts: `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/schedcaller2/` (run.log 179 MB, screenshots), driver summary `scratch/agent/schedcaller2_driver.log`, driver script `scratch/agent/run_schedcaller2.sh`, extracted stall-onset lines `scratch/agent/s180_stalled_lines.txt`.

## Session 181 (2026-07-28) — refuted s180's "id 0 = single specific thread" premise; landed and validated an always-on thread-identity instrument; one soak, died early to a new-looking crash before reaching the stall

Followed NEXT.md's step 1 exactly: source-read only, no rebuild, before designing any fix. Grepped every `osCreateThread_recomp(` call site in `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/*.c` (11 hits, one is the `funcs.h` declaration) and read each one's argument setup back to where `$a1` (the `id` argument, `ctx->r5`) is assigned.

**Finding: `id` is not a unique per-thread identifier in this game — id=0 is the default/shared id used by most non-worker threads.** Of 10 real call sites, 8 pass a literal `id=0` (`ADD32(0,0)` into `ctx->r5`) and only 2 pass a dynamically-loaded id (one loads from a caller-supplied struct field, generic thread-spawn helper). The 8 literal-id=0 sites, decoded from their neighboring `entry`/`pri` argument setup, are: `idle_thread_handle` (entry `0x800017A0`, pri 10) spawning `thread3_video_handle` (entry `0x80001088`, pri 9), which itself spawns a child at entry `0x800016AC` (pri 127); a boot function creating 3 more threads back-to-back (entries `0x80019868`/`0x80019BF4`/`0x8001C328`, pri 117/122/122); one more standalone creator (entry `0x80002E10`, pri 118). This directly contradicts NEXT.md's framing ("identify what guest thread id 0 is" as if it names one thread) — **refuted**, not just unconfirmed.

**Confirmed by runtime data, not just static source-reading.** `osCreateThread`'s real implementation (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/threads.cpp:355`, `t->id = id`) proves the guest `id` argument is exactly the field the `[thr-resume-skip]`/`[thr-resume]` logs print — no host-side remapping. Landed a new always-on, unconditional log line at thread-creation time (`[thr-create-id] id=%d thr=%p pri=%d entry=0x%08X thr_rdram=0x%08X`, right after `t->context = context;` in `osCreateThread`, `threads.cpp`) plus two new fields (`thr=%p pri=%d`) on the existing cheap `[thr-resume-skip]` line — both changes are pure `lib/` host C++, no guest-code regen needed. Rebuilt clean (`cmake --build`, warnings only pre-existing SDL2-version-mismatch linker warnings). Exported patches (`submodule-patches/export.sh`) — committed this session per the hard rule.

One soak (`schedguard1`, copy of `run_schedcaller2.sh` verbatim except the tag) confirms the instrument works and extends the finding with real runtime addresses:

## Session 182 (2026-07-28) — found and fixed a real gap in the s78 refuse gate: it stops FB-map pollution but not a downstream unbounded RDRAM read, root-causing a new crash class; validated fix reached one attempt further into the hold window before an unrelated, already-catalogued Metal-internal SIGSEGV

Per NEXT.md's step 1, re-ran the `schedcaller`-shape soak (`schedguard2`, copy of s181's `run_schedguard1.sh` verbatim except the tag) to try to reach the sustained graphics-task-submission stall with the `[thr-create-id]`/`thr=%p` instrument armed.

**`schedguard2` did not reach the stall — died even earlier than s181's `schedguard1`** (hold-iter 1, ~1s into the 120s hold, vs. s181's ~7s) to a brand-new crash: SIGBUS (signal 10) inside `RT64::FramebufferStorage::store`'s `memcpy` (`rt64_framebuffer_storage.cpp:30`), called from `RT64::State::fullSync`'s color/depth-read-into-storage lambda (`rt64_state.cpp:2227`/`2271`). `[thr-resume-skip]` fired 0 times — 0 new data toward s180's still-open 2nd-confirmation requirement.

**Source-read the crash before instrumenting further (per rule 5).** `FramebufferStorage::store` does an unchecked `memcpy(rdramData.data() + dstIndex, data, size)` where `data = &RDRAM[storageAddress]` — the caller computes `storageAddress`/`readFbBytes` from a `Framebuffer`'s own `width`/`height`/`address` fields with **no bounds check against the RDRAM buffer's actual size anywhere in this call chain**. Cross-referenced the crash-adjacent log: `[fb-get] REFUSE #40 addr=0x00FF3EC0 w=225 h=158 siz=2 oob=1` fired ~1300 lines before the crash (same tick). The math confirms an exact match: `rangeEnd = 0x00FF3EC0 + imageRowBytes(225)*158 ≈ 0x1005CFC`, roughly 8MB past the RDRAM buffer's actual 8MB (`0x800000`) size — reading that far past the buffer's end is exactly the kind of access that SIGBUSes.

**This is a real, previously-uncharacterized gap in s78's `FramebufferManager::get()` refuse gate**: that gate (rightly) keeps a wild-width/OOB-address FB request out of `framebuffers[]`, but it still **returns a `refuseFb` populated with the same wild `width`/`height`/`address` the caller asked for**, with only `readHeight` forced to 0 — the s78 comment explains this was needed to avoid a different assert (`copyRenderTargetToNative`), but it means any downstream consumer that doesn't know the FB was refused (here: `State::fullSync`'s `if (colorFb->height > colorFb->readHeight)` / depth's mirror block) still treats it as a normal, readable framebuffer and reads `&RDRAM[storageAddress]` for `readFbBytes` bytes — with wild dimensions, that read runs off the end of the 8MB RDRAM buffer.

**Fix landed** (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp`, both the color block at ~2222-2254 and the mirrored depth block at ~2284-2312): before calling `workload.fbStorage.store(...)`, compute `rangeEnd = storageAddress + readFbBytes` and skip the store/read (logging `[fbsync-oob-skip] color|depth #%d addr=... bytes=...`, same throttled-log pattern as `[fb-get] REFUSE`) if `storageAddress >= 0x800000 || rangeEnd > 0x800000`, reusing s78's `FramebufferManager::get()` 8MB constant. `colorFb->readHeight`/`depthFb->readHeight` are still advanced to `height` either way, so a skipped read doesn't get retried every tick. Pure `lib/rt64` host C++, no guest regen needed — rebuilt clean (`cmake --build`, only pre-existing imgui/SDL2-version warnings).

**Validated with one soak (`schedguard3`, identical env block/tag-bumped copy of `schedguard2`).** Positive control: `[fbsync-oob-skip]` fired **17/17** (color+depth combined), and — critically — **the exact crash that killed `schedguard2` at hold-iter 1 did not recur**; the process survived past that site and progressed further (`decisionN=8016` at death vs. `7734` in `schedguard2`, hold-iter 3 vs. hold-iter 1) before dying to a **different, already-catalogued** crash: a SIGSEGV entirely inside Apple's Metal shader-compiler internals (`MTLCompilerFSCache`/`MultiLevelAirCache`, no source on our side) — the same RT64-internal-with-no-source-on-our-side class first seen s83 and s96, not a new bug, not fixable at our level. `thr-resume bad=1: 0`, `UnhandledJump: 0`, `missing-func: 0` all held clean.

**Rules out:** "the s78 refuse gate alone is sufficient to make wild FB requests harmless" — it is not; any call site that reads a `Framebuffer`'s dimensions to pull bytes from RDRAM needs its own bounds check, independent of whether the FB ever entered `framebuffers[]`. Confirms the general "wild/OOB FB" bug family (s72/s78) has more than one downstream consumer that needs guarding — this is the first one found and fixed outside the original writeback/tilecopy paths.

**Still open:** the target stall itself. Both `schedguard2` and `schedguard3` died before `[thr-resume-skip]` could fire even once, so s180's "2nd independent confirmation" of the scheduler silent-drop mechanism is still outstanding — this session's fix removes one specific early-crash competitor but the Metal-internal SIGSEGV (non-deterministic per s83/s96, sometimes doesn't recur) is now the nearest remaining obstacle before the repro can reach the stall region again.

**Full detail**: this entry. Code: `lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp` (both read-into-storage blocks) — patch exported (`submodule-patches/rt64.patch`) + committed this session. Soak artifacts: `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/schedguard2/` and `schedguard3/` (run.log, screenshots), driver summaries `scratch/agent/schedguard{2,3}_driver.log`, driver scripts `scratch/agent/run_schedguard{2,3}.sh`.

1. **Get a soak that reaches the stall with the `[thr-create-id]`/`thr=%p` instrument armed** — now one specific early-crash competitor (the `FramebufferStorage::store` OOB read) is fixed; the nearest remaining obstacle is the non-deterministic Metal-internal shader-compiler SIGSEGV (s83/s96 lineage) that killed `schedguard3`. Re-attempt the same soak shape 1-2 more times before considering that crash itself worth a characterization pass (it has no source on our side, so a fix there isn't possible — only working around it by understanding what triggers the shader compile, e.g. a first-time-seen material/shader combination in the hangar scene, is).
2. Try to land a 6th `rdpFs`-onset data point (any soak) to further tighten the ~3500-3800 ceiling band (now: 3560/3561/3784/3740/3747, unchanged this session — neither soak reached that phase).
3. `tickSongSequence`'s 2 unguarded list walks (funcs_25.c:5018-5046, 5050-5077, found s174, not guarded) — still open, still lower priority.

## Session 183 (2026-07-28) — 4th `schedcaller` attempt reached AND SUSTAINED the target stall for the first time (hold-iter 68 vs. previous best 3), but `[thr-resume-skip]` fired 0 times the entire run — weakens, does not confirm, s180's scheduler-silent-drop mechanism as the (sole) cause

Per NEXT.md's step 1, re-ran the `schedcaller`-shape soak again (`schedguard4`, verbatim copy of `run_schedguard3.sh` except the tag, same env block/`STICK_SCHEDULE`). Goal: get past the non-deterministic Metal-internal SIGSEGV that killed `schedguard3` and reach the sustained stall with `[thr-create-id]`/`thr=%p` armed, then cross-reference a `[thr-resume-skip]` firing's `thr=%p` against `[thr-create-id]` to identify the dropped thread (NEXT.md step 2).

**Big jump in reach.** `schedguard4` survived to **hold-iter 68** (wall=75s into the 120s hold) — the deepest any soak in this line has gotten, vs. `schedguard3`'s hold-iter 3, `schedguard2`'s hold-iter 1, `schedguard1`'s ~7s. `fs max: 4010`, a new high (past the previously-tracked "~3500-3800 candidate ceiling" band from s176-179/s181/s182 — see below, that framing is refined this session, not just extended).

**Reached and sustained the actual target stall.** `[vi-fs-decision]` shows a clean, long, uninterrupted plateau: decisions **#9792 through #12480** (2688 decisions logged, the tail ~389 of them at the exact same `rdpFs=4010`) all read `SKIP reason=pair=0 seen=0 addrCh=0 stalled=1 pairs=0` — the canonical sustained-stall signature from s176-182, held far longer than any prior soak reached it. The crash's own `[CRASH][vifs-snapshot]` line confirms it structurally: `decisionN=12490 lastFireDecisionN=9770 decisionsSinceFire=2720 lastFireWasStalled=0 stalledNow=1` — the process was crashing *while inside* the stall, not before reaching it.

**Died to a new-looking crash, still inside the stall, with zero `[thr-resume-skip]` fires anywhere in the run.** SIGBUS (signal 10) inside `rs_free` (`funcs_0.c:3093`), called from `rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` → `static_5_800C9BF0` → `menuOverlayInit` → `mainGameLoop` → `mainBootstrapWorker`. This is the same **shared-heap-corruption walker family** already catalogued (s164's 22nd class was `rs_malloc` ← the same `rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` caller with sane-looking args; s167's 24th class was `rs_free` ← a different caller, `freeManifestSegmentAssets`) — this exact `rs_free ← rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` combination hadn't been logged before, but it's a new data point *within* an existing family, not a new independent bug class.

**This is the key finding, and it cuts against s180's mechanism, not for it.** `grep -c "thr-resume-skip" run.log` → **0**, for the entire ~120s run, despite the process reaching, sustaining (2688 decisions), and eventually dying inside the exact stall region s180 characterized. s180's single prior occurrence found `[thr-resume-skip] tag=run_next id=0 ... bad_total=1` firing immediately before that run's stall onset, and framed it as *the* root cause. This run's stall onset — pinned tightly between decision `#9770` (last `FIRE reason=swap`) and `#9792` (first `SKIP ... stalled=1`), i.e. within ~22 decisions / a few hundred ms, same "tightly-timed" character as s180's finding — has **no scheduler bad-resume event anywhere near it**. Checked the raw log window between those two decisions directly (`sed -n '3862860,3866000p' run.log`, tag-filtered): the **only** non-heap-walk log line in that entire window is the `#9770 FIRE` line itself — no `[lle task]`, `[swap-ack-wait]`, `[thr-resume]`, or `[thr-resume-skip]` activity at all, consistent with s178's "the producer simply stops being invoked, no wait/yield, no error" characterization, but with a producer-stoppage this time that the s84 UAF-guard-skip mechanism cannot explain (it never fired).

**Refines (does not simply extend) the "rdpFs candidate shared ceiling" framing from s176-179/s181/s182.** rdpFs did **not** freeze exactly when the stall began — it climbed steadily to 3999, jumped to 4010 at decision `#9144`, and then **swaps kept firing normally for 626 more decisions** (`#9144`→`#9770`, all `FIRE reason=swap`, `stalled=0`, `rdpFs` pinned at 4010 the whole time) before the actual stall (no more FIREs at all) began at `#9792`. So "rdpFs stops incrementing" and "the graphics-task stall" are **two distinct events, not one** — rdpFs plateaus wherever the RDP opcode stream happens to end for this content, and normal swap/present activity continues for a while after that using the last-submitted content, before the *actual* stall (task submission itself stopping) hits separately, hundreds of decisions later. The specific plateau value (4010 here vs. 3560/3561/3784/3740/3747 previously) is content-dependent, not a fixed hang ceiling — tracking it further as a "ceiling to tighten" (open item 2, prior sessions) is not a productive framing; retiring that framing this session.

**Rules out:** "the s84 `[thr-resume-skip]` scheduler silent-drop is a necessary precondition for this stall" as a general claim — it is sufficient in at least one observed instance (s180) but **not necessary** in at least one other (this session), since the stall was reached, sustained, and crashed-through with zero occurrences of that log line. Does not rule out that s180's occurrence was still a real, valid instance of *a* cause of the stall — multiple independent mechanisms landing on the same externally-observed symptom (`[vi-fs-decision] stalled=1 pairs=0` sustained) is now the better-supported framing than "one root cause".

**Not chased further this session** (per rule 8 posture — this is a discriminating result, not a null, so the right move is to write it up and re-plan, not keep soaking blind): what specifically stops `[lle task]`/`[swap-ack-wait]` being invoked in *this* run's `#9770`→`#9792` window, if not the s84 UAF guard. That is now the open question item -33 was trying to answer, reopened with a refuted leading hypothesis.

**Full detail**: this entry. No code changes this session (pure re-run of existing instruments, no `lib/` edits — `export.sh` not needed). Soak artifacts: `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/schedguard4/` (run.log — 1.7GB, screenshots through `hold_67.png`), driver summary `scratch/agent/schedguard4_driver.log`, driver scripts `scratch/agent/run_schedguard4.sh`/`wait_for_schedguard4.sh`.

### Carried-forward open items (item 1 replaced, others unchanged from s182)

1. **Find what actually stops graphics-task submission in the `#9770`→`#9792` window of `schedguard4`**, now that the leading hypothesis (s84 UAF-guard silent drop) is shown not to be firing in this instance. Candidates to check by source-read first (per rule 5, before instrumenting): (a) the outer hangar-tick loop's own exit/break conditions (s180 already confirmed *a* version of "outer loop stops iterating" — re-check whether that's reachable without going through `resume_thread_tagged`'s bad-context branch at all, e.g. a normal/successful thread switch that simply never switches back); (b) `viRetraceHandlerThread`/`musyxSynthFrame`'s per-VI-retrace tick — does it, or some audio-side blocking call, ever hold a lock or resource the graphics-task producer needs; (c) whether `[rs-malloc-walk]`/`[rs-free-walk]` volume itself (they dominate the log almost totally during and after the stall) points at a heap-exhaustion or allocation-stall condition on the producer's own allocation path. Keep `[thr-create-id]`/`thr=%p` armed regardless (free, no rebuild) in case a *different* run's stall onset does correlate with a `[thr-resume-skip]` fire — s180's mechanism is weakened as a general explanation, not eliminated as *a* possible one.

3. `tickSongSequence`'s 2 unguarded list walks (funcs_25.c:5018-5046, 5050-5077, found s174, not guarded) — still open, still lower priority.
