## Session 223 (2026-07-28) — refuted the mat3x3InverseInto/setupCameraMatrices determinant hypothesis with a well-controlled null (456k+ firings spanning the whole hold), but a same-schedule re-run of s222's exact soak reached mesh-heavy space combat AND the opening crawl for a 2nd-ever time, then froze on a flat ground-color fill (not "torn/striped") with the swap/present pipeline still demonstrably live — non-determinism now proven on byte-identical scripted input, not just suspected

NEXT.md's planned unit: source-read `setupCameraMatrices`/
`traverseSceneGraphRecursive`/`composeNpcOrientationMatrix` end to end for a
transform value that could go degenerate during the post-`SELECT YOUR
CRAFT` camera fly-out, then land ONE targeted diagnostic and re-soak.

**Source read** (delegated to an Explore sub-agent, then independently
verified by direct read, not taken on trust): `setupCameraMatrices`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:19142-21603`) conditionally computes
a 3x3 matrix inverse of the camera struct's own `+0x2C` submatrix
(`$s1+0x2C`, gated on a flag byte at `$s1+0x0`) at `funcs_4.c:21299-21322`,
immediately before calling `traverseSceneGraphRecursive` — i.e. its output
feeds straight into the corrupted-frame render path this whole lineage
(s150/s220/s221/s222) has been chasing. The callee,
`mat3x3InverseInto` (`funcs_5.c:7208-7208+`), computes the determinant via
cofactor expansion then `f10 = 1.0f / det` at guest `0x8001C7E4`
(`funcs_5.c:7326`) — a zero/degenerate determinant produces `+/-Inf` here.
Critically, `NAN_CHECK` (`recomp.h:396`, `assert(val == val)`) passes for
`Inf` (`Inf == Inf` is true) and only catches true `NaN`, and only checks
its own OPERAND, never a result — so an `Inf` here sails past every
downstream `NAN_CHECK` on its own value, and the three adjugate multiplies
that follow (`0x8001C7E8`/`0x8001C7F0`/`0x8001C7F8`) check their input
operands (`Inf` passes) but never re-check the PRODUCT. If any cofactor
term is exactly `0.0`, `Inf * 0.0 = NaN` would be produced and stored
straight into the output matrix with no assert ever tripping — a plausible
"silent NaN, no crash" mechanism matching the observed symptom (permanent
visual corruption, process never crashes) exactly. `composeNpcOrientation
Matrix` (`static_5_800AB1C8`) was read too (matching the s150 backtrace
name) but NOT chosen as the instrumentation target: it already carries 7
guards from s99-s158, all confirmed 0/0 across every soak despite its
entry diagnostic firing 508/508 in at least one prior run (CURRENT-TRUTH
item -9/-10) — re-treading that exact function would be budget-rule-8
territory (a 3rd+ attempt at an already-dead-ended lead), whereas
`mat3x3InverseInto` was untested by any prior session.

**Instrument landed**: `fixup_game_funcs.py` (sibling `N64Recomp` checkout,
untracked there per the s83 flag, not this repo's commit scope) gained a
new patch at `funcs_5.c`'s `0x8001C7E4` div site — entry counter (capped at
first 3 + every 2000th to bound log volume, since this is a generic 3x3-
inverse utility called from ~50 sites, ~1300×/s in practice) plus an
UNCAPPED abnormal-value log (`det==0.0f || isnan(inv_scale) ||
isinf(inv_scale)`) gated behind `ROGUESQ_LOG_MAT3INV=1`. Full regen done
clean-room per the s221-proven recipe (not incremental) to avoid any

## Session 224 (2026-07-28) — the camera's own raw pose field keeps changing for ~60s AFTER the picture (and RDP full-sync counter) already froze, directly answering NEXT.md's discriminating question: this is a downstream scene-graph/render-submission freeze, NOT a stuck camera

Per NEXT.md Step 1/2: `setupCameraMatrices` (`funcs_4.c:19142-21603`) never
reads a separate XYZ translation field from the camera struct passed in
`$s1`/`ctx->r17` — offsets `0x10/0x14/0x18/0x1C` are an integer viewport
rect, `0x20/0x24/0x28` are perspective near/scale scalars, and the only
orientation data in the struct is the `+0x2C` 3x3 submatrix that
`mat3x3InverseInto` conditionally inverts (s223's now-closed lead). World
position/view concatenation happens through a separate fixed-address global
matrix (`0x8012xxxx - 0x23A4`), not through this struct. So the field
chosen — the camera's own field, not a derived product, per NEXT.md's
constraint — is `m[0][0]` of that raw `+0x2C` submatrix, read directly
BEFORE any inversion, logged (`ROGUESQ_LOG_CAMPOSE`, `fixup_game_funcs.py`
funcs_4.c, guest `0x800178A8`) alongside the struct's own gating flag
(`+0x0`) and the struct pointer itself (to catch camera-instance swaps),
every 60th call, uncapped on NaN/Inf. Clean delete-all-funcs regen (not
incremental, same proven recipe as s221/s223), built clean (0 errors).

**Soak** (`campose1`, same `schedulepush2`-derived schedule as
s222/s223's `mat3inv2`, `HOLD_S=350`, synchronous foreground): survived
the full 350s hold crash-free. `[campose-entry]` fired 966/966 times, real
positive control (`camptr` visits at least 5 distinct camera-struct
addresses over the run's early menu/craft-select phase before settling on
one address for the whole flight portion), 0 abnormal (NaN/Inf) — a 2nd,
independent confirmation that this struct field is never corrupted
(complements, does not duplicate, `mat3inv-entry`'s 385/0-abnormal 2nd
confirmation of s223's already-closed determinant null in the same run).

**MD5-checksummed all 350 `hold_NN.png`** (`scratch/agent/checksum_campose1.py`):
this run's picture changes through `hold_82`, then is byte-identical
`hold_82`...`hold_350` — a real-content freeze (checksums 1/12-40/70-76/81/82
all distinct, matching the pattern of genuine motion, not an immediate
dead-hangar hang). Cross-checked against this same run's own `[phase]` log:
the LAST `vi_width` transition in the entire 420s-wall run is at process
time **170.6s** (line 176881, `vi_width=512 origin=0x00690400`) — no further
VI-resolution changes for the remaining ~250s, consistent with the
checksum-observed freeze. `[vi-fs-decision]` at the very end of the run
still shows `stalled=0, reason=swap` with the VI buffer address actively
alternating (`0x690000`/`0x620000`) but `rdpFs` plateaued at **3965** — a
2nd independent soak reconfirming s223's finding that the swap/present
pipeline stays alive through the freeze (ruling out a present-pipeline
stall) while RDP task submission itself has stopped.

**The discriminating result**: correlating `[campose-entry]`'s own line
numbers against this same freeze window shows the camera struct pointer
settles onto its final value (`0x80138D20`, the flight camera) right around
`n=15000` (line 177777, essentially coincident with the 170.6s phase
transition and the checksum freeze onset) — but **`m00` keeps changing for
another ~5880 calls** after that (0.99 → 0.887 → 0.823 → 0.809, a brief
plateau ~0.808 for a few hundred calls, then 0.742 → 0.350 → 0.289 → 0.292 →
0.293 → 0.291), only freezing permanently at **`m00=-0.707199`** at
`n=20880` (line 229189) — roughly **60+ seconds of continued camera-pose
change after the on-screen picture and RDP submission had already gone
static**, before the camera itself also eventually wedges and holds
`-0.707199` for the remaining 36900 calls (~end of the 350s hold).

**This directly answers NEXT.md's Step-3 discriminating question**: the
camera does NOT stop at the same moment the picture does — it keeps being
computed for roughly a minute afterward — so per NEXT.md's own framing,
this is the **"camera keeps changing after freeze onset" outcome**: the
camera-matrix code itself is not the wedge; something downstream (scene-
graph population, node visibility/culling, or draw-command submission
itself — `processSceneNode`/`submitSceneNodeRender`/
`traverseSceneGraphRecursive`) stops producing new drawable content while
the camera (and whatever drives it) keeps running for a while longer. The
camera's own later freeze (`n=20880`) is a secondary event, not yet
explained — plausibly it depends on state that the render freeze already
broke (an animation/timer tied to visible progress), or is an unrelated 2nd
wedge; not investigated this session.

**Caveat (rule 4)**: the *picture*-freeze timing has 2 independent
corroborating signals within this one run (checksum + `[phase]`/
`[vi-fs-decision]` plateau) and is consistent with s222/s223's established
pattern across many runs — well-supported. The *specific new claim* here
("camera keeps moving ~60s past the render freeze") rests on ONE run of
this ONE new instrument — strong and internally clean (966/966 positive
control, 0 abnormal, a sharp and large 60s separation, not a marginal
effect), but not yet independently reproduced. Given the schedule's proven
non-determinism (s223), a repeat run may freeze at a different point or not

## Session 228 (2026-07-28) — overturns s226/s227's "`tools/:*`-specific" framing: `Bash(build/:*)` (a different rule) fails identically via a control test, narrowing the gate to a whole class of `Bash(<dir>/:*)` rules vs. working `Bash(<word>:*)` rules, with a concrete one-line-per-rule settings.json fix proposed for a human

*(Note: this session's header was missing in the original write-up — the
body below ran on directly after s227's closing paragraph with no `##`
break. Added retroactively s229 while appending this session's entry, no
content changed.)*

Per NEXT.md's Step 0 (written by s227), re-ran the control command
`tools/agent/stop_gate.sh --verify` first, before touching the actual
regen work. It failed identically to s226/s227: "This command requires
approval." Per this project's own budget rule (iron rule 8, applied to

**New test**: `build/idontexist_permcheck_s228 --help` — a command
targeting the `Bash(build/:*)` allow rule (a DIFFERENT rule from
`tools/:*`) with a deliberately nonexistent binary, so a "command not
found" response would prove permission WAS granted (failure happening
after the permission layer, inside the shell), while "requires approval"
would prove the block happens AT the permission layer, before the shell
ever runs anything. Result: "This command requires approval" — same
failure mode as `tools/:*`, on an entirely different rule.

**This overturns the s226/s227 framing that the gate is specific to
`tools/:*`/`./tools/:*`.** It is not. Both `tools/:*` and `build/:*` fail
identically. Cross-referencing which rules in `.claude/settings.json` HAVE
been empirically confirmed working this session and prior sessions
(`grep`, `python3`, `pwd`, `git status`/`diff`/`log`/`show`, `git add`) —
every working rule is shaped `Bash(<bare-word>:*)` or
`Bash(<word> <word>:*)`, i.e. the ruled prefix is a complete command
token that is followed by a space in real invocations. Every failing rule
found so far is shaped `Bash(<dir>/:*)` — a bare directory name ending in
a slash, where real commands continue immediately with no space
(`tools/agent/stop_gate.sh`, not `tools/ agent/stop_gate.sh`).

**New hypothesis, sharper than s227's two candidates**: Claude Code's
`Bash(<prefix>:*)` syntax treats `:*` as "exact command-word, then any
argument after a space" rather than a raw string-prefix wildcard — so a
rule intended to match "anything starting with `tools/`" needs the
glob-only form `Bash(tools/*)` (no colon), not `Bash(tools/:*)`. This
would explain 100% of the observed pattern with a single mechanism, is a
known distinction in glob-permission systems, and predicts a specific,
cheap, testable fix. Written up in full in `scratch/agent/BLOCKED.md`,
including the exact settings.json edit to try (`tools/:*` -> `tools/*`,
`./tools/:*` -> `./tools/*`, `build/:*` -> `build/*`, `./build/:*` ->
`./build/*`) and a falsification path (test in an interactive session
first if a human wants to confirm before editing).

(landed s226, `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`) remains unvalidated, third
session running. Everything in CURRENT-TRUTH's "Next steps" that requires

run. **`m00` keeps changing until `n=21240`** (close to s224's own
already-documented `n=20880` figure, same phenomenon, this run's instance).
**`deref0` keeps changing until `n=57900`** — i.e., through nearly the
*entire* remaining run (58560 is the last sample), roughly 2.7x further
past the freeze point than `m00`'s own lag, and `deref0_valid=1`
throughout (never an invalid/out-of-range pointer). This directly answers
NEXT.md's discriminating question: **outcome #2 confirmed** — "deref0
keeps changing after flag/camptr freeze (matching the m00 pattern) →
pointed-to content still live; freeze is further downstream (traversal
walk logic or a content-independent culling check)." Outcome #1 ("deref0
also freezes at/near the same n") and outcome #3 ("deref0_valid=0
throughout") are both refuted.

**What this rules out**: the camera struct's own linkage pointer target
(the memory `flag`/`camptr` points into) is NOT frozen — it keeps being
written to for the vast majority of the visibly-frozen window. Combined
with s225's already-closed finding that `traverseSceneGraphRecursive` /
`processSceneNode` / `submitSceneNodeRender` all keep firing at a steady
rate through the whole freeze, this now closes off "the camera-adjacent
data itself stopped updating" as an explanation at two levels deep (the
struct's own fields, AND the first word of what one of those fields
points to). The freeze must be either (a) in scene-graph traversal logic
that reads this live data but computes/selects the same result every call
regardless of the change (a content-independent culling/selection check),
or (b) downstream of traversal entirely — in DL emission, RDP submission,
or the display-list/framebuffer target itself not reflecting the updated
state. Neither has direct instrumentation yet.

**Two independent lines of evidence** for "downstream, not stuck-camera":
(1) this session's own `deref0` result, (2) s224/s226's prior, independent
finding that `m00` (same struct, different field) also outlives the
freeze point. Two same-struct fields agreeing is corroborating but not
fully independent (common data source) — still label the overall
"downstream freeze" conclusion as resting on the scene-traversal-firing
evidence (s225, a genuinely different subsystem) as the second independent
leg.

## Session 230 (2026-07-28) — found and instrumented a concrete render-cache "epoch" mechanism in `processSceneNode`; diagnostic confirms the epoch is a live, actively-changing value early in a run (not stuck), but two soak attempts with it armed both crashed near the SELECT-CRAFT→mission VI transition, before reaching the freeze window — a same-binary control (unmodified campose3, diagnostic compiled in but not env-enabled) ran clean 424s, isolating the crash to the diagnostic being ACTIVE, not to the new code's mere presence

**Read-only source trace (Probe A from s229's NEXT.md, no build) found a
concrete candidate mechanism.** Delegated a deep read of
`submitSceneNodeRender`/`processSceneNode` (`funcs_4.c`, ~4200 combined
lines of decompiled MIPS-to-C) to a subagent, then independently verified
every cited line myself before acting on it (all confirmed accurate):
`submitSceneNodeRender` reads a global word at fixed guest RDRAM address
`0x8011A894` near its top (`funcs_4.c:10-12`) and unconditionally stamps
it into `MEM_W(node_ptr+0x30)` every call (`funcs_4.c:41-42`).
`processSceneNode` has two near-identical cache-check blocks
(`funcs_4.c:13881-13890` and `:14732-14751`) comparing this same global
against a previously-stamped `+0x30` value — on match it falls through to
`L_80014FE8` and reuses a cached `+0x34` value feeding a render-queue
insert (the same queue the existing s152 diagnostic already confirmed
keeps growing); on mismatch it jumps to a recompute path
(`L_8001513C`/`L_80015404`).

**Important sub-finding: exhaustive grep across every `funcs_*.c` file
for a write to this exact address (the only valid MIPS lui/addiu
encoding, base `0x8012<<16` offset `-0x576C`) found exactly ONE writer**:
`buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial` (`funcs_4.c:22608-22636`), which sets
it to the hardcoded constant `1` conditionally — not an increment. No
per-frame increment site was found anywhere in the recompiled game code
via static search. This raised real uncertainty about whether the
mechanism was even a live "epoch" at all (vs. a one-time material-
registry-generation stamp) — resolved empirically below, not by more
static reading (would have been a 2nd+ full-function read pass on the
same question; chose to instrument and measure instead, per iron rule 8's
spirit and the project's own stated preference for discriminating
measurement over indefinite static analysis).

**Landed a diagnostic** (`fixup_game_funcs.py`, two new patch functions
`_render_cache_epoch_patch_a`/`_b`, both anchored on the existing
`ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r16/r17, 0X30);` lines at the two call sites) gated
by a new env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_RENDER_CACHE_EPOCH=1`. Logs, per site: a
running call counter, the epoch value, the stamped comparison value, a
hit/miss flag, a heartbeat every 500 calls, and an unconditional log of
the first hit↔miss transition after a run of ≥50 consecutive same-result
calls (to cheaply capture change points without flooding output). Full
regen/build succeeded clean (`make_elf.py` → `regen_n64recomp.sh` →
`fixup_game_funcs.py` once → cmake build, all green, patch report
confirmed both sites patched x1).

**campose4 attempt 1** (new tag, copied from s229's `campose3` per
NEXT.md's own instructions, same schedule, `ROGUESQ_LOG_RENDER_CACHE_EPOCH=1`
added): diagnostic fired correctly and immediately answered part of the
question — the epoch value is genuinely LIVE during early gameplay,
climbing `0x24 → 0xE7 → 0x114 → 0x14A → 0x171 → 0x183` across the first
~1500 `processSceneNode` calls (roughly monotonic, not a stuck constant).
This rules out the most trivial reading of H2 ("constant the whole
run"). But the game process crashed at wall≈23s (`hold-iter 3`), a
Bus error at `pc=0x104c4c8ac`, symbol `static_5_800AB658+49104`
(`far=0x380000014`) — well before the previously-observed freeze windows
(`n=15360`+ in s223-s229). Preserved as
`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/campose4_attempt1_crash/`.

**campose4 attempt 2** (2nd of 2 budgeted soak attempts, identical
script): crashed again, even earlier (wall≈21s, `hold-iter 1`), a
different Bus error at `pc=0x1009cfee4`, symbol
`tickTextureMaterialExpiry+612` (`far=0x38000ffb2`). Both crashes'
`[phase] vi_width=512 (was 1024)` transition line landed within 0.6s of
each other (73.9s vs 73.3s) — i.e., both crashes cluster tightly around
the SELECT-YOUR-CRAFT→mission-launch VI-width transition, not at a
random point. Different PC/symbol between the two attempts argues
against a single deterministic fault line in the new patch's own logic
(a genuine bug in one exact line would crash at the same PC every time);
both `far` addresses match the `0x38...`-prefixed garbage-pointer pattern
already common across this codebase's many pre-existing unguarded-deref
crash families (the same family the dozens of existing `GUARD`-suffixed
patches exist to catch). Preserved as
`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/campose4_attempt2_crash/`.

**Control test (not one of the 2 budgeted soak attempts — a
discriminating check, iron rule 1's positive-control spirit applied to a
crash instead of a null result)**: re-ran s229's UNMODIFIED `campose3`
script verbatim (copied to a new tag `campose3control_s230` so as not to

patch code compiled in but `ROGUESQ_LOG_RENDER_CACHE_EPOCH` left unset)

cause to the diagnostic being ACTIVELY ENABLED at runtime (the extra
`fprintf` I/O and branch-history bookkeeping), not to the mere presence
of the new compiled code shifting binary layout. Most likely explanation:
the added I/O overhead perturbs frame timing enough to reproducibly (2/2)
nudge this specific, already-timing-sensitive scene-transition window
into a pre-existing crash-family bug that this exact schedule would
otherwise avoid or hit only rarely — not a new bug introduced by the
diagnostic's own logic. This is a hypothesis, not a proven mechanism;
flagged as such.

**Net result — the core H1/H2/H3 discriminating question (does the
epoch value go constant at/near the already-known picture-freeze point)
is UNANSWERED this session.** The crash pre-empted reaching that window
in both attempts. This is a null result on the main question WITH a
positive control satisfied (the instrument demonstrably fires and
produces real, changing data before the crash, and the control run proves
the binary itself is sound) — legitimate per iron rule 1, but incomplete.
Genuinely new information gained: (1) the epoch is confirmed live/
changing early in a run, ruling out the trivial "stuck from frame 1"
reading of H2; (2) this diagnostic's I/O overhead is load-bearing for
run stability near this specific transition — next session must reduce
it before re-attempting the freeze-boundary measurement.

backend, not the `contrib/metal-cpp` Apple bindings) and

could explain s238's host-side SIGSEGV inside QuartzCore
(`x_hash_table_remove_ptr`<-`CAMediaTimingInvalidate`<-`-[CALayer
dealloc]`<-`CA::Transaction::commit`). No build, no soak — per NEXT.md
and iron rule 8 (the `campose*` soak budget was spent as of s238).
Delegated the file reads to a general-purpose subagent to keep the
source dumps out of the main session's context; verified its key
file:line citations directly afterward (`plume_metal.cpp:2084-2109`,
`rt64_present_queue.cpp:110-120` and `840-860`) before writing them into
this ledger.

**Finding — one concrete, narrow, PLAUSIBLE-not-CONFIRMED candidate**:
`MetalSwapChain::resize()` (`plume_metal.cpp:2084-2101`) calls
`layer->setDrawableSize(drawableSize)` (line 2093) from inside
`PresentQueue::threadLoop()`, which runs on a dedicated background
thread (spawned as `new std::thread(&PresentQueue::threadLoop, this)`,
`rt64_present_queue.cpp:117`, thread named `"RT64 Present"`,
`rt64_present_queue.cpp:855`) — not the main thread, which is what owns
`Cocoa_PumpEvents`/`CA::Transaction::commit` in the crash's outer
frames. `CAMetalLayer` property setters like `setDrawableSize:`
participate in CoreAnimation's implicit-transaction/timing bookkeeping,
which Apple does not document as safe to mutate from a non-main thread
(unlike `nextDrawable`/drawable `present()`, which ARE documented
thread-safe). A race here is a plausible mechanism for exactly this
symptom: corruption introduced by the cross-thread mutation, but only
surfacing later — during a subsequent `-[CALayer dealloc]` inside
`CA::Transaction::commit` on the main thread — rather than crashing
immediately at the mutation site. That fits the observed frame-count-
delayed (not immediate) fault better than a direct double-release at the
resize call site would.

**Important gap, found by the same static read, that keeps this at
PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED**: there is no `SDL_SetWindowSize` or
window-recreation call anywhere in `src/main/` in this repo. The
VI_WIDTH register flip (1024->512, logged at `src/main/
rt64_render_context.cpp:814-838`) is a guest-side N64 framebuffer
register change, not a host OS window resize — no code path was found
in this repo that makes a VI_WIDTH change directly call into
`MetalSwapChain::resize()` or otherwise resize the host window/
`CAMetalLayer`. This means the tight correlation (crash at n=12420/
t≈131s, ~56s after the VI-width transition at t≈74.2s) could be
coincidental — both could be periodic, frame-count-driven events that
happen to land near each other across all 3 soaks — rather than causally
linked through this specific resize path. Do not upgrade this to
"confirmed" without closing that gap.

## Session 243 (2026-07-28)

Ran the `mtldebug1` soak per s242's NEXT.md plan: same `campose*`/guard
set and `schedulepush2` schedule as `malloclog2`, `GAME_EXTRA_ENV="MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1"`
(Apple's Metal API validation layer) instead of malloc-scribble vars,
scoped to only the game process via the s241 `GAME_EXTRA_ENV` mechanism.

**Positive control passed**: `run.log` line 1 is
`Metal API Validation Enabled`, confirming the env var reached the
Metal runtime inside the game process (not silent like `malloclog2`'s
MSL/scribble vars were).

**Result: the soak found a NEW, distinct, much-earlier crash — NOT the
`n=12420`/`t≈131s` host-CALayer-teardown SIGSEGV family under
investigation.** `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER` triggered a fatal Metal validation
assertion at guest decision counter `n=4421` (vs. the family's
historical `n=12420`), well before the SELECT-CRAFT->mission transition
was even reached:

```
-[MTLDebugRenderCommandEncoder setViewports:count:]:3961: failed assertion `Viewport Validation
viewport.originX must not be infinite or NaN.
viewport.originY must not be infinite or NaN.
viewport.width must not be infinite or NaN.
viewport.height must not be infinite or NaN.
```

This aborts (`SIGABRT`, `pthread_kill`/`abort`), not the SIGSEGV pattern
of the s238-242 line of investigation. Stack: `MetalCommandList::
checkForUpdatesInGraphicsState` -> `MetalCommandList::drawInstanced` ->
`RT64::VIRenderer::render` -> `PresentQueue::threadPresent` ->
`PresentQueue::threadLoop`. The `run.log` frame immediately preceding
the crash shows `[pe gate #3183] ... viDiff=1 ... viW=0` — a transient
VI-width read of **zero** — right after an `osViSetMode #12` mode change
one line earlier (`width=512`).

**Static read confirms the exact mechanism (two independent lines of
evidence: dynamic trigger log + static code trace agree).**
`lib/rt64/src/render/rt64_vi_renderer.cpp`:
- `getViewportAndScissor()` (line 103) sets `sdSize = vi.fbSize()`
  (when `removeBlackBorders` is on, which it is here).
- `computeHDSize()` (line 17-19): `hdSize = sdSize * resolutionScale /
  downsamplingScale` — if `sdSize.x` (or `.y`) is 0, `hdSize`'s
  corresponding component is also 0.
- `fromSDtoHD()` (line 21-24): `relativeScale = hdSize / sdSize` — with
  both numerator and denominator 0, this is **0/0 = NaN**, which then
  multiplies into every viewport coordinate downstream, exactly
  matching the Metal validation error text.

So: a transient VI framebuffer width (or height) of 0 during a mode
switch produces a `0/0` NaN in `fromSDtoHD`'s scale factor, which
`MTL_DEBUG_LAYER` catches as a hard abort but which is presumably
silently tolerated (drawn as garbage or clipped) by Metal with
validation off — consistent with why this has never surfaced as a
`[CRASH]` in any prior (non-`MTL_DEBUG_LAYER`) soak despite `vi.fbSize()`
apparently hitting zero at least this once.

**This does NOT confirm or refute H1/H2/H3 for the original s238
host-CALayer investigation** — this is a different call stack, a
different signal (SIGABRT vs SIGSEGV), and fires at a different (much
earlier) guest decision count. It's an open question whether this
`fbSize()==0` transient is a NEW, previously-invisible bug that
`MTL_DEBUG_LAYER` merely exposes, or whether it's incidental/rare enough
to be unrelated to the CALayer crash family's `n=12420` convergence.
**Do not conflate the two families without further evidence.**

This is a single-source finding (one soak) for the trigger *condition*
(`viW=0` at gate #3183), but the causal *mechanism* (0/0 NaN in
`fromSDtoHD`) is confirmed by static code read independently of the
dynamic log — satisfies iron rule 4 for the mechanism, not yet for
"how often `fbSize()` hits zero in general."

This session did not modify `lib/rt64`/`lib/N64ModernRuntime` source
(read-only static trace); no `submodule-patches/export.sh` needed. A
fix (guard against zero `sdSize`/`hdSize` components in
`rt64_vi_renderer.cpp`) is proposed but NOT implemented this session,
per the standing "no speculative fix" rule — the next iteration's work
unit is to add the guard and re-soak with `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1` armed to
confirm the assertion stops firing.

scope (`fixup_game_funcs.py` untracked sibling-checkout state,

## Session 245 (2026-07-28)

**Work unit**: static trace of s244's new scissor-rect Metal SIGABRT
(`Set Scissor Rects Validation (rect.x(77)+rect.width(0))(77) must be <=
render pass width(6)`, `FramebufferRenderer::submitRasterScene`). No
`lib/` edit this session — static read only, per NEXT.md's discipline
(trace first, guard second, confirmed guard third, same as s243/s244).

**Mechanism found, H2+H3 CONFIRMED, H1 refuted-and-refined, from static
read alone (two converging code paths, no soak needed to discriminate)**:

1. **`render pass width(6)` is a genuinely tiny GPU texture, not a
   corrupted read of a bigger one** — it is created from
   `fbPair.colorImage.width` (`rt64_state.cpp:2128`,
   `drawParams.fbWidth = fbPair.colorImage.width`) which is the SAME
   value used to build the `RenderTargetKey` that creates/looks up the
   actual color target (`rt64_state.cpp:2052-2054`,
   `fbKey.colorTargetKey = RenderTargetKey(colorFb->addressStart,
   colorFb->width, ...); colorTarget = &renderTargetManager.get(...)`).
   So a real 6px-wide `RenderTarget` gets allocated — this is H2's
   "degenerate value", not H1's "wrong target's dimensions read by
   mistake".
2. **The only width-sanity guard on this path (`rt64_state.cpp:2015`,
   "s78") only rejects `width == 0` or `width > kMaxSaneFbWidth`
   (`=1280u`, `rt64_state.cpp:70`)** — a width of 6 is neither, so it
   sails through untouched. This is the SAME general class of bug
   already named and partially fixed in a DIFFERENT, unrelated consumer:
   `rt64_framebuffer_renderer.cpp:646-654`'s "s82" comment says
   verbatim *"refuse wild widths (1..257 garbage)"* and gates a
   `saneW` check against `{320, 512, 640, 1024}` — but that guard only
   protects the VI-presentation "last-drawn framebuffer" heuristic, not
   render-target creation or scissor validation. 6 falls squarely in
   the already-documented "1..257 garbage" range. This confirms H3:
   this is the SAME pre-existing wild-width phenomenon s82 already
   named, just reaching a second, previously-unguarded consumer now
   that s244's VI-NaN fix lets the game run long enough to get there.
3. **Why the scissor rect (`x=77`) overflows a 6px target**: traced
   `convertFixedRect()` (`rt64_framebuffer_renderer.cpp:60-91`, the
   function that builds `InstanceDrawCall.triangles.scissor` at line
   1964) and `FixedRect::left/right(true)`
   (`rt64_common.h:73-97`, implementation not re-read but the signature
   and call sites confirm these return raw RDP/N64-native pixel
   coordinates from the game's `SetScissor` command, e.g. up to ~320,
   independent of the destination `colorImage`'s declared width).
   `convertFixedRect()` only applies origin-recentering
   (`computeOrigin`, scaled by `fbWidth`) and misalignment correction —
   it does **not** scale or clip the raw coordinate against the actual
   destination target's pixel width. So when `fbWidth`/`colorImg.width`
   is a wild garbage value like 6, a `SetScissor` command whose
   coordinates were meant for the real ~320px-wide screen (`x=77`)
   passes through nearly unmodified, producing a scissor rect that
   grossly exceeds the actual 6px target — exactly the assertion Metal's
   debug layer caught. This mechanism generalizes: ANY wild-width target
   combined with a normal-screen-scale scissor command will hit this,
   not just this one instance.
4. **H1 (scissor computed against a DIFFERENT target's size than the one
   actually bound) is REFUTED as stated** — `drawParams.fbWidth` and the
   bound `colorTarget`'s actual width both trace back to the same
   `fbPair.colorImage.width`, so there is no cross-target coordinate-space
   mismatch. H1 is better restated as: there is no validation ANYWHERE
   on this path that clips/rejects a scissor rect against the actual
   bound target's dimensions — the existing empty-scissor skip
   (`rt64_framebuffer_renderer.cpp:736-757`, comment: *"Draw calls can
   sometimes end up with empty scissors and cause validation errors. We
   just skip them."*) already established that this general class of
   "bad scissor reaches the Metal encoder" problem is known and handled
   for the empty case, but not for the out-of-bounds case.

**Two proposed fixes for next iteration** (NOT implemented this
session, per "trace first" discipline):

- (a) Extend the s78 width guard at `rt64_state.cpp:2015` to reject the
  same "1..257 wild" range s82 already names (or require a minimum sane
  width), preventing the tiny garbage target from ever being created.
  Risk: unclear if 1..257 is EVER a legitimate width for some real
  small N64 framebuffer use case in this game — s82's guard was scoped
  to a narrow heuristic, not target creation, so widening its scope
  needs care.
- (b) Clip/skip scissor rects that exceed the destination target's
  actual bound width/height in `submitRasterScene`, mirroring the
  existing empty-scissor skip at line 736-757 (add an out-of-bounds
  check next to the `isEmpty()` check, using `fbStorage->colorTarget`'s
  actual `width`/`height`). This is more general — it catches this bug
  class regardless of WHY the target ended up tiny — and needs no
  change to framebuffer/target creation logic. **Preferred**: lower risk,
  same pattern already proven safe in this exact function.

## Session 249 (2026-07-28)

**Picked option 1 from s248's `NEXT.md` (project-wide static sweep for the
"RDRAM-base-constant + un-subtracted wild guest pointer" whack-a-mole
family) over option 2 (`CURRENT-TRUTH.md` housekeeping), since it's real
code and per `ITERATION.md` housekeeping alone doesn't count as
`ADVANCED`. Landed one new guard (`selectPostCrawlCraft`,
`funcs_30.c`) plus a reusable project-wide candidate-finder script; build
clean; 1 soak run showed no regression from the change and no new
information on whether the guarded site is actually hot.**

**Step 1 — grep the idiom shape project-wide, as NEXT.md's first step
asked.** The naive signature (self-referential `ctx->rX = MEM_W(ctx->rX,
0X0)`, matching heapWalker/heapFreeListDequeue's already-fixed shape) hits
794 times across the 45 `funcs_*.c` files — far too broad; most are
one-shot, already-bounded dereferences, not unguarded list-walk loops.
Narrowed with a script
(`scratch/agent/find_unguarded_walks.py`, output
`scratch/agent/unguarded_walk_candidates.json`) that requires the
self-ref load to sit at a labeled loop target which is the destination of
a **backward** `goto` (i.e. an actual loop back-edge, not just any
self-ref line) and have no existing `PATCH` guard already covering it.
This dropped the count to **143 candidate sites across 43 functions** —
still confirmed the exclusion logic works (heapWalker itself, already
fully guarded, correctly does not appear). Full per-function breakdown
is in `NEXT.md` for the next iteration; the JSON has exact file/line/label
per site.

**Step 2 — picked ONE site to actually fix this session** rather than
patch all 143 blind (no time to hand-verify bail semantics for 43
functions in one sitting, and a wrong bail target risks a worse bug than
the crash it's meant to prevent). Picked `selectPostCrawlCraft`
(`funcs_30.c`, 3 of the 143 candidates) because its name matches the
"SELECT-CRAFT" transition this project has instrumented and soaked
against for 30+ sessions. A full end-to-end read of the function (it's a
single ~800-line body, no other `RECOMP_FUNC` boundary inside — same
"decompiler never split it" pattern as `heapWalker`) found:
- Site 1 (`0x800CBBD8`, register `r16`/`$s0`): a "free every node in a
  list" loop — frees an `0x5C` sub-object then the node itself, walking
  via the node's own next-pointer field. **This is the one fixed this
  session.**
- Sites 2/3 (`0x800CBDA8`/`0x800CBDE4`): two near-identical inlined
  list-insert helpers appended to the tail of a list — NOT fixed this
  session, flagged in `NEXT.md` for a future iteration with their own
  trace.

**Important correction to the mechanical grep's own signature**: reading
site 1's loop body found the vulnerable pointer is dereferenced through
**two different registers** on loop entry — `ctx->r4 = MEM_W(ctx->r17,
0X5C)` immediately followed by the self-referential `ctx->r16 =
MEM_W(ctx->r16, 0X0)` — because `r17` and `r16` hold the same
(potentially corrupted) node address at loop entry (`ctx->r17 =
ADD32(ctx->r16, 0)` on every back-edge). A guard placed only before the
self-referential line, matching every prior guard's literal pattern,
would still leave the FIRST dereference (`ctx->r17`) exposed and
reachable — the crash could still happen one line earlier. The guard
added here sits immediately after the loop label, before either
dereference, checking `ctx->r16` (the value both registers share at that
point) against the standard KSEG0 bounds
(`0x80000000`-`0x80800000`, `hi==0xFFFFFFFF`). Bail target: `ctx->r2 =
S32(0X800D << 16); goto L_800CBC04;` — verified by reading forward from
`L_800CBC04` that `r2` there is an independent fixed constant
(`0x800D0000`, used only for one further `rs_free()` at a hardcoded
offset, never derived from `r16`/`r17`), and that the loop's own natural
exit path (`r16==0`) sets `r2` to this exact same constant before falling
into the same label — so the bail is indistinguishable from "list ended
here" to all downstream code, matching this codebase's established
"give up gracefully" bail contract. This asymmetry (mechanical grep
signature vs. the actual multi-register vulnerable window) is worth
carrying into the remaining 142 candidates — do not assume the
self-ref line alone is always the right/only guard point; read the whole
loop body first.

**Build**: mandatory delete-all-45-`funcs_*.c` → `make_elf.py` →
`regen_n64recomp.sh` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`. Patch

loop-back guard (0x800CBBD8) patched x1` — exactly the expected
multiplicity, no duplicate. `cmake --build` exit 0. Binary verified fresh
(`strings build/RogueSquadron64Recomp | grep selectpostcrawl-guard` hits
exactly once, binary mtime matches the build).

**Soak** (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_selectpostcrawlguard1.sh`,
tag `selectpostcrawlguard1`, all `campose11`-baseline guards armed plus
the new `ROGUESQ_LOG_SELECTPOSTCRAWL_GUARD=1`, `HOLD_S=150`): crossed the

## Session 250 (2026-07-28)

**Continued the s249 static sweep: guarded `selectPostCrawlCraft`'s other
2 candidate sites (`funcs_30.c`, 0x800CBDA8 and 0x800CBDE4 — the "two
near-identical inlined list-insert helpers" s249 flagged but didn't
trace). Build clean, no regression. 2 soak attempts: 1st pre-empted
pre-title-screen by an already-catalogued unrelated crash class (0/0
positive controls, uninformative); 2nd survived the full run (`CRASH: 0`)
but got zero positive-control fires of any kind — an honest single-sample
null with weak evidentiary value, not a confirmed clean pass. 140
candidate sites remain project-wide.**

**Full-loop-body read (mandatory per s249's own finding) of both sites.**
Both are byte-identical in shape: a doubly-linked-list "insert at tail"
helper, list head read from an untrusted struct field
(`MEM_W(ctx->r4, 0X20)` for helper A / `MEM_W(ctx->r4, 0X10)` for helper
B), walked to find the tail via a loop at `L_800CBDA8` / `L_800CBDE4`:

```
L_800CBDA8:
    ctx->r3 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0);   // flagged self-ref line (walk)
    ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0);   // peek-load of the BRAND NEW r3
    if (ctx->r2 != 0) goto L_800CBDA8;
```

This is a DIFFERENT shape from `selectPostCrawlCraft`'s own s249 guard
(two *different* aliased registers derived from the same pointer). Here
it's the *same* register (`r3`) dereferenced twice back-to-back: line 1
reads the incoming (possibly-corrupt, carried from the previous
iteration's own unvalidated walk) `r3`; line 2 immediately re-reads the
value line 1 just produced, itself unvalidated. This matches
`renderUnlitMeshFaces`'s s219 GUARD/GUARD3 combo shape (self-ref walk +
peek-load of the freshly-walked pointer), not `selectPostCrawlCraft`'s
own template — a guard only before line 1 would still leave line 2's
peek exposed to whatever garbage line 1 just read. So each site got TWO
guards this session (GUARD1 before the walk, GUARD2 between the walk and
the peek), both using the established `0x80000000..0x80800000` lo-half /
`0xFFFFFFFF` hi-half RDRAM-pointer sentinel check.

**Bail target: plain `return;`**, not a goto to a shared exit label like
s249's own guard used. Verified by reading forward: both sites' natural
loop-exit path writes `MEM_W(0X0, ctx->r3) = ctx->r5` (append into the
old tail's next field) then `MEM_W(0X4, ctx->r5) = ctx->r3` (new node's
prev = old tail) before returning — both use the untrusted `r3` as an
address or a stored value, so bailing into that path would just move the
wild dereference/store rather than avoid it. These are void-returning
internal helpers reached via `jal` (no `RECOMP_FUNC` boundary separates
them from `selectPostCrawlCraft` — they're folded into the same block by
the recomp naming heuristic) with no caller-visible error-code contract,
so silently abandoning the insert on a corrupt list is the simplest bail
this shape supports.

## Session 259 (2026-07-29) — guarded `evalCubicSplineAtTime`'s unguarded pointer per s258's lead; guard was inert this run (0 fires) but the soak advanced past that whole call chain into a BRAND NEW, unrelated crash inside `activateAnimationKeyframe`'s `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` callee, which is precisely localized to a null-only (not range) check at `0x80061EF8`

**Work unit**: s258 left a clear lead — `evalCubicSplineAtTime` (reached via
`static_5_800AB658` → `setupActorAnchorTransformType1` →
`buildPositionAndCallTransformHelper`) had an unguarded pointer feeding a
Bus error. Read all 3 functions in full (`funcs_4.c:25612-26093`,
`funcs_15.c:4019-4930`, `funcs_15.c:5758-5799`). `evalCubicSplineAtTime`
loads `ctx->r16` from the spline-data struct's `+0x8` field (guest
`0x80018FCC`) with zero validation, dereferenced 2 instructions later
(`0x80018FF0`) as the base of the keyframe binary-search loop's first
read — identical "load struct field, deref immediately, no range check"
shape as every other guard in this project (`RENDERUNLIT_GUARD` is the
canonical example). Per NEXT.md's explicit instruction ("guard the
earliest unvalidated load found"), guarded this one, not the later
`ctx->r8`-based reads at `0x800190CC`+.

**Guard mechanics**: unlike `RENDERUNLIT_GUARD` (which reuses an existing
mid-function "list empty" label), `evalCubicSplineAtTime` has no partial-
skip path — the entire rest of the function (search loop, float
interpolation math, AND the r8-based reads) transitively depends on this
one struct. So a dedicated epilogue label (`L_evalspline_guard_exit`) was
inserted immediately before the function's real restore-and-return
sequence (guest `0x80019188`), and the guard `goto`s there directly. This
is ABI-safe because the prologue (`0x80018F9C`-`0x80018FB8`) already saves
`$s0`/`$s1`/`$f20`/`$f22`/`$f24`/`$f26`/`$f28`/`$f30` to their stack slots
strictly BEFORE this guard's anchor point (right after the r16 load) — so
every value the epilogue restores is already correct on the stack, same
ABI-safety reasoning s109 used for `L_dlentry_guard_exit`. New env var:
`ROGUESQ_LOG_EVALSPLINE_GUARD`. Output (`*a2`, the 3 interpolated floats)
is left as whatever the caller already had on a guard fire — leaving
stale data beats a crash, same trade-off every prior guard in this
codebase makes.

**Build**: full regen (delete all `funcs_*.c`, `make_elf.py` →
`regen_n64recomp.sh` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` exactly once — confirmed both
`evalCubicSplineAtTime epilogue label (L_evalspline_guard_exit) patched
x1` and `evalCubicSplineAtTime struct-field pointer guard (0x80018FCC)
patched x1` in the fixup report), clean `cmake --build .`, `strings`-
verified both `ROGUESQ_LOG_EVALSPLINE_GUARD` and (as the same-run control)
`ROGUESQ_LOG_HANGAR_BAY_DEREF_GUARD` present in the binary.

**Soak** (`evalsplineguard1`, ~222MB `run.log`, same `STICK_SCHEDULE` as
every prior soak in this family): `EVALSPLINE_GUARD` got 0 fires
(uninformative on the guard's own question), `HANGAR_BAY_DEREF_GUARD`
(G30/G31) also 0 fires, `unlit-mesh-tracer` still 0 hits
(`renderUnlitMeshFaces` never called) — the game never went through
`evalCubicSplineAtTime`/`buildPositionAndCallTransformHelper`/
`setupActorAnchorTransformType1` at all this run. **The run crashed at
almost the same VI tick as s258** (`update_screen #~8192`-`#8236` vs.

improvement or regression), **but via a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT, never-

`activateAnimationKeyframe` → `setLookupEntryField5ByKey`, Bus error

THIRD distinct wild-value shape, matching neither the `0x80630062` KSEG0-
zero-extension pattern nor s258's `0x7ffffff8`-ish sentinel value).

cannot distinguish "the evalCubicSplineAtTime guard is a real fix that let

run-to-run variance landed on a different code path entirely" (identical
caveat to s258's own g30g31soak1 result). Do not credit the guard with

crash-of-record moved to a new site."

**Localized the new crash precisely** (this part IS a concrete finding,
not speculation): `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` (funcs_15.c:70-130, tiny

## Session 260 (2026-07-29) — closed s259's `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` lead, but it took two guards, not one: the caller-argument guard was a red herring, the real bug was a 2nd-level pointer loaded inside the callee's own search loop. call to `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` (funcs_14.c:2116, the only one of 18
call sites in the file that falls inside `activateAnimationKeyframe`'s own
range 1629-2138) passed an argument (`ctx->r4`, loaded from `$s1+0xF4` at
guest `0x80061EF4`) that was checked ONLY against zero before being handed
to the callee, which dereferences it further with no range validation.

**First guard (`SETLOOKUP_ARG_GUARD`)**: widened the existing `if
(ctx->r4 == 0)` check to the standard KSEG0-range + hi-word idiom, but
implemented it by coercing an out-of-range value to 0 right before the
pre-existing check runs (rather than adding a parallel `goto`), so the
function's own `L_80061F18` bail path handles both cases identically — no
new label needed. New env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_SETLOOKUP_ARG_GUARD`.

accidentally run twice against the same regenerated source on the first
pass (a stray verification re-run), silently double-inserting the guard
block (2 copies of the same PATCH block back to back — harmless
functionally, since it's the same check twice, but violates "fixup runs
exactly once" and would have looked confusing in a future diff or

redirect `fixup_game_funcs.py`'s stdout to a file (`> scratch/agent/*.log`)
and grep it, rather than trusting a terminal `tail`, which can silently
truncate or hide a duplicate run.

**Soak 1 (`setlookupguard1`, 224MB `run.log`)**: `SETLOOKUP_ARG_GUARD` got
**0 fires**, but the run crashed with the **EXACT same signature** as
s259's crash — same call stack (`static_5_800AAD9C` →
`advancePlayerAnimationPhase` → `activateAnimationKeyframe` →
`setLookupEntryField5ByKey`), same `si_addr=0x3c04b1980`/
`x9=0x00000000c04b1980`, same ~VI-8192 crash mark. This is a genuine
discriminating result (not a null result — iron rule 1's positive-control
concern doesn't apply here because the ABSENCE of a fire combined with the
SAME crash recurring is itself informative): `ctx->r4` was demonstrably
clean on every call this run, including the crashing one, so the argument
was never the wild pointer.

**Re-read `setLookupEntryField5ByKey`'s body in full** (funcs_15.c:70-130)
to find the real bug: after the safe first deref (`ctx->r2 =
MEM_HU(ctx->r4, 0x4)`), the function's search loop (label `L_800646BC`)
reloads `ctx->r3 = MEM_W(ctx->r4, 0X0)` **on every iteration** — this is a
table-base pointer stored INSIDE the already-validated struct, a
genuinely distinct value from `ctx->r4` itself, not a re-read of the same
thing. The loop then computes `ctx->r3 = index*8 + ctx->r3` and
dereferences THAT (`ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0)`, guest `0x800646C8`)
with zero validation anywhere. `x9=0xc04b1980` matches this 2nd-level
pointer's shape exactly (a garbage value that's neither in the
`0x80000000`-`0x80800000` KSEG0 range nor zero) — the argument-level guard
could never have caught this because the argument itself genuinely was
fine.

(funcs_15.c), validating `ctx->r3` immediately after its load, bailing via
`ctx->r2 = 0; return;` if out of range — chosen to exactly match the
loop's own "not found" exit (`L_800646F0`, which also leaves `r2=0` and
returns) since no caller anywhere checks this function's return value,
only its side-effect byte write (`MEM_B(0X5, ctx->r3) = ctx->r6` at
`0x800646D8`) on the found-a-match path. New env var
`ROGUESQ_LOG_SETLOOKUP_TABLE_GUARD`.

any code. Same "load a pointer field, deref it without checking" family
shape as guard7/guard8, one level deeper (guard7 protects the FIRST
deref, nothing protected the second).

**Guard idiom, deliberately different from guards 1-8**: NEXT.md's own
analysis (s260) was right that a plain `>= 0x80000000` check would NOT
catch this value — `0x80000068`, and even the bare `0x80000000` base,
both pass a standard KSEG0 lower bound trivially. `ROGUESQ_LOG_
COMPOSE_NPC_GUARD9` instead rejects anything below `0x80001000`: every
literal KSEG0 constant anywhere in this file (and everywhere else in this
investigation's logs) sits at `0x800A0000`+ or higher, and `0x80000000-
0x80000FFF` is the N64's reserved boot-vector/IPL3 region — never a
legitimate game data pointer, so tightening the lower bound to `0x80001000`
cannot reject real data. Bails to the same real epilogue `L_800AB618`
guards 1-8 already proved ABI-safe. File-scoped to `funcs_40.c` per

## Session 265 (2026-07-29) — built and landed the "last-executed-guest-PC breadcrumb" instrument s264 flagged as a generically-overdue investment; verified it works correctly across 6 independent soaks, but the specific `submitSceneNodeRender+19268` crash did not recur in any of them — instead surfacing that this crash is comparatively RARE (2/10 attempts across 3 sessions) next to at least 2-4 other, more-frequent crash classes this session incidentally discovered

Since every recompiled MIPS instruction in `funcs_4.c` already carries its own `// 0xGUEST_ADDR: mnemonic ...` comment (a 1:1 guest-address index, unlike the native ARM64 side which has no such index), stamping a global with that address at each instruction gives EXACT single-instruction localization for free, without any native-side correlation at all. This is the same goal NEXT.md's work unit specified, reached via the more reliable of its own two named methods.

**Implementation** (`g_rs64_last_guest_pc`, a `volatile uint32_t`):
- `recomp.h`: added `extern volatile uint32_t g_rs64_last_guest_pc;` next to the existing `extern int32_t* section_addresses;`.
- `src/main/main.cpp`: defined the global (`extern "C" volatile uint32_t g_rs64_last_guest_pc = 0;`, same pattern as the existing `g_recomp_rdram_for_wp_raw`/`rs64_get_vifs_crash_snapshot` cross-TU globals) and added `fprintf(stderr, "[CRASH][last-guest-pc] pc=0x%08x\n", g_rs64_last_guest_pc);` to the SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler, right after the existing `[CRASH][pc-symbol]` dladdr line.
- `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`: new pass, scoped to `submitSceneNodeRender` only (not the whole binary — this is the one function 3+ consecutive sessions of crashes have converged on, and scoping keeps the diff and the added per-frame overhead small). Finds the function's body span via the same `func_re` used elsewhere in the script, then regex-inserts `g_rs64_last_guest_pc = 0xADDRu;` immediately after every `// 0xADDR: ...` comment line in that span, preserving whatever indentation the comment itself has (branch-delay-slot blocks are indented deeper than straight-line code). Runs LAST in the file so it also breadcrumbs the comment lines already-existing guard patches (DEQUEUE_GUARD etc.) leave behind — desired, since those are still real guest instructions.

**Non-obvious build gotcha found this session, worth remembering**: there are TWO `recomp.h` files in play. `~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h` is the standalone codegen tool's own header (only used by that tool internally); the actual game build's `RecompiledFuncs` target gets its headers from `RogueSquadron64Recomp/lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h` (a vendored copy inside the `N64ModernRuntime` submodule — see `CMakeLists.txt:92-97`'s `target_include_directories`, which lists the `lib/N64ModernRuntime/...` path, not the standalone tool's path, at all). Editing only the standalone copy (which is the natural first guess, since that's the tool whose `.toml`/binary you invoke for step 2 of the regen pipeline) produces a `cmake --build` failure ("use of undeclared identifier 'g_rs64_last_guest_pc'" x20, `funcs_4.c`) with no obvious link to the actual cause. Edited both copies for consistency; only the `lib/` copy is load-bearing for compilation. **Any future header-level addition needs to go in the `lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h` copy, not (only) the standalone tool's.**

Critically, **`last-guest-pc=0x8000b03c` is informative this time** — `beginFrameDLChunk` is itself breadcrumbed (`BREADCRUMB3`), so this is (very likely) the actual crashing guest instruction, not a stale stamp from a different function. `grep` in `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_3.c` located it exactly: `0x8000B03C: lw $v0, 0x0($v0)` (line 10236 pre-patch) — a **4th occurrence of the exact same "reload persistent free-list cache-head global (`0x801163B0`), dereference with zero validation" idiom** that s197's original guard, `CACHE2_GUARD` (s266), and `CACHE3_GUARD` (s270) already fixed at three OTHER call sites — but this is the FIRST occurrence found in `beginFrameDLChunk`/`funcs_3.c` (all three prior sites were in `submitSceneNodeRender`/`funcs_4.c`), and matches the exact shape (deref-then-crash, not write-then-crash) of s197's ORIGINAL guard rather than `CACHE2`/`CACHE3`'s write-side variant. This is also, very likely, `BREADCRUMB3`'s own long-sought target: s268 first caught this exact family in `beginFrameDLChunk` (`+13420`, guest exactly `0x80000000`, unlocalized) before it was breadcrumbed; native offset has since shifted (`+13420` → `+21216`) as later sessions' guard insertions (`CACHE2_GUARD`, `CACHE3_GUARD`) changed the function's code layout, but the guest-side signature (`beginFrameDLChunk`, `si_addr` exactly `0x80000000`) is identical. Treat as the same underlying site now exactly localized, not a new independent one.

**Landed `CACHE4_GUARD`** (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, scoped to `funcs_3.c`): validates the reloaded head (`0x80000000 <= v0 < 0x80800000`) before the `lw $v0, 0x0($v0)` deref at `0x8000B03C`; on failure, resets the persistent cache global to 0 and jumps to `L_8000B050` — the merge point normal execution reaches either way immediately after this idiom (confirmed by reading forward: `r2` is dead there, overwritten by an unrelated load from a different global at `0x8000B058` before any use), exactly mirroring the "cache was already empty" case. New env-gated log: `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_CACHE4_GUARD`.

**Non-obvious ordering gotcha hit and fixed during this patch**: unlike `CACHE2_GUARD`/`CACHE3_GUARD` (which target `submitSceneNodeRender`, a function `BREADCRUMB4` does NOT touch, so their regexes never see `g_rs64_last_guest_pc` lines), `CACHE4_GUARD`'s target — `beginFrameDLChunk` — gets BREADCRUMB3's blanket per-instruction-comment breadcrumb pass applied to its entire body. Since `fixup_game_funcs.py` applies patches sequentially top-to-bottom against one shared `text` variable, and `CACHE4_GUARD`'s block sits (in file order) BEFORE `BREADCRUMB3`'s block, `CACHE4_GUARD` runs on the PRE-breadcrumb text — its regex must NOT include `g_rs64_last_guest_pc` lines, or it silently matches zero times. Written correctly (regex omits breadcrumb lines; the `// 0x8000B034:`/`// 0x8000B038:`/`// 0x8000B03C:` comment lines are preserved in the replacement so `BREADCRUMB3`'s later pass finds and instruments them exactly as it would any other instruction). Confirmed post-regen: `funcs_3.c` `g_rs64_last_guest_pc` count is exactly `1719` (`BREADCRUMB2` x724 + `BREADCRUMB3` x995, matching every prior session — `CACHE4_GUARD` added zero extra breadcrumb lines of its own, as intended), `L_8000B034:` label appears exactly once (no duplication), `CACHE4_GUARD` patched x1.

## Session 284 (2026-08-03) — deliberate `-0x25A4($s1)` grep audit per s283's plan, 29 new guards across 3 functions, one live crash found+fixed via soak

**What ran**: per s283's plan, grepped every `-0X25A4` occurrence across `RecompiledFuncs/*.c`
(`grep -rn "\-0X25A4" .../RecompiledFuncs/*.c`) instead of continuing to wait for soaks to surface
sites incidentally. Found 173 hits across 3 files (`funcs_19.c` x1, `funcs_27.c` x103,
`funcs_40.c` x69). Before trusting the offset match, traced each hit's feeding `lui` value (not
just the `-0x25A4` offset) — this caught a false positive: `npcShieldGeneratorUpdate`
(`funcs_19.c`) loads its `-0x25A4` offset off a base set via `lui $at, 0x8004`, a completely
different address than the hangar-list global's `lui $s1, 0x800D` — same offset, unrelated global
(a float constant table, not a pointer). The other 172 hits all confirmed `lui`-`0x800D`.

Per-function breakdown of the 172 confirmed hits: `hangarInitialize` (`funcs_27.c`) 103,
`static_5_800AB658` 32 (the pre-existing `G1`-`G32` whack-a-mole family), `static_5_800ADB70` 21,
`static_5_800AB1C8` 10, `static_5_800A9270` 4 (fully guarded last session), `static_5_800AAD9C` 2.
`static_5_800AB658` (32/32) and `static_5_800A9270` (4/4) were already fully covered. The other 3
`funcs_40.c` functions had NEVER been audited — delegated 3 parallel classification passes
(one per function) plus a scoping-only sample of `hangarInitialize` to background agents, each
reading the full function body and, for every hit, tracing whether the loaded pointer (or a value
derived from it) reaches a dereference with no preceding `0x80000000`-`0x80800000` range check.

Results: `static_5_800AAD9C` (2 hits) — both unguarded, identical shape (two near-duplicate scan
loops). `static_5_800AB1C8` (10 hits) — 4 already guarded (pre-existing sites 1/3/4/5), 1 safe
(loaded value only ever used as a call argument, never dereferenced in this function), 5 unguarded
(sites 6-10) — two of the five (6 and 10) are a "second-hop" variant: the EXISTING guard at that
site validates the *value loaded from* the dereference, not the pointer used to *reach* it, so the
first-level dereference itself was still exposed. `static_5_800ADB70` (21 hits) — all 21
unguarded, no bounds checks anywhere in the function; the 21 sites collapse into ~9 recurring
2-4-line shapes (load, add loop-index, dereference one or more fields), all converging on the same
single epilogue `L_800AE060`. Total: 28 genuinely unguarded sites across the 3 functions.

`hangarInitialize` (`funcs_27.c`, lines 119802-133178, 13,376 lines) was scoped ONLY, not touched
this session — a 22-site sample (spread start/middle/end) found 21 unguarded, 1 safe (the write
that initializes the global itself), 0 already-guarded; the function has only 5 true epilogues
(returns) across its span plus 244 branch-target labels (not exit points); estimated 5-7 future
sessions to fully classify+guard at the same per-site rigor used here, given the sheer size.

**The patch**: exact source context for every one of the 28 sites was extracted programmatically
(a small script walking backward from each dereference line to its immediately-preceding pointer
computation) and each anchor regex's uniqueness within `funcs_40.c` was verified via a dry-run
match count (all 28 matched exactly once) BEFORE splicing into `fixup_game_funcs.py` — avoiding
the risk of a shared/duplicated anchor text silently patching the wrong location. Landed 28 new
guards (`S284_AAD9C_1`/`_2`, `S284_AB1C8_6`/`_7`/`_8`/`_9`/`_10`, `S284_ADB70_1`-`_21`), same
established recipe (`U32(ctx->rN)` range check, bail to each function's own confirmed epilogue
label — `L_800AB1A4` for AAD9C, `L_800AB618` for AB1C8, `L_800AE060` for ADB70, all found by
reading each function to its closing brace). Full regen pipeline, clean build, patch report
confirmed all 28 patched `x1` each alongside every pre-existing guard (G1-G32, HANGARLIST_GUARD
family) — no stacking/collisions.

**Soak1 (post-28-guard build) crashed, informatively**: reached the scene, then SIGBUS inside
`static_5_800A9270` (native `+1176`, called from `static_5_800AAD9C+4188` — both offsets confirmed
within their own symbols' own ranges via a Mach-O symtab walk, not a nearest-symbol
misattribution). This function was supposedly fully guarded (4/4 sites, s283) — full re-read
confirmed all 4 of its own `-0x25A4` loads ARE still correctly guarded, but found a NEW,
previously-unnoticed bug one hop further downstream: at guest `0x800A92BC`, `ctx->r5` is loaded
from the ALREADY-VALIDATED hangar-list entry's own `+0x4` field (a "next"/child pointer read out
of the list structure), then dereferenced two instructions later at guest `0x800A92C4`
(`ctx->r7 = MEM_W(ctx->r5, 0x0)`) with NO validation of its own — the identical "second-hop" shape
as s282's `G32` fix (validating a value's *source* doesn't validate a *pointer read from* that
source). Guest-relative offset from function start (`0x54`, ~35% through) reasonably matches the
native crash-offset ratio (`1176/3048`, ~39%) combined with the exact call-chain match. Landed
`S284_A9270_SECONDHOP` (bail `L_800A9350`, this function's pre-existing epilogue, already used by
all its other guards). Required a full delete-and-regenerate of `funcs_*.c` before re-running
`fixup_game_funcs.py` (never re-run fixup on an already-patched file — it re-matches the
unconsumed original anchor text and stacks a duplicate guard). Clean rebuild.

**Re-validation**: soak2 and soak3 (`HOLD_S=240` each) both reached the scene and survived past
it, dying during the hold at two OTHER already-catalogued, unrelated sites
(`processSceneNode+1424`, `reserveAndEmitDLEntry+10056`). Neither reproduced the second-hop crash
and no `s284`/`hangarlist` guard fired in either log — 2 informative scene-reaching soaks, same
non-recurrence bar used throughout this whack-a-mole family.

**What this shows / rules out**: closes the deliberate-audit thread for the 3 previously-unaudited
`funcs_40.c` functions — 29/29 now-known unguarded `-0x25A4`-family sites in those 3 functions are

## Session 288 (2026-08-03) — classifies `playerSnowSpeederInit`: REFUTES the s286/287 "may be a dead duplicate" hypothesis and closes the `-0x25A4` hangar-list audit lineage with a clean 0-hit result

Ran the dead-code-detection methodology (s286/287) on `playerSnowSpeederInit` (`funcs_27.c:144145-150543`,
6399 lines, guest range `0x800AAAE0`-`0x800ACD98`) per s287's plan, since it independently reused
label names from all three of `hangarInitialize` chunks 2/3/4's address ranges
(`static_5_800AAD9C`/`static_5_800AB1C8`/`static_5_800AB658`).

**Step 0 (before the 3-check proof): grepped for `-0x25A4($s1)` / `25A4` anywhere in the function's
line range — zero hits.** Verified twice: once against an extracted copy of the function body, once
directly against `funcs_27.c` with an `awk` line-range filter, same result. This alone closes the
audit target — there is nothing to guard here regardless of the function's live/dead status.

**Ran the classification anyway, since NEXT.md explicitly required verifying rather than assuming**:
the "may be a dead duplicate" hypothesis is **REFUTED**, not confirmed.
- Extracted every `// 0xADDR:` comment line (2552 of them) and checked address monotonicity across
  the whole function: **zero decreases, only expected delay-slot repeats** — the guest address
  stream is a single continuous non-decreasing run from `0x800AAAE0` to `0x800ACD98`, the shape of
  genuinely continuous translated code, not a live-prologue-then-spliced-in-duplicate-chunk pattern
  (which is what `hangarInitialize`'s dead chunks looked like — a big backward/discontinuous jump at
  the chunk boundary).
- Directly compared the instruction at each of the three addresses where `playerSnowSpeederInit`'s
  comment stream crosses a known-duplicated function's start address, against that function's own
  real first instruction:
  - `0x800AAD9C`: `playerSnowSpeederInit` has `ori $v0, $zero, 0xFFFF`; `static_5_800AAD9C`'s real
    first instruction is `addiu $sp, $sp, -0x30`. **Different.**
  - `0x800AB1C8`: `playerSnowSpeederInit` has `lw $a1, 0x0($s2)`, continuing a live instruction
    stream (previous line is `lui $a0, 0x8011` feeding an unrelated computation) — not a function
    prologue at all.
  - `0x800AB658`: `playerSnowSpeederInit` has `lwc1 $f0, 0x50($s0)`; `static_5_800AB658`'s real
    first instruction is `addiu $sp, $sp, -0x100`. **Different.**

A single diverging instruction at a byte-for-byte comparison anchor is sufficient to disprove
duplication (the same standard s286/287 used to *confirm* duplication elsewhere — exact match
required). All three anchors diverge. Combined with the whole-function address monotonicity, this
is decisive: `playerSnowSpeederInit` is real, continuously-translated, live code across its entire
span — it is NOT a dead duplicate of `static_5_800AAD9C`/`static_5_800AB1C8`/`static_5_800AB658`.

**What actually explains the s286/287 label-name overlap**: `playerSnowSpeederInit` occupies the
same *virtual* guest-address range as these three `funcs_40.c` functions (they're loaded via a
different overlay context), so its `L_<addr>:` labels share numeric names with theirs by pure
address coincidence — not because it contains a text/byte copy of their bodies. This is the same
overlay-address-reuse phenomenon behind `hangarInitialize`'s dead chunks, but manifesting
differently here: coincidental address/label overlap between two *live* functions from different
overlays, not a live function containing a dead copy of another's bytes.

(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_7.c:13553-14116`, all 563 lines, function bounded by the next
`RECOMP_FUNC` at line 14117) plus its caller context: the `inflate_fast` call site inside
`inflate_blocks` (`funcs_7.c:12336-12351`, the args it loads and passes) and one of the two
`inflate_recomp` call sites in the higher-level streaming-buffer wrapper (`funcs_1.c:2262-2267`,
`:2420-2428` — both structurally identical, a double-buffered read-ahead cache calling
`inflate_recomp` on alternating half-buffers, nothing unusual in either).

**Source-read finding (step 1, negative)**: `inflate_fast` is a faithful, complete instruction-for-
instruction port of the classic (K&M-era) zlib `inflate_fast` core decompression loop — literal
decode, length/distance Huffman table walks, and the final LZ77 copy loop, all present and matching
the expected control flow. Every `MEM_W`/`MEM_B`/`MEM_BU`/`MEM_H` access in the function is
translated straight from the original MIPS load/store with **no bounds or range check of any kind**
— but this is true of every `RECOMP_FUNC` in this codebase before a guard is added; nothing about
this function's *translation* stands out as buggy or different from ~15 other already-catalogued
crash sites in this same investigation (s130-s289). No recompiler-introduced defect found.

**Caller-argument finding (step 2)**: traced the 4 register arguments `inflate_fast` receives from
`inflate_blocks`'s call site (`funcs_7.c:12336-12347`): `bl`/`bd` (single bytes, bit-length values,
loaded from `$s1+0x10`/`+0x11`) are safe (used only to index a small fixed `inflate_mask[]` constant
table, never dereferenced as pointers); `tl`/`td` (the literal/length and distance Huffman decode
table base pointers, loaded from `$s1+0x14`/`+0x18`) are guest RDRAM pointers **used directly and
immediately as the dereferenced base for every symbol decoded in the hot loop, with no address-range
check on either at the call site or on entry to `inflate_fast`**. The other two structurally-trusted
pointers — `z` (z_streamp, loaded from the caller's own stack slot, `ctx->r15`/`$t7` internally) and
`s` (`inflate_blocks_statef*`, `ctx->r24`/`$t8` internally) — are the "self" state objects nearly
every zlib call trusts implicitly; less specific to this function, but equally unguarded.

**Reframing the s272 observation (the actual finding this session, corrects s272's framing)**: s272's
crash record reads `si_addr=0x380000003` (RDRAM base + guest `0x80000003`), and s272's own write-up
already flagged this as "3 bytes past the exact-`0x80000000` signature this whole investigation has
been tracking" — but that observation was never followed up because s272-s288 all believed
`inflate_fast` was a system-library call needing a different localization approach (s289 corrected
that belief). Working the arithmetic through this codebase's actual `MEM_B`/`MEM_BU` macros
(`N64Recomp/include/recomp.h:101-108`, which XOR the byte offset with 3 for MIPS big-endian byte
addressing *before* subtracting the `0x80000000` RDRAM base): a **register holding exactly 0** fed
into any `MEM_B`/`MEM_BU` access with an offset whose low 2 bits are 0 produces precisely
`rdram + 0x80000003` — an exact match for the observed fault, with no need to invoke a large garbaged
64-bit value or an exotic offset. **This means the s272 crash is not a novel zlib bug at all — it is
the same "guest struct field left at 0/uninitialized where a valid `~0x80000000`-range RDRAM pointer
was expected" signature this investigation has guarded roughly 15 times elsewhere since ~s130** (the
`-0x25A4` family, the `G1`-`G32` family, `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList`'s `0x80000004`,
`buildPositionAndCallTransformHelper`'s `0x80000010`, etc. — all small positive offsets from an exact
`0x80000000` base). The most likely candidates for the zero-valued register, per the caller-argument
trace above, are `tl`/`td` (if `huft_build` failed to populate the caller's Huffman-table fields before
this call) or one of the several `MEM_BU(reg, ...)` accesses inside the copy loop where `reg` is `p`
(input pointer, `ctx->r12`) or `q` (output pointer, `ctx->r11`) — but this is not yet confirmed,
only newly plausible; the existing evidence (a single, years-old crash record with a stale
`last-guest-pc`) cannot distinguish between these candidates.

**Instrument landed**: `BREADCRUMB10`, `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, same established
per-instruction `g_rs64_last_guest_pc` write mechanism as `BREADCRUMB`-`BREADCRUMB9`, scoped to
`inflate_fast`'s body only (250 comment-line sites patched, confirmed via the fixup-script's own
report line and a direct grep of the regenerated `funcs_7.c`). No guard was landed — with only 1
crash observation ever and no confirmation of *which* register was zero, guessing a guard site blind

control, and there is no way to force this specific rare crash on demand). The breadcrumb exists

(rather than the stale `beginFrameDLChunk` value s272/s273 both observed), which combined with a
register dump should identify which of `tl`/`td`/`p`/`q` (or another candidate) was zero.

Source-read `tickSongSequence` (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_25.c:4878-5317`). It's a song-sequence-slot lookup + stop-voices tick routine: the incoming caller argument (masked, saved to `ctx->r17`/`s1` at entry per `funcs_25.c:4886`) is linear-scanned against an 8-entry global table (base `-0x6600`, stride `0xEF8`, `funcs_25.c:4903-4946`) to find a matching slot ID. The match "index" accumulates in `ctx->r4`/`a0` as a *conditional* running count across the scan (incremented once per iteration whose slot has a nonzero flag byte) rather than a direct copy of the true loop position — meaning it can reach `8`, one past the table's last valid index, if the matching slot is the 8th one scanned and every preceding slot also had its flag set. That index is reloaded at `funcs_25.c:4950` and multiplied by `0xEF8` to form `ctx->r18`/`s2` (`funcs_25.c:5010-5011`), the table-entry address the two flagged-as-unguarded list walks then dereference (`funcs_25.c:5018-5046` walks the `+0xE78` list calling `stopVoicesByHandle` per node; `5050-5077` does the same for `+0xE7C`). No recompiler translation defect found — this is the same uniform every-`MEM_*`-access-unguarded baseline every `RECOMP_FUNC` has shown since `BREADCRUMB1`. The OOB-index-of-8 shape is inherent to the original N64 game's compiled logic, faithfully preserved by the 1:1 mechanical translation, not something recompilation introduced. Ranked candidates if a crash recurs here: `ctx->r18` (the computed table-entry pointer, first deref `funcs_25.c:5018`) ranks above `ctx->r16` (the list-node pointer loaded from it, subsequent derefs at `5019/5039/5051/5071`).

Of the untouched functions, `func_800AE3F0` (funcs_27.c, 10 sites, the JSON's largest candidate with zero prior mentions) looked most promising on the "caller-controlled" heuristic — but turned out to span roughly 18,000 lines (`160152`-`178336`, the last function in the file, immediately after `hangarInitializeShipShadowHob`), making it both impractically large for a single-session read and likely to overlap the already-closed `-0x25A4` hangar-list-pointer audit lineage (s283-288). Dropped it and picked `stopSongByHandle` instead (funcs_25.c:4390-4818, ~430 lines, 2 flagged sites, zero prior `CURRENT-TRUTH` mentions) — same file and subsystem as `tickSongSequence`, and its name implies a caller-supplied handle argument, the textbook "caller-controlled" shape this whole sweep targets.

Source-read `stopSongByHandle` in full. The incoming handle (raw caller `$a0`, saved to `ctx->r17`/`s1` at entry) is masked (`& 0x7FFFFFFF`) and linear-scanned against the SAME 8-entry global table `tickSongSequence` uses (base `-0x6600`, stride `0xEF8`) looking for a FREE slot (flag byte at `-0x573F` must be 0 AND the handle field must match) — same conditional-count-as-index arithmetic as `BREADCRUMB13`'s finding, confirmed via the same shift-and-subtract multiply-by-`0xEF8` idiom (`funcs_25.c:4749-4757`, `index*0xEF8` computed as `((index<<4)-index)<<5)-index)<<3`). If no match is found, or if the ORIGINAL (unmasked) handle's sign bit was set, the function takes an early-out tail path (`funcs_25.c:4742-4800`) that only sets a status byte and never reaches either list walk. On a genuine match, `ctx->r18`/`s2` (`funcs_25.c:4522-4523`, the computed table-entry address) gates two "call `stopVoicesByHandle` per node" walks (`+0xE78` list, `funcs_25.c:4530-4558`; `+0xE7C` list, `funcs_25.c:4561-4592`) — both null-checked before entry and self-consistently null-checked one iteration ahead of each subsequent deref, same shape as every other list walk audited this project. The 2 sites the static finder actually flagged are narrower: `ctx->r3` at `funcs_25.c:4630`/`4690`, inside a SEPARATE pair of loops (`funcs_25.c:4608-4726`) that walk each of those same two list heads to their TAIL and splice the freed node onto a shared global free list at `-0x2A3C`-base+`0x29C4` — traced the register flow instruction-by-instruction and confirmed each dereference is preceded by a null check exactly one iteration earlier (first iteration dereferences a value already validated by the pre-loop check; each subsequent iteration dereferences a value validated by the previous iteration's loop-continue check) — a standard "walk to non-null tail, no range check" idiom, structurally identical to the free-list-push pattern already characterized in the `heapFreeListDequeue` family (s252-253). No recompiler translation defect found — same uniform every-`MEM_*`-access-unguarded baseline as every other `RECOMP_FUNC`. Ranked candidates if this recurs: `ctx->r3` (the tail-walk pointer, first deref `funcs_25.c:4630`/`4690`) ranks above `ctx->r16` (the `+0xE78`/`+0xE7C` list-walk node pointer, `funcs_25.c:4541/4552/4573/4584`).

tickTextureMaterialExpiry-guard` (s295-297 all ran it). `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md` did not exist
this session (no queued soaks ran between s297 and this iteration, so no new `BREADCRUMB12`

60,000-byte Step-0 maintenance trigger, so this was not a maintenance iteration either. Per the
