comment on the preceding line, `// 0x800A64B4: j L_800A6024`) lands at `funcs_27.c:107269`
(`L_800A6024`). That target sits AFTER the `static_6_800A9ABC` call site (`107079`, per s335) but
BEFORE the `cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` call site (`107938`, per s334/s335). This is a genuine,
self-contained internal loop: every pass from `L_800A6024` through the backward jump calls
`cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` and `submitGfxFrame` (`108253`) and then jumps straight back to the top
— the `static_6_800A9ABC` call at `107079`, which sits BEFORE the loop's entry point, is never
re-executed on any iteration after the first.

**This directly answers s335's open question, refuting hypothesis 2 and confirming hypothesis 1**:
`cinematicLoopBody` is not invoked repeatedly by some outer caller taking a different path each time —
it loops internally. `static_6_800A9ABC` firing once and `cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` firing 1152+
times in s334's log is exactly what one single invocation of `cinematicLoopBody` produces: one setup
call, then N loop iterations.

Checked `cinematicLoopBody`'s own callers too (NEXT.md step 2, `grep -rn "cinematicLoopBody(rdram,
ctx)"` across `RecompiledFuncs/*.c`): two call sites, `funcs_44.c:4825` and `funcs_27.c:156405`. Read
both — they are **byte-identical disassembly** (same addresses, same instructions, same enclosing
function shape, `static_6_800AE518`), the same overlay-duplication artifact family s335 already
identified for `static_6_800A9ABC`/`cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` — i.e., one logical function
recompiled twice into two overlay translation units. Both are simple tail calls: fixed args
(`a0=3, a1=2`), `jal cinematicLoopBody` immediately followed by `jr $ra` with no loop around it. This
is consistent with "some other part of the game calls this wrapper once to start a cutscene, and
`cinematicLoopBody`'s own internal loop then owns every subsequent frame until its exit condition
fires" — did not trace further up to find what calls the wrapper itself; not needed to close this
iteration's question, and would be scope creep beyond the assigned work unit (iron rule 8's spirit).

**Traced the loop's only exit.** Within `L_800A6024`...`108258`, exactly one goto (`107342`, `goto
L_800A64BC`) targets outside the loop body (`108264`, right past the backward-jump point) — the
loop's sole escape hatch. It's gated by the return value of `static_6_800AF550` (`funcs_44.c:6187`,
called at `107331`): nonzero exits the loop, zero (the default/fallthrough path) continues it. Read
`static_6_800AF550` in full (~140 lines, short enough for one pass): it loads a pointer from global
`0x800B0934` (early-outs returning 0 if null), computes a float `f2 = table[0x800A5D70-ish] *
(a2 reinterpreted as float via `mtc1`, no int-to-float conversion) + struct-byte-at-offset-0x2F`,
compares `f2` against two float constants at `0x800A5D70` and `0x800A5D74`, and on the
"not yet past threshold" path increments a debounce counter at struct-offset `0x938`, force-returning
1 (loop-exit) once that counter reaches 7. Every other path returns 0 (keep looping).

**Notable: nothing in `static_6_800AF550`'s body touches any audio-subsystem global, register, MusyX
structure, or DMA/task-queue state.** Every operand is either the per-actor/track struct at
`0x800B0934`, two data-table float constants, or a 7-iteration debounce counter — this reads as an
ordinary elapsed-time/threshold gameplay timer, structurally unrelated to audio. This is **source-level
evidence, not yet a proven conclusion** (the struct fields and the two threshold constants were not
traced back to their producers — did not check whether *something else* [e.g. a delta-time value fed
into the `a2` argument] is itself audio-dependent), but it's suspicious enough to flag explicitly: this
entire investigation thread was opened under the "M5 audio de-stubbing" strategic priority on the
premise that the `reapplyDisplayMode`/VI=640 stall is an audio-stub artifact, and three sessions deep
(s333/s334/s335/s336) nothing found so far — `runVideoFrameTick`'s upstream caller chain, the dead-code
red herring, and now this exit-gate function — has touched audio state at all. It may be a legitimate
(if very slow) cutscene, or a plain gameplay-timer bug, filed under the wrong M-priority.

No code changed, no diagnostics added, no soak run, no `lib/` touched — a source-proof-only session,
same method as s335 ("capture once, analyze many" extended to "read once, analyze exhaustively" for
static control flow — no soak needed when the question is answerable from the text alone).

Pushed the source-read one level further to sanity-check the audio-relevance flag before writing it
down: `static_6_800AF550`'s `a2` argument comes from register `$f20`, set at the very top of the loop
(`funcs_27.c:107279`, `mov.s $f20, $f0`, in the delay slot right after `jal pollControllerInputs` —
so `$f0` at that point is actually the return value of the PRECEDING call, `static_6_800AF360`
(`107270`), not of `pollControllerInputs`). Read `static_6_800AF360`
(`funcs_44.c:5792`): it calls `timeSnapshotFiller` (a real, human-named function — not a `static_N_`
placeholder) to fill a time-snapshot struct, then computes a delta via `floatModulo` against the
previous snapshot. This is the shape of a genuine OS-clock-based per-frame delta-time calculation, not
anything audio-adjacent. So the full traced chain — `cinematicLoopBody`'s loop → `static_6_800AF550`
exit gate → its `a2`/`$f20` input → `static_6_800AF360` → `timeSnapshotFiller` — is, on a pure
source read, **three function-levels deep with zero audio-subsystem references anywhere in it**. This
raises the flag from "worth noting" to "worth prioritizing a runtime check before spending another
audio-focused session here": either the delta-time value is legitimately advancing and this is just a
long (or buggy-duration-table) cutscene wholly unrelated to M5, or something else entirely (not yet
identified) is preventing `timeSnapshotFiller`'s snapshot from advancing. Only a soak with real values
can settle which.

## Session 339 (2026-08-05) — M5 audio: source-proves `submitGfxFrame` structurally cannot produce a `FramebufferPair` and that `cinematicLoopBody`'s self-loop calls the real `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` producer (`runVideoFrameTick`) exactly ONCE, not per-iteration — closes the VI=640 `pairs=0` stall's root-cause chase (s329-s338) in 1 iteration, no new soak

**HYPOTHESIS-ID**: `m5-audio-destub-submitgfxframe-vi-fs-decoupling` (1st and only iteration needed —
closed this session).

**Starting question** (from s337/NEXT.md): does `cinematicLoopBody`'s direct `submitGfxFrame` call
(not `runVideoFrameTick`) decouple from `[vi-fs-decision]`'s `pairs=0` reading — i.e. does
`submitGfxFrame`'s output plausibly reach the same graphics-task queue `[vi-fs-decision]` monitors?

**Method**: pure source-read (per this arc's own convention, s335/s336 already closed 2 prior
questions this way) plus reuse of s337's already-captured soak log — no new soak run.

1. Read `submitGfxFrame`'s full body (`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_3.c:13845`, `N64Recomp` repo — 1289
   lines). Its callee set: `bufferArbiterAllocSlot`, `bufferArbiterMarkSlotReady`,
   `bufferArbiterProducerMark` (×3), `commitMeshDrawBatchRefs`, `drainMeshReleaseQueue`,
   `getInactiveBufferIndex`, `getTimeSinceLastFrame`, `isPreNmiPending`, `osDpGetCounters_recomp`,
   `osDpSetStatus_recomp`, `osRecvMesg_recomp`, `osSendMesg_recomp`, `osWritebackDCacheAll_recomp`,
   `recordFrameTimestamp`, `setPostSwapPendingFlags`, `yieldFromGfxFrame`, `yieldFromSpThread`. No
   `setupCameraMatrices`, no `emitFrameRdpInitDl`, no `runVideoFrameTick`, no `advanceVideoFrame`, no
   indirect (`LOOKUP_FUNC`) calls anywhere in the body.
2. Traced what actually produces a `FramebufferPair` (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_workload.cpp:294`,
   `Workload::addFramebufferPair`, called from wherever the DL interpreter handles a
   `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` opcode). Cross-referenced the `rogue_squadron64` symbol file's existing
   annotations (already on disk from earlier sessions, not re-derived): `emitFrameRdpInitDl`
   (`main_overlay.txt:1096`) is *the* function that emits `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` bytes into the active DL,
   reading the draw-fb address `buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial` wrote. Its **sole caller** is
   `setupCameraMatrices` (`main_overlay.txt:1095`, "runs once per camera/viewport setup"), and
   `buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial`'s only per-frame caller is `advanceVideoFrame`
   (`main_overlay.txt:703`), whose own caller chain is stated explicitly in that file's own comment:
   **"Caller chain: `runVideoFrameTick` → `advanceVideoFrame`."** So the *only* path from any function
   to a `FramebufferPair` is `runVideoFrameTick → advanceVideoFrame → buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial`
   (writes fb addr) + `→ setupCameraMatrices → emitFrameRdpInitDl` (emits the opcode).
   `submitGfxFrame`'s callee set (step 1) contains none of these — it structurally cannot produce a
   `FramebufferPair`. It only advances the buffer-arbiter slot state machine (alloc→ready→producerMark,
   i.e. the SP-task producer/consumer handshake) and kicks housekeeping (mesh-ref commit, DMA
   writeback, dcache flush) — real per-frame work, just not the `[vi-fs-decision]`-relevant kind.
3. Checked whether `cinematicLoopBody` reaches `runVideoFrameTick` some other way. Grepped its full
   callee list (`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_27.c:106842-108531`, ~50 distinct callees) — no direct call to
   `runVideoFrameTick`, `advanceVideoFrame`, or `setupCameraMatrices`. But it DOES call
   `static_6_800A9ABC` (line 107079) — one of `runVideoFrameTick`'s 5 known call sites from s333's
   original grep. Its real (non-dead) definition is `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_43.c:20718`, and its call to
   `runVideoFrameTick` at `funcs_43.c:20975` sits in plain sequential control flow after label
   `L_800A9C68` — not past an unconditional return like s335's dead-code find, so it's live code, not
   an artifact.
4. **The discriminating fact**: `cinematicLoopBody`'s call to `static_6_800A9ABC` (line 107079) is
   BEFORE its internal self-loop label `L_800A6024` (line 107269, s336's already-proven `goto`-loop
   that runs unconditionally for the whole stall). It is called ONCE, in the function's setup section,
   never again once the self-loop starts.
5. **Confirmed at runtime, not just by source-read** — reused s337's already-captured
   `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/s337cutscenetimer/run.log` (1.28M lines, no new soak): it already had
   `ROGUESQ_LOG_MAINGAMELOOP_REACH=1` armed, which is the env gate on the *already-existing*
   `[static6-800a9abc-entry]` diagnostic added in s334 (misleadingly named after the env var, not the
   function) at `funcs_43.c:20721-20734`. `grep -c '\[static6-800a9abc-entry\]'` → **exactly 1** hit,
   `n=1`, for the entire ~600s run. Two independent lines of evidence (source-read + this runtime
   count) now agree.

**Sanity check (Fermi cross-check on a surprising number, per iron rule)**: s333 measured
`runVideoFrameTick` stops after exactly 2 calls total. s334 independently found `mainGameLoop`'s
loop-top counter fires exactly once. This session's `static_6_800A9ABC` count is also exactly once.
1 (mainGameLoop's own call site) + 1 (via `static_6_800A9ABC`) = 2 — an exact match to s333's raw
count, not just a plausible-sounding one.

**Conclusion — closes the entire s329-s338 VI=640 `pairs=0` stall chase, not just this session's
narrower question**: the graphics-task pipeline is not actually stalled in any subsystem-death sense.
`cinematicLoopBody`'s internal per-frame self-loop (1152+ iterations for the whole soak, per s336)
correctly drives cutscene-slot dispatch, speech, buffer-arbiter SP-task submission
(`submitGfxFrame`), and DMA/mesh housekeeping every single pass — all genuinely alive the whole time,
matching every session's audio/buffer-arbiter observations in this arc. What it does NOT do is
re-invoke the one function chain (`runVideoFrameTick → ... → setupCameraMatrices →
emitFrameRdpInitDl`) that emits a `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` RDP opcode — that chain runs exactly once, in
`cinematicLoopBody`'s pre-loop setup, and never again. `[vi-fs-decision]`'s `pairs` counter
(`Workload::fbPairCount`) can only increment off that opcode, so once the current workload advances
past its one-time pair (or if it's simply the initial state), `pairs` reads 0 for the rest of the
scene — a faithful reading of "no new colour-image target this workload," not evidence of a hung
subsystem. **This is very likely not a bug at all** — a cutscene that holds a locked camera/RDP-state
prologue for its duration (rather than re-emitting per-frame camera setup) is a completely ordinary
optimization for a scripted, non-interactive scene; s336 already flagged that this thread had no
audio-subsystem footprint anywhere in its exit-gate trace, and this session's finding is consistent
with that: **the VI=640 "stall" is a characteristic of this particular cutscene's rendering-loop
design, unrelated to the M5 audio gate reversal that was used to reach it.** No visual defect has
been demonstrated — that would need a separate capture-and-look work unit, out of scope here.

**What this means for M5's still-open decision** (item -182..-187): promoting `setDisplayMode`'s (and
now, by this session's finding, plausibly `reapplyDisplayMode`'s too) gate-byte reversal to the
shipped default is no longer blocked by an unexplained stall — the VI=640 condition it was thought to
risk is now a characterized, benign, non-audio rendering-loop property, not an open crash/hang
mechanism. Recommend the next M5 work unit revisit that promotion decision directly rather than
continuing to instrument this thread further.

  `last-guest-pc=0x80054744`.

**Root cause, traced to source**: `0x80054744` sits inside `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_11.c:15057`, function starts at `0x80054650`) — **this is
`BREADCRUMB9`** (landed s276, per `main_overlay.txt:2031` and grep of PORTING-STATE history
s270-s291: "3 callers in funcs_11/32/33... per-entry timer accumulator update with wrap-around").
Reading the exact instruction sequence around the crash PC (`funcs_11.c:15316-15347`): `divu $zero,
$v1, $v0` at `0x80054738` (dividing by `$v0`, loaded via `lh $v0, 0x0($s0)` at `0x80054734` — a
halfword "threshold" field read from the current list entry), then `bne $v0, $zero, L_80054748`
(skip the trap if the divisor is nonzero) — since `$v0==0` here, execution falls through to the
compiler-inserted `break 7` at `0x80054744`, which the runtime's `do_break()` turns into `abort()`.
`do_break`'s argument, `2147829572`, is not a semantic error code — it's the guest PC itself
(`0x80000000 + 0x54744 = 2147829572`, confirmed by direct arithmetic) — a MIPS N64 compiler idiom
this codebase already recognizes and guards elsewhere for `musyxKeyOnVoice` (8 sites,
`fixup_game_funcs.py:939-949`, `do_break` constants `2148076780..2148077008` → early `return`) and
`evalCubicSplineAtTime` (1 site, zero-width-interval guard → `f4.fl=0` instead of trapping).

**This is a genuinely NEW crash signature for `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList`, distinct from its
already-catalogued one.** PORTING-STATE ~26156 (s289/s290 era) documents `BREADCRUMB9`'s known crash
as `si_addr≈0x80000004` — a near-null-pointer dereference (part of the `-0x25A4`/`G1`-`G32` family of
"a register holding exactly 0 fed into a small-offset `MEM_B`/`MEM_BU` access" bugs). Today's crash has
`si_addr=__pthread_kill`'s address (an `abort()` call site, confirmed via the backtrace: frames 4-5 are
`abort`/`err` from `libsystem_c.dylib`) — a completely different failure mode (compiler div-by-zero trap,
not a memory fault) in the same function. The two are not the same bug re-surfacing; this is a second,
independent defect in `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList`'s entry-processing loop.

**Open question — reproducibility**: this soak's gate configuration is **byte-identical** to s328's
`step4gate2` baseline (`setDisplayMode` reversed alone, `reapplyDisplayMode` force-zero) — confirmed via

navigation, and the same 12s stabilization window this session's crash hit). Two explanations, not yet
distinguished: (a) this is a nondeterministic timing race in menu-overlay/craft-select setup order

could vary run to run); or (b) one of the ~15 intervening sessions' unrelated code changes since s328
(other M3 idiom-class guards, other fixup-script edits) introduced or newly exposed this. This is
single-source (1 crash observation) — Iron Rule 4 requires a second independent line of evidence before
this enters "current truth" as a confirmed regression.

**What this does NOT mean**: it does NOT reopen the reapplyDisplayMode question — HA is cleanly

## Session 345 (2026-08-05) — the `m5step5v2_rate_1/2` `rc=137` verdicts were a recipe artifact (a known self-inflicted `[rs-free-walk]` logging blowup, PORTING-STATE Session 209/210), not crash-family #3/#4 signal; fixed the shared soak driver and cancelled/reissued the affected recipes

**Read list**: `docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md`, `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` (s344's writeup), `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md`
tail. Both `m5step5v2_rate_1/2` (the 2 recipes s344 queued, drained by the loop between iterations)
came back `rc=137 | 600s` — a SIGKILL at the loop's hard cap. NEXT.md's own step 2/3 plan expected this
outcome to mean either crash-family #3 (`waitForAnyAudioSlot` pre-title SIGSEGV) or family #4 (the
post-cutscene stall); this session found it was neither.

**Investigation.** Both recipes' verdict `.log` files (`scratch/agent/soak_results/m5step5v2_rate_{1,2}_*.log`)
were EMPTY — the recipe's own `echo "VERDICT: ..."` lines never ran, meaning the whole process (launcher +
post-processing) was killed before reaching them, not merely that the game hung. Read the launcher logs
instead (`m5step5v2rate{1,2}_launcher.log`): both show a completely normal run — `phase width=1024 reached
after 45.7-45.9s` (title), the full `[keys]`/stick schedule through the 240s hold, `hold done wall=275s`,
`done wall=301-302s`, `game process still alive; killing` (the launcher's own routine post-hold kill, not
a hang), then a clean `--- summary ---` block. **The game-side scenario the recipe was driving completed
in ~301s, well inside the 600s budget** — the SIGKILL landed on something AFTER that.

Checked `run.log` size for both: `m5step5v2rate1/run.log` = 8.2 GB, `m5step5v2rate2/run.log` = 7.9 GB.
Every other recipe in this family (`m5step5rate1/2` at ~76 MB, `s343confirm1/2` at ~228-233 MB) produced
1-2 orders of magnitude less. The recipe's post-launcher step is 6 sequential `grep -a` passes over
`run.log` — on an 8+ GB file that never finished before the external 600s watchdog fired, which is why
the verdict `.log`s were empty: the recipe itself was still grepping when it got killed.

**Why the log blew up**: sampled the first 200 MB of `m5step5v2rate1/run.log` — 1,610,567 of 3,603,801
lines (44.7%) are `[rs-free-walk]`. Grepped `PORTING-STATE.md` for that tag and found this EXACT failure
mode already root-caused in Sessions 209-210 (2026-07-28, `unlitmeshtracer4/5/6`): `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_FREE_WALK`
and `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_MALLOC_WALK` log once PER LIST NODE walked, not once per call like every other
`ROGUESQ_LOG_*` var — Session 209 saw a 47x line-count blowup (4.49M → 210M lines) between two runs of the
SAME script with byte-identical instrumentation, and Session 210 confirmed by elimination (stripped all but
one `ROGUESQ_LOG_*` var, log volume dropped ~1470x, real game-tick progress resumed) that the volume itself
was costing enough real fprintf wall-clock to starve actual game-logic progress — not a new behavioral
regression, self-inflicted over-instrumentation. This session's numbers land in the same band: `[rs-free-walk]`
share (44.7%) matches Session 209/210's observed 44-82% range, and the ~40-55x size blowup (76-233 MB → 7.9-8.2 GB)
matches their ~47x line-count blowup almost exactly.

**Open sub-question, not resolved this session**: WHY did this run's walk run away while `s343confirm1/2`
(same script family, same `HOLD_S=240`, run 20 minutes earlier, no code or config change in between) stayed
in the normal 76-233 MB band? Session 209/210's own evidence was that the walker's cost scales with however
many times it gets invoked against however long the free list has grown — consistent with a timing/state-
dependent trigger rather than a fixed per-run cost, but this session did not isolate what specifically
differed between the two soaks. Flagged as open, not blocking: the actionable finding (rc=137 here is a
recipe artifact) does not depend on resolving it.

**Fix landed** (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_s327waitpump.sh`, not `lib/`, no `export.sh` needed): the 4
heap-walker log vars (`ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_MALLOC_WALK`, `_GUARD`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_FREE_WALK`, `_GUARD`) now use
the `${VAR:-1}` default-expansion pattern already used elsewhere in the same file for
`ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME` — every existing recipe that doesn't pre-export these sees identical behavior
(still armed, default 1), but a recipe can now opt them to 0 without forking the 148-line shared driver.
Queued `m5step5v3_rate_1/2.sh` (3rd generation of this recipe family) with the 4 vars set to 0 and 2 new
verdict fields (`runlog_bytes`, `rs_free_walk_lines`) so a recurrence is visible without re-deriving file
sizes by hand. Cancelled `m5step5v2_rate_3/4.sh` (queued, never run) rather than running them unmodified —
they would have reproduced the identical artifact and wasted 2 more 600s loop slots for zero information
(`scratch/agent/soak_queue/cancelled/README.md` updated with the full note, matching the existing
`m5step5_rate_3..6` cancellation precedent from s342).

**Housekeeping**: deleted both 8+ GB `run.log`s (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/m5step5v2rate{1,2}/`) after
extracting the samples above — disk was at 84% used (149 GiB free) before cleanup, 82% (166 GiB free)
after. Not archived; regenerable by rerunning the cancelled v2 recipes if ever needed, though under the
now-fixed driver's unchanged default they'd very likely reproduce the same blowup again (the fix requires
a recipe to opt in, which the cancelled v2 recipes don't).

**Net**: `HYPOTHESIS-ID m5-audio-destub-step5-crashrate-comparison` gained 0 real data points toward the
actual crash-family #3/#4 rate question this session — this was pure recipe-methodology repair, forced by
the loop's own drained verdicts being uninterpretable. 2nd iteration on this hypothesis-id since s344's
reopen (methodology, not yet a 3rd repeat of the same experiment — budget rule 8 unaffected). Next session
should read `m5step5v3_rate_1/2`'s verdicts (drained by the loop) and, if `runlog_bytes` is back in the

### The discriminating check: does allocOrEvictMaterialNode recur?

No. `rate_1`'s crash (item -202) was `allocOrEvictMaterialNode+944`. `rate_3` is
`processSceneNode+1424`. `rate_4` is `trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1192`. Three crashes, three
different symbols — zero repeats of any single symbol across the whole 4-run batch (`rate_2` was the
only clean run). This directly answers s346's open question: `allocOrEvictMaterialNode` is NOT a
recurring family. It stays a single, uncatalogued data point (1/4), below the bar for a guard.

### Are the other two symbols already-catalogued?

Checked both against `docs/` and `PORTING-STATE.md` via grep before writing this up (Iron Rule 4 —
two independent lines before anything enters the ledger as a conclusion; here the two lines are "not
a repeat of rate_1" and "cross-checked against the existing crash catalog"):

- `processSceneNode` is a KNOWN misattribution-prone, multi-offset crash site: Session 151/152
  documents crashes at `processSceneNode+7640` (s151, called it possibly self-recursion or nearest-
  symbol misattribution given the byte offset dwarfing the function's expected small per-node body)
  and references `+6668` elsewhere (Session ~145-150 range). `+1424` this session is a 3rd distinct
  offset at the same symbol. Read together with s151's own caveat about nearest-symbol
  misattribution being plausible at large offsets, the most parsimonious read is that
  `processSceneNode`'s three different crash offsets across sessions are the SAME underlying
  ambiguous-attribution family recurring at different apparent byte offsets, not three separate bugs
  — but this is not proven, only consistent with the existing caveat.
- `trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1192` has NO prior crash citation anywhere in the ledger. The
  only existing mention (PORTING-STATE ~line 108, an old symbol-table session) is an unrelated
  duplicate-symbol-address bug fixed long ago, not a crash report. This is a genuinely new site, but
  — like `allocOrEvictMaterialNode` — a singleton with n=1, not (yet) a family.

### A note on why last-guest-pc and pc-symbol looked inconsistent (not a bug, resolved by reading the source)

`rate_4`'s `last-guest-pc=0x8000b650` doesn't fall inside `trackResourceListWithMappingTables`'s own
guest address range (`0x800538B0`+), which looked at first like a symbolization bug worth
investigating. Reading `src/main/main.cpp:1740-1786` resolved it without new instrumentation:
`[CRASH][pc-symbol]` is `dladdr()` on the HOST crash PC (`ss.__pc`, precise, chosen at s206
specifically to avoid `backtrace_symbols`' frame-pointer-walk misattribution) while
`[CRASH][last-guest-pc]` is a separately-tracked checkpoint variable (`g_rs64_last_guest_pc`), updated
at guest recompiled-function/jump boundaries, not necessarily the guest instruction underlying the
exact host-crash PC. The two fields answer different questions by design; a mismatch between them is
expected, not evidence of a bug in the instrument.

### Tally and what it discriminates

4 real (non-artifact) data points on the m5step5v3 template: `rate_1` CRASH
(`allocOrEvictMaterialNode+944`), `rate_2` CLEAN, `rate_3` CRASH (`processSceneNode+1424`), `rate_4`

as another run; 0/4 matched the historically-named family #3 (`waitForAnyAudioSlot`) or family #4
(post-cutscene "every soak died earlier" stall) signatures specifically — the two families this whole
step-5 comparison was designed to rate.

This splits the competing hypotheses cleanly:
- H1 "de-stubbing concentrated the risk into one new bug (`allocOrEvictMaterialNode`, candidate family
  #5)" — REFUTED. 0/3 recurrence after rate_1.
- H2 "de-stubbing didn't reduce the post-title crash rate at all, it just moved which symbol shows up
  — family #3/#4 specifically go quiet but the background ~20+-family crash population is still live
  and still fires at a similar overall rate" — SUPPORTED by this batch (0/4 on #3/#4, but 3/4 on
  something).
- H3 "de-stubbing measurably reduced the OVERALL crash rate in this window, #3/#4 or not" — cannot be
  evaluated from this batch alone; would need a comparable pre-de-stub baseline crash rate for this
  exact post-title/craft-select window (the existing family #3/#4 baselines are for different
  windows/mechanisms, not directly comparable to a same-window all-cause rate).

n=4 is still small — precisely BECAUSE each crash is a different symbol, no single-family rate is
yet estimable, matching M5-AUDIO-PLAN's explicit warning against over-reading small samples. Queued
`scratch/agent/soak_queue/m5step5v3_rate_5.sh` through `_8.sh` (identical template) to extend the
sample before drawing a firmer conclusion on H2 vs H3.

### What this does NOT show

Does not show `processSceneNode` or `trackResourceListWithMappingTables` are new families requiring a
guard (each n=1, same standard applied to `allocOrEvictMaterialNode`). Does not show the overall
crash rate changed vs. pre-de-stub baseline (no comparable same-window baseline rate exists yet to

## Session 348 (2026-08-05) — M5 audio: drained rate_5/6, found the exact-repeat discriminating result, source-read and GUARDED processSceneNode's unguarded content pointer

Drained `m5step5v3_rate_5` (CLEAN, `crash_markers=0`) and `_rate_6` (CRASH) from the soak queue.
`rate_6`'s crash was the discriminating result this whole batch was designed to find: `last_pc_symbol=processSceneNode+1424` AND `last_guest_pc=0x80014FDC` — BOTH fields byte-identical to `rate_3`'s
crash from s347. Not just the same function (which `processSceneNode` has hit at 2 other offsets
historically, `+6668`/`+7640` per s151/152) but the exact same instruction twice: the strongest repeat
match in the whole 6-run v3 sample, and the first symbol in this comparison to cross NEXT.md's declared
"2+ hits" escalation threshold. Updated tally: overall crash rate now 4/6 (67%, down from the earlier
3/4 estimate but still not zero); family #3 (`waitForAnyAudioSlot`)/#4 (post-cutscene stall) still 0/6;
`processSceneNode+1424` now 2/6, `allocOrEvictMaterialNode+944` and `trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1192`
stay singletons.

Per NEXT.md's own escalation plan, source-read `processSceneNode` in
`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c` around guest PC `0x80014FDC` (grepped the
breadcrumb comment, unique hit at the time). The crash instruction is `ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r16, 0X30)`
— a dereference of `ctx->r16`, which was loaded two instructions earlier (guest `0x80014FD0`) via
`ctx->r16 = MEM_W(ctx->r17, 0X8)`: a "content" pointer read out of a FIELD of the scene-node pointer
(`ctx->r17`). s190's existing guard (item -190-ish, "processSceneNode node-pointer validity guard")
validates `ctx->r17` itself at function entry but never checks the field loaded out of it — so a
corrupt/stale content-pointer field flows straight into an unguarded deref, explaining a fixed,
repeatable crash address rather than a stack-depth-dependent or nondeterministic one. Grepped for the
same load idiom elsewhere in the function and found a second site (guest `0x800153F8`, funcs_4.c:16493-6)
on the sibling-loop continuation path, which jumps back into the SAME shared block (`L_80014FE8`) that
dereferences the SAME `ctx->r16` again at `+0x34`/`+0x38` — same idiom, second site, not a separate bug.

**Landed a fix**, following the s282-s288 idiom-class-closure model the user directive names for M3
work: added `fixup_game_funcs.py` patches guarding BOTH load sites (mirrors s190's guard shape exactly
— range-check `[0x80000000, 0x80800000)`, bail to the function's existing `L_80015528` exit/sentinel,
env-gated diagnostic logging under `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_CONTENT_GUARD`). Hit and fixed a real
methodology trap while writing this: my first attempt placed the new patch code physically BEFORE the
"processSceneNode guest-PC breadcrumb (BREADCRUMB4)" patch in the script, whose anchor text requires
the `g_rs64_last_guest_pc = 0x80014FD0u;` line that BREADCRUMB4 itself inserts — since pristine
N64Recomp output doesn't have that line yet at that point in the pipeline, the regex silently matched
zero times (`re.subn` returning `n=0`, no error, no report line) and the "fix" was pure no-op. Caught
it only by diffing report output against expectation and adding temporary debug prints; moved the new
patch block to run immediately AFTER BREADCRUMB4 in script order, confirmed both sites now report
`patched x1` and the guard text is physically present in the regenerated `funcs_4.c` (lines ~15191 and
~16512). Full regen (`make_elf.py` -> `N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py` -> `cmake --build`) completed
clean, no new warnings/errors beyond pre-existing unrelated ones (DDIV sign-conversion noise in
`funcs_8.c`, present before this session).

Ran one validation soak inline (`s348_contentguard_verify1`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_CONTENT_GUARD=1`
armed via `run_s327waitpump.sh`): crashed at an unrelated, previously-uncatalogued-in-soak-results site

     revisits every frame** (plausibly stub/disabled content given the M5 audio-destub context), not

     noise would produce (odds of two independent random-garbage reads matching are ~1 in 4 billion).

Source-read `coalesceFreeHeapBlocks` at guest PC `0x80002434`
(`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c:4664-4673`, confirmed against the function's
disassembly comments): the function walks the heap's physical block chain by computing `v0 = t0 +
MEM_W(t0, 0x4)` — the current block pointer (`t0`, `ctx->r8`) plus that block's OWN size field — to
locate the next physical block, then immediately reads a 16-bit flags field at `MEM_HU(v0, 0x10)` with
no validity check on `v0` first. If `t0`'s size field is itself corrupt (plausibly from an unrelated,
earlier heap-corruption event elsewhere — this function doesn't need to be the ORIGIN of the corruption,
just the first place that dereferences its downstream consequence), `v0` becomes a wild pointer and this
read is the crash. This is architecturally the same failure shape as every guard landed in this cluster
since s190: an unvalidated pointer-plus-offset walk over heap/list structures with no bounds check before
dereference.

Added a guard at `0x80002434` in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (funcs_0.c-scoped, same range-check-and-bail
idiom and `0x80000000`-`0x80800000` RDRAM bound as every prior guard in this cluster): on out-of-range
`v0`, synthesizes `ctx->r3 = 0` — the same zero the immediately-following `andi $v1,$v1,0x8` / `beq`
pair would see from a legitimately-clear flag bit, sending control to `L_80002358` exactly as if the
next block had genuinely tested "not free." Minimal-behavior-change bail, identical philosophy to

**Source-read** (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_3.c` ~1848-1900, guest range
0x800081DC-0x80008210): found the guest PC 0x80008200 sits inside a SECOND, entirely separate unguarded
linked-list tail-scan loop in this same function, walking a list rooted at `ctx->r4`/`$a0` (NOT the
`ctx->r3`/`$v1` chain the existing s350/s350b guards protect):
```
L_800081FC: v1 = *v1 (0x800081FC, MEM_W(ctx->r3,0)); v0 = *v1 (0x80008200, MEM_W(ctx->r3,0));

```
i.e. "keep following `v1 = *v1` until the node it lands on has a NULL first field" — same
unguarded-linked-list-walk idiom as the loop s350 already guards, no bounds check anywhere. The confirmed
crash site is 0x80008200 (dereferencing the pointer `0x800081FC` just loaded into v1); 0x800081FC itself
(dereferencing the pre-update v1) has not yet been observed to fault and is flagged, not guarded, same
"confirmed site first, sibling pending its own hit" practice as s350→s350b.

**Fix**: added a range-check-and-bail guard at 0x80008200 (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`,
new patch block "drainMeshReleaseQueue 2nd tail-scan loop read guard (s357)"), reusing the existing
`ROGUESQ_LOG_DRAIN_MESH_TAIL_GUARD` env var (already armed by default in `run_s327waitpump.sh`) under a
new diagnostic tag `[drain-mesh-loop2-guard]`. On invalid v1, synthesizes `v0=0` — the value the
following `bne $v0,$zero` check would see from a legitimately-NULL-first-field node, i.e. "treat this
unreachable node as the list's tail and stop walking" — same minimal-behavior-change bail idiom as every
other drain-mesh guard.

**Hit one implementation bug applying this**: the first attempt used a plain Python string as the
`re.subn` replacement (rather than a lambda), and Python's `re` module processes backslash escapes
(`\n`, `\t`, etc.) in plain-string replacements — the fprintf format string's literal `\n` became an
actual embedded newline in the generated `funcs_3.c`, breaking the C string literal across two lines and
failing the build (`error: expected expression` at the `fprintf` call). Fixed by switching to a lambda
callback for the replacement, matching every other multi-line patch in this file (which all already use

**Source-read** (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c:4360-4701`, the full
`coalesceFreeHeapBlocks` function): found the s354 guard's own design was flawed. The guard's comment
claimed forcing `ctx->r3 = 0` on an out-of-range `v0` "sends control to L_80002358 exactly as if the
coalesce loop had genuinely stopped here" — this is false. `ctx->r3 = 0` makes the immediately-following
`andi $v1,$v1,0x8` / `beq $v1,$zero,L_80002358` pair take the branch TO `L_80002358`, which is the loop's
**entry** label, not an exit. Taking that branch re-enters the loop body carrying `ctx->r8 = v0 + 0x10`
(computed unconditionally in the branch's delay slot, `0x80002440`, regardless of which way the branch
goes — MIPS delay-slot semantics) straight into `L_80002358: lhu $v0, 0x0($t0)` (guest `0x80002358`), an
unconditional dereference of that same wild pointer. This exactly explains `verify5`: the guard fired
(bail path engaged, `v0` correctly detected as out-of-range) but the very next loop iteration crashed one
instruction into re-entering the loop, at a host offset (`+1052`) upstream of the original guarded site
(`+3452`) because it's now the loop's TOP rather than its tail-check.

The real "loop genuinely stopped" exit is `L_80002444` — reached when the branch is NOT taken, i.e. when
`ctx->r3 != 0` (flag bit `0x8` set: the game's own "next block in use, stop coalescing here" signal).
Confirmed by reading the rest of the function (`funcs_0.c` ~4702-4865, through to the function's next
loop and `ctx->r8` reassignment): `ctx->r8` is never read again anywhere between `L_80002444` and the
point where it's freshly reassigned (`ctx->r8 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0x10)`, an unrelated second loop over a
different base register) — so forcing the "in use" branch on an invalid `v0` is safe: it drops the wild
pointer without ever dereferencing it again, matching the "treat unreachable state as a safe stop" idiom
every other guard in this project already uses, just applied to the correct branch this time.

**Fix** (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, same guard site as s354, not a new guard):
changed the bail assignment from `ctx->r3 = 0;` to `ctx->r3 = 0x8;` (any nonzero value survives the
`andi ...,0x8` mask the same way the real "in use" flag bit would). Rewrote the patch's header comment to
document the bug and the fix. Same env-gated diagnostic tag `[coalesce-heap-guard]`, same var
`ROGUESQ_LOG_COALESCE_HEAP_GUARD` (already armed by default in `run_s327waitpump.sh`) — no new tag/env
var needed since this corrects the existing guard's behavior rather than adding a new site.

NULL. It dereferences `ctx->r4` (`a0`, the HEAD pointer — loaded from a fixed table slot indexed by

register-offset LDR/STR case (it previously only covered immediate-offset
forms) — a real, reusable tool improvement, verified by manual bit-decode of
the crash instruction before trusting the new decoder's own output.

**Ruled out symbol misattribution first** (the discriminating check before
trusting the `+1696` offset at all): compared `heapWalker`'s vmaddr against
the next symbol (`countDisplayListChunks`) in the Mach-O symbol table — a
10012-byte gap, so `+1696` is genuinely inside `heapWalker`'s own compiled
code, not spilled into a neighboring function via missing symbol-size info.
Also notable on its own: `heapWalker` compiles to ~10 KB / ~2500 ARM64
instructions from ~800 bytes / ~175 MIPS instructions of guest code (a ~14x
expansion) — explains why naive percentage-position interpolation between
ARM64 offset and guest address would have been unreliable.

**Decoded the crash instruction**: `0xb82a6928` at `heapWalker+1696` is
`STR W8,[X9,X10]` (32-bit register-offset store), immediately preceded by
`LDR X8,[X8,#24]` (-28) and `LDR X10,[X10,#16]` (-16). The exact instruction
bytes repeat 3x within a 96-byte disassembly window — matching heapWalker's
known 5x-loop-unrolling signature from the guard1/3/4 work (s157-s218).

**Cross-checked against `recomp_context`'s layout** (`include/recomp.h`:
`gpr r0, r1, r2, r3, ...` with `gpr` = `uint64_t`, so field offsets are
r0=0, r1=8, r2=16, r3=24): offset #16 = `ctx->r2`, offset #24 = `ctx->r3`.
This means the two preceding loads are NOT a raw-pointer chase (the first
hypothesis from s368's writeup) but plain `ctx->r2`/`ctx->r3` struct reads —
X8/X10 transiently held the `ctx` pointer, clobbered by the load result.

**Source cross-check** (Explore-agent sweep of every `MEM_W(...) = ...;`
store in `heapWalker`'s 671-line body, `funcs_3.c:99-770`) found exactly one
match for "store the ctx->r3 value through ctx->r2 as the address, offset
+4": `MEM_W(0X4, ctx->r2) = ctx->r3;`, occurring once per unrolled loop at
guest `0x80007A3C/0x80007A98/0x80007AF4/0x80007B50/0x80007BAC`. `ctx->r2`
here is freshly loaded from a fixed global table slot two lines earlier
(`ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r2, 0X63B0)`) and checked only for `!= 0` (the
surrounding `if (ctx->r2 == 0) {...; goto skip;}` gate that decides whether
the SECOND write executes at all) — never range-validated before being
dereferenced as a write address. Exactly the same checked-non-NULL-but-
unvalidated-pointer idiom as guards 1/3/4, on a new register (ctx->r2, not
the ctx->r3 list-walk cursor guards 3/4 already cover). The sibling write on
the same two lines, `MEM_W(0X0, ctx->r3) = ctx->r2;`, does NOT need a new
guard — ctx->r3 there is the value guard4 just validated two statements
earlier and unmodified since.

## Session 371 (2026-08-05) — M5 Step 6: found and fixed a real host-bridge byte-count bug; PCM confirmed 100% silent (hypothesis 2 CONFIRMED) even under genuine RSP-dispatched real ucode

Before writing the planned `ROGUESQ_LOG_PCM_SANITY` counter, NEXT.md's own prerequisite ("confirm
the sample-vs-byte-count question before writing the iteration bound") required reading
`src/main/main.cpp:677-681` and `lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/audio.cpp:25-36` together.
That read found a real, previously-undetected bug, independent of any runtime measurement:
`ultramodern::queue_audio_buffer` computes `sample_count = byte_count / sizeof(int16_t)` and
passes that **sample count** into the `queue_samples` callback — but the callback's parameter was
named (and treated as) `num_bytes`, and the old code passed it straight through as
`SDL_QueueAudio`'s byte-length argument with no conversion. `SDL_QueueAudio`'s `len` parameter is
a byte count, not a sample count, so every single call queued only **half** the correct number of
bytes to SDL — the back half of every PCM buffer's bytes was silently dropped, unconditionally,
since the day this bridge was written, independent of whether the ucode upstream produces correct
content. `M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md` §4 Step 6 explicitly described this host bridge as "already fully
implemented and functional... confirmed by the runtime survey, not assumed" — **that claim is
overturned** (see `docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` superseded section). Fixed in the same edit: renamed the
parameter to `num_samples` and multiply by `sizeof(int16_t)` before calling `SDL_QueueAudio`.
Added `ROGUESQ_LOG_PCM_SANITY` (`[pcm-sanity]`) alongside it in the same function/build (batch
instrumentation rule — one build, one run for everything this step needs). `src/main/main.cpp`
only, no `lib/` touch, no regen pipeline needed (host-side C++, not recompiled guest code).

Ran two soaks with the new build (`ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE=1` + `ROGUESQ_LOG_PCM_SANITY=1`, HOLD_S=120,
`run_s327waitpump.sh` baseline, all standing guards armed):

- **verify1**: crashed pre-title (`title_reached` blank), `[pcm-sanity]` fired 7 times via the
  s327 emergency direct-`musyxSynthFrame`-pump path (`audtask_n=0` — real RSP `M_AUDTASK` dispatch
  never happened before the crash), all 7 calls `all_zero=1`. Crash signature
  `pc-symbol=musyxSynthFrame+4652`, `last-guest-pc=0x8000834c` — checked against the ledger before
  treating this as new: this is **byte-for-byte the same** pre-title crash already documented at

## Session 373 (2026-08-05) — M5 Step 6 "why is PCM silent" ANSWERED via pure source trace (iteration 2 of m5-audio-destub-step6-pcm-sanity): voice population is structurally blocked by the same gate the boot-hang fix requires

**Work unit**: NEXT.md's iteration-2 follow-on to s371's "PCM is 100% silent" finding — trace WHY,
per the plan's own "source-read-first" instruction (don't build a counter blind). Considered
disassembling `factor5_ucode_b_recompiled.c` (the RSP MusyX ucode itself, 2602 lines of raw
goto-based MIPS pseudocode with no symbol names) first, but that file only contains ~3 DMA
subroutine call sites near its top and is a single dispatched function with no obvious per-voice
loop structure visible without a multi-session disassembly effort (the kind `s193_disasm.py` took
for the heapWalker GUARD5 site) — before investing in that, checked whether the GAME side (which
decides what data the ucode is even handed) already answers the question, since M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md §1
documents ~15 existing env-gated audio instruments and a full s300 source-trace of the gate byte's
consumer.

**Finding, built entirely from source reads (no build, no soak)**:

1. s300 (already documented) established `tickMusyXIfActive` is the ONLY caller of
   `tickActiveSongs`/`tickAndReap3DAudioVoices` — the functions that actually add or advance voices
   — and it fully short-circuits via a single `beq $v0,$zero,...` at its top whenever the audio-engine
   gate byte at `0x800A0F50` reads 0.
2. This session read `reapplyDisplayMode` in full
   (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_23.c:9805-10024`, the recompiled game source, not the RSP ucode).
   Confirmed live in the current source: line 9838-9839 (`0x8008EB7C: sb $zero,0xF50($at)`)
   unconditionally zeros that exact gate byte at function ENTRY, every single call, with no
   conditional guarding it. s304 (already documented) established `reapplyDisplayMode` is called
   every video frame from `runVideoFrameTick` — so this zero-write happens ~60 times a second,
   unconditionally.
3. The function then branches on `reapplyAudioConfig`'s return value (line 9890): if nonzero, it
   skips straight to the tail and returns (rare/failure path); if zero (the common case), it falls
   through and runs a full song/voice/stream reset — `resetSongSubsystemCounter`,
   `initSongSequencerPools`, `resetMusyXEngineState`, `clearStreamedVoiceFlags`, `reset3DAudioLists`
   (lines 9905-10009, all unconditional once this branch is taken) — then would restore the gate
   byte to 1 at the tail (line 10020, `0x8008EC88: sb $v0,0xF50($at)`).
4. That exact tail address, `0x8008EC88`, is confirmed (read directly, `/Users/williambuckley/
   Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` line 269-272) to be the ONE site the current fixup
   regex still force-zeroes (`MEM_B(0XF50,ctx->r1) = 0` in place of `= ctx->r2`) — required to stay
   that way per s343's already-documented result (reversing it broke title-reach 0/5 times across 3
   sessions, s342).

**Net causal chain, fully mechanistic, no gaps**: every video frame, `reapplyDisplayMode` disables
audio, wipes any song/voice/stream state that accumulated since the last frame, and then — because
its own re-enable write is patched to a no-op — leaves the gate at 0 instead of restoring it. The
gate byte is therefore pinned at (or immediately reset to) 0 essentially continuously, so
`tickMusyXIfActive`'s voice-population path never gets a real window to execute. This isn't a second,
independent bug from s371's all-zero-PCM result — it's the SAME mechanism traced one level further
upstream: the RSP ucode was never handed any real voice data to mix in the first place, so producing
exact zeros is the mix step behaving correctly on empty input. **Hypothesis 1 (voice array never
populated) CONFIRMED. Hypotheses 2 (mixing internally gated off) and 3 (wrong buffer read) are now
moot** — there's nothing for either of those failure modes to act on; the data never arrives.

**Confidence note**: this is a static-source conclusion assembled from 3 separately-confirmed prior
facts (s300's gate-consumer trace, s304's call-frequency trace, s342/343's empirical C88-required
result) plus this session's own direct read of `reapplyDisplayMode`'s full body and the current
fixup regex — every claim above was re-verified against the live source this session, not taken
solely on the older sessions' word. It is not a fresh runtime measurement of "0 voices active during
the s371 soak" (no new instrument was armed or run) — that would be the natural confirming
measurement if a second, independent line of evidence is wanted before treating this as fully closed,
but the mechanism is structural (a `beq` gating a function that's the sole populator, fed by a byte
proven to be pinned at 0 by an unconditional per-frame write) rather than probabilistic, so a
runtime recount is unlikely to change the conclusion.

**Deliberately not chased this session**: WHY reversing the C88 site causes the pre-title hang was
never root-caused, even across the original 41-session s297-337 gate-reversal arc (PROJECT-OVERVIEW
§9) — that arc closed on an empirical revert-and-move-on, not a mechanism finding. Reopening it is a
large, separate investigation (the kind that consumed 41 sessions the first time), not a natural
Step 6 follow-on, and re-entering it blind would violate the standing budget discipline. This is
flagged as an explicit open decision for the next iteration rather than started here.

No code changes, no `lib/` touch, no build, no soak this session — pure source read across 2
repositories (`RogueSquadron64Recomp/docs/*`, `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_23.c`,
`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`). `HYPOTHESIS-ID` `m5-audio-destub-step6-pcm-sanity` is now CLOSED —
its question ("why is PCM silent") has a source-grounded answer. See NEXT.md for the follow-on
decision (reopen the C88-hang mechanism vs. pivot to M3 idiom-class audits per the strategic
priority order).

Explicit decision from s373's NEXT.md fork: took **Option A** (reopen the C88-hang mechanism), not
Option B (pivot to M3). Rationale: NEXT.md specified a bounded, source-read-only FIRST probe before
any build, with an explicit fallback to Option B "if [it] doesn't quickly narrow the field." It did
narrow the field — see below — so continuing on Option A is the correct call, not a default.
`HYPOTHESIS-ID: m5-audio-destub-c88-pretitle-hang`, iteration 1 of its budget.

**Method**: grepped every caller of `tickMusyXIfActive`/`tickActiveSongs`/`tickAndReap3DAudioVoices`
and of `waitForAnyAudioSlot` (the function CURRENT-TRUTH's M5 rationale already names as a recurring
crash family — "waitForAnyAudioSlot boot deaths") directly, then delegated the deep multi-file
call-chain trace to an Explore subagent scoped to 3 discriminating questions (own the same method
s304 used for the VI=320 hang, applied to the pre-title hang). Spot-checked the subagent's two
most load-bearing citations myself before trusting them (both confirmed, see below).

**Finding**: `waitForAnyAudioSlot` (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_15.c:7217`) is called from
`cinematicLoopBody`'s cutscene-teardown block (`funcs_27.c:108288`, confirmed independently — the
call sits right after a `static_6_800AF60C`/`static_6_800AF550` timer-threshold check, gate-byte-
independent, so this path fires deterministically once the intro cutscene's timer expires, squarely
inside the pre-title boot window). Its per-iteration body calls `tickMusyXIfActive`, and under
gate=1 (the reversed state under test) this reaches `factor5MutexAcquire` for the first time ever —
which blocks on `osRecvMesg_recomp` against a **single-token** (`osCreateMesgQueue_recomp(...,
count=1)`) message queue set up by `initFactor5Mutex` (`funcs_24.c:5703-5745`, confirmed
independently: `osCreateMesgQueue_recomp` at `0x80091FE4` with `count=1` at `0x80091FE8`, followed by
one `osSendMesg_recomp` at `0x80091FF4`). That exact same queue is **destroyed and recreated every
single video frame**, unconditionally, by `reapplyAudioConfig` calling `initFactor5Mutex` again
(`funcs_24.c:5070`, confirmed independently: `0x80091CAC jal 0x80091FC4` = `initFactor5Mutex`) —
and `reapplyAudioConfig` is itself called every frame from `reapplyDisplayMode`
(`funcs_23.c:9805`), which is called every frame from `runVideoFrameTick` (`funcs_0.c:1459/1780`,
already established s373). Under gate=0 (current baseline) this per-frame queue churn is completely
inert because `tickMusyXIfActive` never reaches `factor5MutexAcquire`. Under gate=1 it is live for
the first time in the project's history. The existing `waitForAnyAudioSlot` safety guard (s301,
`ROGUESQ_WAITFORSLOT_GUARD_CAP`, default 500000 loop iterations) is structurally unable to catch
this: it only increments/checks after a FULL loop-body iteration completes, and a single blocking
`osRecvMesg_recomp` call means the loop never completes even one more iteration to trip the counter.

**Why other subsystems keep ticking while this would hang (explains the s342 log signature)**: the
`[voice-active-gate-hb]`/`[voice-cursor-hb]` heartbeats that stayed live for the full 600s in the
s340bothgates/s342 logs live inside `musyxMixActiveVoices` (`funcs_24.c:2477`), which is on the
separate, gate-independent, VI-retrace-driven `musyxSynthFrame` path (already established
unconditional, `M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md` §1) — not on `waitForAnyAudioSlot`'s call chain. A deadlock
specific to whatever thread runs `cinematicLoopBody`→`waitForAnyAudioSlot` would not stop that
other path's heartbeats, matching the observed "VI stuck at 640, `pairs=0`, but audio/DMA counters
still incrementing" signature exactly.

**What this does NOT resolve** (same subagent's own honest caveat, and correct): whether
`runVideoFrameTick` and `cinematicLoopBody` execute on the same cooperative "thread" context (making
the queue-recreation race actually reachable — this determines if the mechanism is even physically
possible, not just plausible on paper), and how `osRecvMesg_recomp`/`osCreateMesgQueue_recomp` in the
ultramodern/librecomp OS-thread scheduler behave when a queue is recreated while a receiver may be
blocked on it. Neither is visible from the recompiled-C source alone — this is a genuine "source
pass narrowed the field, now needs build+soak" outcome, not a false dead end. Also unresolved: item
-227's original Q2 (what specifically drives the VI 640→1024 transition in the gate=0 baseline) —
no display-mode/VI-width-1024 write or intro-state-machine gate was found in the traced call chains;
this may not matter if the mutex-deadlock mechanism above is confirmed (a deadlocked thread would
prevent ANY downstream progression regardless of what the specific 640→1024 trigger is), but stays
open as a fallback explanation if the deadlock trace comes back negative.

`factor5MutexAcquire`/`factor5MutexRelease`/`initFactor5Mutex` (mirroring the existing

real VI-swap emitter, and even then the signal is inherently harder to attribute than a single write.

rather than spending a build cycle on H4. Rationale: the practical audio question this thread was
chasing is already answered independently — s373 root-caused that PCM stays 100% silent under the

that wouldn't dissolve the real audio-silence problem even if it worked is poor information value
per the effort-calibration principle. `HYPOTHESIS-ID m5-audio-vi640to1024-trigger-site` CLOSED

## Session 389 (2026-08-06) — M3 idiom-class audit: "Lookup" struct-family unguarded table-base-pointer dereference, 4 sites guarded (new `HYPOTHESIS-ID m3-idiom-audit-fresh`, iteration 1)

Read list at session start: `docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md`, `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` (per s388's plan: find a
live recurring candidate from the raw soak logs first, since `SOAK-RESULTS.md`'s own tail has been quiet
since s369), `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md` tail.

**Step 1 — candidate search.** Tallied `[CRASH][last-guest-pc]` across the last ~24 informative soak
runs in `scratch/agent/soak_results/*.log` (s355-s369, the M5 Step 5 guard-hunting arc's own verify
pairs). Two addresses recurred at n=2 independent of that arc's own targets: `0x8000b650` (already
long-catalogued as a STALE `beginFrameDLChunk` checkpoint value that resolves to a different, unrelated
host symbol almost every hit — confirmed noise, not a candidate) and `0x800ad0dc`
(`pc-symbol=findLookupEntryByKey+1864`, hit at s359 and again at s370, both times dismissed in-session as
"off-target" for whichever OTHER guard thread was being verified, never itself investigated).
`0x8000834c` (heapWalker+1696) recurred 6x, but all 6 hits pre-date s369's GUARD5 fix landing — consistent
with, not contradicting, that thread's closure. Picked `0x800ad0dc`/`findLookupEntryByKey` as this
session's candidate.

**Step 2 — investigation (delegated to a read-only Explore agent).** The premise was wrong twice over:
(1) the pc-symbol arithmetic itself doesn't check out (`0x800ad0dc - 0x748 = 0x800aC994`, not the
`0x800aC974` a naive reading might suggest), and (2) more importantly, `findLookupEntryByKey`'s real
guest range (from the generated source's own `// 0x...` address comments) is `0x800642A0-0x800643C0` —
`0x800ad0dc` isn't in it. The address actually falls inside `hangarInitialize`/`static_5_800AB658`
(`funcs_27.c`/`funcs_40.c`, two byte-identical copies of the same giant, already-heavily-patched
"whack-a-mole" function, real symbol `updateHangarBayScene`), at a fixed-global store instruction
(`MEM_W(-0x292C, ctx->r2) = ctx->r3` at a compiler-known address `0x800D0000-0x292C`) fed by a `ctx->r2`
that may be corrupted upstream elsewhere in that same function — not a hash-table dereference at all, and
not safely fixable in one session without much deeper root-causing of that function's own long patch
history. **The `findLookupEntryByKey+1864` pc-symbol label was simply a wrong nearest-symbol
attribution** — same failure mode as the long-catalogued `0x8000b650` staleness, just not previously
flagged for this specific address.

**Pivot, still inside the same idiom-audit unit**: the investigation also found that `findLookupEntryByKey`
itself, and three siblings in the same "Lookup" struct-family (`funcs_14.c`/`funcs_15.c`:
`removeLookupTableEntry`, `getLookupEntryField5`, `relocateLookupEntryToNewKey`), share the **exact same
unguarded idiom** already fixed for their sibling `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` back in s260
(`SETLOOKUP_TABLE_GUARD`): load a table-base pointer from offset 0 of the passed-in lookup-table struct
(`ctx->rX = MEM_W(ctx->rY, 0X0)`), then dereference `index*8 + base` with zero null/range check. This is a
clean, well-scoped, well-precedented idiom class — exactly the s282-288 audit model — so the work unit
became: enumerate the class, confirm each site's shape by direct source read, guard the unguarded ones
using the proven s260 template, prove the excluded site out of scope, verify.

**Enumeration/classification** (direct source read against `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_14.c`/`funcs_15.c`,
confirmed via `RECOMP_FUNC` boundaries):
- `findLookupEntryByKey` (`funcs_14.c:8231-8421`) — table-base read at `0x800642B0` into `ctx->r4`,
  dereferenced at `0x800642C4`. **Unguarded.**
- `removeLookupTableEntry` (`funcs_14.c:8422-8557`) — table-base read at `0x800643DC` into `ctx->r7`,
  dereferenced at `0x800643F0`. **Unguarded.**
- `getLookupEntryField5` (`funcs_15.c:7-69`) — table-base read at `0x80064668` into `ctx->r4` (overwrites
  the struct-arg register in place), dereferenced at `0x8006467C`. **Unguarded.**
- `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` (`funcs_15.c:70-145`) — table-base read at `0x800646BC`. **Already guarded**
  (s260, `SETLOOKUP_TABLE_GUARD`).
- `relocateLookupEntryToNewKey` (`funcs_15.c:146-...`) — table-base read at `0x8006472C` into `ctx->r3`,
  dereferenced at `0x80064738`; a 2nd, independent read of the same struct field at `0x80064774` further
  down, made unreachable once the first read's guard bails (the struct's offset-0 field is never written
  by any of these functions within a single call, so every reload in the same call yields the identical
  value — guarding the FIRST read and bailing early is sufficient coverage without needing a guard at
  every reload site). **Unguarded.**
- `destroyLookupTable` (`funcs_14.c:8857-8896`) — loads the table pointer but only passes it to `rs_free`;
  never dereferences it via the `index*8+base` idiom. **Confirmed out of class, correctly excluded.**

**Fix** (`fixup_game_funcs.py`, N64Recomp repo, untracked as always — see the standing note): 4 new guard
patches, reusing s260's exact KSEG0-range (`0x80000000..0x80800000`) + hi-word (`0xFFFFFFFF`) check.
Bail semantics matched each function's own existing control flow rather than a blanket pattern: plain
`return;` for the two void functions with no stack frame (`findLookupEntryByKey`,
`removeLookupTableEntry`); `ctx->r2 = 0; return;` for `getLookupEntryField5` (mirrors its own real
"not found" default path); `goto L_800647C4;` for `relocateLookupEntryToNewKey`, which — unlike the other
three — has a real stack frame (`sp -= 0x28`, saves `$s0-$s3`/`$ra` at entry), so a bare early `return`
would have left the guest stack unbalanced and corrupted the caller's next register-restore; its own
epilogue label was reused instead. Each guard gets its own env-gated diagnostic
(`ROGUESQ_LOG_{FIND,REMOVE,GET,RELOCATE}LOOKUP_TABLE_GUARD`), matching the project-wide convention. Armed
all 4 by default in `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_s327waitpump.sh` alongside the existing SETLOOKUP guards
(gitignored file, no commit needed).

**Verification.** Backed up the current (already-fixup-applied) `RecompiledFuncs/` tree, deleted just
`funcs_14.c`/`funcs_15.c`, regenerated them fresh from `N64Recomp` (unpatched), re-ran the updated
`fixup_game_funcs.py` against the full tree, and diffed both the fixup report and the full 45-file tree
against the pre-session baseline. Fixup report showed exactly the 4 new lines expected
(`findLookupEntryByKey table-base pointer guard (0x800642B0) patched x1`, etc.) alongside every
pre-existing patch unchanged; the full-tree diff touched exactly `funcs_14.c` and `funcs_15.c`, and within
those files the diff was exactly the 4 intended guard-block insertions, byte for byte, nothing else moved.
Build (`cmake --build . -j8`) clean, reached 100%, no new warnings from the added code. Ran 3 soaks
(`HOLD_S=240`, same recipe/env shape as every other verify batch): verify1 crashed at `hold-iter 11`
(~12s into the hold) at the already-catalogued `coalesceFreeHeapBlocks+4424` family (last-guest-pc
`0x8000247c`, unrelated to the lookup functions); verify2 died pre-title (`process gone while waiting for
phase`, exit code 4 — the known `waitForAnyAudioSlot`-class boot crash, last-guest-pc `0x8000834c`, also
unrelated and not even a scene-reached run); verify3 was fully clean — 304s wall hold, VI traversed the
full `0→320→640→1024→512→640` phase timeline (title → war room → craft-select → transition, 6097 LLE
tasks), 0 crash markers, process still alive at kill. None of the 3 runs crashed inside or downstream of
any of the 4 newly-guarded functions, and none produced a new, not-previously-catalogued crash signature —
both failures are pre-existing, independently-tracked crash families unrelated to this patch. All 4 new
guard fire-counts were 0 across all 3 runs (including the clean 304s run that reached craft-select, where
`activateAnimationKeyframe`'s existing calls into this same struct family run routinely) — a null result
for the guards firing, but not informative against the fix itself: this was always a proactive/defensive
closure of a known-dangerous idiom (proven dangerous once already, for the sibling function), not a
response to an actively-reproducing corruption in this family. No `lib/` touch this session.

Outcome: ADVANCED (a real code change landed: 4 new guard patches closing a well-scoped, precedented
unguarded-pointer-dereference idiom class across the "Lookup" struct-family, matching the M3
idiom-class-audit model; verified via the standard byte-identical-except-intended-diff regen protocol,
clean build, and 3 soaks with no regression). Also corrected a live misattribution: the recurring
`findLookupEntryByKey+1864`/`0x800ad0dc` pc-symbol reading that had been dismissed twice as "off-target"
noise is now understood to be a wrong nearest-symbol attribution for a site inside
`hangarInitialize`/`static_5_800AB658`, not a real hit on `findLookupEntryByKey` — worth remembering next
time that symbol name surfaces in a soak log. HYPOTHESIS-ID `m3-idiom-audit-fresh` stays open (this class
is closed, but the audit model itself continues as the standing strategic-priority-3 work mode) — next
session should pick a fresh idiom-class candidate the same way (Step 1 of this session's NEXT.md), since
the current soak_results population has now been fully mined for this cycle.

**HIGH-PRIORITY finding: s392's chunk 3a (all 29 sites) checks the WRONG register — a guard-placement bug,
not a new crash, but a silent correctness defect that has shipped undetected since s392.** Per NEXT.md's
"after chunk 3b lands" instruction, swept the whole function for remaining raw `-0X25A4` hits before
declaring the class closed. `awk` restricted to `MEM_W(ctx->r17, -0X25A4)` (the specific `$s1`-based
reload, matching this whole audit's actual scope) over the full function span still found 30 raw hits —
all landing inside chunk 3a's already-"guarded" 125940-132777 span, not new/missed sites. Traced one
(`S392_H3A_11`, guest 0x800ACCA0) by hand: the guard's own `reg` parameter (`r3`) is the SAME register the
raw `-0x25A4($s1)` load is about to write into, and the guard text is inserted via
`text.replace(anchor, guard_text + anchor, 1)` — i.e. BEFORE the anchor, not after. For chunks 1/2/3b
(s285/s390/s393) the anchor was deliberately built to START AFTER the raw load line, so the register being
checked already holds the freshly-reloaded pointer by the time the check runs. **Chunk 3a's anchors instead
start WITH the raw load's own comment+code line as anchor line 1** (confirmed by direct inspection of all
29 `_s392_h3a_sites` tuples in `fixup_game_funcs.py` — 29/29 have this shape, 0/29 match the correct
"anchor starts after the combine" pattern chunks 1/2/3b used). That means every chunk-3a guard checks
whatever was in that register from the *previous* instruction, not the value the load is about to produce.

Checked what that stale value actually is for two sites by reading their preceding source: `S392_H3A_11`'s
`r3` was just set by `MEM_BU(ctx->r16, -0X291C)` two lines earlier (a small byte index used in a hash/
multiply idiom, not a pointer); `S392_H3A_1`'s `r3` was set by a similar `lbu` byte load. A byte-range value
(0-255) always fails the `0x80000000..0x80800000` KSEG0 bounds check, so both sites' guards
**unconditionally take the bail branch every single time that code path executes** — not "protects against
a rare bad pointer," but "always skips this code now." This would silently disable real per-hangar-item
processing for however many of the 29 sites share this "stale value is a non-pointer" shape (not yet
counted — needs a per-site check, some stale values might coincidentally look like valid KSEG0 pointers and
pass through, which is arguably worse: a guard providing zero actual protection while looking green).

Why 3 soaks with "0 fires attributable" (s392's own verification) didn't catch this: `ROGUESQ_LOG_S392_H3A_GUARD`
was never armed by any soak recipe run so far (confirmed: `run_s327waitpump.sh` doesn't set it, matching
every prior chunk's precedent of not expecting fire-count lines) — an always-firing bug is invisible to a
soak whose only observable signal is "did a `[[s392-h3a-guard]]` line print," because that print is itself
gated behind the same unarmed env var. The soaks' actual observable ("byte-identical-except-intended-diff
regen, clean build, no NEW crash inside the guarded span") is not violated by this bug — an early `goto` to
the function's real epilogue doesn't crash, it just silently skips code, which produces no signal in any
instrument used so far. This is a `§4.1`-class instrument-that-lies trap (PROJECT-OVERVIEW), specifically
"a counter/log gated behind an env var that no soak recipe arms is not evidence of absence."

**Not fixed this session** — scope discipline: this is a distinct bug in PRIOR session's work, discovered
as a side effect of this session's closing sweep, not this session's planned work unit. Fixing it properly
needs the same anchor-reconstruction-and-reverify treatment as chunk 3b itself (rebuild all 29 anchors to
start after their raw loads, re-verify uniqueness, regen, build, soak) — a full work unit of its own.
Recorded as the new top-priority Next-steps item (ahead of any "chunk 4"/whole-codebase sweep, since this
is a correctness regression in already-shipped work, not new uncovered surface).

Outcome: ADVANCED (chunk 3b landed: 21 new guard sites, correctly placed, verified via the standard regen-
diff-build-soak protocol, 0 regressions attributable across 3 soaks — plus a real, previously-undetected
correctness bug found and documented in prior work, itself a result per the iteration contract's "a
documented dead end is a result" clause).

## Session 394 (2026-08-06) — FIX: s392's chunk-3a guard-placement bug, all 29 sites rebuilt with correct
anchors (`HYPOTHESIS-ID m3-idiom-audit-fresh`, iteration 6)

Top-priority item per s393's NEXT.md: item -243's guard-placement bug (all 29 `_s392_h3a_sites` in
`fixup_game_funcs.py` checked a STALE register because their anchor started WITH the raw `-0x25A4($sN)`
load, so `text.replace(anchor, guard_text + anchor, 1)` spliced the guard BEFORE that load ran).

**Fix mechanism.** Wrote a fresh Python script (no prior script reused, per the task's own anti-hand-
transcription discipline) that, for each of the 29 site tuples: (1) parsed the live `_s392_h3a_sites`
list out of `fixup_game_funcs.py` via `ast.literal_eval` rather than hand-copying; (2) located that
site's already-applied (buggy) guard block in the current `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_27.c` by its own
`s392, SITE_NAME` marker comment, found the raw `-0x25A4` load immediately following the guard's closing
brace, and verified the load's destination register matches the tuple's `reg` field (29/29 matched); (3)
scanned forward from the line after the raw load, collecting lines until either a genuine `MEM_*`
dereference appeared (27/29 sites) or an unconditional `goto` line was hit first (1 site, `S392_H3A_26`
— see below); (4) verified the new anchor is a unique substring (`text.count() == 1`) of the current
file. All 29 new anchors passed on the first pass, no failures, no hand-fixing needed.

**The one non-trivial site.** `S392_H3A_26`'s raw load (`0x800ADA50`, guest addr, `funcs_27.c`) is
immediately followed by an unconditional `j L_800ADB18` to a shared control-flow join with
`S392_H3A_25`'s own separate path (both feed the same downstream `ADD32`+`lw` dereference at
`L_800ADB18`, 0x800ADB18-0x800ADB1C) — no in-line combine/dereference exists to scan forward to before
control leaves this block. New anchor for this one site covers through the `goto L_800ADB18;` line
instead of a `MEM_*` line; this still correctly places the guard immediately after the raw load and
before the value is used (nothing clobbers the register between load and jump), matching the same
"guard right after the fresh load" placement discipline as every other site — a legitimate boundary case
of the same algorithm, not a special-cased exception to it.

values for all 29 sites confirmed unchanged, only anchor text changed, `_s392_h3a_guard_text` function

## Session 397 (2026-08-06) — S285_H1_8 cleanup landed; codebase-wide idiom-class discovery scan finds NO
comparable-magnitude next family (a well-evidenced negative result, per NEXT.md's own contingency)

**Step 1 (small cleanup, per s395/s396's carry-over).** Removed the leftover `S285_H1_8` guard tuple from
`_s285_h1_sites` in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (N64Recomp repo, untracked). It checked `ctx->r4` at a point
where r4 still held a stale value from `S285_H1_6`'s unrelated combine 65 lines earlier — never the fresh
value this site's own `-0x25A4` reload computes three lines later, so it never guarded the real
dereference (found s395), and could occasionally cause a *spurious* early bail out of `hangarInitialize`'s
chunk-1 loop if that stale value happened to look invalid. The real dereference at this exact address
(`0x800AA53C`) is already correctly guarded by `S395_SWEEP_1` (unchanged, anchored right after the real
combine). Deleted rather than relocated — relocating would just duplicate `S395_SWEEP_1`'s check on the
same address. Left a comment in place of the deleted tuple and updated the adjacent s395-era comment
block to point at it, so a future reader doesn't wonder where site 8 went.

**Verified via regen+build**: `make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`, all
clean (0 errors; only the pre-existing `funcs_8.c` `DDIV` sign-conversion warnings). The fixup report
confirms the intended isolated diff: exactly 25 `S285_H1_*` site-patch lines (was 26 before this change —
site 8 alone is missing) plus `S395_SWEEP_1` unchanged, no `SKIPPED` lines anywhere in the report.

**Soak verification: inconclusive, but for reasons unrelated to the change; not a regression.** Three
attempts, none obtained a same-run positive control (iron rule 1) reaching the hangar scene, so none of
them "clean-verifies" the fix by the project's own standard — reported honestly as inconclusive rather than
claimed clean:
- **verify1** (`run_s397_h1_8removal_verify1.sh`, unmodified `run_s327waitpump.sh` default env,

**Why this is still a safe, verified change despite the inconclusive soaks**: (1) the diff is a pure
deletion of one self-contained guard block, confirmed isolated by the fixup report and regen; deleting a
guard can only WIDEN the code paths that execute, never narrow them, so it cannot introduce a new crash
mode by itself. (2) The only dereference at this address is protected by `S395_SWEEP_1`, which is completely
untouched by this change and was already independently soak-verified by s395 with a full positive control
(574 `[hangar-loop]` lines, 0 crashes, 0 fires). Two-source reasoning (construction + s395's prior
verification of the surviving guard), not a fresh same-run positive control — labelled accordingly, not
claimed as a clean soak.

**Step 2 (the actual work unit): codebase-wide scan for the next `-0x25A4`-scale idiom class.** Per
NEXT.md, ran `grep -ohE 'MEM_[WBH][U]?\(ctx->[a-z0-9]+, -0X[0-9A-F]+\)' *.c` across
`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/*.c` (8337 raw negative-displacement loads) and ranked by frequency. The naive
frequency ranking is dominated by false positives: the top two candidates after `-0x25A4` itself
(`-0x5824`, 168 hits; `-0x23A8`, 141 hits) are **100% the mundane MIPS `lui`+`lw` static-global-address
idiom** (`lui $vN, 0x8012; lw $vN, -0x5824($vN)` = a fixed compile-time RDRAM address, never a
runtime-dependent pointer at all) — confirmed by direct source read of every occurrence context, not
inferred. Built a Python classifier (`scratch_classify_displ.py`/`_2`/`_3` in `~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp`,
not part of the git-tracked repo) that traces each load's base register backward through simple
copy/arithmetic chains to determine whether its ultimate origin is a `lui` constant (safe, static-global)
or itself a load from a fixed global slot (the actual `-0x25A4` shape: a POINTER stored at a global address,
reloaded and then dereferenced — the thing that can legitimately be null/stale). Two rounds of bugfixing
the classifier (it initially mis-attributed lines separated by an intervening `lui` reassignment, and
separately couldn't see through 2-hop `lui`-then-copy chains like `-0x76E0`/`-0xF88`, both of which turned
out on manual inspection to also be 100% static-global address arithmetic once traced correctly) converged
on a **zero-candidate result**: after the fixes, NO displacement value anywhere in the codebase shows even
one confirmed case of "base register was itself loaded from a fixed global slot, then dereferenced at a
further negative offset" — including, tellingly, the classifier's straight-line backward tracer couldn't
even reprove the KNOWN `-0x25A4` family this way (it aborts on label/branch crossings, and `-0x25A4`'s own
base register is set once early in `hangarInitialize` and reused across many labels far downstream), so this
is a real limitation of the static heuristic, not proof that `-0x25A4` was unique — but it does mean no
NEW comparable-magnitude candidate surfaced despite two independently-refined passes.

Also checked the `[mesgqueue-guard]` lead flagged unactioned by s395/s396: it's a single guard site in the
shared C++ runtime (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/mesgqueue.cpp:41`, a `mesgqueue_guard_refuse()`
range-check already installed against `mq_` pointers), not a `RecompiledFuncs` codegen idiom at all — out
of scope for the M3 systematic-idiom-audit model (there's exactly one guard site, not a class), and its
"tight retry loop" symptom is a caller-side retry-without-backoff bug in a different subsystem entirely.
Confirmed NOT a viable M3 candidate; still logged as a legitimate low-severity bug for whoever picks it up.

**Net**: Step 1 is a real, verified (by construction + regen/build/fixup-report + s395's prior guard
verification), if not soak-clean-confirmed, code change — ADVANCING. Step 2 is a legitimate discriminating
negative result matching NEXT.md's own contingency clause ("if the scan turns up nothing with meaningfully
high frequency... consider whether the M3 idiom-class-audit model has run its course for THIS project"):
two independently-refined static scans, converging on the same answer, found no next `-0x25A4`-scale
family. This doesn't prove none exists (the classifier has real, acknowledged blind spots around
control-flow crossings) but it does mean grep-frequency discovery — the method NEXT.md prescribed — is
exhausted for now; a genuinely different tool (whole-function/CFG-aware dataflow) or a return to
crash-driven discovery would be needed to find more, and the user directive requires human reconfirmation
before M3 leaves the pure-idiom-audit model. Recommending the human weigh in on M3 (needs a new discovery

reads files in a fixed order (`main_overlay.txt` first) and dedupes by name with first-file-wins
(`if name not in syms: syms[name] = ...`) — so `mission_overlay.txt`'s copies were always shadowed,
dead on arrival. Worse, `main_overlay.txt`'s entries carry `src_file=main_overlay.txt`, and
`vram_to_shndx` routes that source through the **`.text`-range check** (`0x80000440`-`0x800A5130`),
not the mission-overlay range (`0x800A5130`-`0x8010B6D0`) — all 3 addresses are `>= 0x800A5130`, so
they fail that check and get silently dropped as "phantom functions" (`make_elf.py`'s own
`skipped_funcs` counter). **Confirmed with `strings build/roguesquadron.elf`: none of the 3 names
were present in the ELF at all**, and a repo-wide grep of all of N64Recomp (RecompiledFuncs and
everything else) found the names literally nowhere — s54's "build verified" claim only proved the
regen pipeline ran without error, not that these addresses became real code; the sanity check
(`strings`/grep on the actual output) was never done at s54.

dead weight: already being silently dropped, contributing nothing) so `mission_overlay.txt`'s
correctly-scoped copies resolve unshadowed. Ran the full regen pipeline in the mandated order,

   `[Info]` tail-call/indirect-call noise. `grep -rl` for the 3 names now hits `funcs_29.c`/`funcs_32.c`.

   unrelated existing guards), 0 errors/tracebacks.
