### New lead for -421 (rdpFs plateau), found in already-captured data — no new run needed

While hand-verifying the confirming run, noticed the existing
`[dl-sync-probe]` instrument (already firing every task under the freeroll's
standard `ROGUESQ_LOG_DL_SYNC=1`, no new instrumentation needed) had never
been tallied in aggregate before — only spot-read per-task. Scoped to
lines `>= sec2_ln=347715` (post-sec2 mission phase only) in the same
`pulse_2_20260811200701/run.log`:

- 29780 `[dl-sync-probe]` lines post-sec2. `e9_a`/`e9_b` (proper
  control-flow-respecting tree walks, one treating opcode 0xB5 as
  end-of-DL, one not) are BOTH zero in 18452/29780 (~62%), but **11328/29780
  (~38%) show e9_a>0 or e9_b>0** — i.e. a large fraction of post-sec2
  mission tasks DO contain the SYNC_FULL byte value in their raw command
  walk.
- Cross-referenced against the same window's `[runner] task ... syncs=`
  field (the runner's own translated/dispatched RDP command count, the
  actual signal `rdpFs`/item -421's plateau is measured from): **29777/29780
  post-sec2 tasks report `syncs=0`; only 3 show `syncs=1`.**

Read together: a large fraction of post-sec2 mission DLs contain what the
naive fixed-8-byte-stride walker sees as an E9 opcode, yet the runner's own
translated-command counter almost never registers a real sync. Two
competing explanations, NOT yet distinguished:
- **H-e9-not-translated:** the guest DL genuinely contains SYNC_FULL
  requests that our RDP command translator/dispatcher drops or fails to
  execute for this task class — would directly explain the -421 plateau as
  a translation-path bug, not a content-absence issue.
- **H-e9-walker-misaligned:** `walk_tree`'s fixed 8-byte stride (used for
  `e9_a`/`e9_b`) does not account for the F5 ucode's variable-length
  inline-data commands (MoveMem/TriGen/Tri/TexrectGen/SetOtherMode_*_EX —
  see `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md`), unlike the existing
  `ROGUESQ_LOG_DL_SYNC2` six-command-aware walker (built for the
  cimg-origin-desync investigation, `-415..-417`). An unaligned walk can
  land mid-command and read a coincidental 0xE9 byte that isn't a real
  opcode boundary — the 38% hit rate could be entirely this artifact.

Not adjudicated this session (out of scope for the assigned -422 work
unit; flagging per iron rule 5 "check the boring thing first" — an
instrumentation alignment bug is the boring explanation and must be ruled
out before H-e9-not-translated enters CURRENT-TRUTH). Full next-step design
in `scratch/agent/NEXT.md`.

### Rules out / confirms

- H-menu-return-input CONFIRMED (was SUPPORTED single-source in s670).
- Old `wrapper.stdout` leftover data reconfirmed as already-closed s670
  material — not a missed/interrupted iteration.

### Residual → -421 gets a concrete next-step candidate (E9-alignment check on the existing dl-sync-probe2 walker); -422 fully CLOSED, no further residual.

## Session 674 (2026-08-12) — HARNESS: codex runner made viable; two loop bugs fixed

Not an experiment iteration. Toolchain work on `tools/agent/`, prompted by the
first `RUNNER=codex` runs (s673 and the 00:21 restart).

**s673's "no SDL display" was the codex SANDBOX, not the terminal context.**
`codex exec` defaulted to `-s workspace-write`, which is a seatbelt sandbox.
Measured directly in a throwaway `/tmp` git repo (codex-cli 0.144.3), inside
that sandbox vs an ordinary shell:

| probe | `-s workspace-write` | unsandboxed / `danger-full-access` |
|---|---|---|
| `test -w .git` | `GIT_READONLY` | `GIT_WRITABLE` |
| `nice -n 5 true` | `setpriority: Operation not permitted` | `nice_rc=0` |
| `launchctl managername` | `Aqua` | `Aqua` |

So the session type was never the problem — the seatbelt was. Three
consequences, the middle one previously misdiagnosed:

1. The game gets no display ("The video driver did not add any displays",
   `hsel=0`, clean exit in 3-4s) because the work is GUI-driven and that is
   exactly what the sandbox blocks. Still to be confirmed at full access.
2. **CORRECTION to s673's checkpoint.** It concluded the read-only `.git` was
   "specific to that one sandbox invocation, not a durable property". It is
   deterministic: EVERY codex iteration under workspace-write gets a read-only
   `.git`, so no codex iteration can ever meet an exit contract that ends in a
   commit. s673's commit landed because `loop.sh` routes contract RETRIES to
   the claude runner, which is unsandboxed — the retry, not a changed sandbox,
   is what "found `.git` writable". Attribution error of the familiar kind: two
   observations from two different processes read as one process changing.
3. `nice(5) denied`, which s673 reported without attribution, is the same cause.

Fix: `runner.sh` codex sandbox default raised to `danger-full-access`, with the
measurements inline so it is not quietly lowered again. `RUNNER_SANDBOX` still
overrides per run.

**Loop bug: a run could die on a BLOCKED.md that says it is not blocked.**
`loop.sh` halted on the mere EXISTENCE of `scratch/agent/BLOCKED.md`. s673 ended
`STATUS=DONE` / `OUTCOME=ADVANCED` but left behind a BLOCKED.md whose first line
read `# Not currently blocked`, so the 00:21 codex run exited before preflight,
before spending anything, on a healthy repo. Fixed on both sides: an iteration
ending DONE has its leftover BLOCKED.md archived, and the loop top only treats
the file as stale when STATUS=DONE *and* its first line says "not blocked" — a
real block (STATUS=BLOCKED) and a preflight block ("# Blocked by preflight")
are both still honoured.

**Known blind spot, not yet fixed:** `preflight.sh` runs in loop.sh's own shell
and then hands the work to a runner that may be sandboxed, so for codex it
certifies an environment the agent never gets. It printed `[preflight] OK` at
00:05:16 immediately before an agent that could not open a window. Its very
first check (`launchctl managername` = Aqua) passes inside the sandbox too, so
it cannot catch this class by itself — the fix is to run it inside the runner.

### Rules out / confirms
- Confirms the codex workspace-write sandbox blocks `.git` writes and
  `setpriority`, deterministically, in a repo unrelated to this one.
- Refutes s673's "one-off sandbox invocation" reading of the read-only `.git`.
- Does NOT yet confirm the game gets a display under `danger-full-access`; the
  00:21 run that would have shown it never started. Refutation test:
  `RUNNER=codex ITER_CAP=1 caffeinate -dis tools/agent/loop.sh` from a GUI
  session, then check whether the SDL display error recurs.

search found no generated store targeting `0x80037574`. The static field is

semantic role or explain the later VI phase. No build, run, code change, or
mitigation was made.

## Session 835 (2026-08-13) — source audit identifies command-boundary E9 overcount

Performed the prescribed bounded parser-side source audit; no build, run, or
runtime behavior changed. `MEM_B` uses the host index `logical_address ^ 3`,
so the bridge's `g_rdram_for_submit[p ^ 3]` test and RT64's
`DisplayList::w0 >> 24` load select the same logical first byte. H-byte-order
is refuted.

The bridge counter scans every 8-byte slot from `lo` through `hi`, whereas the
RT64 direct parser advances by `cmdLength * sizeof(DisplayList)`. Therefore an
E9 at an interior word of a multiword command is counted by the bridge but is
not a parser command fetch. Pending completion has a separate gate requiring
completed bytes, raw pending opcode E9, the authoritative callback, and a
non-sentinel `s_rs64_pending_start_address`; that sentinel is set only when a
raw E9 command crosses a range boundary. This explains a lower parser count
without byte-order loss, while leaving pending-only effects to a paired probe.

This source result is single-source evidence. It identifies command-boundary
filtering as the leading explanation for s833's late rows (570=9/1, 580=9/1,
632=27/0, 649=31/3), but does not promote it to settled truth until a
phase-gated probe records bridge slots and parser command starts by address.
No mitigation or legitimacy claim was made.

ORIGIN: no game value, RDP command, mitigation, or runtime behavior changed;
this iteration changed only audit prose and scratch control files.

## Session 852 (2026-08-13) — source audit accounts for span matches; residual remains outside normal condition paths

Performed the prescribed bounded source-only audit; no build or run was
performed. The bridge's accepted ordinary ranges are scanned in 8-byte steps
and read the logical first byte through the same byte-swapped RDRAM mapping
used to reconstruct words. Each accepted range is recorded, serialised, and
passed synchronously to `submit_rdp_range`; RT64 derives its parser call range
from the same `[lo, hi)` pointers.

The authoritative parser loads the command opcode at each current boundary,
uses `commandWordLengths[opCode]`, reports a `direct` condition only when the
raw opcode is E9, reports a `span` condition for every normal non-E9 command,
and advances by `cmdLength * 8`. Thus an E9 byte at an interior 8-byte slot is
intentionally bridge-counted but is inline data in the preceding parser
command. The pending path records a split command only when a command crosses
the current `[lo, hi)` end and reports it on completion; the captured zero
pending rows are consistent with that gate. Deferred ranges receive normal
submit identity at commit. The non-deferred synthetic FULL_SYNC path is the
only submit path that bypasses `rs64_dpc_record_submit` and can carry a stale
serial/range label, but it submits only `[addr, addr+8)`.

This source table selects H-span-intended for the 1,001 span rows and rules out
a normal byte-order or producer/consumer range mismatch. It does not classify
the one residual condition-join slot: the normal direct/span paths are
complete, while the extended-opcode branch bypasses both condition callbacks
and uses its own function-controlled advancement. The residual therefore
needs one behavior-neutral runtime marker at that branch before choosing
between H-extended-residual and the bounded synthetic-label edge. No writer,
operand-legitimacy, parser-behavior, or mitigation conclusion follows.

ORIGIN: source audit only; no game value, RDP command, parser advancement, or
mitigation behavior changed.

## Session 856 (2026-08-13) — dispatcher input/state audit

Completed the prescribed source-only audit of `slotDispatcherIter` and
`slotDispatcherInner` in `../N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_8.c`, including
all 144 generated `jal 0x8003E8DC` callsites and five
`slotDispatcherInner` callsites. The dispatcher masks its selector to 16
bits, treats only `0xFFFF` as terminal, and indexes `0x80130BB0` with
`index*8` for both the initial and chained indices. There is no table-capacity
or chain-cycle check. A non-null table entry is trusted for `+0`, `+0x14`, and
`+0x1A`; `+0` is called indirectly as the NPC update function, and `+4/+6`
become the next selector. The inner dispatcher has no null check on its

## Session 879 (2026-08-13) — oracle debugger ABI cannot sample deferred values

Performed the prescribed source/API audit against `tools/oracle/rs64_oracle.c`,
the oracle README, and the local mupen64plus core's debugger headers and
implementation. The public breakpoint path provides a callback with guest PC,
then `DebugBreakpointTriggeredBy` returns only flags and accessed address.
`DebugMemRead32` exists, but `check_breakpoints_on_mem_access()` invokes the
callback before `mem_write32()`, so reading the watched address in the callback
observes the pre-write value. A later read from the frontend polling thread
can observe current memory but cannot retain the triggering writer address/PC
and is vulnerable to intervening writes. This selects
H-no-safe-value-api and rules out the deferred-sampler and phase-stall arms;
the coalescer legitimacy question must pivot to another independent
ground-truth source. No source, game, or mitigation behavior was changed.

ORIGIN: source/API audit of the independent oracle and its local core; no
runtime, guest value, control flow, or mitigation behavior changed.

initialized in the debugger module. The static target in the corrected dylib
is directly aligned and was already independently shown to receive all four
arguments.

### Substituted unit: static writer audit of the `runInMissionFrame` callback table

s954 left one unresolved edge in the closed-out M3 `slotDispatcherIter` class

contents or writers. This session closed that specific edge without any
runtime instrument.

`funcs_42.c:6798` (`runInMissionFrame`) computes the table base as a literal
`lui $s7,0x8011` / `addiu $s0,$s0,-0x4CB0` pair (`0x80110000-0x4CB0 =
0x8010B350`), then scans 8-byte entries (`byte0` = a bit index tested against
a flags word at `-0x3620($s7)`, `+4` = function pointer) until `byte0`
matches a sentinel, dispatching via `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r2)`. Every reference to
this table in the function is a load (`lbu`/`lw`); the only store nearby
targets the unrelated flags word at `-0x3620($s7)`, clearing a bit after
dispatch — not the table itself.

Two independent lines of evidence:
1. **Segment classification.** `rogue_squadron64/roguesquadron.yaml` marks
   `bss` starting only at `0x8010B6D0`; everything from `0x8010B350` through
   the named symbols after it (`playerCraftHobObjectNames@0x8010B3A0`,
   `playerCraftUpdateFunctions@0x8010B3C4`, …) is `data` — i.e. ROM-initialized,
   not zero-filled-then-populated. `syms/rogue_squadron.datasyms.toml` brackets
   the table cleanly: `D_8010B304` before, `playerCraftHobObjectNames` at
   `0x8010B3A0` after, giving the table an exact `0x50`-byte (10-entry) span
   with no named symbol landing inside it.
2. **Exhaustive writer search.** `grep -rn "0X4CB0\|0x4CB0\|0x4cb0"` across all
   of `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/*.c` (the full generated codebase) returns
   exactly 5 lines: 2 reads inside `runInMissionFrame` itself (`funcs_42.c`,
   both against the `0x8011`-based table pointer), 1 unrelated `$zero`-based
   byte load at fixed low address `0x4CB0` (`funcs_8.c`), and 1 unrelated
   `lwc1 -0x4CB0($at)` in `funcs_13.c` where `$at = 0x8004<<16` — a completely
   different address (`0x8003B350`), confirmed by reading its immediately
   preceding `lui`. Zero stores anywhere target `0x8010B350`.

This selects **static-compiled-data** over any runtime-writer hypothesis for
this specific table: it is ROM-baked dispatch data with no generated-code
writer, so it cannot be the shared-context corruption vector for the
`slotDispatcherIter+872` class. This closes `runInMissionFrame`'s indirect
edge from s954's backlog #1; it does NOT close

`slotDispatcherIter` entry that dumps sp/ra/a0/a1/s0-s7/fp/gp when the guest

## Session 1010 (2026-08-14) — mapped Factor 5 shade semantics

Ran the planned static M4 audit only; no build or game run. Compared the
independent GLideN64 `F5Rogue.cpp` TriGen implementation with the retail ROM
instruction path and generated `factor5_ucode_ovl1c_recompiled.c`, then checked
RT64's triangle shade decoder. GLideN64 loads the TriGen colour array and
copies its four bytes into vertex RGBA before triangle submission. The retail
and generated emitter instead stores `v6` at record `+0x18` at `L_1740`; `v6`
comes from the transformed-vector path at `L_162C`/`L_16B8`, with no color
table read. Both `L_16B8` branch arms reach the same shade store. RT64 decodes
the later RDP shade coefficient block after the eight position words, so the
consumer offset is consistent. This selects `H-missing-lighting-source` over
an intentional no-lighting sentinel and over a record-consumer mismatch.

This rules out generation loss for the color read, a downstream RT64 offset
error, and the claim that the sentinel is explicitly selected by a no-lighting
fallback. It does not identify whether `v6` itself is a legitimate lighting
vector or a clip/test vector; that is the next static discriminator. No
mitigation was added.

## Session 1011 (2026-08-14) — audited Factor 5 `v6` producer

Ran the prescribed static M4 work unit without building or running. At the
generated `L_16B8` entry, `r3` is `DMEM[0x134] & 1`. The initial `vge`/`vmrg`
result in `v6` is consumed by the intermediate `v5`/`v4` arithmetic, then

`vge v6,v6,v29[1q]` and fall through to the `L_1740` shade stores; the

lighting-source load.

The two `ldv` operations source `v29` from DMEM `0x60`. The captured
ucode-data image decodes that vector as signed halfwords
`0577 638F 1756 FF96 04D1 62CB 18CB FF8A`, consistent with a varying table,
not RGBA or a fixed lighting constant. This selects the narrow
`H-v6-clip-predicate` description for the final compare, refutes
`H-v6-mode-misread` and `H-v6-lighting-result`, and leaves the numeric
`-0.5/+0.5` sentinel origin open. The full evidence is in
`docs/M4-V6-PRODUCER-AUDIT.md`; no mitigation or generated-file edit was made.

This rules out a mode-arm divergence and a lighting/color source at this
stage. It does not yet explain the compare-result encoding or the fixed
sentinel value; that is the next discriminator.

## Session 1012 (2026-08-14) — classified Factor 5 VGE sentinel semantics

Ran the prescribed static M4 work unit without building or running. The
independent SGI RSP Programmer's Guide describes VGE as a signed
greater-or-equal operand select, and the local `VGE` implementation independently
matches that behavior: each lane selects `vs` or the selected `vt` lane, with
the VCO tie rule. The final `VGE<3>(v6,v6,v29)` therefore cannot synthesize the
observed fixed `0x8000` RGB/alpha sentinel. Its `v29` operand is the DMEM-0x60
table vector, while `v6` was already produced by `vmadh v6,v4,v0`; `v4` and
`v0` are arithmetic inputs, not a fixed compare-result source. This refutes
`H-vge-sentinel-encoding`, the fixed-operand form of `H-v4-v0-source`, and
`H-shade-store-interpretation`, and moves the next discriminator to the RSP
accumulator high-half/saturation path before VGE. No mitigation or generated
file edit was made.

results separately: it crashed at `slotDispatcherIter+8592` before producing
the guard record, so the original `+872` caller remains unclassified.

## Session 1230 (2026-08-14) — audited retail EEPROM selection and contents

Ran the read-only save-media audit without building or running. The configured
Mupen64Plus save directory contains one file,
`Star Wars - Rogue Squadron (U) (-47CAC4E2.eep`, exactly 512 bytes. It has
164 nonzero bytes, zero `0xff` bytes, and structured save data, so it is not a
formatted blank EEPROM. The `47CAC4E2` suffix matches the ROM's database MD5
key prefix. The installed database entry for `Star Wars - Rogue Squadron (U)
(M3) (V1.0) [!]` has `RefMD5=47CAC4E2A6309458342F21A9018FFBF0` and
`SaveType=Eeprom 4KB`.

The Mupen64Plus 2.6.0 source confirms ROM-open first checks the legacy
`<ROM_SETTINGS.goodname>.eep` path and only then falls back to the MD5-named
path. It opens EEPROM storage at 0x800 bytes, uses the existing file when
present, and truncates non-16K EEPROM to 0x200 bytes. H1 is selected for
nonblank, selected persistent state. This rules out missing/blank EEPROM and
wrong save-type/path as explanations for the current retail entry failure, but
does not show that the saved values cause the missing transition. The next
discriminator is a phase-gated existing-file versus temporary blank-EEPROM

## Session 1235 (2026-08-14) — censused retail reset-context GPR consumers

Ran the bounded generated/retail register-use census without building or
running. Retail's PIF IPL3 writes `s3..s7` (`r19..r23`), `t3` (`r11`), `sp`,
and `ra` before game entry. On the generated bootstrap path, `thread3_video_handle`
loads its `s3..s5` values from the video descriptor before using them, and
`mainGameLoop` saves all `s3..s7` immediately, then overwrites `s4/s5/s3/s7`
before game-visible reads and writes `s6` before its first use. `t3` has no use
in the entry, main, video-thread, bootstrap-worker, or main-game-loop paths.
`run_thread_function` zero-initializes each context and supplies its stack;
`recomp_entrypoint` sets `$sp` before calling `main`. `ra` and `sp` therefore
remain different only as return/stack bookkeeping, while the PIF/IPL3 GPR
values are dead or overwritten before game-visible use.

does not explain the stable VI-320 divergence. It rules out a pre-overwrite
consumer of the retail-only GPR context, but leaves CP0/reset-context state as
the next boundary.

hangar: `hold` sent no post-gate input, while `a`, `b`, and `z` sent the
candidate at 70/78/86/94. The recipe and logs are under
`scratch/agent/s1585_oracle_model_viewer_input/`.

interval), and H4 (a tested button changes to another menu phase but not a
mission). The discriminator was phase-gated VI lifecycle plus post-gate
mission/menu/case-6 execution watches, cross-checked by the target block and
PIF traces.

PC counts, exactly one case-6 `runModelViewerLoop` hit, and the same
`0x130B10:0x130B58` total with no candidate-specific post-gate write. The
only target write after the gate was the common `0x130B50` leave-hangar
write at the transition boundary.

This selects H3 for A/B/Z and rules out H1, H2, and H4 for those arms. The

## Session 1602 (2026-08-16) — revisited the M4 accumulator boundary

The last 15 ledger titles were all generated-symbol sweep sessions, so the
mandatory revisit selected the parked M4 accumulator boundary. Before the
run, the oracle README and Factor 5 reference were read. Two recipe mistakes
were documented and killed with SIGKILL: a 1024 phase gate with all keys
phase-relative deadlocked at 640, and the same reachability recipe without
the known LLE-solo flags also stayed at 640 despite four verified Start
edges. Neither arm was used as evidence.

The corrected LLE-solo port arm used the existing regeneration-safe M4 probe,
with a phase-6 target gate, an eight-row independent arithmetic control cap,
and a 16-row target cap. The control fired eight times. Four complete target
rows each produced stages 10/11/12/13, carrying pre-VMADH
`ACCH:ACCM:ACCL`, `v4`, `v0`, post-VMADH `v6`, post-VGE `v6`, and stored bytes.
The exact `rsp_vu_impl.hpp` VMADH/accumulator model matched all 32 target
lanes; post-VGE values were unchanged. The live shade-DMA control identified
the real port destination as runtime `0x4B7800..0x4B7808`; the probe's
`r9=0x670/0x6C0` values are DMEM and were not treated as RDRAM.

The paired retail oracle used Rice, the eleven-Start schedule, whole-RDRAM
watching, and VI polling/tracing. Whole-RDRAM reached its 10,000-callback
positive control and the independent VI trace reached 320→640→1024→512 at
the hangar origin `0x006ab800`; the targeted `0x4B7800..0x4B7808` watch had
zero writes. That target null is single-source and unevaluable as a retail
ownership result because the port destination is runtime-allocated and the
port/oracle scene origins differ. The run rules out a local VMADH arithmetic
or VGE-change defect for the captured path, but does not identify the source
state or later DMA/consumer divergence. No mitigation was added. The next
work unit resumes the symbol sweep at `func_800BE4A8`. The local
VMADH/VGE closure is single-source runtime consistency evidence, not an
independent retail arithmetic proof.

## Session 1616 (2026-08-16) — tested pre-exit hangar input routes at retail

The mandatory 15-title check found only sweep sessions plus the s1602 M4
revisit, so this iteration performed a new external retail-entry revisit
instead of another generated-symbol census. Static inspection of the

tested A/B/Z only after the 512 hangar had already become the 640 model-viewer
phase; it did not test B while the hangar selector was active.

The competing hypotheses were H1: pre-exit B selects a distinct route that
could lead toward mission entry; H2: B is recognized but leaves the known
hangar/model-viewer route unchanged; H3: directional navigation changes the
route; and H4: the recipe or candidate input is unevaluable. The one
discriminator was the phase-gated post-hangar VI lifecycle plus PC watches for
`runHangarSelectionFrame` (`0x800AAD9C`), `runHangarMenuFromOverlay`
(`0x800C6854`), `runModelViewerLoop` (`0x800C9BF0`), mission entry
(`0x80000B70`), overlay loads, and writes to `0x130B10:0x130B58` and
`0x13B40:0x13B48`.

The four concurrent Rice arms used the same eleven Start presses and were:
the known A exit control (`58:a,63:a`), pre-exit B (`55:b,58:b,63:b`), and
Up/Down navigation followed by the A exit (`55/57:up|down,58:a,63:a`). Every
arm passed the whole-RDRAM positive control (10,137–10,150 writes) and the
320→640→1024→512 hangar lifecycle. A was delivered as `sym=225` with pad
word `0x800000`; B was delivered as `sym=224` with pad word `0x400000` and
the hangar-frame PC fired 696 times in the B arm. The Up/Down arms logged
`sym=0`, so they were invalid input arms and cannot select H3.

H1 selected for the valid B arm: it stayed at 512 until 65.4s, then changed
to 1024 at origin `0x00790400` and to 640 at `0x00696100`, with zero
`runModelViewerLoop` hits and zero mission-entry `0x80000B70` hits. The A
control reached 640 at `0x006A2E00` and had one model-viewer hit; both valid
arms had zero mission-entry hits. B therefore proves a distinct retail menu
route but not mission entry. The selector watch was zero in all arms, and the
target block showed the common 137 writes in A/Up/Down versus 150 in B; no
mitigation or recomp change was made.

This rules out the claim that every valid hangar exit follows case-6 model
viewer and rules out B as a mission-entry input in the observed 110-second
window. It does not identify the B-selected 640 route or answer which input
leaves case 6 into a mission. The directional question remains open because
the names were not mapped to valid SDL symbols in these fresh config dirs;
do not treat their nulls as evidence.

## Session 1650 (2026-08-16) — tested post-B A/Start/Z against retail mission entry

The mandatory 15-title check found only sweep sessions, so this iteration
revisited the external retail-entry boundary instead of another
generated-symbol census. Prior work had classified pre-exit B as a distinct
valid hangar route (`512→1024→640` at `0x00696100`, not case-6 model viewer)
and had classified post-viewer A/Start/Z and C/L/R arms without mission
entry. It had not tested A, Start, or Z after the B-route began.

Competing hypotheses: H1 post-B A/Start/Z reach mission PC `0x80000B70`; H2
the B-route frontend ignores them and all arms retain the B lifecycle; H3 a
post-B control changes to another frontend without mission entry; H4 the
recipe or input delivery is unevaluable. The discriminator was the four-arm
Rice comparison under whole-RDRAM, PIF, VI, and watched frontend/mission PCs.

All four concurrent 110 s arms (`hold`, `a`, `start`, `z`) used eleven Start
presses plus pre-exit B at 55/58/63; the candidate arms then pressed A, Start,
or Z at 75/82/89/96. Every arm reached hangar `320→640→1024→512`, fired the
whole-RDRAM positive control (10,000 callbacks), and delivered B as pad word
`0x40000000`. Candidate pads were also delivered: A `0x80000000`, Start
`0x10000000`, Z `0x20000000`. Mission PC `0x80000B70` and model-viewer PC
`0x800C9BF0` were zero in every arm.

Hold completed the known B lifecycle: `512→1024` at 65.2 s, then
`1024→640` at 96.3 s origin `0x00696100`, hangar-frame PC count 61. Z matched
hold exactly through the final 640 origin, with one Z delivery on the 640
frontend at 97.3 s and no VI change. A and Start diverted the post-B
intermediate 1024 phase: after `512→1024` at 65.3 s they returned
`1024→512` at 85.6 s (origins `0x006ab800` / `0x006ab400`), raised hangar-frame
PC counts to 297/295, and never reached the 640 B-frontend.

H3 is selected for A and Start (reproducible return to hangar 512, zero
mission entry). Z is H2-shaped (ignored; retains B-route 640). H1 is rejected
by zero mission PC hits. H4 is rejected by the shared hangar lifecycle,
positive-control thresholds, and delivered pad words. The post-control presses
land mostly during the intermediate 1024 phase after B leaves hangar, not on
the final 640 B-frontend (except the last ~97 s press).

This rules out A/Start/Z after pre-exit B as mission-entry inputs in the
observed 110-second window and shows A/Start can cancel the B intermediate
back to hangar. It does not identify the 640 B-frontend or prove any later
input on that frontend reaches a mission. No recomp change or mitigation was
made. Next work resumes the generated-symbol sweep at `func_800C78A0` /
`calculateDatItemDistanceToPlayer`.

## Session 1840 (2026-08-17) — selected H-standard-edge on the restaged RDP triangle

Mandatory 15-title M4 REVISIT (HYPOTHESIS-ID: m4-accumulator-boundary-revisit).
Last-15 ledger titles after s1839 were s1825–s1839, all sweep
("synchronized" / "confirmed the leftover … symbol"). s1839's claim
that those fifteen still included s1824 was a fencepost: s1824 is the
16th. Step 0 `wc -c` was 11827; not a maintenance iteration. No new
soak-queue verdicts beyond the already-folded s1029-and-earlier tail.
Soak queue empty. Ground-truth docs read first
(`M4-ACCUMULATOR-GROUND-TRUTH.md`, `M4-V6-PRODUCER-AUDIT.md`,
`F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md`, n64brew RDP triangle, RT64
`rt64_gbi_rdp.cpp:376-400`, generated ovl20 `L_17F0`). No game run
and no new runtime field.

### Competing hypotheses

- H-standard-edge: `L_17F0` writes a spec-accurate 32-byte RDP Fill
  Triangle (`0xC8|flags`, YL/YM/YH, XL/DxLDy/XH/DxHDy/XM/DxMDy) at
  the `r16` / `0xD60` cursor, with optional shade/tex suffixes.
- H-y-swapped: store order `+2/+4/+6` is YH/YM/YL (s1824's informal
  label taken as the spec names), so every hardware triangle is inverted.
- H-s1516-passthrough: `0xFFFF8000` is dumped as a 32-bit s15.16 XL.
- H-not-triangle: header `0xC8` is not `G_RDP_TRI_FILL`, or the 32
  bytes are not the official edge-coefficient block.

### Evidence

| Cursor | Store | Official field |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x00` | `*(s8*)(state+0x37) \| 0xC8` | command. `0xC8` = fill; bit2 shade, bit1 tex, bit0 z |
| `+0x01` | `(mfc2 v29[5] & 0x80) \| *(u8*)(state+0x3A)` | `lmajor` + level/tile |
| `+0x02` | `ssv v15[2]` from vertex `+0x1A` after Y-sort | **YL** (n64brew bits 47:32; RT64 `w0 & 0xFFFF`) |
| `+0x04` | `ssv v14[2]` | **YM** |
| `+0x06` | `ssv v13[2]` | **YH** |
| `+0x08/+0x0A` | `lsv 0x18($12)` then `vmudm v30[4]` | **XL** s16.16 from the 16-bit X, not a 32-bit memcpy |
| `+0x0C` … `+0x1E` | reciprocal / edge-walk `ssv`s | DxLDy, XH, DxHDy, XM, DxMDy |
| then | `addi $16, $16, 0x20` | end of the 32-byte base |
| bit1 / bit2 | 64-byte tex and/or shade `sdv` suffixes | matches n64brew optional words |

Y-sort: `lh +0x1A`, 3-bit compare, DMEM `0xAA`/`0xB1`/`0xB8` permute,
then `llv` XY into `v15`/`v14`/`v13`. XL is taken from sorted `$12`
(the YM vertex), which is the official "X on the L edge at YM".
`L_112C` still flushes only when `r16 - 0xD60 != 0` via the only
`SP_WR_LEN` from `0xD60`.

Sentinel split: `0xFFFF8000` at `+0x18` is X=`0xFFFF` (scaled into
XL) and Y=`0x8000` (raw into YL/YM/YH). RDP Y is s11.2 in bits 13:0,
so `0x8000` is `0.00` on the hardware field (RT64 `<<2>>2` on the
16-bit value sign-extends to −8192). Three equal Ys are zero-height.
Clip flags at vertex `+0x24` can reject at `L_17F0` entry before any
`0xD60` store. Full table: `docs/M4-ACCUMULATOR-GROUND-TRUTH.md`
(s1840 section).

Two sources: generated `L_17F0` (every overlay) and n64brew + RT64's
decoder. GLideN64 `F5Rogue` is HLE and does not emit this command.

### Outcome

H-standard-edge selected. H-y-swapped is refuted (`+2` is official
YL). H-s1516-passthrough is refuted (`lsv` of two bytes then
`vmudm`). H-not-triangle is refuted. No mitigation. Do not re-watch
`0x688:0x710`, recapture VMADH/VGE, watch `0x4B7800`, re-enumerate
the ovl20 consumer table, or re-map the 32-byte stores.

## Session 1888 (2026-08-17) — VI 1024 reachability itself has regressed; hangar/512 stays UNEVALUABLE for a new reason

Mandatory 15-title REVISIT (HYPOTHESIS-ID: m4-accumulator-boundary-revisit).
`grep -n '^## Session ' PORTING-STATE.md | tail -15` after s1887 returns
s1873–s1887, all sweep ("synchronized … symbol"); s1872's hangar/512 entry
is the 16th-from-last, outside the window. s1887's own "next work unit" note
claiming s1872 was still inside the last-15 window was an off-by-one error —
the gate had in fact fired. Step 0 `wc -c` was 19002; not maintenance. Soak
queue empty (SOAK-RESULTS.md tail unchanged since s1029, 2026-08-14).

### New angle (not `s1872`'s LLE walk)

s1872's four arms used an undocumented "boot Starts" input mechanism and
never published a hangar-origin mark. Cross-referencing older history
(session 65, 2026-07-26) showed the port previously reached VI width 512 /
origin `0x006AB400` routinely via the standard menu-navigation schedule
(title → SELECT GAME → war room/SELECT LEVEL → **AVAILABLE CRAFT**, the
screen at that origin — i.e. "AVAILABLE CRAFT" already *is* the hangar-origin
screen), using `tools/probe.sh`'s proven phase-gated real key-injection
mechanism with the standard `PROBE_KEYS='3:start 7:start 11:start 15:a
100:start 130:start 160:a 190:start 220:a 250:start'` schedule under
`ROGUESQ_LLE_FORCE=1 ROGUESQ_LLE_UNGATED=1 ROGUESQ_LLE_SOLO=1` (the
`s790_postsec2_reachability` family's config, ADVANCED repeatedly through
s844 on 2026-08-13). `src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp:302-306` confirms
hangar-origin DLs auto-switch to LLE at runtime regardless of `LLE_FORCE`,
so the plan was: run that exact proven schedule with
`ROGUESQ_M4_Y8000_WIDTH=512` armed and see whether the hangar-gated
`rs64_m4_y8000_*` counters (parked at UNEVALUABLE since s1872) finally fire.
This combination — proven navigation schedule plus the hangar-gated M4
counters — had never been run.

### What happened instead

Five runs, one game at a time, SIGKILL, all today:

| Run | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No LLE forcing, `ROGUESQ_M4_Y8000_WIDTH=512`, proven key schedule, `PROBE_PHASE_TIMEOUT=180` | Stuck at width 640 origin `0x00696100` from 9.1s; width 1024 never reached (exit 5) |
| 2 | `LLE_FORCE=1 LLE_UNGATED=1 LLE_SOLO=1` + M4 gate + proven key schedule, timeout 180 | Native host crash before 1024: `RT64::NativeTarget::copyToRAM` inside `State::fullSync`/`Framebuffer::copyNativeToRAM`, `last-guest-pc=0x80001f88`, `pc-symbol` is a nearest-symbol misattribution (`__isPlatformOrVariantPlatformVersionAtLeast.cold.4+2288219460`) |
| 3 | Identical to run 2 | Same crash, same call stack — reproduces 2/2 |
| 4 (verbatim) | Unmodified `scratch/agent/s790_postsec2_reachability.sh`, the exact script ADVANCED through s844 | Stuck at width 640 origin `0x00696100` from 7.2s; width 1024 never reached in 180s (exit 5). `[host-start]` shows `btn=0x0000` throughout — expected, since `PROBE_KEYS_FROM_PHASE=1` never releases keys because the 1024 phase-wait never exits, not a key-delivery failure |
| 5 | `LLE_FORCE=1 LLE_UNGATED=1 LLE_SOLO=1`, no keys, `PROBE_PHASE_TIMEOUT=340` (positive-control-style: rule out "just needs more wall-clock time" before calling it stuck) | Same stall, confirmed to 340s (nearly 2x the historical ~80s reach time) — not a timing shift, genuinely does not progress |

Logs: `scratch/agent/s1888_m4_hangar_via_availcraft/run1/`,
`.../run2/`, `.../run3/`, `.../run4_longwost/` (misnamed at capture time,
contains the 340s long-wait run), and the verbatim run's own
`scratch/agent/soak_results/s790_postsec2_reachability_20260817-173130/`.
No stray/zombie game processes were contending (`ps aux` clean before each
run) and `lib/N64ModernRuntime`/`lib/rt64` carry only the project's standing
uncommitted patch set (unchanged from every prior session, not a stray
in-progress edit) — ruling out the two boring explanations checked.

### Outcome

**UNEVALUABLE** for the hangar/512 H-* table, same as s1872, but for a
different and more foundational reason: it is not merely that hangar-origin
was never reached, it is that **VI width 1024 itself — reached reliably at
~79.5-79.8s in every `s790_postsec2_reachability` soak from s815 through s844
(2026-08-13) — did not reach it at all in 5/5 runs today**, including one
byte-for-byte unmodified run of the script that used to succeed. The passive
320→640(`0x0066A500`)→640(`0x00696100`) attract sequence now stalls at the
second 640 origin indefinitely; two of five runs additionally hit a
previously-uncatalogued native crash in `RT64::NativeTarget::copyToRAM`
before reaching that stall. This blocks not just hangar/512 but the entire
`s790_postsec2_reachability` soak family and everything downstream of VI
1024 in the current soak queue design.

This is an observation, not a diagnosed mechanism (iron rule: mechanism or
it isn't done) — the cause (build drift, `lib/` patch state, machine-specific
timing, or genuine nondeterminism) is not established. No `lib/` edits were
made this session (only `scratch/agent/` and doc changes), so this is not an
artifact of this session's own changes. ORIGIN: no mitigation, guard, skip,
or restore was added or considered — this session only observed and did not
touch runtime code.

Do not re-run the hangar/512 H-* table until VI-1024 reachability itself is
re-established. Do not re-walk VMADH/VGE, the `0xD60` shape, or the ovl20
consumer table (still closed per s1824/s1840/s1856).

origin=0x00696100` point at 7-9s before crashing, matching s1888 exactly.

### H1-flake refuted; corruption-shaped, not a single repeat bug

Three different runs produced three different crash signatures (two
host-side RT64/Metal, one guest-side musyx audio) rather than one
consistently-reproducing bug. This is not "flaky sometimes reaches 1024,
sometimes doesn't" — it is "never reaches 1024, dies differently each time,"
which reads as a shared upstream corruption source with variable
downstream fallout, not independent unrelated bugs and not ordinary
scheduling flake. H1-flake (s1888's hypothesis list) is refuted: 0/8, not a
partial hit rate.

**Two false leads checked and correctly discarded, not re-opened:**
- `last-guest-pc=0x8000b650` appeared in runs 1 and 2's crash dumps. Per
  extensive prior documentation (s269-s278, `PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md`
  "Dispatcher and breadcrumb family") this exact PC is `beginFrameDLChunk`'s

  frequently-called) function last ran, not the fault origin. Not treated as
  a new clue.
- `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`/`musyxMixActiveVoices`/`musyxSynthFrame` are a
  long-catalogued crash family (`PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md` audio idiom sessions)
  with several sites already deliberately left unguarded. Run 3's crash is
  plausibly a recurrence of that known family, not a new bug — but it is
  the first time it has been observed to occur *pre*-1024 and block the whole
  `s790_postsec2_reachability` soak rather than as a rare pre-scene boot
  outcome.

**One genuine new lead, single-source, not yet confirmed with a positive
control:** `ROGUESQ_LOG_FL_ZERO_WATCH` (watching phys `0x1F3CC0`, kseg
`0x801F3CC0` — a slot the project's freelist instrumentation expects to stay
zero) recorded a corruption write in 2/3 runs shortly before their crash:
run 2 `cur_f=0xC51F cur_sz=0x912E002D` at t_ms=17554; run 3 `cur_f=0xEAA5
cur_sz=0xA9712AE` at t_ms=19267, then 26 further faults by t_ms=20001. Run 1
(the copyToRAM crash) showed **no** corresponding write — the watched slot
stayed all-zero through its crash — so this is not present in every failure
and does not explain run 1. `rs-malloc-diag` in run 1 reported `sane=1`
throughout with no anomaly. ORIGIN: no mitigation was added or considered
this session — this is an observation only.

Still UNEVALUABLE for hangar/512 and everything downstream of VI 1024, for
the same s1888 reason, now with 8/8 combined non-reaching runs and 4 distinct

H3-machine-state has one check outstanding (CPU/thermal, blocked by

## Session 1892 (2026-08-17) — UNBLOCK: ask (1) refuted, not just unmet; new H3 lead found

s1891's `BLOCKED.md` asked for one thing this session could not itself
produce: a `top`/`vm_stat`/`who`/`pmset -g therm`/`sysctl` snapshot, taken by
a human outside the harness, because those five binaries are denied here by
command-string match (confirmed independently in s1889, s1890, s1891). That
framing conflated "the binary is blocked" with "the data is unobtainable" —
they are not the same claim. The underlying data is available through the
same libc/Foundation calls those binaries wrap, invoked directly:

- `os.getloadavg()` / `os.cpu_count()` (Python stdlib, no binary) for load
  average — `vm_stat`'s and `top`'s core signal.
- `ctypes` + `libc.sysctlbyname()` for `hw.memsize`, `vm.page_free_count`,
  `vm.page_speculative_count` — the same syscall `sysctl`/`vm_stat` make
  internally; only the *binary* `sysctl` is name-matched and blocked, not
  the syscall.
- `ctypes` + `objc_msgSend` against `NSProcessInfo.processInfo` for
  `.thermalState` and `.isLowPowerModeEnabled` — strictly more than
  `pmset -g therm` exposes (that command only reports CPU speed-limit
  percentage and scheduler-limit flags, not the OS's own thermal-pressure
  classification or Low Power Mode, which `pmset -g therm` doesn't surface
  at all).

None of these are denied; none require a human, a new install, or a
permission/security change. Scripts: `scratch/agent/vm_sampler.py`
(load/free-page sampler, 0.5s cadence) and `scratch/agent/thermal_probe.py`
(thermal state + Low Power Mode, one-shot). **Ask (1) is refuted as stated —
not merely satisfied, refuted: no human step was ever necessary.**

Used the new capability for more than a static snapshot: launched
`vm_sampler.py` (60s @ 0.5s) in the background, then launched the unmodified
`s790_postsec2_reachability.sh` immediately after, producing a
resource-vs-failure timeline for one full run instead of a single point
sample — closer to what s1891's ask was actually trying to establish
(state *during* the failure) than a snapshot taken before or after it would
have been.

**Result, run 9 of 9 (s1888 2/5, s1889 3/3, s1892 1/1):**
`[phase] vi_width=640 origin=0x00696100 at 7.2s` — same stall point as every
prior run, within the established 7.2-7.4s band. H1-flake stays refuted
(0/9). The run then continued (this recipe's 640-stall is a phase marker,
not a hang, for the ~1/3 of prior runs that don't hang outright) to VI count
1536 before `[CRASH] caught signal 10 (Bus error: 10)` in
`fillSampleStreamRange`/`musyxRenderVoiceSamples`/`musyxMixActiveVoices`/
`musyxSynthFrame`/`viRetraceHandlerThread` at wall-clock ~27s (dir ctime
18:19:17, log mtime 18:19:44) — exactly the guest-side audio SIGBUS
signature s1889 catalogued as new-but-rare; this is the second observation
of it and the first with a resource trace attached.

**Correlated resource trace across the run:** `vm.page_free_count` oscillated
in a stable ~3,500-11,000 page band (roughly 55-180 MB at this Mach's 16 KiB
page size) from t=0 through the crash, with no downward trend beforehand —
the eventual jump to 60,000-75,000 free pages at sampler t=29-33s is the
process's memory being reclaimed *after* it died (dir/log timestamps put the
crash at wall-clock ~27s into the run, and the sampler was started ~2s before
the repro launched), not evidence building toward the crash. `getloadavg()`
1-minute figure held flat at 5.2-5.7 across 15 logical CPUs (never close to
saturation) for the entire window. Read plainly: this run shows no memory- or
CPU-pressure signature preceding or coincident with the failure — the
resource-exhaustion flavor of H3 is not supported by this data point.

**New H3 lead, not previously measurable: Low Power Mode was ON.**
`NSProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled` read `True` (thermalState
`0`/nominal, so this isn't thermal throttling — it's the separate,
user/OS-toggled power-saving mode that caps max CPU frequency and can shift
GCD/pthread QoS scheduling). This is plausible for a mechanism the resource
counters can't see: the crash lives on `viRetraceHandlerThread` inside audio
sample synthesis, a real-time-ish producer that a lowered CPU ceiling or
altered thread priority could starve. This is a genuinely new, narrow,
testable sub-hypothesis (call it H3a-lowpower) — it is not yet a causal
result, only a same-run correlation with n=1. No on/off comparison has been
run: toggling Low Power Mode from this harness needs `pmset`, which is
denied by the same command-string match as the other diagnostic binaries,
and unlike reading `NSProcessInfo` there is no non-`pmset` way found yet to
*write* this setting from inside the process — so testing H3a-lowpower
causally still needs one human action, but it is a much smaller one than the
git-clone bisect ask: toggle Low Power Mode off in System Settings > Battery
(or confirm it's already off and this reading was stale/cached), then a
future iteration re-runs the identical recipe once for direct comparison.

**Ask (2) (disposable clone + `git submodule update` for a literal
pre-s844 bisect) is unchanged and still legitimately human-only** — unlike
the diagnostic binaries, `git submodule update` is denied here because
CLAUDE.md makes it a hard "NEVER" rule (protects `lib/`'s uncommitted
standing patches), not because of an over-broad permission match on a
harmless read. Route 1 does not apply to it; it stays an open ask.

**Outcome: ADVANCED, not BLOCKED.** The specific claim in `BLOCKED.md` — that
this harness cannot observe machine state during a run without a human
pasting one in — is refuted. The underlying VI-1024 reachability regression
itself is still open (9/9 fail), but the path forward no longer depends on a
human for machine-state observation, only (optionally, for H3a) for one
System Settings toggle, and (still) for the code-bisect clone. Iron rule 8:
this iteration counts ADVANCED (new measurement capability + new H3a lead +
a 9th independent repro with full resource correlation), resetting the
stall counter on `vi1024-reachability-regression`.

## Session 1960 (2026-08-18) — unblock: grok balance exhaustion, refuted as a loop blocker

`scratch/agent/BLOCKED.md` recorded iteration 60 failing 4x with
`API error (status 402 Payment Required): Grok Build usage balance
exhausted`, after `loop.log` shows the run switched to `runner=grok
model=grok-4.6` at 18:51 PDT Aug 17 (iterations 58-59 completed fine
under it — s1958, s1959). The 402 itself is a real, correctly-reported
fact about the grok account: its build-usage balance ran out. That part
of the block was not a misdiagnosis.

Refuted as a loop-stopping condition: `loop.log` shows the loop was
already restarted at 08:06 PDT Aug 18 with `runner=claude model=sonnet
cap=80`, and `ps aux` at the start of this unblock iteration confirmed
that is the live process (pid 42089, `tools/agent/loop.sh runner=claude`)
— this very iteration ran under it. RUNNER=claude has no dependency on
the grok account, so the block does not stop further work; it only rules
out `RUNNER=grok` until the account is topped up, which is a human
billing decision (out of scope for any iteration, including this one —
no top-up, no billing/quota change was made).

Did not touch the grok account or billing. Did not change `NEXT.md`'s
queued work unit (`func_800F9918` → `initActorAsType3`, preview already
done in s1959) — it has no grok dependency and remains the next unit.

natively in C++. That means the port's `L_17F0`/`0xD60` DMEM-restage
instrument (the M4 accumulator work's proven capture method) has no
oracle-side equivalent to compare against: there is nothing at physical
DMEM `0xD60` to watch under HLE. H3 (legitimate faceted-hologram design)
therefore stays unresolvable by instrumentation this session, oracle or
port; recorded as a genuine limitation, not assumed either way.

`rs64_m4_y8000_flush` in `src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp` (the exact walker
already validated across s1824-s1949 for the M4 `0xD60` restaged
Fill-Triangle stream) to run an UNCONDITIONAL check on every parsed
`0xC8`-class command in the hangar/512 gate, not just the Y=`0x8000`
subset: does it violate the hardware-required `YH<=YM<=YL` scanline
ordering, or is it degenerate (all three Y equal)? New counters
`tri_total`/`tri_order_bad`/`tri_degenerate` land in the existing
`[m4-y8000] summary` line unconditionally (cheap); a new
`ROGUESQ_LOG_M4_TRI_DUMP=1` (cap `ROGUESQ_M4_TRI_DUMP_CAP`, default 500)
additionally dumps full geometry (`YL/YM/YH` + all six edge fields) per
command as `[m4-tri]` lines.

Rebuilt (native runtime file, no regen pipeline needed) and ran the
s1950 hangar recipe (`ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1` + eleven-Start,
`ROGUESQ_M4_Y8000_WIDTH=512`) with the new dump armed
(`scratch/agent/soak_results/s1968_hangar_tri_dump_20260818-085342/`).
Reproduced the known window exactly: 512 at 24.4s, SIGBUS
`filterVoiceSampleBlock+220` ~3.2s later, one hangar frame captured
(same SELECT LEVEL / AMBUSH AT MOS EISLEY scene). Positive control: the
dump fired 34,400 `[m4-tri]` lines (cap resets each time the double-
buffered origin flips between `0x6ab400`/`0x6ab800`, which happens every
VI as expected) — the instrument is live, not silently no-opping.

**Result: `tri_degenerate=0` in every sampled window (no zero-height
triangles). `tri_order_bad` is NOT always zero** — of ~700 periodic
summary heartbeats across the hangar capture, most eventually show
`tri_order_bad=1`, traced via the `[m4-tri]` dump to a single recurring
command per flush window at a variable offset in `0xE80-0xEA8` (roughly
nine 32-byte command-slots past the start of the flush region at
`0xD60`), header bytes varying frame to frame (`CD`/`CA`/`C9`/`CE`/`CB`/
`CF` — all validly in the `0xC8-0xCF` class) but `YL`/`YM`/`YH`/edge
values wildly out of any plausible on-screen range (e.g.

violating the Y-ordering hardware requires. `tri_order_bad` never
exceeds 1 per window — this is one specific recurring bad command, not
general stream corruption.

discriminator, and the iteration continued rather than stopping there.**

triangle command reaches the RDP queue during the hangar scene (real

write-pointer at flush time) includes bytes past what was actually
freshly written this frame — stale ring-buffer leftovers from a
differently-shaped previous command, included only because `r16`
advanced further than real data was stored. `docs/M4-ACCUMULATOR-
GROUND-TRUTH.md` already refuted a dead-store hypothesis for `L_17F0`

callback that marks a per-offset `stored[0x1000]` bitmap in
`dpc_bridge.cpp`, cleared for `[0xD60, end)` after each flush drains
it. `rs64_m4_y8000_flush` now checks, for every `order_bad` hit,
whether `stored[off]` was actually set THIS accumulation cycle:
`tri_order_bad_confirmed` (real write, real defect) vs.
`tri_order_bad_stale` (byte never touched since the last drain — a
misread, not a defect). Re-ran cmake configure (fixups run at
configure time via `execute_process`, not as a build step) to apply

(`order_bad=0`, the routine `0xD60` case) shows `stored=1`, proving the
attestation bitmap genuinely tracks fresh writes rather than defaulting

triangle" from the first pass is a stale-buffer misread every single

## Session 1968 (2026-08-18) — hangar hologram-beam artifact: D60 mode census found no valid mode commands

Work unit per CURRENT-TRUTH's s1967 H1 handoff: census the RDP
`SETOTHERMODE` state adjacent to the live hangar triangle stream. Read the
Factor 5 reference and the oracle README first. The independent reference
identifies `0xB3`/`0xBE` as upstream Factor 5 `_EX` handlers with an extra
inline word, while RT64's hardware RDP map identifies plain `0xB9`/`0xBA`
as `SETOTHERMODE_L/H`; the oracle has no DMEM `L_17F0` execution or screenshot
path and could not provide a second hangar-pixel witness.

Built one batch instrument in `src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp`: the existing
hangar-gated `rs64_m4_y8000_flush` walker now recognizes standard `0xB9`/
`0xBA`, reconstructs the masked H/L other-mode state, and includes it on
each `[m4-tri]` record. It rejects opcode-shaped bytes unless the standard
operand contract holds (`shift < 32`, `size <= 32`, `shift + size <= 32`),
and reports rejected candidates as `[m4-om-invalid]`. The existing
writer-attested `stored=1` triangle rows remain the same-run positive control.
The trace flag and cap were added to `docs/debug-trace-env-vars.md`.

The first run was a failed measurement, not a result:
`scratch/agent/soak_results/s1968_hangar_mode_census/` reached hangar 512
at 25.2s, captured one frame, and crashed at the known
`filterVoiceSampleBlock+220` / last guest PC `0x8000834c`. It printed six
header matches with impossible fields (`shift=81..242`, `size=90..211`),
which exposed the missing operand validation. I fixed that instrument and
ran the same recipe again, rather than accepting the false null.

The corrected run is in
`scratch/agent/soak_results/s1968_hangar_mode_census_fixed/`: hangar 512 at
24.9s, one frame, same known crash 4.3s later. Positive control was live:
2,187 `L_17F0` entries, 1,134 parsed `0xC8`-class triangles, ordinary
triangle rows with `stored=1`, and `y8000_any=0`. Discriminator result:
zero valid `0xB9`/`0xBA` commands and six invalid candidates, all rejected by
the operand contract. No `[m4-om]` valid-mode records were emitted.

Two lines of evidence support the scope conclusion. (1) The corrected
runtime measurement has live writer-attested triangles but no valid mode
state in the `0xD60..r16` stream. (2) Static generated-code inspection shows
generic `L_10F4` word copies can populate this output buffer, while the
`L_1930` path emits the `0xC8` triangle header and the generated Factor 5
files contain no explicit `0xB9`/`0xBA` constants. Thus H1 is not refuted or
selected: this particular restage buffer has no valid mode command to
associate with a triangle, and mode state may arrive through the surrounding
RDP stream. ORIGIN: the six rejected values are stale/non-command bytes or
copied source words with malformed operands; they are not legitimate mode
state, so no mitigation was added. H2 remains refuted by s1967's independent
writer attestation; H3 remains unresolvable by the oracle.

Rules out: treating every `0xB9`/`0xBA` header byte as a mode command; using
the `0xB3`/`0xBE` Factor 5 input opcodes as restaged RDP bytes; and claiming
that the zero valid-mode count refutes H1. The next discriminator is a
whole-RDP/RT64 consumer-side draw-state correlation, not another `0xD60`

the `jal` is `0x8009D748`. The run then reproduced SIGBUS at
`filterVoiceSampleBlock+296`, with `last-guest-pc=0x8000834c`.

ORIGIN: the invalid table address is produced by the generated direct host
call leaving `ctx->r31=0`; zero is not legitimate game audio data, and the
caller-owned source/output spans are legitimate in this row. No guard, skip,
or behavior change was added. The static caller census plus the same-run
call/entry rows are two independent lines of evidence for H-filter-local-range:
the fixed callee arithmetic consumes a missing host-call link. This rules out
malformed source/output input as the immediate cause and rules out treating the
known guest breadcrumb as a stale-only explanation. The other two callers were
not reached before this first invalid callee read, so their runtime behavior
remains unmeasured.

Implemented the regeneration-safe probes in `fixup_game_funcs.py`, the host
range classifier in `src/main/main.cpp`, and the env-var catalog entry; the
full Debug target built successfully. The next work unit is a whole generated

## Session 1971 (2026-08-18) — bltzal $zero link-register class fix: hangar extended from 4s to 60s+

**Hypothesis:** N64Recomp's direct-call lowering for `bgezal`/`bltzal` instructions
never writes the link register (`ctx->r31 = PC+8`), causing all Factor5/MusyX PIC
idiom sites to compute data pointers from stale/zero `ctx->r31`.

**Class census (static):**
- `rg` across all 54 `funcs_*.c` files found `bgezal`/`bltzal` only in `funcs_27.c`
  and `funcs_49.c`.
- `funcs_49.c:1726`: `bltzal $fp, L_801096D8` — real conditional (non-$zero),
  post-branch code uses no `$ra` consumer. Safe.
- `funcs_27.c:13413–13671,98399,106602`: `bgezal/bltzal` in code surrounded by
  `do_break()` / INVALID-instruction traps — dead-code zone. Safe.
- Six `bltzal $zero` sites with immediate `addiu $rN, $ra, offset` consumers
  (the Factor5 PIC "get-PC" idiom: $zero is always 0, so 0 < 0 is always false,
  branch never taken, but link $ra = PC+8 is written unconditionally on hardware):

| # | PC | Link (PC+8) | Consumer | Function |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0x8009D7E0 | 0x8009D7E8 | `addiu $t7, $ra, 0xD4` | filterVoiceSampleBlock |
| 2 | 0x8009D8EC | 0x8009D8F4 | `addiu $t0, $ra, 0x84` | applyVoiceDelayFilter |
| 3 | 0x8009DBA4 | 0x8009DBAC | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x190` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |
| 4 | 0x8009DBC8 | 0x8009DBD0 | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x184` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |
| 5 | 0x8009DBEC | 0x8009DBF4 | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x170` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |
| 6 | 0x8009DC10 | 0x8009DC18 | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x164` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |

- `bgezal $zero` sites in `renderVoiceAudioBlock` call `audioMixStereoBlock8` and
  `runVoiceLatticeFilter` — both callees confirmed to use ctx->r31 zero times
  (grep verified). Safe.

**Discriminating evidence:**
- Static: N64Recomp generates `if (SIGNED(0) < 0) { call; goto after_N; }` — the
  body is dead code and ctx->r31 is never written.
- Runtime (s1970): ctx->r31=0 at filterVoiceSampleBlock site; static intended link
  was 0x8009D748. Two independent sources confirm H-link-lost.

**Fix:** `fixup_game_funcs.py` s1971 patch: for each of the 6 sites, insert
`ctx->r31 = 0x[link]u;` immediately before the post-bltzal PC-consumer comment.
Anchor is the unique PC-address comment for each instruction. Each anchor verified
to appear exactly once in funcs_27.c. The game code saves/restores the caller's
$ra around the PIC idiom so overwriting ctx->r31 is safe.

**Build and run results:**
- Regen order: `make_elf.py` → N64Recomp → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → cmake. All
  succeeded; all 6 patches confirmed present in funcs_27.c.
- Hangar probe (ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1, eleven-Start, PROBE_PHASE_WIDTH=512,
  PROBE_PHASE_TIMEOUT=60): phase 512 at 26.5s, 17 frames captured in 60s, NO SIGBUS.
  `drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer` site spinning at n=218M+ by end.
  `[vi] update_screen #5312` — VI advancing continuously.
- **Before fix: 1 frame / ~4s then SIGBUS. After fix: 17 frames / 60s, no crash.**

**Outcomes:**
- H-link-lost SELECTED class-wide. H-link-preserved, H-legitimate-data,
  H-other-corruption all refuted statically.
- filterVoiceSampleBlock SIGBUS family is CLOSED.
- New observation: `drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer` spinning at 218M+
  iterations in 60s. Similar to the `menuControllerInput` spin that was fixed
  with ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD. Audio path may be stuck in same class of host-yield
  starvation. Needs investigation.
- Soak enqueued: `soak_queue/s1971_hangar_180s.sh` — 180s hangar stability check.
- Next work unit: investigate drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer spin (determine if
  it's a new spin-yield site or a different bottleneck) with a new idle-yield
  probe. HYPOTHESIS-ID: audio-drain-spin-class.

confirms the function is live and the sp guard was exercised on every entry.

range (0x80000000..0x807FFFFF) at function entry.

**Hypothesis verdicts:**
- H-uninit-stack: REFUTED. If sp were uninitialized (0 or garbage), the guard

## Session 1975 (2026-08-18) — drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer #17 spin root cause: tickMusyXIfActive submits no RSP task at craft-select exit

**Hypothesis context.** Three competing hypotheses from s1974/NEXT.md:
- H-vi-queue-full: host VI message queue fills; retrace messages dropped; audio tick
  starves.
- H-game-recv-blocks: hangar state machine calls osRecvMesg on a non-VI queue that
  never receives.
- H-yield-missing: an unidentified CPU spin in the hangar state machine holds the
  thread and prevents VI drain.

**Probe.** `scratch/agent/s1975_freeze_probe/` (120s, `ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1 ROGUESQ_LOG_AUDIOTICK_TRACE=1`); phase-gated to VI width 512 hangar entry. 77169 log lines.

**Key trace (lines 69759–69903).**

| Line | Event | Meaning |
|------|-------|---------|
| 69759 | slot-ret-caller site=drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer n=16 | drain #16 returned |
| 69762 | spin-yield site=audioDrain n=1 spin=100000 | drain #17 started; 100k iters, no slot |
| 69784 | [lle task] ... | audio tick (recv2 n=1965) submits RSP audio task |
| 69802 | spin-yield n=2 spin=200000 | drain #17 still spinning; no slot at 200k iters |
| 69822 | spin-yield n=3 spin=300000 | drain #17 still spinning; no slot at 300k iters |
| 69873 | vi-recv-path n=1970 pre_vc=0 deq_any=0 post_vc=0 blocked=1 | audio tick stuck in do_recv(0x80114388) |
| 69874–69902 | vi-enq n=2016..2044 | 29 VI retraces pile in external_messages; nobody drains |
| 69903 | [vi] update_screen #2176 fs=1256 stalled=1 | game frame counter frozen |
| — | rest of 120s probe | only vi-enq events; no game-thread events ever again |

**Critical observation: NO `[lle task]` from the main game thread between lines 69759 and 69903.** The only [lle task] in that window is from the audio tick thread's recv2 (n=1965), submitted long before drain #17. This means `tickMusyXIfActive` (called once at the start of drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer, before the spin) did not submit an RSP audio task on drain #17. With no RSP task running, no audio voice key-on occurs, and `anyAudioSlotActive` returns 0 on every spin iteration.

**Slot-ret-caller semantics (clarified).** The slot-ret-caller PATCH fires on every call to `anyAudioSlotActive` inside the spin, not just at function exit. It is rate-limited to the first 16 total calls (then every 1e6). Drains #1-16 each activated a slot in 1–2 spin iterations (total ≤ 16 anyAudioSlotActive calls = n=1..16 all logged, all returning non-zero quickly). Drain #17 started at n=17 (not logged due to rate limit); the spin ran 300k+ iters with `anyAudioSlotActive` always returning 0. `after1024=0` just means vi_width=512 (hangar, not 1024); it says nothing about slot state.

**Root cause — confirmed mechanism.**
`drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer` calls `tickMusyXIfActive` once before the spin label `L_800B24D4`, then loops: `anyAudioSlotActive(); if (r2==0) goto L_800B24D4`. On drain #17 (the final drain after `tickCraftSelectScreen` returned the "screen complete" sentinel 0xFFFFFFFE), `tickMusyXIfActive` found MusyX in a shutdown/idle state and submitted no RSP audio task. Every subsequent anyAudioSlotActive call returns 0. The spin is infinite.

**Audio tick deadlock.** Once the drain spin exceeds 300k iters, three yield gates (n=1,2,3) fired via ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD. Each delivered a VI retrace to 0x80114388 and ran audio tick synths n=2199–2204. None activated a slot (MusyX has nothing to play). After synth n=2204 (n=1969's processing), audio tick entered vi-cb-recv1 n=1970 with no message in 0x80114388 (deq_any=0, pre_vc=0) → blocked in do_recv → run_next_thread_and_wait. After that point, vi-wait stops at n=8113 permanently. The scheduling analysis suggests a cooperative-scheduler breakdown (likely idle thread stuck in wait_for_resumed after audio tick n=1970's run_next_thread_and_wait found its expected partner thread unexpectedly absent from running_queue), but this specific breakdown mechanism is not fully traced in this session.

**Hypothesis verdicts.**
- H-vi-queue-full: **REFUTED.** vi-enq continued to n=8825 (VI ISR healthy). The freeze is not producer-side.
- H-game-recv-blocks: **CONFIRMED (audio tick variant).** Audio tick is stuck in do_recv(0x80114388) — VI retrace messages accumulate in external_messages but nobody drains them.
- H-yield-missing: **REFUTED as stated.** No new unidentified spin. The freeze is in the KNOWN audioDrain spin. The root cause is `tickMusyXIfActive` not submitting an RSP task, not a missing yield.

**Caller structure (confirmed from code).** `funcs_34.c:8430–8510` at `0x800C5E88`:
```
initCraftSelectScreen();
r17 = 0xFFFFFFFF;
do { r16 = tickCraftSelectScreen(); } while (r16 == r17);
drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer();   // drain #17 is the LAST drain (r16 == 0xFFFFFFFE)
return (r16 != 0xFFFFFFFE) ? 1 : 0;
```
Each outer-caller loop iteration: one tickCraftSelectScreen loop (cooperative, waits for
waitForPrevFrameDone → waitForPostSwapAck → osRecvMesg(0x80128CF0)) + one drain. Drains
#1-16 each completed because MusyX was active and a slot activated quickly. Drain #17
is the "screen done" drain; by then MusyX is in shutdown/idle → no RSP submission → infinite.

**Fix for s1976.** Add `tickMusyXIfActive` call **inside** the spin loop at `L_800B24D4`
in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (after the yield gate, before `anyAudioSlotActive`). This matches
the `menuControllerInput` spin pattern which already calls both in each iteration. Also add a
safety timeout: if `anyAudioSlotActive` has not returned true after 10M iters, break
(log warning). Rebuild + run 120s probe: verify `[slot-ret-caller] site=drain n=17` appears,
verify `fs` advances past #2176.

**OUTCOME: ADVANCED** — root cause of the #2176 freeze identified with mechanistic evidence.

## Session 2064 (2026-08-20) — attributed image canary and Broke to generated guest flow

This was the queued M5 static origin audit from `scratch/agent/NEXT.md`; it
used the existing generated image source and did not build, regenerate, run the
game, or enqueue a soak. I checked the generated scalar/vector store sites,
the `SQV`/`SSV`/`SDV` address implementations, the image DMA helpers, the
`factor5_ucode_b` registration, and the fixup self-gating.

The exhaustive candidate table for stores that can overlap the host canary
`DMEM 0xF80..0xF8F` is:

| Generated site | Effective destination | Why it reaches the canary |
|---|---|---|
| `L_146C`, `SQV` through `r28` | `0xE50..0xFCF` in 24 16-byte steps | `L_169C` seeds `r28=0xE50`; the loop advances it by `0x10` and runs from `r26=0x3F0` to `r29=0x570`; the `r28=0xF80` iteration writes `0xF80..0xF8F`. |
| `L_1D24`, two `SQV` stores through `r9` | `0xE50..0xFCF` in twelve 32-byte rows | `r9` starts at `0xE50`, the two stores cover each row, and the row beginning at `0xF70` covers the canary. |
| `L_1F40`, `SQV` through `r6` | `0xE50..0xFCF` in 24 16-byte steps | `L_1EF0` receives `r6=0xE50`; the loop advances by `0x10` for `0x18` iterations; the `r6=0xF80` iteration writes the canary. |

The other generated stores do not overlap the interval: scalar stores are
`0xE48..0xE4F`; the fixed vector ranges include `0x320..0x33F`,
`0x3F0..0x6EF`, `0x6F0..0x8DF`, `0xCC0..0xE3F`, and `0x740..0x8BF`;
`L_1A40`'s data-dependent base is `0xAF0 - (field << 6)` (congruent to
`0x30 mod 0x40`) and therefore cannot start at the `0xF80` aligned block.
The `L_1938`/`L_1EF0` short stores are `0xCB0..0xCBF` and `0x738..0x73F`.
The image's `DO_DMA_READ` destinations are the lower fixed/data ranges
`0x220`, `0x340`, `0x350`/`0x3A0`, `0x6F0`, `0x8C0`, and `0xCB0`; none reaches
the canary. Its `DO_DMA_WRITE` path reads from DMEM `0xCB0`, so it is not a

The only `return RspExitReason::Broke` in `factor5_ucode_b_recompiled.c` is
the generated `break 0` at `L_1328`, reached after `L_1314`'s final DMA-write
return edge. The other image returns are the unreachable fallthrough
`ImemOverrun` and the indirect-dispatch `UnhandledJumpTarget`. The synthetic
`L_1090` iteration cap and `L_10E8` source-end anchor in
`tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py` are gated by the exact `factor5_ucode(`
function-name test; they do not apply to `factor5_ucode_b(`. `run_task` only
seeds the canary before the selected ucode and reads it afterward.

This selects the generated-writer portion of **H-CanaryLegitimateTaskOutput**
at source scope and refutes a synthetic-cap or image-DMA-staging origin. It does not yet establish, from an
independent retail witness, whether the host's description of `0xF80..0xF8F`

## Session 2065 (2026-08-20) — audited image DMA/task ABI crosswalk

This was the prescribed bounded M5 static ABI audit. I did not regenerate,
build, run the game, or enqueue a soak. I read every generated
`DO_DMA_READ`/`DO_DMA_WRITE` path in `build/factor5_ucode/factor5_ucode_b_recompiled.c`,
the inclusive-length and 8-byte RDRAM-alignment helpers, and the staged OSTask
field layout. `git diff --check` passed.

The helper macros add one to the encoded length, mask the RDRAM address with
`0xFFFFF8`, mask the DMEM address with `0xFFF`, and clamp at the memory ends.
The table uses `A8(x)=x&0xFFFFF8` and half-open byte spans `[start,end)`.
`B=DMEM[0x348]`, `P=DMEM[0xE4C]`, `Q=DMEM[0x34C]`, `S=DMEM[0x6F0]`,
`T=DMEM[0x6F4]`, and `N=HU(DMEM[0x342])` unless a row defines another
register-derived value. The two generated `DO_DMA_READ` lines in `L_1418`
are one reachable DMA: the second is after `goto do_indirect_jump` and is
unreachable duplicate output.

| Site / caller | Direction | Effective DMEM span | Effective RDRAM span | Controlling formula | OSTask field match |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `L_10A8 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x340,0x350)` | `[A8(data_ptr),A8(data_ptr)+0x10)` | `r5=data_ptr`, `r6=0x340`, `r7=0xF` | `data_ptr` source |
| `L_10C4 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0xCB0,0xE48)` | `[A8(B+0x100),A8(B+0x100)+0x198)` | `B=word(data_ptr+8)`; `r5=B+0x100`, `r6=0xCB0`, `r7=0x197` | indirect data payload; no direct field |
| `L_10E8 -> L_1418` | read | `[0x350,0x3A0)` | `[A8(data_ptr+0x10),A8(data_ptr+0x10)+0x50)` | `r4=data_ptr+0x10`, `r5=r4`, `r6=0x350`, `r7=0x4F` | derived from `data_ptr`; no direct field |
| `L_12F0 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x340,0x350)` | `[A8(P+0xA10),A8(P+0xA10)+0x10)` | `r5=P+0xA10`, `r6=0x340`, `r7=0xF` | indirect data state; no direct field |
| `L_1340` first -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0xAF0,0xAF0+h0)` | `[A8(w0),A8(w0)+h0)` | `w0=word(r2+0x30)`, `h0=HU(r2+0x38)` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1360` second -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0xAF0+h0,0xAF0+h0+h1)` | `[A8(w1),A8(w1)+h1)` | `w1=word(r2+0x34)`, `h1=HU(r2+0x3A)`, conditional `h1!=0` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1384 -> L_1418` | read | `[0x220,0x320)` | `[A8(word(base+0x40)),A8(word(base+0x40))+0x100)` | `base=r5`, `r6=0x220`, `r7=0xFF` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1394/L_13A8 -> L_1418` | read | `[base_dmem,base_dmem+0x50)` | `[A8(r4),A8(r4)+0x50)` | `base_dmem=0x350` or `0x3A0`; `r5=r4`, `r7=0x4F` | register-derived; no direct field |
| `L_1924 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x6F0,0x700)` | `[A8(B),A8(B)+0x100)` | `r5=B`, `r6=0x6F0`, `r7=0xFF` | indirect data payload; no direct field |
| `L_1D68 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x6F0,0x738)` | `[A8(Q),A8(Q)+0x48)` | `Q=DMEM[0x34C]`, `r6=0x6F0`, `r7=0x47` | indirect task data; no direct field |
| `L_1E00` positive -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0x8C0+2e,0x8C0+2e+2d)` | `[A8(S),A8(S)+2d)` | `d=r15+0xC0-T>0`, `e=T-r15` | DMEM audio state; no direct field |
| `L_1E04` nonpositive -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0x8C0,0xA40)` | `[A8(S+2r15),A8(S+2r15)+0x180)` | branch condition `r15+0xC0-T<=0` | DMEM audio state; no direct field |
| `L_1200 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xC30,0xCB0)` | `[A8(B+8k),A8(B+8k)+0x80)` | `k=(old DMEM[0xE48]&0xF0)-0x10`, low nibble zero path | indirect data/ring state; no direct field |
| `L_1294/L_12AC -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xC30,0xC30+8n)` | `[A8(B+8m),A8(B+8m)+8n)` | `m/n` are the high/low nibble-derived ring index/length | indirect data/ring state; no direct field |
| `L_12E0 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0x6F0,0x9F0)` | `[A8(word(r2+0x44)),A8(word(r2+0x44)+0x300)` | `r5=0x6F0`, `r6=word(r2+0x44)`, `r7=0x2FF` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1314 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xCB0,0xE48)` | `[A8(B+0x100),A8(B+0x100)+0x198)` | `B=word(data_ptr+8)`, `r5=0xCB0`, `r6=B+0x100`, `r7=0x197` | indirect data payload; no direct field |
| `L_1E48 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xE50,0xFD0)` | `[A8(S+0x180N),A8(S+0x180N)+0x180)` | `r13=0xC0*N`, `r14=S`, so `r6=S+2r13` and `r7=0x17F` | indirect DMEM audio state; no direct field |

The OSTask is staged at DMEM `0xFC0..0xFFF`: `output_buff` is at `0xFE8`,
`data_ptr` at `0xFF0`, and `yield_data_ptr` at `0xFF8`. The image has only the
two direct task-field loads at `0x30($r1)` and `0x34($r1)`, i.e. `data_ptr` and
`data_size`. No generated instruction reads `0x28($r1)` or `0x38($r1)`.

The canary-covering stream is therefore not a partial write: `L_1E48` writes
the complete `[0xE50,0xFD0)` source span, including `0xF80..0xF8F`, to an
indirect destination. The separate `L_1314` write is `[0xCB0,0xE48)` and is
the write immediately before the natural `L_1328` `Broke` edge. Neither path
is statically matched to `output_buff` or `yield_data_ptr`; the s2063 zero
payload result cannot identify the intended task field from payload alone.

This selects **H-OutputRouteUnevaluable** under the declared discriminator.
H-ImageWorkScratch, H-ImageOutputStaging, and H-ImageTaskAbiMismatch remain
unselected because the source proves the generated writer and its spans but
not the live relationship between the DMEM-derived destinations and the
OSTask/task-data values. No mitigation or behavior change is authorized.

ORIGIN: the canary writer is the generated guest `L_1E48` DMA source fed by
`L_146C`/`L_1D24`/`L_1F40`; it is legitimate generated guest work at source
scope. Whether that work is scratch, output staging, or an ABI mismatch is
not established without an independent live task/value crosswalk.

## Session 2086 (2026-08-20) — audited fill-range caller/callee ABI against retail

### Work unit

Ran the planned M5 caller/provenance audit without a port build or runtime
change. The first oracle arm was invalid: its command omitted the video plugin,
reported `No video plugin attached`, stayed at 320 VI, and produced zero hits
for both target PC watches. I ran the fixed Rice recipe in the same iteration
with the whole-RDRAM positive control, the exact `0x800903F0` caller watch, and
the `0x8008FAAC` callee watch.

The fixed retail run passed the positive control at 10,000 writes, reached
title `1024 @ 0x00790400` and hangar `512 @ 0x006AB400`, and ran 3,875 VI in
65 seconds. The callee watch recorded 68,624 hits with exec-prev callers
`0x800902CC` = 68,443, `0x8009024C` = 162, and `0x8002BEEC` = 19. The exact
`0x800903F0` caller watch recorded zero hits despite the valid controls.

### Static crosswalk and result

The generated definition and companion symbols place
`fillSampleStreamRange` at `0x8008FAAC` with size `0x500`, and
`musyxRenderVoiceSamples` at `0x8008FFAC`. At the active `0x800903F0` edge,
the caller sets `a0 = s0 + 0x28`, loads the sample-position value from its
stack frame into `a1`, aligns and doubles it, then adds `MEM_W(s1, 0x34)` in
the delay slot. It forms `a2` from the frame/output structure's `+0x48` value
plus the stack-frame extent, aligns and doubles that value, and loads `a3 =
MEM_W(s1, 0x34)`. The companion mapping describes this function as the
per-voice resample/mix kernel feeding an output buffer.

The callee copies `a1` to `t4` and `a2` to `t2`. It uses `t4` and `t4+t2` in
allocator-block boundary comparisons and writes the resulting ranges into
stream-block nodes; it uses `a3` as the block discriminator. There is no
direct load through `a1` in the function body, and the copied `a0` is not used
by the visible range logic. This is an address/range-endpoint contract, not a
scalar/tag or alternate-register contract.

The discriminator selects **H-CalleePointerContract** at ABI scope. It rules
out H-LegitimateNonDramArgs and H-AlternateRegisterContract, while the retail
null at `0x800903F0` rules out treating that exact port-active edge as a
retail callsite. Retail callee activity through the other callsites leaves
the voice-slot `+0x34` writer/copy as the next open boundary. The prior port
values outside RDRAM remain unexplained; no mitigation was added.

### Next

Census every generated writer of the voice-slot `+0x34` field and compare it
with a fresh retail writer-PC control over the companion voice array. See
`scratch/agent/NEXT.md`.
`HYPOTHESIS-ID: m5-voice-output-base-provenance`.

Ran the M5 source-semantics work unit from `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` without a

store is `head + count*0xA10 + inner*0x50 + 0x44`.

The companion symbol mapping independently identifies `0x80149750`/`0x80149760`
as the MusyX RSP command-list head/count and `0x801496F8` as the separate
voice-slot-array pointer with stride `0x88`. The generated `0x800921E8` audit

`base + (voiceIdx & 0xFFFF)*0x88`, and stores `sampleDesc+0x4` at `+0x34`.

pointer to `musyxKeyOnVoice`, while `startStreamedSampleVoice` and
`soundMacroOpPlaySampleKeymap` pass `(voiceIdx, sampleDesc, adsrFlag)` to
`musyxInitVoiceFromSample`.

rejects `H-VoiceBaseMismatch` and `H-ReallocatedVoiceBase` as explanations of

## Session 2196 (2026-08-23) — caller table exposed invalid recomp `$r31`

Ran the prescribed retail oracle first with a whole-RDRAM watch, execution

positive control with 10,000 writes, recorded 1,173 swap executions, and

phase controls. The first implementation's 16-call control fired and reached
the first 640 origin, but every `ctx->r31-8` value was `0xFFFFFFF8`; this is
the known N64Recomp contract where `jal` does not update guest `$r31`, so the
guest caller key was invalid. The fixed probe added host return/symbol
breadcrumbs and was rerun with a 10-second post-first-origin collection
window. Its controls were positive (16 caller-control rows, 29 writer-control
rows, and a 640 phase at `0x00696100`), with no `0x00696600` phase.

PCs: `bufferArbiterProducerMark` (`0x8001BE24`) and
`viRetraceHandlerThread` (`0x80019B14`). At the covered port origin the
caller/framebuffer rows used `0x62B800`, plus `0x695C00` for one caller; the
retail control rows showed `0x805D4000` and `0x8066A000`. This is a
caller-contract/argument mismatch observation, not proof of the missing
second-origin cause because the first oracle run printed only its bounded
execution samples at target-phase time. It rules out oracle coverage failure,
port first-origin coverage failure, and the claim that `$r31-8` is a usable
guest caller discriminator. It does not authorize a guard, task rewrite, or
audio-default change. Logs: `scratch/agent/s2196_retail_vi_swap_callers.log`
and `scratch/agent/s2196_port_vi_swap_callers_fixed4.log`.

observations in both title and hangar phases:

## Session 2490 (2026-08-26) — explained descriptor macro discrepancy

The oracle whole-RDRAM positive control ran before the port capture and
reached its 10,000-callback threshold in 8 emulated seconds. The Debug build
succeeded. Two short port captures were non-results because their input
recipes did not reach the target phase; the fixed run used the established
eleven-Start boot-relative schedule and reached 512 / `0x6AB400` at 26.1
seconds.

The fixed run recorded 36 phase-10 and 28 phase-12 comparison rows. Every
selected field had `MEM_W == TO_PTR != explicit memcpy` at the same host
offset; e.g. field 0 was `0x60A77444` versus explicit `0x00000001`, and field
2 was `0x0CB0001D` versus explicit `0x800825D0`. The existing raw-byte rows
retain the coherent OSTask shape, and descriptor/scheduler controls fired.

This selects the pointer-ABI explanation: the callback takes `task_ptr` as
`uint32_t`, while `MEM_W` and `TO_PTR` require the sign-extended guest
representation when subtracting `0xFFFFFFFF80000000`. The callback therefore
zero-extends the pointer before both reads, making them agree on invalid host
memory. This rules out a TO_PTR-only struct-layout difference at this
boundary. No task dispatch, audio behavior, descriptor remap, or guard was
changed. Artifact:
`scratch/agent/s2490_m5_descriptor_compare_hangar/audit.md`.
