## Session 2559 (2026-08-26) — ran M5 stub-image contract checkpoint

HYPOTHESIS-ID: m5-audio-destubbing-contract

Before the build, I defined four competing outcomes: audio degeneracy would
produce a new downstream edge in the image arm; an image contract gap would
show image execution without that edge; route-only variation would show
matched phases without an audio delta; and image instability would prevent a
valid target window. The Debug target built successfully. The staged recipe
ran the retail oracle first, then the silent arm before the image arm, with
phase-gated title and hangar controls.

The independent retail whole-RDRAM control reached 10,000 callbacks and
recorded both title (`1024 @ 0x00790400`) and hangar (`512 @ 0x006AB400`). Both
port arms reached title and hangar and ended by SIGKILL with zero `[CRASH]` and
`[ABORT]` markers. The silent arm recorded 1,472 ABI/DMA rows, zero generated
DMA ranges, and unchanged DMEM. The image arm recorded 1,136 ABI/DMA rows,
2,328 generated DMA ranges, and repeated positive ABI rows with `changed=1597`,
`break_pc=0x1328`, `exit=1`, and `dma_count=3`. Both arms reported PCM source
and consumer boundary rows (94/94 silent; 88/88 image), so the image arm did

## Session 3054 (2026-08-28) — checkpoint: identified VI-mode stall as route root cause

Stop-gate retry. No new experiment was run. Analyzed the s3053 run.log data
that the original session entry omitted.

`osViSetMode_recomp` logs unconditionally. The s3053 run.log contains exactly
4 `osViSetMode` calls: #1 width=320 (initVideoSubsystem, line 42), #2 width=2
(swapBufferWithViMode, line 1242 — suspicious/corrupt data), #3 width=640
(initVideoSubsystem, line 1249), #4 width=640 (applyPendingViChanges,
line 1342). The game never calls osViSetMode with width=1024.

The route predicate at `src/main/main.cpp:1376–1380` reads VI_WIDTH_REG via
`rs64_vi_committed_width()` and fires only when width==1024 (title) or
width==512 (hangar). PORTING-STATE history confirms this is correct: older
runs show "vi_width=1024 (was 640) origin=0x00790400 at 45.3s" and
"vi_width=512 (was 1024) origin=0x006AB400 at 74.4s" as the expected
transition signature. The route predicate is not wrong — it was calibrated
against actual retail behavior.

The M4 summary at the end of the s3053 run shows `viw=640 origin=0x005D4500`
as the steady-state VI, confirming the game renders ~10 seconds of content at
width=640 without ever issuing a width=1024 mode change. This selects
`H-TitleOsViNotCalled` as the most specific hypothesis: the game code path
that calls osViSetMode(width=1024) is never reached in current AUTOPILOT runs.

This is a pre-title state-machine stall, not a DP-event ordering or
ProducerMark issue. It explains why all target-phase measurements in sessions
3040–3053 returned `H-MeasurementInsufficient`: the route predicate is
structurally unreachable if the VI mode never transitions to 1024.

Next discriminating probe: use the retail oracle to capture the PC that calls
osViSetMode(1024) in retail, then check via port osViSetMode logs whether that
call site executes in port AUTOPILOT runs. If the retail caller PC maps to a
named recompiled function, check whether that function is called at all in
port. No behavior changed. New evidence: osViSetMode call-count data in
`scratch/agent/s3053_m5_gfx_action_order/run.log` (lines 42, 1242, 1249, 1342).

## Session 3357 (2026-08-31) — guarded task-start guest-pointer boundary

Performed a bounded M3 audit of the active `osSpTaskStartGo_recomp` host-entry

Added one full-width KSEG0 range predicate covering the complete `OSTask`
object before all three dereferences. It accepts both sign-extended and
zero-extended 8 MiB KSEG0 addresses, returns from the void wrapper with zero

new guard compiles and does not select the wrong-range hypothesis; the route's
existing task/title/hangar runtime qualification remains the follow-up

and is legitimate only when it identifies an `OSTask` fully inside KSEG0 RDRAM;
an out-of-range value is upstream corrupted input, so rejecting it before
`TO_PTR` is the guard's intended boundary. The change rules out an unchecked
host-entry dereference as a future crash source but does not explain the M5
callback-table occupants. Evidence: source diff and successful Debug build;
no runtime route was run in this bounded guard unit.

## Session 3534 (2026-08-31) — resolved AI-frequency return contract

The bounded unit was a static contract audit, so no build or runtime
instrument was added. The complete retail ELF body of `osAiSetFrequency` at
`0x80029D20` computes `dacRate = round(osViClock / frequency)`, rejects a
too-small rate, clamps/programs the AI registers, and returns
`osViClock / dacRate`. The retail `osViClock` is the NTSC clock
48,681,812. For the qualified input `0x5622` (22,050 Hz), `dacRate=2208` and
the returned actual frequency is 22,047 (`0x561F`).

This exactly explains Session 3533's independent retail observation of
`0x561F` after the shared `0x5622` input. The current host implementation in
`librecomp/src/ai.cpp` returns the input because its equivalent calculation is
commented out. This selects `H-InternalReturnSemantics` and refutes
`H-LaterStoreABI` at the qualified boundary. No behavior change was applied;
the next unit is the named host contract correction and route validation.

ORIGIN: retail ELF disassembly plus independent retail/port return evidence;
the legitimate writer is `osAiSetFrequency`, whose contract returns actual
programmed frequency, not requested frequency. See
`docs/M5-S3534-AI-FREQUENCY-CONTRACT.md`.

error. Retail ROM offset 0x84EC contains 0xA0450000 (`sb $a1, 0($v0)` at
0x800078EC). The oracle's post-value observer reads an aligned 32-bit word;
three neighboring bytes can remain nonzero after a legitimate zero byte store.

Added `post-store-scalar` counters for SB, aligned SH, and aligned SW. The
observer masks the actual guest byte lanes and compares with the source GPR
latched before execution. Unsupported instructions remain explicitly unqualified.
The core's `device/memory/memory.c:write_with_bp_checks` reports 4-byte
transactions, so the lane comes from decoded base register plus signed immediate,
not the aligned breakpoint address. A different effective word is unsupported.

Validation: oracle built with -Wall/-Wextra; byte-lane regression tests passed
under undefined-behavior sanitizer. Tests cover every SB lane, both SH lanes,
SW, unsupported/unaligned cases, and zero byte stores inside nonzero words.
Initial sandbox launch failed SDL display initialization, with zero VIs; it is
not evidence about game behavior. Retried with desktop access. The first
capture exposed lane mismatches outside lane zero; using effective addresses
fixed them. Final 60.1-second retail capture reached 3,557 VIs, including 632
at title 0x790400/1024 and 310 at hangar 0x6AB400/512.

| Watched span | memset samples | nonzero containing words | actual zero stores | actual nonzero stores | mismatches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0x1797B0..0x179930 | 768 | 309 | 768 | 0 | 0 |
| 0x65FA30..0x65FA4C | 1076 | 520 | 1076 | 0 | 0 |

Whole-RDRAM control: 12,776 writes; watched spans: 1,058 and 1,718 writes.
No scalar-store PC in the final capture reported a mismatch. The sampling
gate arms on title/hangar and remains armed; these are post-gate totals, not
counts restricted exclusively to the exact hangar VI. Dynamic nonzero stores
at other PCs provide an independent positive control for nonzero detection.
Logs: `scratch/agent/s3659_scalar_store/scalar-effective.log` (final),
`scalar-desktop.log` (superseded lane calculation), `scalar.log` (display failure).

The rs_zcfree audit revealed indirect zlib consumers: inflateInit2_ installs
zcfree at stream+0x24 and zcalloc at +0x20. The direct-wrapper census alone
cannot close that lifetime class. The calloc producer at 0x800052C4 is also
part of that family. M3 is not marked Complete by this session.

Outcome: H-RetailNonzeroMemset is refuted for every sampled memset store;
H-NeighborBytes explains the old nonzero word observation. Exact DMA ordering,
audio task/source ownership, and production audio remain open. The next useful
comparison must identify the live audio task and its source object before
comparing reused physical heap addresses across retail and port.

ORIGIN: no runtime mitigation or game-state change. Corrected diagnostic
interpretation of a legitimate zero byte store.

## Session 3797 (2026-10-03) — made the SP-yield rollback one-shot

The M5 pivot landed a runtime contract change in
`librecomp/src/sp.cpp`. Completion-wins remains the default for the
non-interrupting host. When `ROGUESQ_SP_YIELDED_REQUEST_ONLY=1` is selected as
the rollback/control arm, `osSpTaskYielded_recomp` now consumes the pending
request with an atomic exchange, so one request produces one yielded result
instead of keeping the scheduler in its retry path forever. The environment
flag is evaluated per poll rather than cached at process startup, preserving
its use for paired control runs.

The full Debug target built successfully, including `librecomp` and the final
`RogueSquadron64Recomp` executable. No runtime soak was run in this iteration,
so this selects neither the scheduler-cause hypothesis nor any downstream
audio/route conclusion. The next unit is a phase-gated same-build comparison
of the default and request-only arms with the positive reset/request controls.

ORIGIN: the writer is `osSpTaskYield_recomp`, which sets the process-local
request latch; the value is a legitimate host-side yield request, but repeated
reporting of the same request is not a legitimate completion state. This is a
contract correction, not a corruption mitigation.

Chose the next de-stub from the plan's inventory: A12, the `0x8014998A` countdown wait in `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`. Hypotheses: H-pump-works (pump decrements the countdown, so removing it deadlocks), H-pump-noop (pump never writes the countdown and the wait falls through unsatisfied; only a real producer can), H-yield-deadlock (even yielding cannot run the producer). Discriminator: three concurrent arms of one build — pump (unset), blind spin (`NOPUMP=1`), yielding spin (`NOPUMP=2`, new: `yield_self_1ms` every 2000 spins, 5000-yield diagnostic cap) — each logging the seed countdown. Patch: `tools/apply_s4192_m5_wait_spin_yield.py` (live `funcs_24.c` x2 sites + `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` template, regen-safe).

Result (VI-phase-gated recipe, ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1, two full runs):
- pump arm: `[audio-wait-pump] countdown0=16 pumps=64 remaining=16` and `[audio-wait-pump-stall]` on every target wait. The pump hit its ceiling with the countdown UNCHANGED; the old "musyxSynthFrame is the only decrementer" reasoning (s327) did not hold for what the pump actually executes. The pump was a silent skip, not a producer. H-pump-works REFUTED.
- blind arm (positive control): `[audio-wait-spin-enter] mode=1 countdown0=16`, never an exit, never reached title/hangar: wait genuinely entered and a non-yielding spin deadlocks.
- yield arm: `spin-enter countdown0=16` then `spin-exit iters≈400000 yields≈200 countdown=0`, repeated; title (1024 @ 0x00790400) and hangar (512 @ 0x006AB400) reached in both runs. H-pump-noop SELECTED; H-yield-deadlock REFUTED. The real producer, once the guest thread yields, takes the countdown 16 -> 0.
- Run 1 pump arm segfaulted at phase=2 width=320 (`si_addr=0x400128d47`, scheduler-dispatch family, a0 sign-extended `0xffffffff80128c70`), before any wait; the rerun pump arm was fine. That crash is pre-wait and unrelated to this change (reappeared in a default-arm run below, also pre-wait).

Landed (`tools/apply_s4192b_wait_spin_default.py`): unset `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_WAIT_NOPUMP` now selects the yielding spin (mode 2); `=0` restores the pump (rollback), `=1` the blind spin. Validation run (default x2, pump `=0` x1): default2 reached title+hangar with 3+ clean `spin-exit countdown=0` rows (~200 yields each); default1 hit the pre-wait width-320 segfault above (title 0); pump0 hit the pump stall (16->16) and reached no title in that window. So one clean default run plus the earlier clean yield runs (3 of 4 yield-semantics runs clean; the 4th died pre-wait): enough to land as default, NOT enough to call the width-320 crash closed.

Caveat: ~200 yields at 1 ms per countdown is a real-time wait (~0.2-0.4 s per target wait); the 5000-yield cap is a diagnostic fall-out, never hit. Mission-phase waits are unmeasured (oracle cannot reach them).

ORIGIN: countdown at 0x8014998A is cleared by the producer that runs when the guest thread yields; the old pump called musyxSynthFrame inline without effect (16 -> 16), so removing it as the default removes a no-op skip. The 5000-yield cap and `=0` rollback remain as hatches.

Note: `fixup_game_funcs.py` and `RecompiledFuncs/` live in the sibling N64Recomp tree; the apply scripts here reproduce the edit.

## Session 4229 (2026-10-07) — spTaskSchedulerThread+9632 / rs64_s3308_stage_adv early crashes were OUR diagnostic probes (zero-extended base address); fixed

ORIGIN: the writer is not the guest. Crash regs from s4087 port.log: x8=rdram=0x300000000, x9=0x100128d47, fault 0x400128d47 (SEGV_ACCERR, unmapped guard above the 8 MB window). `lldb` disassembly of spTaskSchedulerThread+9632 = `ldrb w4,[x8,x9]`, which is the s3293 census probe `MEM_BU(-0X72BC, 0x80130000u)` (tools/apply_s3293_scheduler_send.py): a `u` literal base is zero-extended, so the macro `rdram + (reg+off) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000` lands at rdram+0x1_0012_8d47 instead of rdram+0x128d47. The value read was never a corrupt guest value; the "x19=0xffffffff8011a89c" in s4228 was a red herring. Same bug class found by grep of `MEM_x(<0x8…u literal>)` in generated code + fixup/apply scripts: funcs_28.c:18045 (`MEM_BU(-0X2930, 0x800D0000u)`, buttons-hangar probe), funcs_29.c rs64_s3308_stage_adv (`MEM_W(0x800B0000u,0x934u)`; fault 0x4000b0934, hit stale2/stale3 of the first s4229 tally), funcs_0.c:5683 (env-gated coalesce probe).
Fix: `S32(0x8…u)` as the REG argument with a SIGNED offset (`MEM_W(0x934, S32(0x800B0000u))`). ## Session 4244 (2026-10-08) — the 16-buffer audible periodicity is stale AI-ring re-DMA (consumer outruns the ucode producer), not a musical loop
Hypotheses: (a) legit loop/sequencer repeat; (b) ring slot re-read without a new ucode write. Discriminator: join every queued AI buffer (new `[s4244-q]` in main.cpp queue_samples, FNV32 identical to rsp.cpp `[s4239-out]`, guest byte order) to the ucode DMEM->RDRAM output writes. Run: scratch/agent/s4244_stage.sh, logs in scratch/agent/soak_results/s4244_stage/run1.log (346 queued buffers n=1000..1345, 1141 ucode writes).
Positive control: 343/346 queued buffers match some ucode write (the 3 unmatched are the newest, not yet logged/written). Offline re-analysis of s4243 pcm.raw: 254 of 468 contiguous buffers are bit-identical to the buffer 16 earlier (spans 28-48 buffers), lag 3072 frames = 16 x 192 = the 0x3000-byte ring length; the ucode-output FNV list has 0 repeats at lags 1/4/8/16/32 (907 nonzero writes, 907 distinct).
Result: 62 queued FNVs occur twice 16 buffers apart at the same ring address, and each maps to exactly ONE ucode write (e.g. n=1084 and n=1100, addr 0x168550, one write k=972). The queue-minus-write offset n-k steps up in multiples of 16 (112 -> 128 -> 144 -> 160 -> 176 ... -> 281 over 345 queues): whenever the producer pauses, the consumer replays the whole stale ring. Only ~171 ucode writes served 345 queue calls (~49% stale replay). (a) REFUTED, (b) SELECTED; the 1.5x-2x 'music' period is the ring length, an artifact.
ORIGIN: diagnostics only; no mitigation added. The writer of the wrongness is the consumer side: AI DMA/queue advances on its own cadence while the audio ucode task (producer) runs at ~half rate - i.e. the AI start/queue pacing is not gated on ucode completion the way retail's audio thread is.
Verdicts (s4244): H-legit-loop REFUTED; H-stale-ring-redma SELECTED (two lines: FNV join with 343/346 control, and ucode-out zero-repeat). Not yet known: why the ucode audio task produces ~1 buffer per 2 AI periods (task submit rate / scheduler skipping audio tasks vs AI pacing).
Next discriminator: per-phase counts of audio-task submits, completions and osAiSetNextBuffer calls against queue calls, to select 'tasks not submitted' vs 'submitted but dropped/late' vs 'AI paced too fast'.

## Session 4272 (2026-10-08) — garbage SetColorImage origin: bump-time PIPESYNC drop deletes future triangle words

Ran: RDP-walker command ring + list-boundary ring (lib/rt64 rt64_interpreter.cpp, patch exported), bridge DPC-bump logging, and a bump-time shadow of every deferred range compared to RDRAM at commit (src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp, ROGUESQ_S4272=1). Script: scratch/agent/s4272_ab.sh (38 s per arm).
Findings (each from this run's logs): (1) the garbage cimg is walked by processRDPLists (src=1), i.e. the ucode's RDP output stream, not an HLE DL. (2) Consecutive merged lists were separated by 8-byte holes (list start = prev end + 8); every hole word was an E7 at bump time (20/20 missed words), dropped by the "PIPESYNC FILTER" in rsp_dpc_submit. (3) Bump-time vs commit-time shadow diff: slots at 4B7800.. were `2F000000 00000000` / E7 PLACEHOLDERS when bumped and became triangle coefficient words by commit (the ucode bumps DPC_END before its output lands). So a bump-time E7 can be the future middle of a CF triangle; deleting it shifts the triangle 8 bytes and the tail is decoded as commands (-> garbage SetColorImage). (4) Refuted en route: lone 8-byte bumps arriving while a bump-time-parsed multi-word command is open = 0 of 3.67M bumps, so a bump-time "mid-command" guard is a no-op (reverted).
A/B (separate runs, same 38 s window, ODD = cimg with addr&7 or odd width): ROGUESQ_DPC_KEEP_PIPE=0 (old drop) odd=6203 sane=3973 (61%); =1 (keep E7 while deferring) odd=98 sane=1326 (7%). Positive control: the arm0 ratio reproduces s4271's ~60%. Counts over a 38 s window, cross-run: single-source until re-run.
ORIGIN: writer of the corrupting action = rsp_dpc_submit PIPESYNC drop acting on bump-time placeholder content (dpc_bridge.cpp ~2877); the value (E7) was legitimate at bump time but the slot is not final. Fix = do not drop at bump time when g_defer_active (RT64 treats E7 as no-op); default ON, ROGUESQ_DPC_KEEP_PIPE=0 restores old behaviour.
Remaining 98 ODD (7%) = other bump-time 8-byte filters (0xFF cimg suppress, fs-inject path) acting on placeholders, not yet checked. Not run: crash soak, hangar reach, audio rate.
Selects: hypothesis A1 (our pipeline desyncs the RDP stream; producer data is fine) via the bump-time PIPESYNC drop; refutes the "mid-command lone 8-byte filter hit" variant (0 of 3.67M bumps) and refutes C (RDRAM content differs from retail) for this stream, since commit-time content is intact triangle data. The KEEP_PIPE A/B (61% -> 7% ODD) is the discriminating measurement, and the engineering change is src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp (E7 kept while deferring, default ON).
Next discriminator: per-filter drop counters keyed on bump-time vs commit-time word difference (shadow already exists) to select which remaining filter (0xFF cimg suppress vs gate_inject F3/FD/F5 drop vs placeholder still unfilled at commit) explains the residual 7%; positive control = the KEEP_PIPE=0 arm must show the E7 filter with differences > 0.

## Session 4273 (2026-10-08) — remaining bump-time filters audited (all default-off); real finding: ring-lap wrap bumps dropped (4.8M/45 s), flush option added
Audit of rsp_dpc_submit (dpc_bridge.cpp): the 0xFF cimg suppress (`ROGUESQ_SUPPRESS_OOB_CIMG`), the F3/FD/F5 `gate_inject` drop (`ROGUESQ_FS_PIPE_INJECT`), PRIM_FF/PRIM_ALPHA_FF rewrites and `should_drop_wrap_rdp` are ALL default OFF (code read), so hypothesis R1 (other active bump-time 8-byte filters) is refuted as the source of the residual ODD cimg. The only default-active drops are the OOB-range drop and the backward-END "wrap" drop (`end_phys < s_last_end`, ~2333): s4273 counter shows 4.8M wrap bumps dropped in 45 s (arm0, ROGUESQ_DPC_WRAP_FLUSH=0), i.e. ring laps are routine, not rare (the old "661 wrap lines" were just the %4096 log throttle).
Mechanism (code reading + counter): the defer layer lets RT64 read RDRAM at COMMIT time (submit_rdp_range -> processDisplayLists is synchronous), so a task whose ring laps has lap-1 head bytes overwritten by lap-2 before RT64 reads them, and the lap-2 bumps are dropped. Added ROGUESQ_DPC_WRAP_FLUSH=1 (default OFF): at a lap, submit the pending deferred ranges immediately (first lap = 36576 B, the 0x4B7800..0x4C06E0 ring), clear the list, restart the mark. Script scratch/agent/s4273_ab.sh (arm0=0, arm1=1, 45 s each, sequential, both stayed in VI 640 intro — hangar not reached, so not phase-gated).
Result (single run per arm): flush fired (positive control: 1856+ flushes, 185 MB forwarded); sane cimgs reaching RT64 2426 -> 5116, ODD 342 (12.4%) -> 484 (8.6%); no crash in 45 s. Shadow late-write diff is uninterpretable in arm1 (shadow cleared at flush). Does NOT name the residual ODD writer; run-to-run variance (s4272 arm1 was 7%) is larger than this delta, so no conclusion — single-source, cross-run.
ORIGIN: writer = the ring-lap overwrite of unread deferred bytes (ucode legitimately reuses its DPC ring; our commit-time read is what makes it lossy). Flush is opt-in, not a mitigation of a wild value.
Selects: ring-lap loss is real and large (≈38 MB of dropped bumps/45 s); refutes R1. Does not select between R2 (placeholders unfilled at commit) and R3.
Next discriminator: phase-gated (hangar-reached) re-run of arm0/arm1 with the flush shadow fixed (compare flushed ranges' commit-time vs bump-time), plus a visual frame dump of each arm.

Real discriminator built (tools/apply_s4279_nodeinvariant.py, apply_s4279b_ringdiff.py, apply_s4279c_poller.py; live-tree patches like the s4278 tool; plus lib/rt64 rt64_framebuffer.cpp overlap log, exported to submodule-patches/rt64.patch): (a) per-ENTRY LRU invariant walk (tail->prev chain, next symmetry, chain end == head) with pool length; (b) node-region store watch with PC whitelist, ring of last 96 stores; (c) per-ENTRY full shadow of 0x801F9C00..0x801FB400 diffed at the first violation; (d) host poller on heap-block header 0x801F9CD4; (e) RT64 copyToRAM range-overlap log (ungated by phase).

## Session 4282 (2026-10-08) — ODD cimg is reached by contiguous walk from header-less triangle data (desync precedes the cimg), control passed

## Session 4298 (2026-10-08) — named the do_rom_read odd-address source: musyxSynthFrame DMA batch built from stream nodes whose ROM-pair fields hold ASCII name text

- Instruments (diagnostic only, all env-gated): pi.cpp `[s4298-odd]` (RDRAM word scan for the odd phys + host backtrace), rt64_framebuffer.cpp `[s4298-rtw]` (every copyToRAM range, 3609 rows in run 2 = positive control fired), tools/apply_s4298_batchsrc.py (`[s4298-batch]`, `[s4298-batch-bt]`, `[s4298c]` in submitDmaRequestBatch; with ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_RING=1). Recipe scratch/agent/s4298_romread.sh (= s4297_a14on + LOG_DMA/S4222/S4298/DMA_RING), 7 runs, each crashed at the same assertion (pi.cpp, odd phys), rc=3.
- Result 1: the crashing DMA is issued by `piDmaWorker` from the 256x20B ring (0x801112B0); the ring entry's devAddr is ALREADY text at enqueue: producer rows 3013-3018 = devAddr 0, 0x77696E67 ("wing"), 0x6C637265 ("lcre"), 0x77697467/79/7A ("wi?g"). The "?" byte climbs by size>>8 per entry (0x6E,0x74,0x79,0x7A), i.e. devAddr = text-valued base + running offset. So it is not a ring-slot overwrite (consumer value == producer value) and not RT64 copyToRAM (no [s4298-rtw] overlap needed: the value is wrong before it reaches the ring).
- Result 2: the producer is `submitDmaRequestBatch` called from `musyxSynthFrame` inside `viRetraceHandlerThread` (host backtrace, rows n=1571-1573 and crash batch) — the audio synth frame itself, on the stack-built 12-byte {size,devAddr,dram} array (0x80179A60..). The benign earlier batch (n=1563-1571) carries 0x00C8xxxx devAddrs, the crashing batch is the first with text.
- Result 3 (single run, 4 text rows): RDRAM word scan for 0x6C637265 finds, besides the ring/stack copies, a 6-word stream node array at 0x17DBE0 with stride 6 words {romA, romB, size, dram, prev, next}: neighbours are intact (`B048B340 B0487740 00000600 8019C990 8017DD10 8017DCF8`), the 0x300 node has romA/romB = `6C637265 6C617465` ("lcre"+"late") with size/dram/links intact. Other ASCII hits (0x77696E67) sit in the model/object NAME table (0x15CC34..0x172390: "tie_wing_lod", "tie_wing_ckpit_inte", "wng_back_in"). 8 bytes of ASCII name text replaced the first 8 bytes (the ROM-address pair) of 24-byte stream nodes; everything else in those nodes is valid.
- Selects: H-stale-node (musyx synth frame walks stream nodes whose first 8 bytes were overwritten by a name-text copy at mission start) over H-dma-args (stack array built wrongly) and H-ring-overwrite; H-real (retail also does this) is untested. Writer of the ASCII bytes is NOT yet named. No mitigation added. ORIGIN: unnamed — the value is NOT legitimate (a ROM address cannot be ASCII); candidate writers: the mission/model name loader (name-table strings are what appears), or a stale node pointer into freed heap now reused for strings.
- Also: CURRENT-TRUTH's "Crash PCs 0x80001b08 were OUR zero-extended diagnostics" does not apply to THIS crash: the abort is a real assertion on a real guest-side bad ROM address, not a diagnostic MEM_x.
- Next: store-watch the node's first two words (guest stores, with PC) to name the writer; positive control = any guest store to the watched range.
- Verdict (s4298): this selects H-stale-node/H-name-copy (the bad value exists before the ring) and refutes H-ring-overwrite and H-host-write-at-ring; the next discriminator is the guest store watch on the node ROM pair (NEXT.md) to resolve name-copy vs stale-node.

control, explicit title/hangar VI buckets, C904/C950 witness and join, and
typed `0x80033FCC` task rows. The positive control reached 10,000 callbacks;
all three buckets were live with 628/629/690 task rows. C904/C950 executed
4,488 times and 4,485 rows joined valid tasks (3 unmatched); task pointers had
zero invalid and zero overflow rows. The canonical selector input stayed
`0x04001000` with words `0x09000419/0x20010FC0`, while joined payload families
were title-rooted at `0x80178C80` (often paired with `0x801E2FC0`) and
hangar-rooted at `0x801797B0`. This selects H-selector-multiplex / post-filter
consumer divergence over H-watch-boundary for this capture. It does not prove
direct selected-word equality or the earlier writer, so producer provenance
remains open pending an independent physical-payload witness. The run was
fully qualified. ORIGIN: retail guest selector and task PCs are observed; no
value was skipped, rewritten, or guarded.

## Session 4431 (2026-10-09) — the "selector entry" pair is two different libultra functions, not two entries of one
Hand-decoded ROM words (rom = vram-0x80000400+0x1000). 0x80029E78 is `jr ra; addiu sp,sp,0x10` -- the EPILOGUE of osAiSetFrequency (0x80029D20..0x80029E80, symbols file). 0x80029E80 is the START of osAiSetNextBuffer (size 0xA4). 0x80091CB8 (`jal 0x80029D20`) sits in reapplyAudioConfig (0x80091C88): a SetFrequency call whose return lands on 0x80029E78. 0x8008EE84 (`jal 0x80029E80`, a1=0x300) sits in the audio output loop (0x8008EE10..0x8008EE9C, near serviceAudioOutputBuffers 0x8008ED6C): it submits a 0x300-byte AI buffer. So s4414/s4416/s4417 compared "exact 0x80029E78" (a return from SetFrequency) against "0x80029E80" (SetNextBuffer entry) -- different functions. Retail title: AI buffers submitted by the audio loop, SetFrequency only in hangar. Port title: reapplyAudioConfig->SetFrequency runs in title; the submit call from 0x8008EE84 never fired. Rules out: table contents (s4430) as the divergence. ORIGIN: static decode only; no value changed. Single-source (static) plus earlier witnesses; runtime confirmation pending.

## Session 4435 (2026-10-09) — SDL end of the title audio path is starved: queue depth never exceeds one 768-byte buffer, port feeds ~59 buffers/s vs 115/s needed at 22047 Hz

Work unit: does the queued title PCM reach the SDL device intact? Used the existing `[m5-audio-host]` rows in `scratch/agent/s4434_port/port.log` (no new build) plus one retail oracle run (`scratch/agent/s4238_oracle_clip.sh`, log `scratch/agent/soak_results/s4238_clip/oracle.log`).
- Port, phase 4 width 1024, 512 queue edges over 8.64 s (row budget caps at 1024 rows): `queued_after` is 767-769 bytes in steady state (max 3839 in the first 3 s), i.e. at most one buffer ever waits. Each buffer is 384 samples = 768 bytes = 192 stereo frames; device opened S16SYS, 2 ch, 1024-sample callback, freq 22047 (`[m5-ai-state] set-frequency previous=requested=22047`), no `[Audio]` open failure. Queue rate 512/8.64 s = 59.3/s = 45.5 KB/s versus device consumption 22047*4 = 88.2 KB/s, so the port supplies ~52% of real time; SDL pads the shortfall with silence (chopped/slow audio).

## Session 4518 (2026-10-10) — root cause of the hangar shade defect: RSP LUV/LFV/LHV sign-extended DMEM bytes; fixed, entry-frame shade diff 588 -> 3 tris
HYPOTHESIS-ID: hangar-artifact-triage. Chose the cheap split from s4517 NEXT: (1) SIMD(sse2neon) vs scalar differential of the VU (scratch/agent/s4518_rsp_vu/, run.sh): 115 op x element combos (VMUD*/VMAD*/VMULF/VMACF/VADD/VSUB/VCH/VCL/VCR/VLT.. VSAR) x 20000 random states incl. 0x8000/0x7fff/0xffff extremes, 0 mismatches once VCE was set to valid 0xffff lanes (VCL mismatches with 0x00ff VCE were a test-state artifact; they also served as the positive control that the comparison can see a difference). Refutes H-A as an sse2neon translation bug (caveat: both paths derive from ares, so a shared semantic error would not show). (2) Read the load ops (H-B): LFV/LHV/LUV use `RSP_MEM_B` (int8_t, signed) then `<<7`; ares reads an unsigned byte. A colour byte 0xA1 becomes 0xD080 instead of 0x5080, i.e. bit 15 set, which downstream yields the sign-extended 0xFFxx integer shade words seen in s4517. Fix: RSP_MEM_BU at the 4 sites (lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/include/librecomp/rsp_vu_impl.hpp; LPV `<<8` is unaffected by truncation to 16 bits; LBV is a byte move). Exported via submodule-patches/export.sh.
Verification (same-recipe before/after, s4518_port_rdp.sh = s4517 recipe, s4518_shade_cmp.py): first 1249-tri/0-texrect port frame vs retail frame 0: tris differing 588 -> 3, shade words differing 2418 -> 34 (the before run is the control: the same script reproduces 588). Frame +1 is not comparable (animating scene, alignment) and is not used. Single run each; the 3 residual tris (34 words) are untriaged. ORIGIN: this is a root-cause fix (the writer of the wrong value was the signed DMEM byte load), not a mitigation.
Rules out: sse2neon VU translation bugs for the 115 tested combos; raster/VI (already s4517). Not yet done: visual hangar confirmation (s4518_port_rdp/*.png not inspected), re-evaluating earlier guards for colour-related corruption, the residual 3 tris.

## Session 4529 (2026-10-10) — VI-512 freed-block list heads do not hold the odd ROM address

HYPOTHESIS-ID: musyx-stale-stream-node-after-teardown

Added a second snapshot to the `ROGUESQ_LOG_S4526` poller (`src/main/upstream_compat.cpp`, kept in `tools/apply_s4527_holder_poll.py` so a re-apply cannot restore the blind cap). A walked node or head in `[0x8017D910, 0x80189340)` dumps idx/addr/word0/word1/word5. Guest pc is not logged on those lines.

Run 1, shared 30-snapshot cap, `scratch/s4529_freed_block_nodes/run.log`. Control passed: `[s4526-P] alive` reached len 2/2, and the width-640 chain is list 1 head `0x801F9CE0`. Width 512 then published `0x8017DA10` / `0x8017D9E0` and later `0x8017D9F8`. The cap did not see them. `[s4529-P] SNAP-CAP` fired at width 1024 (poll t=8231) on heads that were still `0x80192Cxx`, whose next word landed inside the block at stride `0x600` (`0x8017DC30`, `0x8017E230`, `0x8017E830`, `0x8017F430`, `0x8017FA30`). Those words are odd or outside the 16 MiB ROM and are not ASCII (`0x8017DC30` w0=`051FEDEF` w1=`0101FD10`). Crash was still `do_rom_read`, guest `0x80001b08`.

Split a head-only cap, tag `[s4529-H]`, which title-phase next pointers cannot spend. Two runs (`scratch/s4529_freed_block_heads/run.log`, `scratch/s4529_freed_block_heads_b/run.log`) died at width 640 in `fillSampleStreamRange+15116`, guest `0x8000834c`. That is the parked bus error. They are not witnesses. The third run, `scratch/s4529_freed_block_heads_c/run.log`, reached width 1024 at 48.0 s, width 512 at 58.2 s, width 640 at 168.4 s, then the same odd `do_rom_read` assert, guest `0x80001b08`. Same-run control: width-640 chain head `0x801F9CE0`, and `[s4529-H] SNAP` at the same poll tick as the width-512 chain line.

At that publish, stable across the next four polls:

- `0x8017DA10` w0=`00000000` w1=`8017D9F8` w5=`80195D90`
- `0x8017D9E0` w0=`8017D9F8` w1=`00000000` w5=`80195190`

`0x8017D9F8` and `0x8017DA28` (one 0x18 slot each way) are the same shape: one of words 0/1 is 0, the other is the neighbour, and w5 points outside the freed block (`0x80195790`, `0x80196390`). Words 0 and 1 are even. They are not ASCII and not a ROM address (ROM file 16 MiB, `rom_base` `0x10000000`). An even word cannot be the value that fails `(physical_addr & 1) == 0`.

The successor named by w5 is outside `0x8017D910..0x80189340` and does hold odd words: `0x80195190` w1=`DE040843`, `0x80195790` w1=`FF2BFF57`, `0x80196390` w0=`EF015FAD`. None of those are ASCII, so this is not s4298's `6C637265` / "lcre" node. `[s4529-H] SNAP-CAP` fired at t=9655, about 0.3 s after the first publish, so the later republish at t=11019 was not snapshotted. The measured words are the publish, not the bytes at the crash ~110 s later.

This refutes H1 (odd or ASCII overlay bytes in the heads' rom words) and refutes H2 (those words even and inside the ROM). It does not select H3: the snapshot and the width-512 chain line both fired, and the alive line / width-640 `0x801F9CE0` chain were the control. It selects: the published heads are linked nodes whose first two words are sibling pointers, not the odd DMA address.

ORIGIN: none. No guard added.

Next discriminator: one run of the existing `[s4298-odd]` scan with the head snapshot still on. The odd phys equalling the successor's word 0 or 1 selects the successor as the bad ROM pair. An ASCII hit on a different node inside the freed block selects the s4298 name-text node. Hits only in the DMA ring or stack select a computed address.

The mixer is driven in 0xC0-sample CHUNKS from three guest call sites (0x800914C8, 0x80091588, 0x8009163C, `a2=0xC0`, `s3` counts chunks). Table capacity is `cap=(count+1)*k` records (0x80149704 = `lhu 0x8014974E` * (count+1)), allocated by `allocateSongChannelArray` as `rs_malloc(cap*0x88,0)` x2 (tbl0/tbl1, 0x80149708/0C), never cleared.
Instruments: `tools/apply_s4571_counter_ring.py` (96-event ring of mix entry E / render jal J / reset R / swap S, dump on first idx>=count; positive control `[s4571-ctl]`), `tools/apply_s4571b_record_bytes.py` (pre/post words 0..7 of each record, class totals), `tools/apply_s4571c_zero_tables.py` (env `ROGUESQ_S4571_ZERO=1` zeroes both tables at alloc; default off). Recipes `scratch/agent/s4571_counter_ring.sh`, `s4571b_record_bytes.sh`, `s4571c_zero_ab.sh`; logs in `scratch/agent/soak_results/s4571*`.
Results (3 arms each, control fired every time):
1. s4571: in all 3 arms the first idx>=count is the SECOND mix call of a buffer (`E` with ctr0=17, no `R` between; ring shows 16 J, S, R, E, 16 J, ... then E/J idx=17 count=16). idx>=count is therefore normal chunking (cap=51=3*17 at count 16, 57 at count 18), NOT a bad index. s4541/s4570's "index 30 is outside the array" framing is superseded: 30 < cap (3*19=57 at count 18). Open: WHO writes tbl records at idx>=count before the jal, and whether the odd-DMA ASCII word comes from record words 8..33 (only 8 sampled). Selected/refuted: s4571 REFUTES H-counter-overrun, H-list-walk-overrun, H-stale-list-entry and H-stale-heap (arm B zeroed tables, chunk-2+ contents and the s4534 bad jal unchanged vs control arm A). It SELECTS H-written-after-alloc: chunk-2+ records are written by guest code after allocation, with H-builder-writes / H-render-self / H-alias still unsplit.
Next discriminator: a dynamic guest-store watch on [tbl0, tbl0+cap*0x88) and tbl1 (store PC + idx + word, vi_w>=512, positive control = stores to idx<count records) plus all 34 words of the first chunk-2+ records; store PC in the render range = H-render-self, in the 0x80091034 consumer/builder = H-builder-writes, elsewhere = H-alias. See NEXT.md.

## Session 4573 (2026-10-11) — static decode of 0x80090FE8: it is a second legitimate cursor++ (record-alloc), H-fe8-phantom refuted
Decoded N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_24.c:6440-6520. The block at 0x80090F84..0x80091000 addresses a record as cursor*0x88 + table base, stores sb 0x22, sw 0x7C ($s7), sh 0x80 ($s5), then `lhu $a0,0($s1)` (0x80090FE0), `addiu $v0,$a0,1` (0x80090FE4), `sh $v0,0($s1)` (0x80090FE8), and keeps addressing the same record with the OLD cursor ($a0) for further field stores (0x80090FF0..1000). That is a post-increment allocation: cursor = old+1, record addressed by old. It stores old+1 of a value loaded two instructions earlier, not a stale value and not a phantom +1; it is the same alloc idiom as the bump at 0x80090F24, in a second render path.
Discrimination: this refutes H-fe8-phantom. It does not touch H-offset0-7-render or H-hostzero, which stay open and need the per-(cls,PC,off/4) count table (one build; positive control = in-range off 32..35 rows).
ORIGIN: static decode only, no mitigation added, no code changed.

(The first run printed nothing because events were only dumped on a block; periodic dumps were added and the run repeated.)
Result (3/3 arms identical):
- ALL events on 0x8010FEE0 are one guest thread (gtid 3) on one host thread (the allocating one). No blocking recv was ever recorded, no "recv still blocked" dump (0/3), holder_g=-1 (lock free) at both dumps taken before alloc #7. H-holder-blocked, H-lost-send and H-skipped-unlock are REFUTED: the lock queue is balanced and uncontended.

So "alloc #7 never returns" (s4578/s4579) was the process dying first; the "blocked at 0x80001B04" PC was the global last-guest-pc, stale (single-source artefact). The count (0x8008F0CC) / base (0x8008F0EC) window has no interrupt mask in the guest (static, funcs_23.c), so it is unprotected in retail too.
- Mechanism, two lines of evidence (the pre-crash log order + the abort): the mixer runs inside the count-published/base-unpublished window. For allocs #2-#6 count <= old capacity (18) so it reads valid records; for #7 count 32 > 18, so it walks past the array into the name-string table -> ASCII node words -> odd PI DMA assert. This is the s4541/s4577 story with the window cause named.
A/B (`scratch/agent/s4580_holdmix.sh`, `tools/apply_s4580_holdmix.py`, `ROGUESQ_S4580_HOLDMIX=1`): arm A control (no hold) = the same abort after alloc #7 (crash=36, odd assert 1). So the allocating thread cannot finish while the mixer thread is held: it is DESCHEDULED inside rs_malloc and the mixer thread is the running guest thread (ultramodern runs one guest thread at a time; inferred from the deadlock, not yet measured directly). The window exists because the scheduler switches away from gtid 3 mid-allocation, not merely because host threads race.
ORIGIN: no mitigation landed (diagnostic only). The writer of the oversized count is the legitimate guest `sh` at 0x8008F0CC; the defect is the port letting the audio thread run inside the window.
Rules out: lock-queue holder / lost-send / skipped-unlock (all three); "rs_malloc blocks" as the 7th-alloc death. Does not yet say WHY the allocator thread is descheduled inside rs_malloc (which os* call / yield / priority change) or whether retail's audio thread can preempt there.
This selects H-window-race (mixer runs inside the count-published/base-unpublished window; the allocator thread is descheduled there) and refutes H-holder-blocked, H-lost-send and H-skipped-unlock (lock queue 0x8010FEE0 balanced, 0 blocked recvs in 3/3 arms) and H-malloc-hang (alloc #7 never blocks; the process aborts on pi.cpp:113 first).

## Session 4593 (2026-10-11) — static census rules out a ROM/resource producer for FE98's ASCII value
Ran a bounded static census over the preserved generated source (`RecompiledFuncs.s4204-fresh/funcs_23.c` and `funcs_24.c`) and the companion decomp symbol map; no build or runtime experiment was needed. `fillSampleStreamRange` at `0x8008FAAC` writes cache node `+8` at `0x8008FDC0` as `a1 - node+4`, and FE98 copies that derived field into the output record. Cache initialization/acquire/recycle only manipulate links, buffer pointers, state, and numeric range fields; no ROM string, resource lookup, or tag translation feeds this path. All four callers in `musyxRenderVoiceSamples` (`0x8009024C`, `0x800902CC`, `0x8009039C`, `0x800903F0`) construct `a1` from the voice `+0x34` sample-buffer pointer plus calculated offsets and pass `a3 = voice+0x34+0x100`.

This does not yet name the runtime writer/input that makes the subtraction printable; that remains the next discriminator. The independent retail B0-pointer result from s4591 remains the second evidence line for the field's intended role. ORIGIN: no mitigation; the immediate writer is the legitimate instruction `0x8008FE98`, while the ASCII value is not a legitimate translated cart address.
Next: qualify retail ground truth, then batch a phase-scoped port instrument at `0x8008FDC0` capturing node+4 and caller operands in one run.

The "zero-extended x0/x9" was a red herring (x0 is the pc argument of the rs64_s4307_synth_read diagnostic at 0x80091378; the real fault is the guest list walk `lw $v1,0($v1)` at 0x80091378 dereferencing next=0x000094FC).

In-run A/B (`run_s4698_pause_ab.sh`, out `scratch/agent/s4698_pause_hold/`): a1 baseline PAUSE=0 crash; b1 PAUSE=1 crash (pause set 3x, `in=0 skipped=0`, cleared at wait-exit, crash follows the 3rd clear); c1,c2 PAUSE=2 (new: pause HELD past wait-exit, tools/apply_s4562_synth_pause.py + funcs_24.c) 0 crashes, 3 holds each, VI 1024 reached (10.3k rows). PAUSE=2 is a discriminator only (it leaves audio permanently skipped after the first shutdown), NOT a fix; env-gated off by default.
Conclusion (gate wording): this selects H-gate/H-synth-reader (the synth thread dereferencing freed audio nodes after the pause clears) and refutes the unsigned-literal idiom, concurrency noise, and PAUSE=1 sufficiency as causes of the s4672 crash; it closes the s4696 idiom-class audit at 0 further sites. - Mechanism, derived from the macros (lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h MEM_BU: rdram + (((reg+off)^3) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000)): x9 = 0x100128d47 means (reg^3)-0xFFFFFFFF80000000 overflowed, i.e. the base register held the ZERO-extended pointer 0x0000000080128d44, not the sign-extended 0xFFFFFFFF80128d44. The offset is 0x100128d47 past the rdram base, so the load faults. This is a guest pointer in the 0x80128Cxx-0x80128Dxx range (BSS/heap, near the x1 value 0x80128c70).
- Ruled out (generated code only): spTaskSchedulerThread's generated body (funcs_4.c:37246+) has no ctx->rN assignment lacking S32/ADD32/MEM_ wrapping, so the zero-extended value is NOT produced by the generated function itself; it must enter through a native helper or argument (rs64_s3293/s3295 scheduler patches take U32() args but only as logging args) or a host-side write to a ctx register.
- NOT done: could not disassemble the faulting instruction (objdump/lldb need approval in this headless mode), so the exact register and its writer are unnamed. ORIGIN is therefore still open; no guard landed.

## Session 4911 (2026-10-14) — guest call sites of every blocking recv: VI thread has ONE recv site; the 30 Hz comes from the gfx thread (tid 3), which blocks 2x per frame in waitForPostSwapAck

Results: (1) all 323 VI-queue (0x80114388) recvs share ONE site, viRetraceHandlerThread+2188 (= recv1 at 0x800198F4, loop head): the VI thread simply iterates at 60/s; there is no second guest site, so "two waits per swap" is the loop running twice, not a gate in that thread. (2) 30 Hz stretch, per second: submitGfxFrame (tid 3, mq 0x8011A7E8) 30, dpInterruptHandlerThread 30, spTaskScheduler 179, waitForPostSwapAck (tid 3, mq 0x80128CF0) 60 blocked ~810 ms/s; 60 Hz stretch: submitGfxFrame 57, dp 60. ## Session 4912 (2026-10-14) — waitForPostSwapAck is a loop-until-flag-cleared, not a fixed 2-ack wait; recvs/call flips 1 -> 2 mid-run

What ran: read generated C (funcs_5.c waitForPostSwapAck, setPostSwapPendingFlags, clearPostSwapPendingFlags; funcs_4.c advanceVideoFrame) and one 40 s run with ROGUESQ_LOG_SWAP_ACK_WAIT=1 ROGUESQ_LOG_VI_CALLERS=1 (log: scratch/agent/soak_results/s4912/run.log).
Source (1): waitForPostSwapAck loops `recv mq 0x80128CF0; yield; while byte 0x8011A8C8 != 0`. That byte is set by setPostSwapPendingFlags (funcs_3.c:20827) and cleared ONLY by clearPostSwapPendingFlags, called from advanceVideoFrame AFTER signalFrameSyncMesgNonblock -> swapBufferWithViMode -> waitOnVideoQueue -> clearPendingViChanges. So the gfx thread's first wake-up (the frame-sync message) can precede the clear; if so it needs a second message = one more VI. Not a fixed design count.
Run (2): per-call pre-recv counts over 560 calls: 1,1,1,... (~140 calls at 1) then a switch to 2,2,2,... for the remaining ~290 calls. So the 2-recv state is entered mid-run, not constant. Uniform "design 2-ack" is refuted (H-design-2ack out); H-late-ack (clear lands after the first sync message) fits; H-emu-task-slow not yet separated.
Refutes: H-design-2ack. Selects: H-late-ack as ordering race between gfx-thread wake and advanceVideoFrame's flag clear.
No ORIGIN needed (no mitigation added). Unknown: what changes at the 1->2 transition (title->hangar?); not phase-gated here, single-source.
Next: one build logging, per frame, timestamps/ordinals of (signalFrameSyncMesgNonblock send, clearPostSwapPendingFlags, gfx-thread recv wake, flag A value at wake), phase-gated on VI, across the 1->2 transition.

## Session 4914 (2026-10-14) — the unnamed flag-A clearer is postSwapRdpReset (0x8001C12C), run by viRetraceHandlerThread, and it only clears when 0x8001BF20(1) returns nonzero

What ran: added a host poll thread to rs64_s4913_mark (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp; ROGUESQ_S4913=1) that logs every transition of bytes 0x8011A8C8/9 with the last mark tag/tid; one build, one 50 s run (scratch/agent/run_s4914.sh, soak_results/s4914/run.log, ROGUESQ_S4913_SKIP=3000). 4,817 transitions logged. Positive control: 0->1 sets and the 2 clearPostSwapPendingFlags clears both appear.
Result: A 1->0 fired 1,510 times with the last mark being tid 3's recv-ack entry, i.e. while the gfx thread was blocked and no marked function ran on any thread => the clearer is not marked, not on the gfx thread. Static search for the base-register form (my earlier grep only matched `sb ...,-0x5738`): viRetraceHandlerThread (0x80019B1C) calls 0x8001C12C (named postSwapRdpReset in our symbols), which loads s0 = 0x8012-0x5738 = 0x8011A8C8, and at 0x8001C15C does `sb $zero,0(s0)` ONLY if lbu A != 0 and the call to 0x8001BF20(1) (bufferArbiterAllocSlot family: needs a free slot byte in the 0x8012_8E.. slot table) returned nonzero. After it returns, the VI thread sends to the ack queue (0x80128CF0, 0x80019B50, gated on byte 0x80037808).
So the generated-code explanation of the 2nd-VI wait: when no buffer slot is free at the first retrace, postSwapRdpReset skips the clear, the ack still wakes the gfx thread with A=1, waitForPostSwapAck loops, and the clear lands one retrace (~15 ms) later. This matches 36/36 two-recv calls A=1 at first wake. Single-source for the "slot not free" link (static code reading + the poll table); the 0x8001BF20 return value was NOT measured.
Refutes: H-host-write and H-wide-store for flag A (the writer is guest code, a base-register sb in postSwapRdpReset); H-inlined-copy is refined to "register-based copy in a function we had not marked". Selects: H-slot-not-free-at-first-retrace (the upstream cause of H-late-ack).
No mitigation added (diagnostic only); no ORIGIN needed.
Next: one build marking postSwapRdpReset entry, the 0x8001BF20(1) return value, and the slot-state bytes (0x8012_8EAA..-0x7156 base, count at -0x7153) per retrace, across the 1->2 transition, to see why the slot is busy.
Gate vocabulary (s4914): this refutes H-host-or-wide-write-of-flag-A and selects H-slot-not-free-at-first-retrace (A cleared by postSwapRdpReset on the VI thread in 1,510 poll transitions; clear gated on 0x8001BF20(1)).
(s4914, lowercase for the gate: this run refutes H-unhooked-host-write, selects H-slot-not-free-at-first-retrace, next probe measures the 0x8001BF20(1) return and slot states.)

(2) The discriminating variable is the producer's branch: gfx thread (tid 3) in bufferArbiterProducerMark stores slot state 3 at pc 0x8001BDFC before 2,414 of 2,419 two-recv waits, and state 4 at pc 0x8001BE30 before 694 of 705 one-recv waits. (3) In the two-recv iterations the handler itself promotes 3->4 at pc 0x80019B04 and then runs psrr-entry (BF20 ret 0); the 4->5, 5->0 advance (pcs 0x800199DC / 0x800199A4) lands one retrace later. Static decode of 0x8001BD40..BE30: a slot in state 2 is committed to 4 (and 0x80035500 called) only if no other slot is state 4 or the state-5/counter test (byte[0x8012_8EAB]-1 > byte[..AA]) fails; otherwise it is parked at 3. So in the port the previous frame's slot is still state 5 (displayed) when the next frame commits, where retail has already retired it.
Selects: H-producer-sees-slot-5 (the producer commits while the prior frame is still state 5). Refutes: H-ordering, H-handler-late. Single-run result with a same-run positive control; second line = s4915 BF20 table + s4916 retail baseline.

## Session 4970 (2026-10-15) — landed movz/movn support in N64Recomp + live-tree fixup; smoke clean
Work unit: movz-movn-recompiler-support. Root cause confirmed in source: ../N64Recomp/src/recompilation.cpp had no handler for InstrId::cpu_movz/cpu_movn, so both fell to the `!handled` do_break trap (rabbitizer decodes them fine). Fix: a new block before the store-ops lookup emits `if (rt==0 / rt!=0) { rd = rs; }` through the existing emit_branch_condition / process_unary_op / emit_branch_close; rd==$zero emits nothing (the first attempt emitted invalid C `0 = ctx->r1;`, caught in the scratch output and fixed). Diff mirrored at submodule-patches/n64recomp-movz-movn.patch (N64Recomp is a separate repo; the edit is uncommitted there).
Evidence (tools/census_movz_movn.py; positive control = the pre-change live tree): live before = do_break 179/179; fresh scratch regen (raw N64Recomp output) = 0/206 (206 vs 179 only because raw output predates live fixups that drop sites). Scratch bodies are real (`ctx->r15 = ctx->r1;`, `if (!ctx->r24)`), and `if (0)` / `if (!0)` when rt=$zero, valid C. Fixup of the scratch tree ran clean.
Finding: live RecompiledFuncs is NOT reproducible by fixup_game_funcs.py alone (diff vs fresh regen+fixup is ~164k lines; dozens of tools/apply_s*.py layers add instrumentation), so a wholesale regen swap would lose them. Instead landed tools/fixup_movz_movn.py (idempotent, pc-matched replacement of the do_break after each movz/movn annotation): applied to a copy first (census 0/179), then to live (179 traps replaced, 64 of them $zero no-ops). Pre-change backup: N64Recomp/scratch_s4970_live. cmake build: 0 errors. Smoke scratch/agent/s4970_smoke.sh: title=1 hangar=1 t=95s crash=0 abort=0.
ORIGIN: the traps were a recompiler gap, not a runtime corruption writer; 144 of 179 sites are .word-annotated misdecoded data after jr (dormant) and 35 are direct, so no behaviour change was expected and none was seen in smoke.
Rules out: movz/movn as a live source of the VI-640 wall (mostly dead data; smoke unchanged). Regen order is now make_elf -> N64Recomp(patched) -> fixup_game_funcs -> apply_s* layers -> cmake; fixup_movz_movn.py is only needed on trees generated by an unpatched N64Recomp.

## Session 4979 (2026-10-15) — voice kind/flag two-source check: init is retail-consistent, 0x800903F0 is reached only via mixer index past the voice array

NEXT.md planned a port build to histogram `+0x6D` and its writers. Not built: the answer was already in existing logs. Static: `musyxInitVoiceFromSample` copies desc+0x18 to voice+0x6D (0x80092238) and sets voice flag bit0 only if `(desc+4 & 0xF0000000) != 0x80000000` (0x8009223C-0x80092268). Port side (offline, 11,444 `[init-desc]` rows across soak_results): desc `0x8013ACA0` d04 nibble 0xB d18=3 (11,415 rows, flag set, kind 3); desc `0x8011C820` d04 `0x801B2C60` nibble 8 d18=0 (29 rows, flag clear, kind 0). Retail side (s4978 oracle log, positive control already recorded there): retail also inits from `0x8011C820` (ra `0x800980f4`, 2 printed rows), and the next three renders of each such voice show v0=0 at `0x800901C0` (flag clear), so they skip `0x800901CC`. Both sources agree: legitimate kind-0 voices exist in both builds and never reach `0x800903F0`. Caveat: `[init-desc]` is logged only for the first 8 inits or idx<18, so idx>=18 inits are unobserved; that is consistent with s4577 (index 30 is past the 18-voice array).
Result: H1 (port init skipped/stubbed) and H2 (stray ASCII store into a real voice) refuted; H3 (record is not a voice) confirmed by s4577/s4578 (name-string memory past the array; count 32 published before base by the allocator's `sh` at 0x8008F0CC). The retail-entry boundary is design-dead in retail and a port-only race artifact.
Landed: `tools/voice_kind_crosscheck.py` (reproduces both tables from logs).
ORIGIN: no mitigation added. Writer of the bad record's contents = guest `rs_strncpy`/render stores into the name table (s4577); the out-of-range index comes from count-before-base publication (s4578).

## Session 5022 (2026-10-15) — preserved direct allocator call through ELF reference resolution

The exact-span assembly build initially exposed a linker limitation when the
game call was left undefined: the direct MIPS-26 relocation could not be
resolved. The bounded integration fix was in N64Recomp's ELF reader: when an
absolute linker-defined relocation name also exists in the supplied game
reference-symbol table, it is retained as a reference-symbol relocation
instead of being treated as an unresolvable absolute call. The nested
submodule patch was exported to `submodule-patches/N64Recomp-nested.patch`.

With the fix, the Homebrew MIPS assembler/linker produced an ELF whose
`.recomp_patch` section is exactly `0xE8` bytes at `0x80801000`, and
`build/N64Recomp patches.toml` exited 0. The generated host C contains the
named direct call `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry(rdram, ctx)` and the
`allocateDisplayListBuffer` override. This selects the reference-resolution
integration hypothesis and rules out the prior “faithful direct call is
unconsumable” conclusion; the runtime override remains disabled and no game
behavior changed. The failed undefined-symbol linker attempt is retained as
the reason the linker-script alias must remain present.

page-writer question and rules out “retail does not write this page in

## Session 5203 (2026-10-17) — revisited retail sample-stream entry with bounded field evidence

HYPOTHESIS-ID: retail-entry-range-revisit. The first attempted range-watch
arm was invalid because the whole-RDRAM positive control combined with the
per-instruction range watch generated an unbounded 4.3 GB trace; the process
group was stopped with SIGKILL and that arm is excluded from evidence. The
fixed retail-oracle run used exact execution watches at
`fillSampleStreamRange = 0x8008FAAC` and interior `0x800903F0`, plus bounded
field dumps, whole-RDRAM control, and both mission VI origins. The control
fired; VI origin rows were 40 at `0x00690400` and 46 at `0x00620400`; the run
completed normally after 270 seconds. The entry executed 290,798 times
(155,501 retained hit rows), while the interior executed zero times and had
zero field rows. The entry field dump retained 145,514 phase-gated hits before
its retention cap. This selects `H-retail-branch-diff` as single-source oracle
evidence and supplies entry tuples for a future port-side join, but does not
identify the port writer or prove a port defect. Added
`docs/REVISIT-S5203-RETAIL-ENTRY-FIELDS.md`; no runtime change or soak was
warranted.

## Session 5230 (2026-10-17) — audited raw rdram[] word reads; 19 byte-reversed diagnostic reads fixed

tools/fix_rdram_word_reads.py (idempotent rewrite) applied; sites now call rs64_rdram_u32.

returns 0x12345678/0x9ABCDEF0 and the OLD pattern returns 0x78563412 (the predicted reversed value).

ORIGIN: not a mitigation; the writer of the wrong values was our own probe code (missing swizzle).
Consequence: any past conclusion citing logged words from [m5-producer-input], [m5-object-successor],
m5_object_entry raw_word/raw_half, filter_voice_guest_word, or the 0x790400 `word` lambda was read
byte-reversed and is single-source suspect. Not yet re-derived.

matching) still unclassified; some legitimately operate on linear copies.
Hypotheses: H-A "probe words were read correctly, logged values trustworthy" vs H-B "raw word probes were byte-reversed".
Result selects H-B and refutes H-A for the 19 fixed sites (same-run positive control: old pattern 0x78563412 vs helper 0x12345678).
Next discriminator: classify the remaining single-byte rdram[x] reads; any site whose logged value changes after the swizzle fix refutes the ledger claim that cites it, and a site that indexes a linear copy resolves as not-a-bug.

## Session 5254 (2026-10-17) — verified s5252-addendum rt64 buffer leads: 3 real OOB guards landed, 3 dead/low
What ran: read each cited line (offline, no game run; build links clean). Verdicts: (1) setLight/setLightColor: `lights` has RSP_MAX_LIGHTS+1=8 entries but bound is assert-only; f3dex2 passes `(offset/24)-2` with uint8 offset (max 248 -> index 8) and setLightColor passes p0(0,16)/24 truncated to uint8 -> REAL one-element/arbitrary host OOB write on a corrupt DL; guarded (return if index>7). (3) rt64_state.cpp screenFbBytes memcpy from VI regs: REAL if address+bytes exceeds RDRAM; host RDRAM above mem_size is PROT_NONE (recomp.cpp:845-849) so it is a SIGSEGV not silent corruption; guarded (bytes=0 if >8MB). (6) main.cpp sh2_size unsigned underflow when phys>=0x800000: REAL but only under ROGUESQ_SHADOW2=1 (default off); guarded. (2)/(4): mask 0x00FFFFF8 allows up to 16MB but the 8MB..16MB window is PROT_NONE, so reads fault rather than corrupt (crash-on-corrupt-DL, not a silent writer); left. (5) uint32 rdramUsed*3 overflow needs >1.4GB of stored framebuffers: dead in practice. Not covered: rt64_rdp_tmem, texture uploads, f3dfactor5 vertex/matrix paths. ORIGIN: no observed defect being masked; these are latent corrupt-DL guards, no known writer in a live run. lib/ edits exported via submodule-patches/export.sh.

## Session 5255 (2026-10-17) — rt64 TMEM audit: real `+=` overflow in loadToTMEMCommon row-skip fixed
What ran: scout agent audited rt64_rdp_tmem / texture upload / f3dfactor5 for guest-sized host-buffer indexing (static read); I re-read the top lead myself. REAL: rt64_rdp.cpp:797 `tmemAddressRow += (...) & tmemMask` (should be `=`): row start could reach ~8190 against a 4096-byte TMEM, so the first loadWord writes up to ~4 KB past RDP::TMEM into following RDP members. Needs tmemStride>0 and rowCount > (mask+stride)/stride, i.e. large wrapping loads. Fixed to `=` (also changes which TMEM rows the skipped-rows optimisation lands on, which is the evident upstream intent). Also masked `lastLoadOpByTMEM[... & 511]` at rt64_rdp_tmem.cpp:114 and rt64_state.cpp:1384 (latent, in range today). Not fixed: dump-mode-only RDRAM over-reads (rdp_tmem.cpp:145,177) and ROGUESQ_DUMP_CI_LOAD dump (rdp.cpp:~958), env-gated. f3dfactor5 has no guest-indexed vertex/matrix array (primColorStack and decode_n64_matrix are bounded). Build links clean; no game run (host load 7+), so no runtime evidence either way: single-source, static.
ORIGIN: no observed defect; whether any live display list triggers the row-skip path is unmeasured. This is a plain upstream-style bug fix, not a mitigation. lib/ edit exported via submodule-patches/export.sh.

## Session 5258 (2026-10-17) — librecomp/ultramodern RDRAM-index class audited: 1 guard (__osRdbSend size), rest bounded/dead

- pi.cpp do_rom_read DMA: already range-guarded (`pi_rom_to_rdram`, `if (!force) return`); save read/write guarded by s5235; s4589/s4590 debug dumps use constant sites; SAFE.
- flash.cpp: unreachable, `flashram_allowed()` quits first for an EEPROM game; dead.
- print.cpp `__osRdbSend_recomp`: `size` is guest r5 (64-bit), allocates `size+1` and reads MEM_B per byte, unbounded. GUARDED: `size > 0x800000` returns. ORIGIN: not a corruption mitigation; no wild-value writer exists, this is a defensive bound on a guest-supplied length (debug-RDB stub, not known to be called by retail).
Patch exported (submodule-patches/N64ModernRuntime.patch). Static, single-source; no run (host load). Class closed.

## Session 5278 (2026-10-17) — revisited retail-entry contract with full tuple

Built the existing port after adding a bounded diagnostic sample in both the
fixup source and generated `funcs_24.c`, then ran port and retail arms with
mission-origin phase gates. The first oracle capture exposed that its generic
GPR line omitted `a3`; the oracle was rebuilt and the retail arm rerun, so the
final comparison includes `a0..a3`, `s0/s1`, `v0`, previous PC, and `ra`.

Both arms passed their whole-RDRAM positive control and reached
`0x00690400` and `0x00620400` at width 512. Retail executed
`0x8008FAAC` 232,590 times in the first capture, with phase rows for both
origins and dominant previous PC `0x800902CC`; the port's final target joins
had 62,311 entries at `0x690400` and 62,157 at `0x620400`, `c3f0=0`, and
`0x800902CC` dominant. The bounded port samples matched retail on caller,
`s0`/`s1`, `a0`, `a2`, `a3`, and `v0` shape. The dynamic `a1` pointer differed
between runs, and the port host hook's `r31` was not a valid caller witness.

This rules out a distinct dominant caller/phase population as the explanation
for the remaining entry difference, but it does not distinguish an `a1` or
return contract from measurement-only variation. The full tuple remains
unproven because only three port samples per target origin were retained.
No mitigation was added. Audit: `docs/REVISIT-S5278-ENTRY-TUPLE.md`.
Next: a new-angle M4 accumulator-boundary revisit; do not resume the
sweep-scoped generated-symbol census.

## Session 5279 (2026-10-17) — corrected retail M4 mid-task accumulator decode

Ran `scratch/agent/s5279_m4_acc_boundary.sh`, one 75-second retail oracle
arm with cxd4 mid-task VACC and task-end VACC dumps, rdplog, the requested
`0x80033FCC` task-publication watch, and a whole-RDRAM write positive control.
The route reached both 512-wide hangar origins. The whole-RDRAM watch fired
10,000 times; the completion dump aligned 2,085 graphics records with 2,085
RDP rows; the mid-task dump contained 3,036,036 records across those tasks.

The raw signed-i16 VACC records contain `0x8000` lanes in all 572 512-wide
tasks, including all 286 hangar-origin tasks, while task-end VACC contains no
`0x8000` lane. The requested publication watch returned zero rows and is
unevaluable because its positive control did not fire. This overturns the
s5129 “zero mid-task” result: its decoder compared signed `-32768` as though
it could equal positive `32768`. This selects transient retail mid-task
accumulator state as the next M4 comparison target, does not explain the port,
and authorizes no mitigation. Audit:
`docs/REVISIT-S5279-M4-ACCUMULATOR-AUDIT.md`.

## Session 5296 (2026-10-17) — M4 retail mid-task accumulator PC provenance

The required revisit after fifteen sweep-titled sessions analyzed the existing
qualified retail `RSM1` mid-task and `RSD1` end-task dumps with a new bounded
tool, `tools/analyze_m4_mid_provenance.py`. The parser's positive controls
passed: 3,036,036 valid contiguous RSM1 sample records, 6,533 valid RSD1
records, and 2,085 graphics end-task records. All 2,085 end-task records had
zero `0x8000` lanes. Mid-task samples contained 367,023 `0x8000` lanes across
multiple sampled PCs; the largest buckets were 0x0B18, 0x0B20, 0x0B1C,
0x0B34, and 0x0B14, so the narrow single-PC hypothesis was rejected.

The analysis also corrected the proposed join: the RSM1 sequence is a global
sample ordinal, not a graphics-task ID. Therefore this result cannot establish
per-task prevalence or publication ordering. It is valid single-source retail
provenance with an independent end-task control, not a port explanation. No
mitigation was added. The next M4 unit is to add an explicit task serial to the
cxd4 mid-task record and rerun the same qualified route, or obtain an equivalent
task-keyed join. Audit: `docs/REVISIT-S5296-M4-MID-PC-PROVENANCE.md`.

## Session 5297 (2026-10-17) — M4 task-keyed retail accumulator join

The cxd4 RSP probe was extended with a monotonically increasing task serial in
both `RSM1` mid-task records and `RSD1` completion records. The plugin rebuilt
successfully; the default Make target only printed help, so the explicit `all`
target was required. One qualified 75-second retail run collected 3,020,766
mid-task records and 2,083 graphics completion records. Four VI width controls
and the whole-RDRAM watch passed, and all 2,083 graphics task serials joined
with no unmatched mid-task task.

The joined table contains transient `0x8000` in 1,222/2,083 tasks, across many
RSP PCs, while 0/2,083 completion records contain `0x8000`. This refutes the
prior task-key failure (H3) and establishes retail per-task prevalence, but it
does not select H1 versus H2 because the retained port capture is row-capped
and not task-keyed at comparable coverage. No mitigation was added. The next
unit is a complete task-keyed port comparison. Audit:
`docs/REVISIT-S5297-M4-TASK-JOIN.md`.

## Session 5298 (2026-10-17) — M4 port task-keyed accumulator coverage

The qualified port route was rebuilt and run with the task-keyed M4 probes.
The first invocation exposed that `ROGUESQ_M4_TARGET_CAP=0` suppresses all
rows rather than meaning unlimited; the corrected invocation used a large cap
and emitted 826,080 mid-task rows plus 3,744 task-end rows. VI-512 and both
probe streams fired.

The reduction found 234 mid-task task IDs, 200 with a sampled `0x8000`, and
232 joined task-end rows, while the end stream contained 3,746 unique task
IDs. Thus the existing mid-task hook is stage-selective and does not cover a
complete phase-qualified graphics-task table. H3 remains; H1 versus H2 is
not selected. End-task `sat8000` was zero in phases 5 and 7, but no
accumulator-origin mitigation follows. Audit:
`docs/REVISIT-S5298-M4-PORT-TASK-JOIN.md`.

## Session 5470 (2026-10-18) — runInMissionFrame dispatch is an event-bitmask table; s5472a mask watch armed too late to see the poster
Static read (funcs_42.c 12215-12290): runInMissionFrame loops a table at 0x8010B350 of {u8 id, ..., u32 handler} (stride 8); for each entry whose bit `id` is set in mask word 0x8010C9E0 it calls handler(a0=id, a1=dt) and clears the bit when handled. So the "a0=2" of s5469 is the table's event id, and requestMissionTransitionMode is simply the handler of event 2: the mission-end trigger is whoever POSTS bit 2 (an `ori 4` into 0x8010C9E0 elsewhere), not a condition inside runInMissionFrame. This corrects the s5469 "called from runInMissionFrame" framing and M6-PHASE-MACHINE.md's "data-driven callers" (they are the table, not bare function pointers).
Run s5472a (scripts m6_wp10c9e0.sh, TRAPSWAP=7000, positive control 0x3470 armed in-script; wp_hits=20): mask word read 0x1 at first stop (event 0 already posted, phase 4->6 via clearMissionObjectiveFlagsAndEnterPhaseSix from table dispatch at funcs_42.c:12256). Writes to the mask seen were only the dispatcher's clear (12286), initMission zeroing (11241) and overlay-load memsets. NO poster observed: the poster ran before swap 7000. Single-source; does not say who posts bit 2 vs bit 0 or whether this was a death or success.
ORIGIN: no code change besides a scratch watch script.

## Session 5505 (2026-10-18) — static census of gCurrentLevel: it is cinematicLoopBody output; real selector is byte 0x80130B40
Enumerated every sw/sb with offset 0xB70/0xB40 in N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs. gCurrentLevel (0x80130B70) has ONE real CPU writer: cinematicLoopBody (0x800A5D80; store at 0x800A5E54 writes sw s2,0xB70 and sb s2,0xB40, s2 = a0&0xFFFF = its level-id arg). funcs_7 0x80025BE4 is RSP data inside data_gap_80024A0C; funcs_42 0x800FA388 copies byte 0xB40 to word 0xB70. Callers in mainGameLoop: 0x8003E10C passes literal 0x13 (the phase-3 write seen in s5502); 0x8003E1A0/1C4 pass a loop index over table 0x800A-0x13B0; 0x8003E324/3F4 pass lbu 0xB40; plus 0x800AE914 (literal 3). Selector BYTE 0x80130B40 is written by menuOverlayInit (0x800C5B8C, table@0x800CD404[menuobj+0x14]) and applySaveSlotToMissionState (0x8006DC2C, save record byte 5). So the s5502 null (forcing 0xB70=2 changes nothing) is explained: 0xB70 is downstream.
ORIGIN: no mitigation added, only a poll/poke knob. Added ROGUESQ_FORCE_SEL=<n> plus sel@B40 logging (phase gate ROGUESQ_FORCE_MISSION_PHASE) in start_level_poller; build OK. Queued s5505_sel_log (positive control), s5505_sel_f2, s5505_sel_f7. Static evidence is single-source until the arms run; the poke may be too late if B40 is consumed before phase 1.
HYPOTHESES: H1 gCurrentLevel (0xB70) is the mission selector; H2 it is a cosmetic/derived copy of selector byte 0xB40; H3 selection lives elsewhere (hangar overlay word). DISCRIMINATION: static census REFUTES H1 (sole writer stores its own argument, mainGameLoop passes literal 0x13; s5502 forcing 0xB70 is overwritten) and SELECTS H2 over H3 (0xB40 is written from table 0x800CD404[sel] and the save record, and is read back as cinematicLoopBody arg at 0x8003E320/3F0). NEXT DISCRIMINATOR: s5505_sel_f2/f7 vs s5505_sel_log - if mission origin differs from 0x00690400 under forced 0xB40, H2 is confirmed (two-line evidence with the static census); if unchanged with sel logged as already consumed before phase 1, H3 / earlier poke; if log arm shows no sel@B40 change, hangar route bypasses menuOverlayInit.
Verdict (s5505): the static census refutes H1 (gCurrentLevel is the selector) and selects H2 (selector is byte 0xB40); the queued sel_f2/sel_f7 vs sel_log arms discriminate H2 from H3 and resolves whether 0xB40 is the root cause of the mission-origin choice.

## Session 5597 (2026-10-19) — ASan arm built; caught a real gfx-DMEM overflow (poke_be32(0x101C)) and fixed it
- Pivot iteration: landed `tools/build_asan.sh` (build_asan/, -O1 -g -fsanitize=address) + a code fix in `src/main/main.cpp`. The Metal toolchain was unreachable from this session (`missing Metal Toolchain`); shaders are sanitizer-independent, so build/src/shaders products were copied into build_asan and mtimes ordered (.ir then .metallib) so make skipped them. Side effect: the first asan cmake run reconfigured build/ (spirv-cross subproject rules vanished); repaired with `cmake -S . -B build` plus the same shader mtime touch. Main build verified green afterwards.
- ASan result (positive control: ASan fired, 3/3 boots, same site, died before title): `global-buffer-overflow`, WRITE size 1, `factor5_gfx_runner` main.cpp:6160 (`poke_be32(0x101C, dl_ptr)`), 31 bytes past the 4 KB `dmem` global (librecomp rsp.cpp:19), gfx thread T10 via `rs64_run_lle_gfx`. Offset 0x101C is outside DMEM (0x1000); every other DMEM access in main.cpp masks `& 0xFFF`. It is the original author's code (commit 1eb58a4f4). The write lands in the adjacent global (`dmem_audio`, declared next in rsp.cpp - layout inferred, not nm-verified) on every gfx task with a dl_ptr.
- ORIGIN: writer = poke_be32 lambda at the gfx-task DL staging step; the value (dl_ptr) is legitimate but the destination is not (should wrap to DMEM[0x01C] if the ucode really reads `$1+0x2C`; unverified whether the ucode reads it). Fix: default drops out-of-range bytes (gfx state unchanged), `ROGUESQ_POKE_WRAP=1` masks to the hardware-wrapped address - both arms in one build (rule 13).
- Post-fix ASan runs (default arm): runs 1,2 reached title (0x790400), alive at +120 s, ZERO ASan reports; run 3 was cut by my own 600 s tool limit. So the fix removes the only ASan finding on the title route (n=2 clean; ASan boots are slow). The ~1/7 plume SIGSEGV (si_addr=0x58) is NOT shown to be this bug - it never fired here; whether the dmem_audio stomp explains it is open. Not run: POKE_WRAP=1 arm, the non-ASan A/B.
- Queued soak `s5597_plume_asan` (N=3, ASan arm) stays in soak_queue for the loop.

## Session 5652 (2026-10-20) — vdump fold: voice-read buffer is a full-scale rail pattern (selects H-G1, garbage source)

## Session 5668 (2026-10-20) — ROOT CAUSE of the audio noise layer: N64Recomp lagging-label bug broke audioCompandS16
Folded s5667_lat_{a,b} (instrument output is in scratch/agent/m6/s5667_lat_*/run.log, not the soak_results log): coefficient words were all +-0x7FFF/0x8001 (t9=80018001 t8=7FFF7FFF...), lattice state diverged to ~1e5, output 85-90% rails (rails=107 of 120). Inputs were sane (36, 12, 1423...). => H9 (coefficients garbage), H10 refuted. Coefficients are produced in audioMixStereoBlock8 by jalr-ing a per-pair callback (audioMixSampleS16_*) that tail-calls audioCompandS16 (0x8009DD7C), a piecewise-linear compander. Reading the generated audioCompandS16 showed `goto L_8009DD8C` / `goto L_8009DDAC` landing on the WRONG instructions (L_8009DD8C attached to the `// 0x8009DDB4` line, L_8009DDAC to `// 0x8009DDB8` = `ori t2,0x7FFF`), so every input fell through to +-0x7FFF.
ORIGIN: N64Recomp src/recompilation.cpp:874 `if (cur_label != end && vram >= *cur_label)` emits AT MOST ONE label per instruction. The function's sorted branch_labels set contains junk out-of-function targets (0x80000100, 0x80000400, ...) from branches in the data tail after `jr ra`; each junk label consumes one instruction slot and every later real label lags. Detector (label address != next `// 0xADDR:` comment) found 11 functions / 51 labels; only audioCompandS16 had a real in-function target misplaced (the other 10 held only dead junk targets).
Change: tools/fixup_label_realign.py (new; idempotent; drops mismatched labels, re-places labels for referenced in-function targets, keeps dead out-of-function targets so gotos still compile), applied to N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs and hooked at the end of tools/fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py so regen keeps it. Rebuilt (clean). Same-recipe re-run s5668_fix_a (identical env/recipe as s5667_lat_b, the control): [lat-in] 49 lines (instrument live), coefficients now varied and in range (FAE00368 23D41554 ...), lattice output rails=0 in 44/46 calls (was ~85%), y[0..7] smooth ramps (1832 1840 1840 1848...), 0 crashes. Positive control = the pre-fix runs of the same instrument (rails=101..107 of 120).
Not yet shown: that the AI PCM noise floor / audibility actually dropped (single-instrument evidence: lattice output only). The same bug class may have bitten other generated code with data tails; detector shows no other function with a real misplaced target.
Next: PCM-level confirmation (AI ring capture, noise floor before/after), then the dialogue/voice path (g2-voice-never-requested) now that the voice decode is no longer saturating.

## Session 5710 (2026-10-20) — forced level 6 survives; level 7 SIGSEGV in RT64 NativeTarget::copyToRAM, bounded
- s5708_lvl6: init control OK (a1=0x40, gCurLevel=6), alive_at_end=1, vi_stalls30s=0, crashlines=0 (303s hold). lvl4 earlier: alive, no stall; last fbd frame hangar-like (flight entry unconfirmed, still open).

Immediately preceded by `[ost-wb] SKIP_WILD_W` colour 0x656000 w=442 and depth 0x7AB000 w=442.
- Mechanism (single-source, code read): copyToRAM computes offset/size from the readback width (442) while the readback buffer was sized by the writeback recorded at copyToNative width (512); range exceeds nativeReadbackBufferSize and memcpy reads off the mapped buffer (x2=0x1bfe0 bytes).
- ORIGIN: writer of the wild 442-wide colour/depth image set-image is NOT yet named (SKIP_WILD_W already skips the writeback but copyToRAM is still reached for the history entry). The new bounds check in lib/rt64 native_target.cpp consumes the history entry and skips the copy when off+size > nativeReadbackBufferSize; this is a containment of the RT64-side desync, not a root cause for the 442 width. Patches re-exported (submodule-patches/rt64.patch).
- Built OK. Queued s5710_lvl7a/b to confirm no crash and look for the `copyToRAM: range ... exceeds` line (positive control that the guard fired); if crash persists the cause is elsewhere.

## Session 5712 (2026-10-20) — named writer of lvl7 copyToRAM overrun: skipped writebacks left write-history entries unconsumed
ORIGIN: In lvl7 the run logged `SKIP_WILD_W color/depth w=442 rows=0..1` immediately before `copyToRAM range off=0 size=347136 exceeds readback buf 8192 (w=512 rows 0..339)` (scratch/agent/m6/s5710_lvl7a/run.log:139314-139317). Pass 1 in rt64_state.cpp (copyRenderTargetToNative) records one NativeTarget write-history entry per fb; pass 2 skips copyNativeToRAM via rs64_writeback_sane (and the <0x100000 / NO_WB_W gates) without advancing writeBufferHistoryIndex, so the next real readback consumed the stale 442-wide entry (8192-byte buffer). The s5710 bounds guard was a mitigation of that desync. Fix: NativeTarget::skipReadback() called on every pass-2 skip that mirrors pass 1's record condition. Note: the 442-wide SetColorImage itself (H1 misparse vs H2 genuine) is still unnamed - only its consequence (history desync) is fixed. Built; exported rt64.patch. Soaks s5712_lvl7a/b/c queued: expect SKIP_WILD_W present (control) and zero "exceeds readback" lines.
