## Session 5775 (2026-10-21) — orientation return 2 is one store at 0x800FF6F0

Static trace, no run. Retail ROM `build/rogue_squadron.z64`, mission overlay, `stepObjectOrientationTowardTarget` at `0x800FEF10` (size `0xEF0`), disassembled with `mips64-elf-objdump -m mips:4000`. Full trace: `docs/M6-S5775-ORIENT-RET2.md`.

The function has one `jr ra` (`0x800FFDF8`). It returns stack byte sp+0x497 (`lbu` at `0x800FFDB4`, `addu v0, t3, zero` at `0x800FFDF4`). `0x800FFCF8` compares that byte to 2; it does not produce the return. Three stores touch the byte and nothing else does. `0x800FEF70` writes 0 on the a1==0 early exit. `0x800FFA40` writes 1 (the caller's non-death arm). `0x800FF6F0` is the only store of 2: both entries set `t3` with `addiu t3, zero, 2` and do not clobber it.

That store is the jump-table block for slots 0 and 5 only (`0x800A9450` entries 0 and 5 both point at `0x800FF610`; slots 1..4 do not store 2). The gate is `abs(asin(dot(object+0x1C, record+0x10))) < 15` and `acos(dot(object+0x10, record+0x10)) < 90`. The symbols `sinfApprox` / `constMinusSinfApprox` are asin and acos: the first clamps to ±1 and returns ±pi/2, with Taylor coefficient 1/6, and the second subtracts that from pi/2. Scale `0x800A9480` is 180/pi.

Two fills share the record array, distinguished by byte0. byte0==1 is a nonzero `sampleTerrainAtNpcPosition` commit and stores 2 whenever the angles pass. byte0==0 is a `findSegmentObjectSphereHit` commit and stores 2 only when the angles pass and the float at record+0x24 is not < 0.7. The store-2 path also snaps object+4/+8/+12 from the record and zeroes object+0x28/+0x2C/+0x30/+0xE8. The caller's beq at `0x800B2928` still leads to jal `0x800B2EC4`.

This selects H3 (the epilogue copies a loaded byte; the immediate 2 is the store at `0x800FF6F0`). It refutes H1 (the epilogue does not write 2, and two predicates reach the store, so it is not one compare). It refutes H2 (one epilogue, not several). Which predicate fires on the death route is unmeasured: H-terrain (byte0==1) vs H-npc (byte0==0).

ORIGIN: no mitigation. The 2 is the game's own immediate, stored by its own alignment test.
DISCRIMINATION: H3 selected. H1 refuted. H2 refuted. Next discriminator is one log at `0x800FF6F0` (byte0, byte1) against the return-1 store at `0x800FFA40` as the control, on the s5774 death route.

## Session 5800 (2026-10-21) — offline trace: projectile direction has an upstream position-difference input

## Session 5801 (2026-10-21) — corrected projectile-direction provenance to object mesh transform

Read the required current-truth, next-work, and soak-tail artifacts. The
planned bounded static audit checked the exact generated call at
`spawnProbeDroidGroundImpactEffect` (`funcs_36.c:0x800CA3E4`) and the callee

object/mesh-derived, not texture-lookup-derived. It preserves H8b (a real
upstream position difference) over orientation-only and stale-stack paths, but
does not yet split target-object position from firing-object attachment/local
mesh position. No build or runtime run was needed. Single-source static
evidence; no crash/stall datum and no mitigation landed. The next unit is the
bounded object/mesh field audit named in scratch/agent/NEXT.md.

## Session 5802 (2026-10-21) — classified projectile object/mesh transform path

Read the required current-truth, next-work, and soak-tail artifacts. The
planned bounded static audit inspected `getObjectMeshTransformOrLocal` at

no new result relevant to this work unit, and no mitigation was landed.

## Session 5816 (2026-10-21) — slot byte +0x1A is a reentrancy depth, NOT a lifetime countdown; s5814's "timeout destroy" reading is superseded
Ran the s5814 discriminator (tools/apply_s5816_slot_expiry.py, mirrored into fixup; host VI counter `rs64_vi_n_g` added in rt64_render_context.cpp). Two keyed 405 s holds on the g1_inv1 route (s5816_slotexp, s5816b_post), 0 crash / 0 stall.
Code read: slotDispatcherIter increments +0x1A before the update call (both branches store age+1) and decrements after it (0x8003E9D0..D8), so net 0; destroyNpcSlotByIndex runs only if the post-decrement byte is 0 AND +0x14&8 is set at 0x8003E9E8.
Measured: pre-call flag8 visits = 0 in all 196 windows of 128 VI (positive control: ~90-145 visits/VI, so the hook fires); post-update age histogram n=2.88M: age==1 2,883,385 (99.99%), age==2 199, age 0/3+/255 = 0; flag8 set post-update only 3083 times. So hypotheses (b) "countdown decremented too often" and (c) "init wrong" are moot: there is no countdown. flag 0x8 is a destroy-REQUESTED flag set by the update callee/others during the pass, executed at depth 0. msg 2 NPC destroys are therefore requests from some writer of slot +0x14 bit 3, not an expiry timer.
Rules out: lifetime-timeout destroy for class-1 NPCs (s5814 note); the pass-rate hypothesis. Single-run pair, two instruments agree (pre/post). Next: name the writers of +0x14 |= 8 (RS64_S5798_ST-style store tracing on +0x14 with bit3 transition + backtrace) for class-1 NPC slots.
Discrimination (s5816): selects H-destroy-request-flag (bit 3 of slot +0x14 is set by a writer; destroy is deferred to depth 0) and refutes H-lifetime-timeout, H-countdown-too-fast and H-countdown-init-wrong (pre-call flag8 visits 0/196 windows, post-update age==1 in 2,883,385 of 2,883,584 visits, positive control 90-145 visits/VI). Next discriminator: trace every store that sets bit 3 of slot +0x14 (pc + class(+0x70) + backtrace for first 8 distinct pcs); outcomes: dominant pc inside the NPC update fn selects H-self-despawn, a pc on a kill/handler path selects H-external-setter, a setter whose compare inputs look wrong selects H-port-divergence.

## Session 5941 (2026-10-22) — decoded why levels 10/15 enter the viewer: planet-intro state of menuOverlayInit
Read generated N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_34.c (menuOverlayInit) and funcs_35.c (getPlanetAssetForLevel 0x800C6900). menuOverlayInit is a state machine on u16 [s1-0xB0] dispatched via jump table 0x800A75C0; state 1 (L_800C5AA8) calls getPlanetAssetForLevel(level) and, if result != 0xFF, sets state 6, which calls runModelViewerLoop(0, asset) (0x800C9BF0) at 0x800C5C34. getPlanetAssetForLevel: level 0->0, 5->1, 10->2, 15->3, all others 0xFF (skip viewer). So the viewer is the retail planet-intro for levels 0/5/10/15, not a recomp misdispatch (H3 rejected; H2 not supported — the force path reaches the correct state). Level 5 (asset 1) passes the same viewer and reaches mission at 81 s (s5715 lvl5a), so the viewer exits for assets 0/1 but not 2/3 under the same autopilot keys. Open: what exit condition differs for asset 2/3. A subagent was dispatched to trace runModelViewerLoop exit conditions; its result was not yet in at session end (see NEXT.md). No game run this session. Single-source (static reading + one soak log).
Addendum (s5941, subagent static trace of funcs_36.c:15160, single-source, unrun): runModelViewerLoop has ONE exit: 0x800B4168 returns nonzero (:17096) -> :17214 -> setUnlockBitAndPersist(asset+1) -> return. It is armed (0x800B4048) only if G1 (A/START & 0x9000, gated by isUnlockBitSet(asset+1) = bit asset+1 of byte 0x8013A663) or G2 (auto-advance 0xB8($sp), set only in state 0xBA==4 when an item timer exceeds const 0x800A79B8) fires. Bits are only written on exit. Ranked: H1 buttons locked (bits 3/4 clear for assets 2/3) AND G2 never fires; H2 armed but 0x800B4168 never completes. Existing [mv-ship-arm] probe (:17136) discriminates: absent in a lvl10/15 run => H1; present => H2. Refinement: add one print at 0x800CA4AC of 0xBA($sp), MEM_BU(0x8013A663), 0xB8($sp) every 60 frames; level 0/5 = control. Note ROGUESQ_FORCE_UNLOCK=<level> may not set bits 3/4 — check it.

## Session 5967 (2026-10-22) — G3: image_read_en (othermode-lo 0x40) is inert in rt64, so the retail/port 0x552078 vs 0x552038 delta cannot cause the white pillar stubs

Planned unit: in-run image_read_en toggle. Before building it, grepped the renderer for any consumer of the bit.
Result: `IM_RD 0x40` is defined at lib/rt64/src/shared/rt64_f3d_defines.h:87 and referenced NOWHERE else under lib/rt64/src (grep IM_RD excluding contrib = the define only); `OtherMode` (src/shared/rt64_other_mode.h) has accessors for alphaCompare, cvgDst, clrOnCvg, cvgXAlpha, alphaCvgSel, forceBlend, blender inputs, cycle/text bits but none for bit 6; shaders read otherMode only through those accessors. So a toggle of this bit is a guaranteed no-op by construction and a run would only produce an uncontrolled null. H-rdp-imgread is refuted statically (single-source: code reading; the force-ALL-tris-off positive control would also have been vacuous for this bit).
Consequence: the remaining hypotheses for port-only white stubs are H-dl (port builds extra/different geometry or texture state) or content. The 0x40 delta is just retail's blender reading memory colour, which rt64 always emulates via framebuffer blend.
No code changed, no run. ORIGIN: n/a (no mitigation added).
Next: pair by texel content (hash TMEM/LOADBLOCK payloads per tri in both retail rdp dump and port) and list port-only tris' texture hashes.

## Session 6018 (2026-10-23) — G1c levers located; in-run alt-arm instrument built, 3 arms queued

What ran: static read of generated code (N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs). Two distance levers found. (1) Terrain: `buildVisibleTerrainGridAroundCamera` (0x800437B0, funcs_9.c) builds the camera frustum planes, then a square cell window centred on the camera whose half-extent is camera-height-scaled by the float at `lui 0x8004; lwc1 -0x5AC8` (= 0x8003A538) at 0x80043A2C; that window feeds `binPolygonIntoTerrainGrid` (0x8004286C) and `streamTerrainGridCellsByDistance` (0x80042B50, NOT yet read - may carry its own cap, L-budget). (2) Objects: `selectMeshLodAndSubmitForRender` (0x80058068, funcs_12.c) first calls `transformVec3ToNpcLocalWithScale` with radius = mesh+0x44 * (f22+f20) (a range/cull test; zero return skips draw), then picks the LOD slot by comparing the transformed distance against a 5-float threshold table (default 0x800A-0x1350 = 0x8009ECB0, or override at obj+4). The 0x80137CE4 detail index is read by the per-craft anim/detail init, not by this selector (single-source from PROJECT-OVERVIEW s1797 row).
Built (lib/N64ModernRuntime events.cpp, g1c::apply, patch exported): ROGUESQ_DD_RADIUS=<m> scales the 0x8003A538 float, ROGUESQ_DD_LOD=<m> scales the 5 LOD thresholds, ROGUESQ_DD_DUMP=1 prints them, ROGUESQ_DD_ALT=<N> alternates retail/scaled every N VIs inside ONE run with a `[g1c] state=` marker (iron rule 2). Build clean; not yet run.
Queued (lvl1, 300 s, with RDP tricount + RT64 drawn logs already armed by m6_god_common.sh): s6018_g1c_pos (radius 0.25x, positive control - tris MUST fall in scaled state), s6018_g1c_r2 (radius 2x), s6018_g1c_lod2 (LOD 2x).

NEXT DISCRIMINATOR: s6048_dd2b vs dd1b/dd3b -- if dd2b/dd3b survive 300 s with [spanbound] skips, H-spanoverflow is the sole cause; if they still crash with zero skips, it is refuted for that crash and the next lldb watch targets the next corrupted word.

## Session 6053 (2026-10-23) — named the wrapper: our own s6040 clamp treated footprint MAXIMA as counts (fixed; soaks queued)
- Code read of funcs_9.c buildVisibleTerrainGridAroundCamera: 0x80042944..0x800429BC store DB0=floor(min x), DB4=ceil(max x), DB8=floor(min z), DBC=ceil(max z) (MAXIMA). ORIGIN: diagnostic only ([s6129] block dump + partition-pointer print in rs64_s6063_malloc, ROGUESQ_HEAPLOG-gated, src/main/upstream_compat.cpp); no mitigation landed.

Rules out: extra rs_malloc callers, FB-pool-as-many-allocs, fragmentation. Selects: capacity - fix is either (a) lift the RT64 8 MB rdram cap so osMemSize 12-16 MB gives the carve room (s6114 saw RT64 crash >8 MB; owner approved expanding memory), or (b) shrink the carve (depth/second fbs at 1045 wide are not needed for display).

## Session 6196 (2026-10-25) — classified the wide command-node tail

Extended the phase-4 `ROGUESQ_LOG_G1D_READS` witness so a `mem=0x170` `len=0x10F` command-source DMA dumps its big-endian words and follows pointer-shaped words. One paired 12 MB 4:3/16:9 run (`scratch/agent/s6179_g1d_rdp_words.sh`) fired the controls in each arm: 160 phase-4 `[g1d-join]` rows, 400 `[g1d-copy]` rows, and 32/28 `[g1d-root]` rows whose normalized sequences agree (seq1 `root_norm=0x003BD0`). The extracts are `scratch/agent/soak_results/s6196/ctl.tail` and `wide.tail`. The run was SIGKILLed once those controls and the node dumps were on disk.

The DMA the RSP actually reads is 24-bit: control `0x80B2D820`, wide `0x80AEF620`, delta exactly `0x3E200`. `[g1d-root]` masks that address to 23 bits (`0x32D820` / `0x2EF620`) and both arms read a zero page there (`nz=0`, hash `0xE6A1D1C5`). That is why the s6195 head looked empty. The real node is not empty (control `head_nz=69` hash `0x150149B3`, wide `head_nz=136` hash `0xA185C6DA`).

On the first root-relative node, and again on the second (`0xB313F0` / `0xAF31F0`): offsets `0x00..0x24` are five pointers that differ by `0x3E200` plus five identical words (`0x06000000`, static `0x80037658`, `0x07000000`). The pointer at `+0x108` references an RDP list (`E7`, `B9`, `B7`, `B6`, `BE`, `FA`) that matches after the same relocation, so this refutes that list as the width-bearing input. From offset `0x28` through the tail, wide is the word `0x00010001` (one `0x0001FFFF` at `+0xDC`) where control is zero, except control's fixed-point block at `0x78..0xB4` (`05200002`, `01750000`, `03ADFFFE`, `01770000`, `03A7FFFE`, `FC2A0000`, ...). The first tail word that survives relocation normalization is at `+0x100`: `0x00000000` versus `0x00010001`. Treating `0x00010001` as a pointer lands in identical static code at `0x010001`, so it is not a relocated pointer.

This selects H-command for the node body and refutes H-relocation and H-other for those words. The writer of `0x00010001`, and whether control's `05200002` block merely sits past the `0x10F` window in the wide arm, is still unnamed. No rendering value changed.

ORIGIN: diagnostic only. The added lines log an env-gated DMA snapshot and do not skip, clamp, or rewrite guest or RDP data.

First 8 words: `00000000,00000000,E6000000,00000000,FD100000,80AE5F20,E8000000,00000000`. `0x80AE5F20` is at +0x14, immediately after `FD100000`. `0xFD` with low 6 bits `0x3D` is the RDP SetTextureImage the existing image scanner counts as `kind=ti` (docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md: raw RDP commands pass through the shared table; no F5 handler synthesises them). The address is inside `[0xA6A000, 0xB00000)` but it is not one of `0xA6AA10`, `0xAE6120`, `0xAE5520`, `0xAE5320`, `0xAE5120`, and `(0xAE5F20-0xA6AA10) & 0xFFF` is not 0. Two witnesses, one DMA dump and one RDP scan.

The other three wide lines are not body reads of new chunks. idx 151 `dram=0x80AF08B0` `ov=0x7` is the tail of the chunk-150 transfer. idx 152 `ov=0x7` is the tail of the chunk-151 transfer; the 4-line cap stopped a later full read of chunk 152, so this run does not say chunk 152 was unread. idx 156 `dram=0x80AF0FE0` `ov=0x8` covers only the last 8 bytes of that chunk. Do not treat that line's first 8 words as DMA-read.

The 48-line `[g1d-img-hit]` cap logged 23 distinct wide TI addresses. Eighteen of them are `0xAE4920` through `0xAE6B20` in steps of `0x200`. None is at or above the pool base `0xAE6E00`. The next two steps of that ladder would be `0xAE6D20` (still below) and `0xAE6F20` (inside the pool). `ti_hit` is 5120, so the cap cannot say the ladder stops. That is the next discriminator: every distinct phase-4 TI address, and how many sit at or above the live pool base. Do not patch. Do not skip `copyNativeToRAM`. Do not retarget `0x8096D600`. Do not write `0x801163E8`. Do not change n=3 `t0`. Do not raise `osMemSize`. Do not move `f0`.

Superseded: "chunks 151..156 may be unread because no `[g1d-ptr]` word_at falls there." Believable because that probe's keep-set is the exact prefixes plus a `0x1000` stride, and `0xAE5F20` fails both tests while still lying in `[0xA6A000, 0xB00000)`. Chunk 151 is DMA-read, and the word at +0x14 is a texture pointer that list missed.

## Session 6248 (2026-10-25) — H-native-white refuted by source: RT64 clears colour targets to opaque black
Planned: add ROGUESQ_WB_NATIVE_BLACK and re-measure the 0.174 residual. Before building (boring-first), read the clear path: RenderTarget::clearColorTarget (rt64_render_target.cpp:353) calls commandList->clearColor() with defaults, and plume RenderColor() defaults to r=g=b=0,a=1 (plume_render_interface_types.h:730) = opaque black. It runs whenever readHeight==0 (rt64_state.cpp:2412). So a "native target not cleared to black" arm would be a no-op; H-native-white is refuted (single-source, code reading; no run). White/non-black residual therefore comes from content read INTO the target from RDRAM (readHeight>0 region, or rows beyond the read span) or from fill/other ops, not an uncleared target.

## Session 6277 (2026-10-26) — C-patch qualification #2: argument passing + guest store (setRngSeed), reserved-name limitation found
- Unit: second C-patch qualification beyond the argument-free isCinematicActive probe. First target `rand` (0x80003430) FAILED in the toolchain: N64Recomp emits the game function as `rand_recomp` (libc-reserved rename) and strict mode then reports "rand_recomp is marked as a replacement, but no function with the same name was found in the reference symbols" (patching under either name fails). So libc-named game functions (rand, and by extension any other reserved name that got `_recomp`) cannot be C-patched without a N64Recomp change; not pursued.
- Switched to `setRngSeed` (0x80003460, `*(u32*)0x80003470 = a0`): patches/rng_patch.c, syms.ld `rng_seed`, PATCH_WEAKEN += setRngSeed, and fixup_patches_host.py wraps the generated patch body with a per-call shadow check (stored == a0).
- Two arms, same recipe (title boot 45 s from build/, SIGKILL): ROGUESQ_RAND_CTL unset -> `[patch-live] setRngSeed call=1 seed=0x00000001 stored=0x00000001 mismatches=0`; ROGUESQ_RAND_CTL=1 (deliberately corrupted expectation, positive control) -> `mismatches=1`. Both arms 0 crash/abort lines. So: C patch is live, receives a0 correctly, performs the guest store at the right address, and the check can fail. Single call per boot, so this validates calling convention, not throughput. Rules out: a0/arg-register mishandling in the patch pipeline.
- Side finding: setRngSeed's old hand hooks (m5 writer parity, probe gate, S5798 store log) are bypassed while the patch is live; they are instrumentation only, but any session needing them on that store must drop setRngSeed from PATCH_WEAKEN.
ORIGIN: no mitigation machinery; qualification probe only (shadow check is env-gated diagnostic around a semantics-identical patch).
s6277 addendum — hypotheses and discrimination: H-argbug (the C-patch pipeline mishandles argument registers or the guest store address, so a patch with parameters diverges from retail) vs H-ok (calling convention and store are faithful). Discriminator: same recipe, patched `setRngSeed`, stored value vs a0 per call, with a corrupted-expectation control arm. Outcome: normal arm mismatches=0 (stored==a0==0x1), control arm mismatches=1 => the check can fail and did not on the real arm. H-argbug REFUTED for the one observed call (single-source, n=1 call/boot, calling convention only); H-ok selected. Second finding: reserved libc names are unpatchable (N64Recomp strict mode, `rand_recomp`) — hypothesis "rand can be patched like any leaf" REFUTED by the toolchain error.
NEXT DISCRIMINATOR: a patch of a high-frequency stateful function with a real purpose (e.g. a G1d widescreen HUD x-position or the dd>=3 display-list pool allocator), patched vs unpatched in one recipe with a patch-fires control; outcome map: mismatch/divergence -> H-argbug revived for multi-call/state paths; clean + 300 s hold -> pipeline fit for production patches.
s6277 verdict line: the two-arm run selects H-ok and refutes H-argbug (calling convention and guest store faithful for the observed call); the toolchain error refutes "rand is patchable" and closes reserved-name patching as a route. The next patch must discriminate multi-call stateful behaviour (see NEXT DISCRIMINATOR above).

## Session 6280 (2026-10-26) — dd3 "wild pointer" crash was the s6278 wrapper's own wrong base address; real dd3 failure is DL pool exhaustion
- Unit: run the s6278/s6279 dd3 recipe under lldb (SIGBUS stop; game stdio redirected to a file that a wrapper tails so the harness still sees it) to name the writer of 0xd4400005.
- lldb result: frame #0 is NOT guest code but `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry` host wrapper, patches.c:1407 (`MEM_W(4, head)`), caller reserveAndEmitDLEntry <- submitSceneNodeRender <- processSceneNode. `head`=0x54400001 (a MIPS `bnel v0,zero` word). Cause: tools/fixup_patches_host.py used base `(int32)0x80000000` with offsets 0x8EF8/0x8EF0/0x8F00, i.e. it read guest 0x80008EF8 (code) instead of 0x80128EF8. Both s6278 arms and the s6279 FIND_OFF arm crashed in that wrapper, hence "identical". The finder WAS being called (non-NULL returns), so "uncalled" was also wrong; and `last-guest-pc 0x8000afe0` was just the last recorded guest pc.
- Fix: base -> 0x80120000, rebuilt. Rerun (dd3 norm, tag g1_lvl1s6280_dd3_norm att1): `[patch-live] findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry calls=1,2,4,8,16,32 nulls=0 bad=0` (the C patch is live and its invariant holds over 32+ calls; ctl arm not run, so bad=0 has no positive control this session), then `[find-null] call=59 nulls=1 buckets=2048 usedhead=0x801605C0` (first 64 buckets empty) and SIGBUS si_addr=0x380000004 last-guest-pc 0x8000ade8 = null+4 deref of the NULL return by the caller. This is the old s6102 dd>=3 "finder null node" crash: the DL chunk pool is exhausted after ~58 chunks per frame at dd3.
- Rules out: memory corruption / wild-writer hypotheses (H-stale-ptr, H-pool-overrun) for dd3 boot; the s6278 H-uncalled verdict; s6279 patch exoneration (void). Selects H-exhaustion (single-source: one run, one attempt; the 0 non-empty buckets beyond the 64 dumped is not shown).
- ORIGIN: no mitigation machinery added; a diagnostic bug fixed. Note the wrapper-diagnostic lesson: a crash whose frame #0 is host diagnostic code is the instrument's, check lldb frame #0 before theorising about the guest.
- Not done: ctl arm (ROGUESQ_FIND_CTL) positive control for bad>0; sizing of the pool.

Ran: fixed-range census `[f5-hosttgt]` (src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp, in rs64_f5_host_write_begin/after, independent of the VTX range registry) for `0x735560..0x7355D0`, one DD3 level-1 EDGE_FORCE_RED arm (g1_lvl1s6349_host_target_write: mission_t=8s, hold 130s, alive, 0 VI stalls, 0 crashlines). No pi_rom/pi_sram/zmemcpy/phase<=6 host write ever overlapped the range. The phase-7 writes are the RSP writing RDP command bytes (E7/E6/FD/F5 patterns) into the buffer, i.e. the range is reused later. The "red" test (any of 3 byte lanes == 0xFF) fires on the 0xFF sign byte of negative coordinates, so the "red boundary bytes" chased s6330-s6348 are plausibly legitimate position data, not a colour corruption. ### Session 6349 addendum — discriminator run offline: H-false-positive SELECTED for 0x735560
Discriminator: docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md says TriGen fetches vertex arrays and colour arrays from SEPARATE RDRAM addresses (PrepareVtxData vs PrepareColorData), so a VTX source range is positions. Decoding the logged 32 `read=` bytes as big-endian int16 quads gives (-92,-273,-92,0), (-86,-247,-145,0), (-119,-247,-119,0), (0,-299,-46,0): 8-byte x,y,z,pad records. 0xFF appears only at byte offsets 0/2/4 mod 8 (counts 3/2/4), the HIGH bytes of the three shorts; the low bytes and pad lane never 0xFF. Two independent lines (spec layout + decoded values) select H-false-positive: the "red" detector counts int16 sign bytes of negative coordinates. Refutes H-real-colour and H-mixed for this range (other registered ranges 0x72D898, 0x7364D8, 0x736A00 not yet decoded - next check). The s6330-s6348 "red colour writer" thread chased a detector artifact; the "independent red VTX-boundary word" was position data. Next discriminator: decode the other three ranges the same way, then re-aim at the real G3c(a) edge measurement.
Verdict wording for the ledger: the position-layout decode selects H-false-positive and refutes H-real-colour for 0x735560; it resolves the s6330-s6348 red-writer question for this range and closes the host-write branch (no pre-phase-7 host write). The next discriminator is the same field decode on 0x72D898, 0x7364D8 and 0x736A00.

## Session 6362 (2026-10-26) — terrain has no CPU Vtx writer: RSP TRI_GEN builds positions from height bytes at cell+0x44

Static survey (single-source, subagent read of N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs, nothing run). The earlier iteration assumed a CPU Vtx y store; there is none. Terrain is drawn by F5 TRI_GEN (0x05): the RSP reads 25 signed height bytes from params[2] (y = s8<<4) and builds x/z from the grid (reference/gliden64/F5Rogue.cpp:301-316); colours come from params[3], a 25x4 RGBA array. The NEXT.md-assumed tables are not positions: *(0x80137A54) is per-vertex unit normals (emitGridCellTileStrip* 0x80049814/0x80049BBC/0x80049FB8), *(0x80137A50) is the 5x5 RGBA colour-grid pool (cell+0x48). Height bytes are written by selectGridCellTileVariant 0x80046030 (sb at funcs_10.c:2196, out ptr stored at cell+0x44) or set to tile-record+5 by processGridCellByDistance 0x80048BAC. They reach the RSP via renderFlatMeshFaceGroup 0x8001108C (params[2]=cell+0x44 at 0x8001178C, funcs_4.c:7728); flat cells instead pack four corner heights inline (funcs_4.c:7486-7518, words (h0<<20)|(h4<<4)&0xFFFF etc). Same twin path in renderUnlitMeshFaces 0x80011C9C.
Rules out: any Vtx-position hook in 0x8004A6C0/B644/B930 (explains the s6359/s6360 colour+alpha nulls). Implication: the y-fade/smoothing arm must scale height bytes at/before 0x8001178C (copy into a scratch 25-byte buffer, lerp toward horizon by radius), plus the flat-word path at funcs_4.c:7501/7518.
ORIGIN: no mitigation code added this session (analysis only).

## Session 6480 (2026-10-27) — link-table structure read from code; pool census instrument is uninformative (positive control failed)
Read the generated code: *0x80136FCC is a pointer to a pool of 12-byte rows allocated by 0x80041EF0 (n rows, n = hword@0x80130C4C + 0x50(sp) + result of 0x8006B694, computed in load_level_hmp at 0x80044554). ## Session 6482 (2026-10-27) — row+2 writer 0x800487F8 is a 12-byte-node list push/unlink, no distance gate (H-object-bound, single-source)
Read generated MIPS->C for 0x80048790-0x800487F8 (funcs_10.c:~10340-10407). The routine indexes node = pool(*0x80136FCC) + idx*12, unlinks via halfword +2 / +0, then pushes onto head index at 0x80136FC0 and stores into node+0/+2. ## Session 6521 (2026-10-27) — span grid is fully written at both dd; the 0x80 bytes are clamp values written by the stream function itself
Built tools/apply_s6521_spanw.py (reuses the s5798 per-store hook; range 0x80130DB0+0x2000; env ROGUESQ_SPANW=1; per-PC counts split by column <32/>=32 and by stored value 0x80, ever-written bitmap, current 0x80 count per column half). - Ever-written bitmap: 4096/4096 in both column halves in BOTH arms from dump 1 (boot clear at pc 0x80000420/24, 512 stores). Grid is 2 layers of 64x64 (+0x1000). Unwritten-grid reading from s6520 is REFUTED; H-writer-bound and H-init are dead.
- The 0x80 bytes come from the same function: 0x80042A74/78 (clear-to-0x80, 100% value 0x80), 0x800426D8 (1519275/1597888 = 95% 0x80 at dd4) and 0x80042820 (6128247/10550596 = 58% 0x80 at dd4, 5245459 stores at col>=32 vs 8424 of 1358190 at dd1). 0x80042820 is `sb trunc(clamp(f0, f12, f10))` in a per-row edge-interpolation loop (0x80042760..0x8004282C), so 0x80 = -128 is a lower-clamp saturation (or the row clear), not a missing write.
- dd4 writes ~620x more x>=32 stores than dd1 through the edge loop, i.e. the widened window drives the loop into columns dd1 never touches, and a majority of the results saturate at -128.
Discrimination: selects H-clamp (the span rejects are saturated edge values from the edge-interpolation loop) over H-unwritten; refutes H-writer-bound, H-init, H-stride-alias (writes land at expected cols). Single-source (one pair of runs); which of f12/f10 bounds, and whether the interpolation inputs (a1, f2/f22 scale, f4) are legitimate at dd4, is open.
ORIGIN: observation only; no mitigation added.

## Session 6522 (2026-10-27) — span edge-loop clamp probe: bounds fixed ±byte, inputs finite (H-clamp-legit)
Built tools/apply_s6522_clampprobe.py (ROGUESQ_CLAMPP=1, funcs_9.c probe before the 0x80042820 sb; pre-clamp f4, bounds f12/f10, f2, f22, col/row/layer). One build, scratch/agent/s6522_clamp.sh, pinned lvl1 dd1 vs dd4 concurrent 150 s, both rc=0, 0 crash/stall.

## Session 6523 (2026-10-27) — span-grid consumer decoded; scale arm cuts dd4 EMPTY 24%→14% (H-scale partial)
Static decode (mips64-elf-objdump of the splat ELF, no run needed): the consumer at 0x80042D50 loads span min A=[0x80130DB0+cell] and max B=[0x80131DB0+cell] with signed `lb`; cell skipped as empty when A==-128 AND B==-128 (the boot/clear sentinel); else rejects when A < rec[3] or rec[4] < B (rec = 30-byte HMP cell record, typically 0x6D/0x6D), writing 127/127 on reject. H-consumer-bug (lb vs lbu) REFUTED: signed compare is what the writer's clamp expects. The writer (scanConvertTriangleToSpanTable 0x80042760 loop) stores clamp(trunc(f22 * planeheight(col,row)), -128, 127), f22=40 passed in a3, plane height from absolute (col,row), so the byte is height*40 in a signed byte. A terrain span that saturates at -128 in both layers is bit-identical to the "empty" sentinel: a representation collision, not a data bug.
Built tools/apply_s6523_spanscale.py (ROGUESQ_SPANSCALE=s divides f22 at 0x800422C8 and rec[3]/rec[4] at 0x80042D88/9C by s; s=1 is stock). scratch/agent/s6523_spanscale.sh: pinned lvl1, three concurrent 150 s arms, all arms_rc=0. [ret-sum] on mission+load tables: dd1 s1 EMPTY 6/2492 (0.2%), dd4 s1 680/2825 (24%), dd4 s4 371/2653 (14%); `[spanscale] s=4` printed once only in the s4 arm (positive control for the patch firing). Selects H-scale as a real contributor (EMPTY falls 24%→14% when byte range is widened 4x) but not sufficient at s=4. Single-source, per-arm phase confound from s6517 not controlled (key counts differ per arm); dd4s1's first attempt hit fail_att1 (runner retry) so its numbers are the retry. Harm to the rendered frame is still unmeasured.
ORIGIN: diagnostic arm only (env-gated, default stock); no mitigation added.
Next: s=8 and s=16 arms plus a rendered terrain-fraction comparison; monotone fall toward 0.2% = H-scale (then bake a dd-derived scale into the knob), plateau = H-reject-by-design.
Verdict (s6523): this run refutes H-consumer-bug (consumer uses signed lb; compares match the writer's signed clamp) and selects H-scale as a partial contributor (dd4 EMPTY 24% -> 14% at SPANSCALE=4, dd1 0.2%); H-reject-by-design is not yet refuted (14% residual). Single-source.
Next discriminator: SPANSCALE=8 and 16 at dd4, EMPTY counted only in mission-table keys 745+, plus a fixed-pose terrain-fraction frame per arm. Monotone fall toward 0.2% selects H-scale; a plateau near 14% selects H-reject-by-design.

## Session 6537 (2026-10-27) — span-bypass per-swap cap (ROGUESQ_BYPASS_MAXCELLS), arms queued

Built the s6536 follow-up: tools/apply_s6537_bypasscap.py (registered after apply_s6529 in fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py) wraps both span-reject force sites so a would-reject cell (r2==1) is flipped to accept only while fewer than ROGUESQ_BYPASS_MAXCELLS cells have been force-accepted in the current swap (rs64_swap_n); unset = unlimited = bit-identical s6529. Cells are walked by distance, so the cap keeps the nearest N extra cells. Build passed (Debug cmake, regen-safe via fixup). Gotcha fixed: importing apply_s6529 module-level SystemExit("already") killed the first draft of the script; wrapped in try/except.
Four soak recipes queued (scratch/agent/soak_queue/s6537_cap_{0,40,120,inf}.sh): pinned lvl1 dd4, g1b + fb dumps, 300 s. cap=inf is the positive control (must reproduce s6536 accept-all: ~127 ms/task, ~10.5 tasks/s); cap=0 should approach opt-out (~55-65 ms, 14-18 tasks/s). No result yet; the arms are cross-run (pinned pose, so same view) — compare sd_wall, tasks/s and terrain fraction per cap.
ORIGIN: not a corruption mitigation; cap is a performance dial on an intentional opt-in (dd>1) predicate bypass whose reject cause is span-grid saturation at -128 (s6526).

Session 6537 discrimination (added after Stop-gate feedback): this is a behaviour knob (a gameplay-visible cap on the dd>1 bypass), not an instrument. It splits two hypotheses from s6536's H-more-tris. H-cost-linear: gfx task cost rises proportionally with force-accepted cells, so terrain gain and frame cost trade 1:1 and no cap is free. H-cost-front-loaded: the nearest few cells carry most of the 0.047 -> 0.209 terrain-fraction gain while the far tail carries most of the extra triangles, so a small cap keeps most of the gain at near-retail cost. Discriminator (next iteration, from the four queued arms cap=0/40/120/inf on pinned lvl1 dd4): terrain fraction and sd_wall ms/task per cap. If fraction(40)/fraction(inf) >= 0.6 while sd_wall(40) <= 1.3x sd_wall(0), H-cost-front-loaded is selected and the cap becomes the dd>1 default; if both ratios track linearly, H-cost-linear is selected and the knob is exposed with the tradeoff reported to the owner. cap=inf must reproduce s6536 (~127 ms, ~10.5 tasks/s) as the positive control; otherwise the wrapper changed behaviour and the arms are invalid.
Gate wording: the four cap arms discriminate H-cost-linear from H-cost-front-loaded; the fraction/cost ratios above are the criterion that selects one of them, and a cap=inf result off s6536 refutes the arm set. No conclusion is claimed this session.

## Session 6553 (2026-10-27) — dd>1 NULL node is the DL-chunk allocator returning NULL (code reading), A/B launched
Ran: read the recompiled `renderFlatMeshFaceGroup` around the crash store 0x80011524 (funcs_4.c). The "NULL node" `a0` is not a pool entry: it is the result of `jal 0x8002221C` at 0x80011480, called when the DL chunk list head `*0x801163B0` is empty (0x80011470 `bne a0,zero`). The result is appended to the doubly-linked list (head 0x801163B0, tail global 0x8011A7DC) with no NULL test, so an empty chunk cache gives `sw v0,4(a0)` with a0=0 (host 0x80000000). The pool-cap lift of POOLX>1 draws more cells per frame, which drains the 0x108-byte chunk cache. ## Session 6689 (2026-10-31) — 21:9 heap tail on the depth image named and removed (RT64 depth write-back was the writer); hangar SIGBUS persists, real fault is a bad voice-list pointer from table 0x800CC4F8

HYPOTHESIS-ID: g1d-heap-image-overlap (closed) -> g1d-hangar-voice-ptr. Step 0: CURRENT-TRUTH
56,776 bytes, no maintenance. No new soak verdicts. Screen check script lacks Quartz (module
missing); runs drove the route normally (mission reached every attempt), so the screen was unlocked.

Instrument (one build): `ROGUESQ_FLOOR_WATCH=hex,...` (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp) adds up to 8
physical watch words to the existing floor-writer instrument (guest-exact store PC via the
store-parity hook, host RT64 writes via rs64_floor_writer_begin/after; requires
ROGUESQ_FLOOR_DEPTH_DIR, writes rdram.jsonl). Positive control: the instrument's own
bzero/memset control at 0x1FF0020 fired (4 guest-exact records), and boot-time F5 ucode RDP
output stores at the same words fired (208 host records each).

Run 1, 21:9 forced lvl1, watch e4-0x10..e4+0xC (0xB55FF0..0xB5600C): 5/5 crash, same SIGBUS
0x7FFF0002. Writer timeline (last attempt): guest coalesceFreeHeapBlocks 0x800024A4 writes the
flags-8 terminator at e4-0x10, guest buildHeapFreeList 0x800020F4/FC writes a FREE header at e4
(0x00010000, size 0xA9FE0 = exactly the w1024 depth image 0xAA000-0x20). Then host RT64
`native-swap` depth write-back (phys 0xB56000 len 694272 = 1024x339x2) overwrites it; at the next
rebuild the header word reads 0xEB8CEB90 (depth values). ORIGIN: ensureHeapInitialized
(0x80001940-0x800019A8) computes gap = *801163E4 - (slot+fbsize); gap==0 (retail 4:3) -> heap
[slot, slot+fbsize); gap!=0 -> heap [slot, e4+fbsize) with the gap punched, i.e. it ALSO takes the
buffer at e4 as heap. Retail treats that buffer as spare; our wide carve made it the live depth
image. So the game legitimately hands out the depth buffer, and RT64 legitimately writes depth
there: the layout is ours (s6201 carve), the value is legitimate from both writers.

Fix (tools/apply_s6031_far.py apply_s6689_heapslot, wired in fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py, live
funcs_0.c patched): wider than 4:3, `bne $v1,$zero` at 0x80001944 falls through to the retail
gap==0 branch, so the flags&4 heap is [slot, slot+fbsize) and never reaches e4. 4:3 untouched
(rs64_g1d_wide()). With it the s6631 heapcap walker hits the game's own terminator (fl=0008,
did=0) at every rebuild: 21:9 cut=0x80A0AFF0, 16:9 0x80662B50.

Run 2, 21:9 with the fix, same watch: heapslot in force (did=0 fl=0008 every rebuild) but STILL
4/4 crash (3x si_addr 0x7FFF0002, 1x 0x4DF24008 si_code=2). So H-heap-image was a real overlap
but NOT the crash cause. Run 3, 16:9 with the fix: mission_verified_130s, 0 crash (fbhash
distinct 2952/3765) -> 16:9 unchanged.

Fault decode (static, single-source): mallocVoiceLineStruct (0x800CBF60) does `lhu 0($a0)` on its
first argument; MEM_HU swizzles addr^2, so 0x7FFF0002 means a0 == 0x7FFF0000. The caller
craftSelectionVoiceLineHelper (0x800AE264) loads a0 = word[0x800CC4F8 + (s1-1)*4] with
s1 = byte[0x800CC404 + byte[0x800CD6E8]], gated on word[0x800CDA18]==0 and byte[0x800CDA08+s1-1]==0.
Either s1 is 0/out of range at 21:9 (index -1 or past the table) or the table/index memory is
overwritten. The ELF's segment vaddrs do not map 0x800CC4F8 to data (reads code), so the table
was not resolved offline. Not watched yet. lib/ not edited (export.sh not needed).

Rules out: heap-tail/depth-image overlap as the 21:9 hangar SIGBUS cause (fix in force, crash
persists, same site). Level-select tear check (s6631 scorer) not re-run with heapslot.

Verdict: the watch run selects H-image (the depth-image overlap is real: RT64 native-swap depth
write-back is the writer of the heap header at e4) and refutes H-owner (no guest owner store
corrupts it). The fixed run (heapslot in force, crash 4/4, same site) then refutes H-heap-image as
the cause of the 21:9 hangar SIGBUS, and the fault decode localises the crash to the voice-list
pointer from table 0x800CC4F8. Next discriminator: ROGUESQ_FLOOR_WATCH on 0x0CC4F4..0x0CC500,
0x0CD6E8, 0x0CDA18 at 21:9 and 16:9 — a writer touching the table selects H-overwrite, no writer
with an out-of-range s1 selects H-index.

## Session 6693 (2026-10-31) — 21:9 level-select tear: RAM->depth reload and the clearDepthOnly fast path are refuted as sole causes; the 1024-wide depth fb never registers the per-frame clear

What ran: one RT64 build (lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp, exported to submodule-patches/rt64.patch)
adding `ROGUESQ_DEPTH_RELOAD=skip|clear|nocopy` (fullSync depth reload kill-switches),
`ROGUESQ_NO_DEPTH_FASTCLEAR=1` (disable the clearDepthOnly fast path) and `ROGUESQ_LOG_DEPTH_PAIR=1`
([depth-pair] per fullSync pair: fb range, w/h/readHeight, lastWriteType, isLastWriteDifferent,
lastWriteRect; [depth-reload]; [depth-fastclear]). Harness scratch/agent/s6693_depthrl/ab.py
(g1d_floor_inputs.run_arm, scorer g1d_row_noise vhf, clean 3.8-6.8, torn 15-28). 9 runs, 0 crashes.
(First attempt aborted on `FixedRect::left()` of a null lastWriteRect in my log; fixed with isNull.)

Scores, level-select frames VI 1350-1650 (later frames are post-select, clean in every arm):
| arm | select-frame vhf |
|---|---|
| 21:9 base | 15.3-21.3 (torn) |
| 21:9 reload=skip | 10.5-11.5 |
| 21:9 reload=clear | 9.5-11.4 |
| 21:9 reload=nocopy | 23.5-25.0 (no-op at 21:9: diff is always 0) |
| 21:9 NO_DEPTH_FASTCLEAR | 20.7-23.7 (torn) |
| 21:9 fast clear on (repeat base) | 11.0, 19.2-20.3 |
| 16:9 base / reload=skip / NO_FASTCLEAR | 5.1 / 5.6-6.8 / 5.1 (clean: positive control) |

Census (same runs): at 16:9 the 796-wide depth fb 00B7BD80 reads `h=340 lastWriteType=Color diff=1
lwr=0,0 796x340` on every pair, so the clear (fill FFFC with cimg = zimg) reaches the depth target
via copyFromTarget each frame. At 21:9 the 1024-wide depth fb 00B56000-00BFF800 reads `h=339
lastWriteType=Depth diff=0 lwr 1023x339` on all ~590 pairs: the state-thread FramebufferManager never
sees the 340-row colour write. A 340-row get() would raise maxHeight to 340 and set lwt=Color. The
640-wide fbs at both aspects behave like 16:9. [depth-fastclear] shows identical conditions at both widths
(prev pair fillRectOnly=1, siz=2, rect bottom 340), so the fast path is not the width split. Only one
RAM->depth reload per run (rows=339 at start).

Reading: the depth is not cleared per frame at 21:9. The level-select camera is static, so the floor
is redrawn at the same Z it wrote last frame and the strict compare rejects it in stripes. That
fits a one-time reload change (skip/clear) shifting the score for the whole run without fixing it.
Rules out: H-reload as the cause (it modulates, does not cure), clearDepthOnly fast path (kill switch
no effect), H-writeback chunking (diff never set, so no reload chain to feed). Selects: the 1024-wide
clear pair is not registered against fb 00B56000 in the fullSync/submit bookkeeping (H-clear-lost).
The cause is still open: either a different FramebufferManager instance (the workload queue keeps
its own fbManager, which the fast path updates as type Depth), or the clear pair carries a different
cimg width/address at 21:9. Single-source so far (one census, two arms agreeing).
ORIGIN: no mitigation landed; kill switches are diagnostic, default off.
Verdict: selects H-clear-lost; refutes H-reload (kill-switch modulates 19->11, never clean),
refutes H-fastclear (NO_DEPTH_FASTCLEAR still torn), refutes H-writeback (diff never set at 21:9).
Next discriminator: log every fillRectOnly clear pair in submitFramebufferPair and fullSync (cimg
addr/width/rect, clearDepthOnly) at 21:9 vs 16:9 to split H-cimg / H-manager / H-skip (NEXT.md).

## Session 6694 (2026-10-31) — 21:9 level-select floor tear fixed: the game's scissor lrx (w*4)&0xFFF wraps to 0 at w=1024, so the depth clear is clipped empty

What ran: NEXT.md discriminator (H-cimg / H-manager / H-skip). One RT64 census build under
ROGUESQ_LOG_DEPTH_PAIR: [clr-submit] (wide 16b fill-only pairs after FramebufferManager::get in
submitFramebufferPair), [clr-sync] (same pairs in fullSync getFramebufferPairs), [clr-lwt] (pairs that mark
an fb colour-written), [clr-pre] (raw drawColorRect before the isEmpty/s78 gates), and [scissor-raw]
(raw G_SETSCISSOR words per distinct cimg, lib/rt64/src/gbi/rt64_gbi_rdp.cpp). Harness
scratch/agent/s6694_clr/run.py (g1d_floor_inputs.run_arm + g1d_row_noise vhf). 5 build-run cycles, 0 crashes.

Results:
- [clr-submit]/[clr-sync]/[clr-lwt] at 21:9 list every other clear (640-wide, 00B6A000/00B95C00) but
  never 00B56000; at 16:9 the 796 clear 00B7BD80 appears in all three (positive control).
- [clr-pre] 21:9: `addr=00B56000 w=1024 raw=0,0-0,1360 empty=1` x291, while the RDP fill itself is
  (0,0)-(4095,1359) FFFCFFFC (ROGUESQ_LOG_FILLALL). So the rect was clipped to zero width: H-skip, by scissor.
- [scissor-raw]: the full-fb scissor at 21:9 is `w1=00000550` / `02000700` (lrx=0); at 16:9 `00C70550`
  (lrx=3184 = 796*4). Writer: setupCameraMatrices, 0x80017370 `andi v0,v0,0xFFF; sll a0,v0,12` on
  (int)(width[0x8011A838]*4.0) -> 0x1000 & 0xFFF = 0. Second builder 0x80017814 (camera scissor) emits 4092.
- Value is NOT legitimate: 1024.0 is unrepresentable in the RDP's 12-bit 10.2 field; our FB_WIDTH=1024
  widening put it there. ORIGIN: writer = game scissor builder 0x80017370 fed by our s6113 fb-width patch;
  fix clamps at the writer, not downstream.

Fix: tools/apply_s6031_far.py apply_s6694_scissor clamps lrx to 0xFFF (1023.75, covers pixel 1023) before
the mask at 0x80017370 and 0x80017814; wired into tools/fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py (funcs_4.c) and live
patched. No-op at retail widths (<=640 -> 2560). A first attempt patched only 0x80017814 and changed nothing
(still lrx=0, vhf 19-26) - that dead end is how the second site was found.

After (same harness): 21:9 [scissor-raw] `00FFF550`/`02FFF700`; depth fb 00B56000 `h=340 lwt=1 diff=1 lwr
1024x340` every frame (16:9 shape); select frames VI 1400-1650 vhf 7.15-7.98 (was 19.1-26.0); post-select
3.9-5.6; 16:9 control 4.9. Visual: floor and console ring drawn
(screenshots/s6694_21x9_levelselect_before_after.png: top=before, middle=after, bottom=16:9).
Two lines of evidence: the depth-fb bookkeeping census and the scorer/visual.
Residual: noise at the top-right block (x~690-760, top rows) and right column (x>~950) of the 21:9 select
frame - undrawn pixels, which is why vhf sits at 7.2 rather than <7. Separate defect, next unit.
Verdict: selects H-skip (by zero-width scissor); refutes H-cimg (addr/width correct) and H-manager (no
manager split; the clear never reached either). The census logs stay env-gated (ROGUESQ_LOG_DEPTH_PAIR).

## Session 6695 (2026-10-31) — 21:9 level-select right-edge residual fixed: two host-side scanners assumed retail screen geometry (spike cull x>960, radar-disc box shift in every scene)
Unit: NEXT.md g1d-levelselect-right-residual (noise block x~690-770 rows 20-130, noise column x>~955 rows 170-336).
Hypotheses at start: H-wrap2 (another 12-bit x field wraps at w*4=4096), H-fov (geometry ends), H-stale, plus H-footprint.
Runs (all 21:9 level-select route via tools/g1d_floor_inputs.run_arm, ~35-60 s each; scripts in scratch/agent/s6695_fpx/):
- Window capture (shot.py, screencapture of the RT64 window): the holes are on screen too, not only in the RDRAM dump.
- FP_XSCALE 1 vs 4 (run.py): pixel-identical holes -> terrain footprint (s6144) is not the cull. H-footprint refuted.
- FILLALL at w1008 and w1024 (w1008.py): level select only fills depth (one 0..W x 0..340 fill/frame), no colour clear,
  so holes = pixels nothing draws. (The w1008 frame lacked the doorway hole, but that was a different pose: confound.)
- Static: setupCameraMatrices' other 5 andi 0xFFF sites are y/ulx fields; emitFrameRdpInitDl's 3 are width-1.
  No further game-side wrap. H-wrap2 refuted (single-source, static).
Writer 1 (right column): our rs64_spike_scan (src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp) bounds x at 320+guard(640)=960, a 320-wide
  viewport assumption. At w1024 every ordinary triangle past x=960 was zeroed. Evidence: CULL_SPIKE=0 + LOG_SPIKE arm
  logged 1850 "bad" tris in level select, e.g. op 0F V=(950.8,242)(983.5,267.5), normal wall tris, and the column
  filled in. Fix: track SET_COLOR_IMAGE width in the scan; images wider than 640 get the guard measured from their own
  right edge (<=640 unchanged, so 4:3 culling is byte-identical). Fixed arm: 0 bad tris, column vhf 13 -> 5.5.
Writer 2 (doorway block): our rs64_region_scan (s6158/s6159 radar-disc HUD shift) moves every <=130 px tri/texrect
  centred in the fixed box x 669-810, y 20-135 by +256 px in EVERY scene. At level select that box holds the room seen
  through the doorway ([region] TRI op=0F x=625..753 y=37..168 at swap 384), pushed off-screen. It also shifted
  thousands of title-phase texrects (flight-route census: swaps 250-1250 TEXRECT 12k matches). The disc tris are op 0F
  like scene geometry, so no opcode gate exists. Fix: fixup tools/apply_s6695_radarmark.py stamps the swap number at
  renderRadarMinimap entry (0x800C5F90, funcs_34.c, registered in fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py); the shift applies only
  within 8 swaps of a radar draw (ROGUESQ_SHIFT_REGION_ANYWHERE=1 restores the old behaviour). New
  ROGUESQ_REGION_LOG_CAP (default 400) for the census.
Verification: level-select arm: [region-gate] shift=off for the whole run, 0 spike tris, select frame vhf 5.41
  (s6694 7.2-8.0; target <7), doorway-box noise 6.1 (was 15-23). Positive control, lvl1 21:9 flight
  (tools/g1_lvl1_aspect_arm.sh s6695gate): gate turns on at swap 2482 (flight) and stays on, radar disc still inside
  its ring at the right edge like the ungated run, mission_verified_130s, 0 crashes.
  Sheets: screenshots/s6695_21x9_levelselect_before_after.png, screenshots/s6695_21x9_flight_radar_gate_check.png.
Caveat: the after-frame pose doesn't show the doorway, so the doorway fix rests on the mechanism (gate off + logged
  doorway tris in the box) plus the box metric, not on a same-pose visual. Pre-existing, not touched: a grey radar
  wedge stays at x~690 top in flight (s6159 "RA leaves the wedge behind").
ORIGIN: both writers are our own host-side scanners (spike cull s6083/s6084, region shift s6158/s6159), not the game.
  The values they hit were legitimate game geometry. The fixes narrow each scanner to where its premise holds.
Verdict: selects H-host-scanner (two host-side writers), refutes H-wrap2 (no further 12-bit wrap), H-footprint and
  H-stale (holes are undrawn, not stale). G1d level-select residual closed. Next: G3d turning-shake timing (ITERATION 3c).

## Session 6696 (2026-10-31) — G3d turning shake root-caused and fixed: s6372's per-vector-load getenv() made every gfx task ~5x slower (30 -> 17 game fps, bunched presents)
Ran: (1) offline census of every archived scratch/agent/m6/*lvl1*/run.log [g1b] line (new tools/g3d_g1b_census.sh, 631 runs,
flight seconds t>=60, medians). Retail/dd1 lvl1 sat at 30 tasks/s and ~9-11 ms send_dl per task from s6013 through s6363
(10-26 21:10); from s6390 (10-26 23:29) every lvl1 dd1 run is 8-17 tasks/s at 50-110 ms/task, cpu ~= wall, and it never
recovered (s6442 l1 17/48.8, s6457 17/50, s6582 12/70). lvl10 moved 6-8 -> 23-25 ms. The window holds only the s6364-s6390
spike-probe commits. (2) Diff of that window: s6372 added rs64_vld_note() (src/main/main.cpp), called from every RSP vector
LOAD (LBV..LWV in librecomp rsp_vu_impl.hpp), which ran `getenv("ROGUESQ_SPIKE_DMEM")` uncached on each call (~2.4M loads/s
in flight); s6375 made SDV copy 96 lanes into a snapshot on every SDV, armed or not. (3) Fix: flag cached once in a static,
SDV snapshot gated on new rs64_sdv_snap_enabled(); ROGUESQ_G3D_LEGACY_TOGGLE=<sec> re-enables the old per-load getenv + SDV
copy in alternating windows inside ONE run ([g3d] line per flip). (4) One run, lvl1 forced route, s6457 recipe (G1B + G3C_LOG
per-VI stamps), toggle 20 s, 10 flips, 203 s hold, alive, 0 crashlines, 0 stalls. New tools/g3d_toggle_fold.py:
  fixed : 65 s, VI 61.1/s, tasks 29.7/s, send_dl 10.9 ms (cpu 9.7), present dt p50 16.5 / p95 20.0 ms, <2 ms 1%, >50 ms 0%
  legacy: 76 s, VI 61.1/s, tasks 17.6/s, send_dl 52.1 ms (cpu 45.9), present dt p50 7.5 / p95 61.5 ms, <2 ms 41%, >50 ms 10%
Positive control: the legacy windows reproduce the s6457/s6458 numbers (17-18 tasks/s, ~50 ms, 3-4 bunched presents then a
~60 ms gap) inside the same process, and already pre-flight (3.7 -> 7.0 ms at the first flip).
Mechanism of the shake: send_dl runs the LLE F5 ucode on the Gfx thread; ScreenUpdateActions queue behind it, so a 50 ms task
holds 3-4 VI presents which then drain within 0.1 ms. Owner sees ~17 game fps delivered in bursts.
Two lines of evidence: cross-run census step aligned with the introducing commits + same-run toggle A/B.
Verdict: selects H-thread (Gfx thread busy ~50 ms per task), named writer = our own s6372/s6375 diagnostic hooks. Refutes H-log
(logging identical in both arms; fixed arm is clean with full soak logging) and H-present as an independent cause (presents bunch
only because they queue behind send_dl on the same thread). Supersedes s6458 "G3c(c) closed as retail judder" and the s6390-s6695
absolute frame-cost numbers (G1c dd cost tables, sd_wall/tasks/s figures): all carry the ~40 ms/task overhead; dd ratios measured
then are distorted. s6455's arm-independent camera jerk was measured in that era too (10-27; census s6448/s6450 lvl1 at 14-17 tasks/s).
ORIGIN: no mitigation; the writer of the cost is our own diagnostic code (s6372 rs64_vld_note uncached getenv, s6375 unconditional
SDV snapshot). Removing the per-op cost is the root-cause fix; ROGUESQ_SPIKE_DMEM probes behave as before when armed.
Next: owner judges the feel (retail and FPS60); re-measure G3c(c) camera jerk on the fixed build if shake is still reported;
re-baseline dd4 cost (s6390-s6582 cost numbers are void).

## Session 6702 (2026-10-31) — lvl1 dd8 crash root-caused: s6569 malloc spill arena leaked every block; coalescing free list landed, 304 s clean

Folded the s6701 soaks. lvl10 dd8 (pnorm cap): 301 s clean, late frame full-screen terrain+craft+HUD (fold tri_p90=1 /
terr 0.99 is a scorer miss on a steep downward view, not a bad render). lvl1 dd8: CRASH at 219 s, SIGBUS
si_addr=0x38000000a in instantiateNamedMeshInstance+1220 <- orientedNpcHandler <- spawnNpcOfType <- spawnOrientedNpc <-
sprayEffectEmitterNpcHandler <- destroyNpcSlotByIndex <- runInMissionFrame. 0x38000000a = rdram base + (guest 0x0000000A -
0xFFFFFFFF80000000): a guest NULL+0xA read. Immediately before it: `[spill] req=0x634 arena full`, then
`[zmemcpy] OOB skip dst=0x58`.
ORIGIN: the writer of the NULL is rs_malloc itself, legitimately: the 8 MB heap is full at dd8 and the s6569 spill fallback
(src/main/upstream_compat.cpp rs64_s6569_spill, a 4 MB bump at 0x80800000) also returned 0 because it NEVER reclaimed.
tools/apply_s6569_spill.py made rs_free return early on spill pointers, so all 2101 spill allocations in 219 s leaked
(bump 0x20 -> 0x9B6F0 -> 0x2DF650 -> 0x3E1A30 -> full). Not corruption; our own allocator bug.
Fix: spill now keeps live/free maps (addr -> rounded size); malloc takes first fit from the free list (split) before bumping;
rs64_s6569_isspill (called only from the rs_free hook) releases the block, coalesces neighbours, and returns a top block to
the bump. Unknown/double frees are logged and ignored. ROGUESQ_SPILL_LEAK=1 restores the s6569 leak. No regen needed (the
generated free hook already calls isspill). Mutex-guarded.
Run (same recipe as s6701, lvl1 dd8 STORE_DIAG=0 DD_UNSAFE, -O2 build): hold 304 s, alive, 0 stalls, 0 crashlines,
arena full 0, unknown frees 0, 1059 bump allocs + 769+ reuses, 1537+ frees. Live spill per 30 s: 39K, 1732K @60 s, then flat
1734-1762K to 300 s, i.e. steady state with ~2.3 MB headroom; max bump 0x1BB2C0. Fold: vi 61.0, 29.8 tasks/s, gfx 8.7 ms,
terr 0.046. Late fb (fb_0009600) full-screen flight, terrain/craft/HUD.
Evidence lines: (1) s6701 old binary exhausted at 219 s with monotonically growing bump; (2) fixed binary plateaus at 1.74 MB
live under the same recipe. Same-binary positive control queued: soak_queue/s6702_spillleak_ctl_dd8_lvl1.sh
(ROGUESQ_SPILL_LEAK=1, expect "arena full"). Until it folds, the A/B is cross-binary (single run per arm).
Also NEXT item 2 answered offline (no run): refolding s6701 lvl5 dd4 vs dd4 FPS60 with --tmin 140/200 (past the t=74 START
pause, which the 95 s flight keys clear): dd4 30.5/30.7 tasks/s gfx 13.6/13.2 ms; FPS60 44.0/45.4 tasks/s, gfx 16.3/15.2 ms,
p10 27/29. H-fps60-cost: FPS60 at dd4 reaches ~45 fps, not 60; the pause barely moved the s6701 numbers.
Rules out: the lvl1 dd8 crash as a parked "rare dd4/dd8 gfx SIGBUS" recurrence (only run with "arena full" in m6/).
Verdict: selects H-spill-leak (our allocator never reclaimed, so exhaustion was certain under sustained dd8 play) and refutes
H-heap-demand (the game's real overflow demand exceeds 4 MB): live spill plateaus at 1.74 MB. Root cause fixed, not guarded.
Next discriminator: the queued same-binary ROGUESQ_SPILL_LEAK=1 control must reproduce "arena full"; if it does not within
300 s, compare its bump growth rate against s6701's (~18 KB/s) before trusting the cross-binary A/B.

## Session 6705 (2026-10-31) — G1e: async RT64 consumer of LLE RDP ranges (ROGUESQ_RDP_ASYNC) lands; same-run toggle lvl5 FPS60 dd2: -1.2 ms/task, +5.6 tasks/s, frames sane; short of the 2 ms target
Engineering change: src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp `ultramodern::rdpq`. ROGUESQ_RDP_ASYNC=1 queues each LLE RDP range
(contiguous submits merged up to 4 KB) to one worker thread ("RS64 RDP async", QoS user-interactive) that runs
processDisplayLists. The command words are COPIED at submit time (the ucode reuses its RDP ring within a task, H-dep), and RT64
reads the copy (processDisplayLists takes the command base pointer; textures still come from core.RDRAM). FIFO order; send_dl
(RAII scope) and update_screen/shutdown drain, so dp_complete and present still follow every range of the task. Submits outside
send_dl stay synchronous. ROGUESQ_RDP_ASYNC_TOGGLE=<s> (events.cpp g1b tick) flips it at the [g1b] second boundary, which now
ends `as=<0|1>`. tools/g1e_gfxbusy.py: `env AS=1` splits by as= (HK=1 still splits by hk=). Default OFF, behaviour unchanged.
First run crashed at t=10, exactly when async switched on: SIGBUS in rs64_dpc_defer_end. ORIGIN: our own always-on s4280 cimg
walk (dpc_bridge.cpp) maps RT64's SetColorImage events (rt64_rdp.cpp:469, off = cmd pointer - state->RDRAM) back to RDRAM by that
offset. For a copied range the offset is garbage, so the memcpy went wild. This is a diagnostic misreading the copy, not a render
hazard. Fix: the walk skips tasks that queued async ranges (rs64_rdpq_task_async), and RT64::g_s4280_n is cleared after such a task
drains, so a later sync task never reads stale offsets. Patches re-exported (events.cpp).
Run (scratch/agent/s6705_async.zsh; lvl5 FPS60 dd2 STORE_DIAG=0 G1B, toggle 10 s, 301 s hold): alive, 0 crashlines, 0 VI
stalls. From 140 s on, first second after each flip dropped: as=0 n=80 49.3 tasks/s, sd 11.70 ms (median 12.34); as=1 n=74 54.9
tasks/s, sd 10.46 ms (median 10.52). From 40 s on: 50.8/9.89 vs 54.5/9.14. The instrument is the s6704 toggle, which resolved
+4.9 ms in its positive control. Render check: fbd frames from both arms (docs/img/g1e_s6705_async_sheet.png, top sync, bottom
async) show terrain, craft and HUD with no spikes or garbage (single run, eyeball).
Verdict: H-overlap partly selected. Async overlap is real but saves ~1.2 ms of the ~5 ms RT64 share (s6704 sample: ~46% of
send_dl). H-dep was handled by construction (copy) and no corruption was seen. H-rt64-bound not yet discriminated: the worker may
be busy for most of the task, or most RT64 work may land at task end (the fullSync after the RSP finishes), leaving nothing to
overlap. Next: per-task RSP wall vs worker busy vs drain-wait split, in the same toggle run.
Verdict wording: selects H-overlap (async windows -1.24 ms mean / -1.82 ms median per task, +5.6 tasks/s, same run). Refutes
H-dep as a blocker for the copy design (no garbage or missing geometry in async frames). Next discriminator: per-task RSP wall vs
worker busy vs drain wait (selects H-endload, H-worker or H-producer; scratch/agent/NEXT.md).

## Session 6706 (2026-10-31) — G1e: async RDP split selects H-endload: 3.4 of 4.0 ms RT64 work is the task's final deferred-commit range (~120 kB), which arrives only after the RSP exits
Engineering change: src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp `rdpq` gains a per-task split under ROGUESQ_G1B=1 (no cost otherwise): one
`[g1e-aq] t= as= n=` line per wall second per arm (as = mode at task entry) with per-task means of total (send_dl scope),
rsp (entry -> drain entry), drain wait, worker busy wk, worker busy after drain entry wk_tail, producer copy, sync RT64 ms
(processDisplayLists inside a sync task), kB, jobs, submit calls, pending jobs at drain entry, last job kB/ms. New fold
tools/g1e_aq.py. Recipe scratch/agent/s6706_aq.zsh (= s6705 toggle recipe, lvl5 FPS60 dd2 STORE_DIAG=0, 10 s toggle).
Run: 301 s hold, alive, 0 crashlines, 0 VI stalls. [g1e-aq] from 140 s (as=0 4353 tasks / as=1 4269 tasks):
  as=0: total 10.36 ms, sync RT64 4.62 ms, 350 kB, 9462 submit calls per task.
  as=1: total 10.15, rsp 6.64, drain 3.51, wk 4.20, wk_tail 3.50, copy 0.35, 65 jobs, 10787 calls, last job 122 kB / 3.50 ms.
From 40 s: as=0 8.98 / sync 4.22; as=1 9.10, rsp 5.67, drain 3.43, wk 3.96, wk_tail 3.41, last job 120 kB / 3.41 ms.
[g1b] same-run split (g1e_gfxbusy AS=1): as=0 50.8 tasks/s sd 11.34 ms; as=1 53.5 / 10.64 (s6705 was 49.3/11.70 vs 54.9/10.46).
Positive control for the split: the as=0 arm reports wk=0/drain=0 and sync RT64 4.6 ms, the as=1 arm wk 4.2 ms, i.e. the same
RT64 cost seen from both sides (single run, two independent clocks: Gfx-thread inline vs worker-side).
Mechanism (code read, dpc_bridge.cpp): the defer layer holds every DPC_END range until the ucode exits (rs64_dpc_defer_end,
main.cpp:6658, so RT64 never sees garbage streams on UnhandledJumpTarget). Only a ring lap (s4273 wrap flush) releases ranges
mid-task, and it submits them one 8-byte bump per call (~9.5k processDisplayLists calls per task, unmerged). The final lap is
merged at defer_end into one ~120 kB range: that is the last job, 3.4-3.5 ms, and it can only start after the RSP is done.
Verdict: selects H-endload (wk_tail 3.50 of wk 4.20; only 0.70 ms of RT64 work overlaps the RSP). H-worker refuted (worker busy
4.2 ms << total 10.2 ms). H-producer partial: rsp(as=1) 6.64 vs sync rsp-minus-RT64 5.74 = +0.9 ms producer cost (copy 0.35 ms,
the rest mutex/merge), which eats most of the 0.7 ms overlap: net per task -0.2 ms in the aq clock, -0.7 ms in [g1b].
s6705's -1.2 ms reproduces as -0.7 ms here (cross-run, same recipe; treat the async gain as 0.5-1.2 ms).
Next lever: stream the deferred ranges to the worker during the task (flush every ~16 kB when async is on, the same path the
wrap flush already takes mid-task), so the last-lap 120 kB is processed while the RSP still runs. Risk class is the same as the
existing wrap flush (garbage streams after UnhandledJumpTarget are no longer droppable for already-flushed bytes).

drain (Gfx-thread clock) agree.

## Session 6710 (2026-10-31) — G1e: lvl5 FPS60 dd4 shortfall is the game's serial frame loop (cpu + own gfx-task wait > ~10 ms/frame), not guest-CPU saturation or audio

Instrument (lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern, exported to submodule-patches): under ROGUESQ_G1B=1 a new per-second
`[g1b-gt] t= sum_cpu= slot.osid:cpu/blk ...` line. threads.cpp registers each host thread running a guest thread in a slot
(mach port + OSId; first build keyed by OSId&63 collided, OSId 0/1/2 are reused); events.cpp reads thread_info CPU deltas;
mesgqueue.cpp books osRecvMesg blocked time (empty queue, BLOCK) clipped to the [g1b] window, with still-blocked threads
booked at the tick. tools/g1e_gt.py joins [g1b], [g1e-aq] (arm 0/2/3, Gfx ms/task), [g1b-gt], [s4265-agg] aud and the
s4911 per-(mq, site) blocked table for one OSId.
Runs: scratch/agent/s6710_gt.zsh (s6708 recipe: lvl5 FPS60 dd4, ASYNC_TOGGLE=10 + NODRAIN=2, STORE_DIAG=0, + S4265,
second run + S4908), m6/g1_lvl5s6710_gt_dd4 and _gt2_dd4: both 300 s, 0 crashlines, 0 VI stalls.
Positive control: in the slot build every guest thread's cpu+blk+rest sums to 1000 +-2 ms/s (rest = runnable-not-running
<= 46 ms/s); in the first build the unique OSId 3 already summed to ~991-993.
Result (t>=160, gt2): game thread = OSId 3 (slot 8), the only guest thread with real CPU. CPU 0.29-0.42 s/s in every arm and
quartile (as=3 slow 25%: cpu 292, blocked 682 ms/s at 42.8 tasks/s). Its blocked time is two waits inside its own frame:
mq 0x8011A7E8 at submitGfxFrame (the "wait for task done" after kicking the SP task; scales with the gfx task: as=3 fast
151 / slow 345, as=0 175 / 388 ms/s) and mq 0x80128CF0 at waitForPostSwapAck (VI ack, 420-550 ms/s). Audio: ~53 tasks/s,
SP queue wait 0.01 ms everywhere. Per second (139 s), (cpu + 0x8011A7E8 wait)/frame vs tasks/s r = -0.63: <10 ms 55.7/s
(n=65), 10-12 43.3, 12-14 44.2, 14-16 40.4, 16-18 40.9, >18 38.5. Run 1 shows the same cpu/blocked split for OSId 3.
Verdict: H-guest refuted as the sole cause (guest CPU < half the wall even in the slow seconds); H-audio-rsp refuted;
H-wait refined to H-serial: the game's submitGfxFrame kicks the gfx task, waits for it, swaps, then waits for the VI ack,
so guest CPU and the gfx task never overlap and any frame with cpu + gfx above ~10 ms costs an extra VI. Why the
budget is ~10 ms rather than 16.7 (VI phase of the ack, kick/done delivery latency) is not yet measured.
Rules out: further Gfx-thread overlap tricks alone reaching 60 at dd4 without also cutting guest CPU or RSP time.
ORIGIN: not a mitigation — diagnostic instrument only.
Discrimination: selects H-serial; refutes H-guest (as sole cause) and H-audio-rsp. Next discriminator: one per-frame
timeline ring (VI edge, ack recv, kick, RSP end, DP-done send/recv, swap) splits H-phase vs H-latency vs H-rsp vs H-cpu.

## Session 6711 (2026-10-31) — G1e: per-frame timeline selects H-rsp: lvl5 FPS60 dd4 frames miss the VI when the gfx task's RSP segment exceeds ~14 ms (slow camera phase 13-18 ms, ~1 MB RDP out); guest run (~4 ms), kick/done latency and VI phase are not the cause

Instrument (lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern mesgqueue.cpp/events.cpp + src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp, exported to
submodule-patches): ROGUESQ_G1E_TL=<file> arms a lock-free 2^18-mark ring of (us, code, arg, OSId, g1b slot), flushed
in 4096-mark chunks from the VI thread to <file>.<pid> (no per-frame stderr). Marks: VI edge, update_screen begin/end,
osSpTaskStart kick (type), Gfx-thread task start, RSP ucode exit (after rs64_run_lle_gfx), send_dl return, dp_complete,
guest osRecvMesg block/return/ready, osSendMesg, host enqueue_external, osViSwapBuffer. Offline: tools/g1e_tl.py.
Threads are keyed by g1b slot: OSIds repeat (several slots report OSId 0), first build keyed by OSId was unusable.
Run: scratch/agent/s6711_tl.zsh (lvl5 FPS60 dd4, ASYNC=1 NODRAIN=1 constant, STORE_DIAG=0, G1B=1; forced route),
mission_t=7 s, hold 241 s, alive, 0 VI stalls, 0 crashlines. A first attempt was void: pkill missed the orphaned
m6_god_common.sh, which relaunched a second game into the same file (two interleaved VI counters, 109 "tasks/s");
both killed, dump path now carries the pid, rerun clean.
Positive controls: ring gfx kicks 54.9/s vs independent [g1b] tasks 54.87/s (207 s); swap-centric frames 54.9/s.
Frame structure (trace read + table): VI edge -> VI handler (slot 5) posts 0x8011A420 -> spTaskSchedulerThread (slot 6)
kicks the queued gfx task at VI+0.22 ms; slot 5 acks the game (0x80128CF0, game returns VI+3.0 ms); the game runs
~3.7 ms (overlapping the RSP), blocks on 0x8011A7E8 (dpInterruptHandlerThread = slot 7 relays dp_complete in 0.2 ms),
swaps, waits for the next ack. So a frame makes its VI iff kick + gfx task + wake + post-swap fit one VI period.
Result (t>=40 s, 11350 swap frames): 1-VI frames n=9879: run 3.68 ms, task (start -> RSP exit) 4.59 ms, done-wait 2.70;
2-VI frames n=1438: run 5.51, task 10.65, done-wait 7.28. P(>=2 VIs) by task ms: <4 0.09, 4-6 0.02, 6-8 0.04, 8-10 0.08,
10-12 0.10, 12-14 0.17, 14-16 0.56, >=16 0.88. Latencies: kick -> Gfx task start 0.01 ms, dp_complete -> game wake
0.2-0.9 ms. [g1e-aq] per second: fast seconds (>=45 tasks/s, 175 s) rsp 4.6 ms/task, 267 kB, 398 calls, 17.3 us/kB;
slow seconds (32 s, 35 tasks/s) rsp 13.2 ms, 789 kB, 1626 calls, 16.8 us/kB; worker 2.0 ms, copy 0.15 ms (no
back-pressure). Slow seconds recur in a ~8 s cycle (tasks/s 60,60,60,40,31,33,55...) = the autopilot orbit facing the
dense dd4 terrain; RSP time per kB of RDP output is constant, so it scales with the geometry submitted.
Verdict: selects H-rsp (the RSP-side gfx task, linear in RDP output, is the VI-miss term; budget ~14 ms, not 10);
refutes H-phase (kick is VI-aligned at +0.2 ms; the game's 3 ms ack phase overlaps the RSP), H-latency (all handoffs
<1 ms), H-cpu (guest run 3.7-5.5 ms and overlapped). s6710's "~10 ms cpu+gfx" budget was a per-second blend, superseded.
Not yet split: inside the 13-18 ms, LLE interpreter vs our in-RSP RDP bridge work (dpc_bridge per-command: spike cull
default ON, ROGUESQ_LOG_RDP_TRICOUNT/FB_HASH/LOG_RT64_DRAWN armed by the coverage recipe, defer ranges ~1600 calls/task).
Side check queued (not run here, one game at a time): scratch/agent/soak_queue/s6711_nodrain_hangar_route.sh (natural
hangar/menu route under ASYNC+NODRAIN, fb dumps).
ORIGIN: not a mitigation — diagnostic instrument only.

## Session 6718 (2026-10-31) — G1d 21:9 mission-intro pillarbox fixed: the intro's 640x340 video state is now widened (768 at 21:9) end to end; same-build A/B bars 227 px -> 0-1 px, lvl1 mission_verified_130s at 21:9 and 16:9

**Question (NEXT g1d-intro-pillarbox).** Why is the lvl1 mission-intro flyover pillarboxed at 21:9 (s6717, 227 px/side
of 2720, ragged right edge) while flight fills?

**Offline (s6717 run.log, no new run).** [fbw] pfm/vsu show the game's video states 320x224, 640x480, 640x340,
512x448, 512x340; FB_WIDTH (s6113/s6115) widened only 512x448/512x340. The intro (and the ~6 s attract flyover) is
640x340 with a 640 VI mode (origin 0xA4B100). RT64 showed it height-filled at ~PAR 1 (2266/1188 = 1.907 vs
640/340 = 1.88), hence the bars. Selected H-fbw-cap (the fb is 640, not a scissor or VI crop). Also the s6104
guPerspective patch multiplied the intro's aspect by ASPECT_SCALE (2.0) while its viewport stayed 640, so the
intro was horizontally squeezed: pyramid width ratio 16:9/21:9 measured 1.47 vs 1.54 predicted by k.

**Fix.** intro_w = (fbw*3/4+7)&~7 (768 at fbw 1024; 597 at 16:9 -> stays 640). tools/apply_s6031_far.py
apply_s6718_intro0 (pfm 640x340 alloc -> intro_w, sets rs64_g1d_intro_w; pfm precedes osViSetMode) and
apply_s6718_intro4 (vsu 640x340 -> intro_w and rs64_g1d_vs_intro; 640 camera viewport scaled intro_w/640;
perspective factor intro_w/640, or 1.0 when not widened), wired in the vendored fixup. upstream_compat.cpp
osViSetMode widens a 640 VI mode (width, xScale, field origins) while intro_w is set. First run: intro BLACK
(t60-80 lit 0.05): rt64 last-drawn / vi-follow width allowlists (320/512/640/1024/FB_WIDTH) rejected 768 as
"wild-w", so presents stayed on the old 1024 buffer. Added the intro width to both allowlists (lib/rt64,
exported to submodule-patches/rt64.patch). ROGUESQ_G1D_INTRO=0 restores the old path.

**Result (one build, three lvl1 runs, scratch/s6718/, tools/g1f_bar_score.py).**
| arm | intro t60/t70 bars L/R | flight | verdict |
| 21:9 on | 1/1, 1/1 (lit 0.997) | fills | mission_verified_130s |
| 21:9 ROGUESQ_G1D_INTRO=0 (control) | 227/225, 227/225 | fills | mission_verified_130s |
| 16:9 on | 1/1 (intro_w 0, persp 1.0) | fills | mission_verified_130s |
The control reproduces the s6717 bars in the same build. The 0-1 px bars and the visual frames are two lines of
evidence. The ragged right edge is gone. The pyramid is wider, consistent with the squeeze removal.
screenshots/s6718_21x9_intro_before_after.png (top = off, bottom = on). The w20 178 px left bar and the w80 black
frame appear in both arms (transitions), so they are not from this change.

**Data.** 16:9 intro w60 shows one thin line from the left edge to the hilltop (spike class, single frame).
The s6104 perspective factor also applies to every other unwidened scene (640x480 menus). If any of those draw
3D, they carry the same squeeze. That is the next unit.
ORIGIN: not a mitigation; the writer of the pillarbox is our own FB_WIDTH patch set (s6113/s6115 width match list).
**Discrimination.** This selects H-fbw-cap (the intro fb is 640 wide; widening it to 768 removes the bars, and the
same-build control keeps them) and refutes H-scissor (the fb was 640, not a 1024 fb with a narrow scissor) and H-vi (the VI
did not crop a full-width image). Next discriminator: H-squeeze vs H-none for 640x480 scenes (NEXT.md), using an object
width ratio at 4:3 vs 21:9 on the hangar route.

## Session 6720 (2026-11-01) — G1d wide-aspect title screen fixed: the interlaced 512x448 title VI mode (width 1024 = 2x512, xScale 0x333) was never widened; now width 2*fbw, xScale/field origins *fbw/512, pillar clear + centre scissor

**Question (NEXT g1d-title-garble).** Why is the title still (Luke / X-wing, START/OPTIONS) garbled at 16:9/21:9
(left half black with an orange smear, right half the still at ~2x) and clean at 4:3?

**Runs (scratch/s6720/).** title.sh: boot with ROGUESQ_AUTOPILOT=10:start (single press; the title appears at
t~12), window captures every ~0.5 s. Reproduced at 21:9 on the first run (a219).
Arm table, 21:9, one setting off per arm (w012 frames):
| arm | title |
| 4:3 retail (r43) | clean (positive control) |
| default 21:9 | garbled: black left half, still 2x in the right half |
| ROGUESQ_HUD_ANCHOR_AUTO=0 / G1D_640PERSP=0 / WINDOW_FIT=0 / CULL_SPIKE=0 / ASPECT_SCALE=1 | same as default |
| ROGUESQ_VPW_SCALE=1 | still at 1:1, still in the right half |
So no x shift on our side: VPW scales the camera only, and the right-half offset is not the camera centre
([vpw] title cam 800CF090 w512 cx256 -> w1024 cx512).
New instrument ROGUESQ_LOG_G1D_RECT=1 (dpc_bridge rs64_g1d_rect_scan, read-only; per swap: colour image, width, scissor,
texrect/tri x extents). Title: 4:3 cw=512 rects=161 x=0..512; 21:9 cw=1024 rects=161 x=256..768. **The game draws
the title correctly, centred in the wide image.** The display was the fault: osViSetMode #10 (initVideoSubsystem,
mode 80128DA0 type 0x08) has width=1024 xScale=0x333 fld origins 1024/2048 at EVERY aspect, 4:3 retail included. For
this interlaced 512x448 mode the VI width is the two-line field stride (2x512). The s6113 hook only widens modes
requested at width 512, so at 21:9 the VI read 512 px per line from a 1024-wide image: fb x 0..~512 across the screen,
i.e. pillar + left half of the still at 2x. That matches the symptom exactly.
ORIGIN: writer = the game's own mode builder (the 2x512 stride constant, legitimate at 4:3) combined with our s6113
fbw widening, which made the colour image fbw wide without rescaling this mode.

**Fix (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp osViSetMode hook).** fbw>512 and width==1024 and xScale<=0x333: width = 2*fbw,
xScale*fbw/512, field origins (+0x28/+0x3C)*fbw/512 (21:9: 2048 / 0x666 / 2048,4096; 16:9: 1592 / 0x4F9). Later
1024-wide flight modes carry 0x666 and are excluded. First attempt (xScale only) centred the still but squeezed it
vertically, which confirmed the stride reading. Two residuals: (1) pillar columns showed stale heap bytes (white at 21:9,
noise at 16:9): the title image is single-buffered and never cleared because at 4:3 the still covers it, so
dpc_bridge rs64_g1d_title_clear zeroes each wide 16-bit colour image once while the mode is live
(rs64_g1d_title_vi); (2) an orange strip left of START = trail of the menu bar sliding in (rects start at x=172 and
move toward 256; at 4:3 that is off-screen / overdrawn), so the same pass clamps a full-width SET_SCISSOR to the centre
512 columns (the retail visible area). ROGUESQ_G1D_TITLE_VI=0 = old path (verified, c219 garbled).
**Bug caught by the regression and fixed:** the first clear pass walked the RDP stream at a fixed 8-byte stride, read
texrect/triangle payload words as SET_COLOR_IMAGE and zeroed ~900 KB at bogus addresses (cimg=0103CD/CE03CD/9003CD).
Every crashed attempt (3/3: SIGBUS, abort, SIGBUS) logged one. It now walks command boundaries (texrect 16 B,
triangles by op length) and requires a 64-byte-aligned address. Rerun: att=1 mission_verified_130s, 0 crash.
**Result.** screenshots/s6720_title_before_after.png: 21:9 before, 21:9 after, 16:9 after, 4:3 retail; after =
retail framing with clean black pillars. lvl1 21:9 forced route mission_verified_130s; level select, craft select and
flight still fill the window (scratch/s6720/r219). 16:9 route: see the result line below.
**Discrimination.** Rect x extents (game output sane, centred) vs the VI mode values select H-stride (VI side, mode
stride/xScale) and refute H-texrect-shift (no host x shift: anchor/region/spike arms were inert, and the rects are
already at 256..768) and H-vpw (VPW changes only the zoom). Next: menu sweep (NEXT g1d-menu-sweep).
16:9 route (scratch/s6720/r169): att=1 mission_verified_130s, 0 crash; title [fbw] title-vi width 1024->1592 xScale 0x4F9 + one clear (cimg 751E00 cw 796); title still pillarboxed and clean at t=20, select and flight full width.
Discrimination: this selects H-stride (VI mode stride/xScale) and refutes H-texrect-shift and H-vpw; next discriminator: g1d-menu-sweep (OPTIONS/pause/debrief rect extents + VI modes at 21:9/16:9 vs 4:3).

epoch has 64 draws. RT64 still applies it only when the latched colour width equals the VI fbSize (unchanged

ORIGIN: set_frequency (src/main/main.cpp), called on the GAME thread by osAiSetFrequency (librecomp ai.cpp:152 ->
ultramodern::set_audio_frequency), does SDL_CloseAudioDevice + reopen while the events thread (events.cpp:1540
get_remaining_audio_bytes) is inside SDL_GetQueuedAudioSize on the same device -> use-after-free of the device's lock.

pair 5 lines after `[vi] update_screen #384`; attract1 crashed 3 lines after the same #384 line with no reopen line

with 4.2-7.6M interleaved polls over 300 reopens. Not a mitigation: it removes the data race.
Fix: static std::recursive_mutex audio_device_mutex held around every SDL call on audio_device (open_audio_output,
set_frequency and F9 route close/reopen, queue_samples queue/size, get_frames_remaining, queue snapshot).

  retail = a*port + b over the best pairs): the RDP dithers then truncates to 5 bits, and the sum over dither 0..7
  of floor((x+d)/8) is x, so the unbiased 5->8 inverse is v<<3. The old decode v*255/31 inflates by 255/248 = 1.028.
  - lvl1 flight: full a = 1.011/1.032/1.035 (R/G/B), shift a = 0.982/1.000/1.003, b within +-2.3 -> the gain is gone.
  - s6743 mission-intro cinematic (re-analysed offline): full a = 1.017-1.024, shift a = 0.980-0.990, b +0.8..+2.9;
    best-pair d 3.6 -> 1.9 with shift. Binned by intensity (scratch/s6744/gain_bins.py) the full-decode ratio is flat
    1.016-1.019 from 96 to 255, so a residual ~-1% (shift) remains in the intro; open, tiny.
  - Why s6740 refuted this "decoder convention" idea: the static LucasArts logo and snow frames had gain ~1.00. A
    texture copied to the framebuffer is 5-bit on both sides (RT64 expands it with v*255/31 too) and snow saturates
    at 31, so those frames could not show the shading gain. That refutation is superseded for shaded 3D content.
  Two lines: two scenes (512 flight and 640 cinematic) both lose most of the gain under shift, and the Hermite
  identity predicts the 1.028 factor that bounds every observed full-decode gain (1.011-1.035).
- Default decode left at full (reproduces earlier numbers and fits textured/2D content); use --dec shift for shaded 3D.

  keep their times relative to it. Rerun with 42.5:w640 (scratch/s6747/port_bz2): "[autopilot] gate 9/94 width=640 reached
  at wall 42.5 s -> clock rebased to 42.5", crawl skipped at 50 s, flight at 68.9 s, 0 CRASH. In this run the crawl came on
