## Session 6755 (2026-11-01) — G3: lvl4's late scripted event is a song end on the audio clock (same length in AI buffers in both arms); fixed duplicate VI edges in the VI thread (deadline truncated to whole us)

Context: the first attempt at this iteration timed out (rc=124) with no entry. Its runs are in scratch/s6755 (retail_a..g,
retail, port1..5; dt-pinned lvl4 s6754 recipe with different XTRACE_MEM blocks). This session's runs are in scratch/s6756.
Ran / read:
- tools/g3_tick_mem.py (left uncommitted by the timed-out attempt; now takes G3_FROM/G3_TO/G3_IGN and prints the VI
  column) on scratch/s6755/retail vs port5, block 0x8010C9E0:18. Event mask word +0 = 0x100 at tick 2302 retail and
  2315 port. Its dt timer +0x0C is bit-identical in both arms. +0x3C = 0x100 at tick 2123 and +0x00 = 2 at tick 2143 in
  both arms.
- Static (generated C; PROJECT-OVERVIEW s5753 store map): bit 0x100 is set at 0x800EE85C in tickSongFadeTimer
  (0x800EE730) when byte 0x8010C264 != 0 and isSongHandleActive(*0x8010C0E0) (0x800957AC: 8 MusyX song slots at
  0x80149A00 stride 0xEF8, active byte +0xEC1) returns 0. So the event waits for a song to finish.
- s6756 retail/port (song-state spec: 0x8010C0E0, 0x8010C260:44, slot headers 0-3): handle 0 -> 1 at tick 2145 in both
  arms (0x8010C270 slot = 0x0007000f), back to 0 at tick 2303 retail / 2318 port. No playback-position word in the slot
  headers.
- Instrument: runAiAudioStreamPlaybackLoop feeds fixed 0x300-byte AI buffers (osAiSetNextBuffer jal at 0x8008EE08 /
  0x8008EE84). Port marker rows added there (tools/fixup_rand_trace.py s6755 block, also wired through the vendored
  regen); retail uses --exec-trace-also on the same PCs. New tools/g3_ai_clock.py (oracle rows: the pc= field is the
  executed PC; column 3 is the trace site).
  Positive control: rows fire in both arms (retail 11213, port 9075 buffers).
- Result (retailb vs portb): song = 635 retail vs 640 port AI buffers, equal within 1%, so the sequencer runs on the
  audio clock. Buffers per "VI": retail 1.912 (nominal 22048/192/59.94 = 1.916), port 1.866 over the flight and 1.788
  in the song. Port s4245 setnext in flight (phase 7): 114.9 buf/s = 22055 Hz wall, nominal. So the port's audio was
  right and its VI column was ~3% fast.
- rs64_vi_n_g counts update_screen. The [phase] rows give 61.9-63.3 update_screen per wall second. The G1E timeline
  (ROGUESQ_G1E_TL, portc) shows 9050 VI-thread edges against total_vis 29..8955 (59.999/s), with 123 edges repeating
  the previous total_vis. Each repeat is followed 0.00-0.01 ms later by arg+1, i.e. two loop passes at one instant.
ORIGIN: the writer is ultramodern vi_thread_func. Its deadline `start + (total_vis * 1000000us) / 60` truncates to
whole us, up to 0.67 us before the true boundary. When sleep_until(next - 2ms) wakes early, the s6456 spin exits inside
that window, and `floor(now * 60) + 1` returns the previous total_vis. The loop then runs again with no sleep, enqueuing
an extra ScreenUpdateAction and an extra VI retrace message (remaining_retraces--). The value is not legitimate: it is a
VI that hardware never delivers.
Fix (lib/N64ModernRuntime events.cpp, patch exported): the deadline rounds up to the exact ns boundary, plus a guard
that total_vis always advances. ROGUESQ_VI_TRUNC_DEADLINE=1 restores the old deadline.
Two arms, same recipe (portc control on the old binary, portd fix; tools/g3_vi_edges.py):
- repeats 123 -> 0
- VI edges 60.828 -> 59.999/s
- AI buf/VI 1.866 -> 1.914 (retail 1.912)
- song 343 -> 334 VI (retail 332), 640 -> 639 buffers
- song end tick 2316 -> 2312 (retail 2302-2303)
The residual tick gap is pacing: retail mupen drops frames (2.115 VI/tick in the song), while the port holds 2.000.
With dt pinned, retail therefore runs fewer ticks per audio second. In normal play dt is measured, so sim time per
audio time agrees. Swap rate is 32.4 -> 32.1/s whole run (1-VI swap intervals 956 -> 863, mostly outside the mission
loop: in flight the port is exactly 2.000 VI/tick). Not chased.
Rules out: H-pi and H-clock for the lvl4 event (the trigger is song end, measured in audio buffers); a slow port audio
clock (wall 22055 Hz).
Supersedes: the port "VI" figures in s6749 (update_screen 61-62/s, now explained) and s6752-s6754. Those counted
update_screen, including the 1.4% repeated VIs.
Does NOT establish: why the game swaps at 1-VI intervals outside flight (863 per run); any audible effect of the old
extra VIs.

Root cause of the clamp (static, menu code 0x800C5E14-0x800C5E6C): a3 = 15 raised to 16 by 0x80130B4C&0x00200000 (or

copies record word +0xC bits 9-22 into 0x80130B4C, and the record starts at save copy +0x2C (rec[5] -> B40 = +0x31), so
save byte +0x39 = 0x60 sets both bonus bits. Verified two arms, same recipe: without it a3=15 (run 1); with it
(scratch/s6770/ul) a3=16, unlockMask 0x00080000, B40=16. run.sh adds it automatically for LEVEL>=16.

SDV byte loop :355/357 = 124, LDV :201 = 36, byte()/element() accessors 203, scalar W/H byte loops ~60. The ucode .c call
at :447 (429, inclusive) is the DPC bridge (s6716 H-bridge-essential, unchanged).
Discrimination: selects H-dispatch(-ish): per-access scaffolding (byte-at-a-time DMEM through xor-3 addressing + the select
guard) ~35% of ucode self; H-vec math (VMADN/VMADM/VMUDL bodies) is the remainder, each op < 4%; no single H-hotloop block.
Change (lib/N64ModernRuntime, exported to submodule-patches/N64ModernRuntime.patch):
- rsp.hpp: rs64_dmem_w/_w_set/_h/_h_set (DMEM keeps each 32-bit word byte-reversed, so an aligned BE word is one native
  access and an even halfword sits at addr^2); RSP_MEM_W_LOAD/W_STORE/HU_LOAD/H_LOAD/H_STORE take them when aligned (audio
  dmem-store hooks still run).
- rsp_vu.hpp: r128::word(n) = BE vector word n as raw u32 [3-n].
- rsp_vu_impl.hpp: aligned fast paths LDV/SDV (e%4==0, e<=8), LLV/SLV (e%4==0), LSV/SSV (e even), LQV/SQV (e==0, word
  aligned, 16-(addr&15) bytes); unaligned/odd-e keep the byte loops; hooks/notes unchanged. Element-select table now
  `alignas(16) static constexpr uint8_t shuffle[16][16]` (same bytes, generated from the old _mm_set_epi8 rows) + _mm_load_si128.

Findings: (1) NEXT.md's "rsp_vu.hpp:75 = r128::byte() const" was a mislabel: line 75 is `r128::operator=(__m128i)`, the vd
writeback of VMADN/VMADM/VMADH<8>, i.e. vector-math latency, not an accessor; H-lbv and H-other-ld are refuted (LBV/SBV/LUV
<1% each). (2) H-unaligned refuted for SDV: with DMEM on, the byte-loop line (rsp_vu_impl.hpp:366) has no samples; SDV's 9.6%
sits on the fast path. Disassembly of the hot SDV addresses shows why: `ldr x12,[sp,#0x390]; ldr x8,[x12]` before each access.
g_dmem_cur is `inline thread_local uint8_t*`; every uint8_t store may alias it, so the compiler re-fetches it through a spilled
TLS address after each DMEM store. The ucode's MIPS GPRs are stack slots too ([sp,#0x290] etc.).
Change: rsp.hpp gains `RS64_DMEM_BASE` (default g_dmem_cur) used by RSP_MEM_B/BU, rs64_dmem_*, and the static-inline DMA
helpers. CMake compiles the gfx ucode TU with -DRS64_DMEM_BASE=dmem -DRSP=RS64_RSP_GFX: the gfx ucode only runs on the gfx
thread where g_dmem_cur == dmem (only M_AUDTASK swaps in dmem_audio, rsp.cpp DmemGuard), and the type rename keeps its
RSP:: template instantiations (external-linkage inline) from being merged by the linker with the audio TU's (factor5_ucode_b,
aspMain.cpp), which must keep the per-thread base. All rsp.hpp helpers are static inline (internal linkage). New
src/rsp/factor5_ucode_tls.cpp compiles the same fixed-up .c a second time as factor5_ucode_tls on the old base (same -O2 +
inline threshold); main.cpp picks per gfx task: ROGUESQ_G1E_DMEMBASE (default 1), _TOGGLE=<sec> ([g1e-dmembase] lines), and
falls back to the TLS arm (one warning line) if g_dmem_cur != dmem. Function-local statics in factor5_ucode are only env caches
and diagnostic counters (checked), and ucode state lives in the shared dmem, so the arms can alternate per task.
tools/g1e_fast_ab.py --key dmembase. lib/ edit exported (submodule-patches/N64ModernRuntime.patch).

every run. s6779's "inset never" and s6780's "left never" were two faces of one flaky defect.

4x5 black tiles + border, and ~200 emblem tris) is absent from the submitted stream, right panel control present; good
state = 237 texrects, retail rdplog 237. Not RT64, not a ucode cap (0 [ucode-cap] fires).
Three-way RAM diff (oracle --fb-dump 0:800000 vs ROGUESQ_RDRAM_DUMP_DIR, scratch/s6781/memdiff.py) over the menu
overlay data/bss: slot array 0x800CF180 stride 0x48 (built in the 0x800B49A8 loop): slot0 = inset, slot1 = left panel.
Missing slot = +0x15=1, +0x16=0, alpha(+0x18)=0, state(+0x41)=0. Slot state machine 0x800B883C (jump table
0x800A68B8): state 4 fades out and requests an image (0x800B3F24 -> sendServiceMessage to the format-message worker,
request id counter 0x800CC854); state 0 polls 0x800B3FD8 (tryRecvServiceMessage, ONE message per frame) and fades in the
slot whose id (+0x20) equals received byte +0x17.
ORIGIN: the worker tickFormatMessageWorker 0x800B3650 builds each completion on ITS OWN STACK (sp+0x10, id word at +0x14,
written at 0x800B37F8-0x800B3800) and sendServiceMessage queues the POINTER (no copy), then the worker frees the request
and loops. Marks via tools/fixup_rand_trace.py (0x800B380C send, 0x800B3FA0 request, 0x800B4004 receive;
ROGUESQ_XTRACE_MEM=800B380C:6:0:8,800B3FA0:6:58:2,800B4004:3:0:8). Port (2 runs): ids 2/3/4 requested on one VI,
completions 1 VI apart (VI 1096/1097/1098), menu receives at 1097/1099/1100 = ids 2,4,4 from the same buffer 0x801DBE58 -
id 3 (left panel) lost. Retail (oracle --exec-trace 0x800B380C + -also 0x800B3FA0/0x800B4004, RS64_XTRACE_MEM): each
completion takes ~60 VI (1753/1873/1930/1992), menu receives each 1 VI later, ids 1,2,3,4 distinct. The value is
legitimate guest data overwritten by a legitimate later completion: a latent game race that hardware timing never
exposes (the port's native-speed worker does).
Fix tried first and REJECTED: block the worker after its send (osSetTimer + osRecvMesg on a private queue below sp) until
the menu queue drains. Worked (3/3 EI) but unregisterServiceWorker osDestroyThreads the worker and frees the node that
holds its stack with no exit message, so a pending timer could write freed heap. Replaced by:
FIX (tools/fixup_menu_worker.py, wired into fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py after fixup_rand_trace; host side
src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp rs64_menu_worker_sent/recv): after a successful send record (msg pointer, full id word)
in a host FIFO; after the menu's lbu at 0x800B4004 return the recorded id for that pointer. Stale entries: the id
counter is reset to 1 by initFormatMessageWorker (0x800B3EC8), so an id <= the last recorded clears the FIFO. A first
staleness rule using the dest queue validCount popped live entries (validCount read 0 right after a successful send) and
was dropped. No guest memory or scheduling change. ROGUESQ_MENU_WORKER_FIFO=0 = old.
Same-build A/B (scratch/s6781/fifo*): fix press16 a/b + press21 -> EI 17/17, 15/17(+2 fade-in), 16/18(+2 fade-in),
restored ids "2 3" / "3" / "3"; control FIFO=0 press16 -> -I 17/17, received ids 1 2 4 4. 0 crash lines. Owner sheet
scratch/s6781/selgame_fix_sheet.png (retail | before | after).
Census seed (main + menu overlay only): stack-payload sendServiceMessage sites 0x8000582C, 0x800058FC (main),
0x800B380C (fixed), 0x800C5880 (menu); other overlays not yet disassembled. Queued soak s6781_menufifo_lvl1_dd1.
Discrimination: selects H-create-side (guest never submits the panel) and within it H-race (stack completion overwritten

## Session 6782 (2026-11-01) — stack-payload service-message class audit CLOSED: 8 stack-formed send sites in main + 3 overlays, 1 live (s6781, fixed), 3 doorbells, 1 dead, 3 synchronous; s6781 FIFO soak clean

HYPOTHESIS-ID: service-msg-stack-payload-audit (closed).

Soak fold: s6781_menufifo_lvl1_dd1 rc=0, hold 304 s, 0 VI stalls, 0 crash lines (FIFO fix on, lvl1 dd1).
Method (offline, retail ROM): disassembled main (ROM 0x1000, vram 0x80000400) and the mission/menu/cinematic overlays
(0xA5D30/0x10C2D0/0x137580, vram 0x800A5130) with mips64-elf-objdump; enumerated every jal sendServiceMessage
(0x80006F78) AND raw osSendMesg (0x80033410), traced the message register back to its definition. Control: the ROM holds
exactly 14 `jal 0x80006F78` words = the 14 sites the disassembly found (10 main, 4 menu, 0 mission/cinematic); 56 osSendMesg.
sendServiceMessage (read this session): writes msg+2 seq, +4 flags=0, +8 = sender's reply queue, then osSendMesg(dest+464,
msg, NOBLOCK) (retry if a3&1) - pointer only. 0x8000703C = reply: sets +4|=0x40, sends the same pointer to msg+8.
Classification (tools/audit_service_msg_stack.py reproduces it; exits nonzero on any new unaudited stack site):
- LIVE: 0x800B380C tickFormatMessageWorker completion (fixed s6781).
- Doorbell, payload never dereferenced: 0x8000582C/0x800058FC (self-sends to the worker at 0x801126BC whose tick 0x80005570
  calls blocking recv 0x80006F24 and discards v0, reading only its ring at 0x801112B0); 0x800C5880 tickSongAssetLoadWorker
  (0x800C5834) completion to the requester, received only at 0x800C3B4C (menuSubtype02Handler) which tests v0 != 0.
- Synchronous: 0x80004BE4/0x80004D0C/0x80004F28 send a heap ring message whose +0x10 points to an 0x80FF-tagged object at
  the sender's sp+16; the sender then loops on blocking recv until that object comes back (server 0x80004540 writes +12
  and forwards it), so the frame outlives the use. Their async branches (0x80004C3C/0x80004F8C) take a caller buffer
  (a1 of 0x80004AAC/0x80004E70): of 43 callers the only non-literal one (0x80054F9C/0x80054FBC) passes s3 = 0, so the
  caller-buffer path never runs in retail code.
- Dead: osSendMesg 0x80091E78 in shutdownAudioEngine sends a stack quit byte 0xFF to the AI queue 0x80149670 then frees
  the buffers runAiAudioStreamPlaybackLoop uses (a real use-after-free if it ran: a garbage byte keeps that loop alive).
  Its only caller shutdownMusyXEngine (0x8008ECA4) has no jal, no lui/addiu formation and no pointer word in the ROM
  (same search finds the worker entry 0x80005570 formation as control); agrees with ledger s~28672 "no callers at all".
- Heap payloads (not this class): 0x80004540, 0x800492D8, 0x8006F2B4, 0x800B3FA0, 0x800C3B38.
Residual (single-source, not demonstrated): the game worker queue (0x80138920) has two menu consumers,
pollServiceMessageByte 0x800B3FD8 (reads +0x17) and 0x800C3B4C (doorbell). If SELECT GAME image completions and song-load
doorbells were ever pending together, one consumer could eat the other's message; the s6781 FIFO then keeps a stale front
entry (same worker stack pointer every time) until the next id reset. Only matters if both screens' workers coexist.
Discrimination: selects H-safe for every site except the one s6781 fixed; refutes H-live (no other stack completion is
read after its sender can reuse the frame). No game run this session (offline audit + soak fold).

  0x800426A4-D8 and their 0xDB0 twin clamp trunc(height x scale) to the floats at 0x8003A4E8/EC and 0x8003A4F0/F4 = 127.0 /

25213 buffers = 1.912 buf/VI. Port (same pre-fix build) from VI 13: seven 19-20 VI gaps at VI 96, 371, 738, 1406, 1976,
2825, 3960, each immediately before a width change or audio re-init, plus 3-5 VI gaps at 737-760/974/2593/2807/2954.
Inside a gap the port logs no guest rand row at all.
Mechanism (log correlation, every 19-20 VI gap): each sits on an audio re-init (thr-create-id, s4572-pub, and TWO
"[audio-route] output=... rate=22047" lines); 6/7 also carry the waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone spin (s4192 mode 2) +
s4562 pause, but the boot one (VI 96) has no spin, so the spin is not the common term. The [audio-route] line comes
from src/main/main.cpp set_frequency, which closed and reopened the SDL/CoreAudio device on EVERY osAiSetFrequency,
even 22047 -> 22047. On hardware osAiSetFrequency is a DACRATE register write.
Fix (src/main/main.cpp set_frequency): same rate with an open device returns immediately; a real rate change (boot
48000 -> 22047, the G2b 32006 crawl and back) still reopens. ROGUESQ_AI_REOPEN_ALWAYS=1 restores the old behaviour.

(REOPEN_ALWAYS=1, positive control): 16 [audio-route] opens, each reopen 143-161 ms, the seven 18-20 VI gaps reproduce
(95, 370, 738, 1406, 1976, 2826, 3961), 1.866 buf/VI. Side datum: the fix arm hit the mission load 640 at 42.6 s vs
47.6 s and flight at 61.2 vs 66.5 s on the same autopilot schedule (not chased).
Two lines: independent retail oracle (no gap) + same-build A/B toggling only the reopen.
ORIGIN: the writer of the gap is the host set_frequency (SDL close/open blocks the guest thread calling
osAiSetFrequency); not legitimate (retail never stops the AI feed). Root-cause fix, not a guard.
Residual: 3-5 VI gaps at the title (VI 737, 974) in both port arms, retail max 2 VI (~60 ms; unnamed).
Verdict: the retail control selects H-port and refutes H-retail; the same-build A/B closes the thread with the root cause

title switch) and 5-6 VI @ 971-979. Each is a REAL underrun: queue bytes before the resuming buffer = 0 (aiwall 79-107

buildScaledFormatTextElement > rasterizeFormatMessageGlyphs > buildDebrisMeshFromCells (69 ms), OSId 7 =

the text glyph cell-mesh builders.) The AI feeder is viRetraceHandlerThread > musyxSynthFrame.
Mechanism: ultramodern delivers host-thread messages (VI retrace, AI drain) only inside a guest OS call
(dequeue_external_messages) and swaps to a ready higher-priority thread only at check_running_queue, so a low-priority
thread computing without OS calls cannot be preempted. Retail preempts on the interrupt (retail oracle s6807: max 2 VI).

thread, dequeue external messages + check_running_queue (a swap only ever goes to a higher-priority ready thread, as on
hardware). tools/fixup_preempt_point.py (run from fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py, idempotent) calls it at the entry of
rasterizeFormatMessageGlyphs, buildDebrisMeshFromCells, rebuildDebrisCellGeometry, emitDebrisCellFaces,
buildDebrisCellBitfield. ROGUESQ_PREEMPT_POINT=0 disables.
A/B, same build, sequential: fix1/fix3 (title route) top gaps [2,2,2,2,2], qzero only the boot row (VI 13); ctl1
(PREEMPT_POINT=0, positive control) gaps 4@740, 5@973, qzero at VI 744/978/1096 = pre-fix. 0 crash lines in all arms.
Two lines: AI-trace queue depth + run-token stamps per VI, and an independent host stack sample naming the busy function.
ORIGIN: the writer of the gap is ultramodern's cooperative scheduler (no preemption between OS calls); not legitimate
(retail preempts). Root-cause class fix, applied at the sites measured; other long OS-call-free stretches on low-priority
threads would show the same signature (token held by a low-pri id across a gap) in g3_title_gap.py.
Queued: scratch/agent/soak_queue/s6808_preempt_lvl1_fps60.sh (lvl1 FPS60 300 s hold + AI trace).

## Session 6817 (2026-11-02) — G3 FPS60 lvl14 scrape: the collision resolver's per-pass deflection step is K*dt (a quantum, not a force), so FPS60 deflects half per contact tick; fixed (max(dt,1/30) under FPS60): contacts 7 -> 4, exit pitch = 30 Hz exactly, hit50/s 0.057 -> 0.094 (30 Hz 0.107), death none -> 90.6 s (30 Hz 81.3)

Static (generated C, rodata from ../rogue_squadron64/build/roguesquadron.elf mission overlay 0x800A5130):
- integrateCraftVelocityAndCollide 0x800AECF8 = pos += impulse(+0x198)*dt, impulse-magnitude rumble/sound tiers, impulse
  cleared. dt-correct; not the term.
- 0x800FEF10 (misnamed stepObjectOrientationTowardTarget; f24 = a1 = dt) is the craft collision resolver: sweep = vel*dt,
  up to 5 passes (counter sp+0x48C < 5, 0x800FFA3C). Each pass with a contact takes one jump-table case (0x800FF47C..0x800FF98C):
  rotate the orientation matrix by K*dt (0x8001CC3C/0x8001CD6C; K = +-120 deg/s heading cases, +-180 deg/s pitch cases,
  rodata 0x800A9468..0x800A94A8), add K'*dt to the caller's angle accumulators (a2/a3 = sp+0x168/0x16C), clamp +0xD8/+0xDC to
  0 if pointing into the surface, then re-sweep with vel*dt.
- Player record 0x80137DB0 words 54-56 (+0xD8/+0xDC/+0xE0) are heading/pitch/roll in DEGREES (not velocity; s6816 called
  them vel). Trace s6816 seed 1: per contact tick pitch -30 at 30 Hz = 5 passes x 6 deg; FPS60 -15/-15/-15/-9/-6/-9 = 5/5/5/3/2/3
  passes x 3 deg, plus one heading +10 (5 x 2 deg). So the step per pass is a deflection QUANTUM scaled by dt: at FPS60 the
  craft deflects half per contact tick, stays at the surface, takes 7 contact ticks (20 hp each, per tick) instead of 2.
Fix: tools/fixup_fps60_scrape.py (wired into fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py after preempt_point): the ten case multiplies use
  rs64_scrape_dt(dt) = max(dt, 1/30) when ROGUESQ_FPS60 is set; ROGUESQ_FPS60_SCRAPE=0 restores; sweep multiplies keep dt;
  retail (no FPS60) untouched. Built in place (build/RogueSquadron64Recomp).

  Note: "384 px past the edge" is retail's tolerance taken relative to the wide edge; on a centred 21:9 frustum the

command. Recipe scratch/s6851/abd.sh (s6850 abd.sh + DIAG=2, SAT arm, bin deleted after scan).
Run 1 (lvl17 21:9, 200 s hold, alive, 0 stalls): control ZERO-W in the forced-overlay window = 12 binwalk lines, all

24C2221A,00BE01CC = ul.x 760 lr.x 776.5; bin 2402221A,00FE01CC = ul.x 1016 lr.x 8.5). -> This selects H-late and refutes H-shadow and
H-split refuted. The writer between walker and RT64 is rs64_region_scan (called after rs64_g1d_rect_wrap in
rs64_dpc_record_submit): the s6159 HUD-anchor radar-disc shift, auto-set by ROGUESQ_ASPECT (main.cpp: region
669,810,20,135, shift 256 at w1024), adds dx*4 to both texrect x fields and masks with 0xFFF, so a rect in the box at
ul.x >= 768 lands past 1024 and its lr.x wraps (lr < ul -> RT64 drops it).

ours; the game's rect at ul.x 760 is valid).

texture origin unchanged; a rect pushed wholly past the field becomes zero-width). ROGUESQ_G1D_SHIFT_SAT=0 = old.

Control: u30 vs u30b 695/695 rows identical; u30 vs u60 0 rows. Same-site positive control for the row filter: 695-755 rows fire per arm, and [camlog] pitch agrees with the holds (0.06233/0.06316/0.06055, the s6876 values).
Result, sum|d word 5| per caller: updateEffectObjectOrientationQuat +10636 1.40/2.20/2.20 (u20/u30/u60); +41236 0.00000 in all arms. buildEffectObjectWorldTransform never appears in [camcall2]: it changes no row 1 word while the row filter is on. Its 8/10 share in s6876 was call count, not effect.
Mechanism: +10636 applies a whole-angle correction (site 0x8004E45C by address order, inferred; angle = 90 - 57.29578*asin(x)). The smallest rotation it applied is 0.0815 deg in every arm. sinfApprox (0x8001C400, really asin) returns exactly pi/2 for x > 0.99999899 (ROM 0x3F7FFFEF at 0x80000810), and acos of that is 0.08156 deg. So any error below 0.0816 deg reads as zero and the camera holds. Two lines: measured floor in 3 arms, ROM constant. The explicit 0.01 deg thresholds (0x8003A988/8C) never bind at this site; the +41236 site, gain scaled, does go down to 0.0100.
Why dt shows: pitch climbs in steps of 0.0011-0.0018 rad, then stops at the first point inside the zone. Step sizes and gaps differ per dt (u20 gaps 1,2,2,4; u60 4,5,7,14), so the last step lands at 0.06233, 0.06316 or 0.06055. That is why pitch is not monotonic in dt: it is a stopping point, not a dt term in a formula. Zone width 2 x 0.08156 = 0.163 deg; arm spread 0.1495 deg (u30 - u60) fits. lvl5's 0.00039 rad fits too.
Not explained: s6875's upper figure 0.26 deg exceeds one zone width, and that figure came from other rows. Not measured here. The target direction the correction aims at was not logged. dt does not appear in this site's code as read, but the target comes from position deltas, so dt reaches it through motion; inferred, not traced. Oracle not run, so retail behaviour at 1/60 is not observed; the clamp itself is a ROM constant.
Failed: my first reading said the in-place site could not change word 4 because a1 row 1 is 0,1,0; samples were at zero angle and it does change word 4 (sum 0.69 on u20), it leaves word 5. Rotation angles from the matrix trace looked quantised (0.0810, 0.0992...); that was the 6 decimal log, off-diagonal terms give a smooth histogram. Second wait command timed out at 600 s, harmless.
ORIGIN: no mitigation added. Writer of the pitch is the retail correction above, value legitimate.
DISCRIMINATION: selects H-quat, refutes H-build, and refutes H-early for the holds measured (the holds are set in flight at swaps 3042-3112 and later). Root cause of the dt-dependent pitch is the retail asin clamp dead zone. No fix: changing it departs from retail, and FPS60's offset is within the band retail itself allows.
Rules out: a dt term in the camera pitch formula at the site read; buildEffectObjectWorldTransform as a pitch source. Thread g3-optin-frame-diff closes as measured for lvl1, per NEXT.md.

Batch 1 (no W rows): on-screen 59.8-59.9 in all 60 fps arms, CA dropped 0.00. 21:9 arms queued 2 presents per workload (115-120/s), 4:3 queued 60. First scorer read was wrong twice: it crashed on the SIGKILL-truncated row, and it judged "new" against the previous queued row, which miscounts when the skipped copy comes first. Fixed before use. The first order model (buffer of a workload = vi of its first row) was an assumption, so W rows replaced it; the batch 1 model figures are not quoted.

Batch 2 (W rows, SCREEN_JOB on), fwd/held/miss/BACK per s: 21:9 dd4 47.5/4.34/6.17/2.00, 4:3 dd4 59.9/0/0/0, 21:9 dd1 29.8/0.80/15.26/14.16, 4:3 dd1 60.0/0/0/0. Width selects it, dd does not. ORIGIN: rt64_state.cpp needStaticPresent, `screenFbSize.x >= 1024u`, session 21, written for the retail 1024-wide phase that has no earlyPresentCandidate. 21:9 flight VI width is 1024 (`[phase] vi_width=1024`), 4:3 is 512, 16:9 768. So the early-return never fired and each VI pushed a stale-origin present behind the early one. Present thread keeps only the last queued entry (skipPresent = writeCursor != threadCursor), so which of the two ran depended on phase. This is not a guard: the rule was over-broad, and it now holds only once early presents have stopped.

Two gate bugs found by a hide test (window hidden 10 s by osascript in flight), neither shipped. First version counted handlers, so one lost handler would leave it short for good; review caught that. The timeout resync I added for it was itself wrong: it over-credited, and b_g2h sat at 72.1 after the hide, identical to control, with the gate silently open. Replaced by the highest reported id, which needs no resync. Final build, c_g2h: while hidden presents ran 32/s (8 logged timeouts by power-of-two sampling, so at least 128 fired, CA reporting at=0), and after the window came back latency returned to 45.4/48.2, on-screen 60.0. The default arm b_d3h kept presenting at 60/s when hidden. The 32/s is not only presents: with the gate the game's own [g1b] tasks fell to 32-33/s for those seconds and returned to 60 after, so hiding the window slows the game with the gate on. Control b_d3h held 60 tasks/s through its hide, so the gate causes this. Same cause is expected whenever CoreAnimation stops reporting promptly; a fix would skip the wait once the handler reports at=0. Batch 1 ran the count build with no timeout logging, and bw_g2 the resync build with 0 timeouts, so the id build is confirmed only by c_g2h and cw_g2 (45.3/48.4, 0 timeouts). 4:3 unhidden has not been run on the final build except c_g2h's pre-hide flight.

## Session 6887 (2026-11-04) — PRESENT_INFLIGHT=2 fixed off screen and qualified through hide, resize, fullscreen and minimize; 312 s flight holds 48 ms

Planned: is ROGUESQ_PRESENT_INFLIGHT=2 safe through resize and fullscreen (NEXT g1e-present-latency), with the hidden-window slowdown fixed first.

ORIGIN: the slowdown was our own s6886 gate. s6886 rings, offline: while hidden, the default arm's reports arrive ~50 ms after the present with presentedTime 0, i.e. only when later presents replace the drawable. Under the gate that delay was 186 ms and presents ran 16/s, each wait running out its 50 ms cap. The value is legitimate; the gate's assumption that a report means a free queue slot holds only on screen.

Fix, plume_metal.cpp: the gate opens on a report with presentedTime 0 or on a timeout, and closes on the first report of a present that reached the screen. Transitions log as [s6887], power-of-two limited. Each gated run logged one timeout: g near hide onset (id 7131), w near the fullscreen toggle (id 10228, about t=170 s by id; position inferred from id and log order, not stamped). The timeout path also covers a handler that does not fire, which these runs did not exercise.

## Session 6893 (2026-11-05) — G5a writer named: tile variant pool overrun at dd>1, fixed and matched-pair tested; owner re-flight still needed
HYPOTHESIS-ID: g5a-walker-junk. Two loop iterations: the first hit the 3600 s cap (rc=124) with this work uncommitted and left its arm chain running; the second killed the chain, audited it and finished. s6892 (commit 2e3d822fd) has no ledger entry of its own: it added the walker guard, tools/apply_s6892_walker_guard.py.

ORIGIN: selectGridCellTileVariant (0x80046030) writes 25 bytes to pool[phase] + 25*count with no bound. The count (0x80137168) resets per frame in updateGridLayerScroll. initGridLayerFromLevelData sizes each pool from the map's flagged cells (LEVEL=4: 90 entries, req 0x8CA). A dd>1 window can pass that, and the block after pool[1] was the sky object, so its +0x18 mesh pointer took tile bytes. The value is not legitimate; retail's window stays inside the pool as far as measured (dd1 not measured here).
Fix, tools/apply_s6893_tilepool.py, default on, ROGUESQ_TILEPOOL=0 old: pools scale by K = ceil(dd)^2, x2 above 640 wide (ROGUESQ_TILEPOOL_K overrides), and the writer's slot index is clamped to the pool. K=1 at dd1 4:3, so the retail size is kept. Only the writer's own increment and retail's high-water word 0x8009DEC0 read the count; both stay unclamped and the clamp makes extra cells share the last slot.

Arms, LEVEL=4, FPS60, 16:9, hardware write watch on object +0x18 (scratch/s6893/g5awatch.py, wp_<arm>.log; 400-hit log cap):
| Arm | dd | Pool | Forced add | Peak count | Writer hits | Watch control | End |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tour | 2 | old build | 0 | 94 (RDRAM count and hw 0x5E) | 4 on 8082EBB0+0x18 | fired | SIGABRT, Unhandled jump target 0x3002 in ucode |
| ctlA | 2 | TILEPOOL=0 | 90 | not logged | 4 on 802C5000+0x18 | none | EXC_BAD_ACCESS, slotDispatcherIter |
| ctlC | 2 | K=1, clamp only | 90 | 136, cap 90 | 0 of 2 total | 2 planted | alive, 132 s hold |
| ctlB | 2 | K=8 | 90 | 137, cap 720 | 0 of 4 total | 2 planted | alive, 132 s hold |
| d4live | 4 | K=32 | 0 | 97, cap 2880 | 0 of 342 total | none planted; RT64 hits show it live | alive, 174 s hold |
| d4on | 4 | K=32 | 0 | 59 | 0 logged, cap reached | 2 planted | alive, 272 s hold |
| d4off | 4 | TILEPOOL=0 | 0 | not logged | 0 logged, cap reached | 2 planted | alive, 235 s hold |
| fix, corner | 2 | K=8 | 0 | under 90, 84 | 0 | planted | alive, 428/466 s |

What this shows: ctlA vs ctlC is the matched pair: same heap layout, same object address 802C5000 watched, forced overflow; without the bound the object is overwritten and the game crashes, with it 0 writes. d4live is the natural case: count passes 90 with no lever and nothing lands. Two lines (RDRAM read-back and hardware watch) name the writer on the natural tour.
Corrections to the first iteration's reading: fix and corner are NOT evidence for the fix, since they never reached 90, and K moves the heap so a clean run alone could be layout luck. d4on vs d4off does not discriminate: d4on peaked at 59, the object sits at 8074Axxx in the main heap at dd4 (not after the pool), and both watches hit the log cap. Natural peak varies a lot between runs of one route (59, 84, 94, 97): unexplained.
Not shown: that this is the owner's crash. Same object, same word, same kind of junk bytes, but 0x26282B2B itself was not reproduced naturally (the tour gave 0x2F303030, the lever 0x34343434) and that value in logs is the guard's planted test. Only the owner's mission flown past half way can close G5a. One crash per unfixed arm, n=1 each. Bigger pools were checked on LEVEL=4 only: spill used 0x2391F0 of 0x400000 at dd4, 0 arena full; a level with many more flagged cells could use far more, so scratch/s6893/census.zsh is queued as s6893_census_1-4.
New, open: at dd4 16:9 RT64 copyNativeToRAM writes pixels on the watched word at 8074A380/8074AC60 (171 memmove + 171 swap hits in d4live, no plant, so the plant did not cause it). The real guard never fired (no rs64_s6892.log in d4live, only the planted line in d4on and d4off), so nothing read that word afterwards, which suggests a dead block reused as an offscreen colour image and a stale watch. Inference, single-source: block liveness not checked. No VI origin at 240 rows covers the address, so the image, if that is what it is, is not a displayed frame. If the block is live this is a second corruption route.

## Session 6895 (2026-11-05) — G5b: flat-sky frames are RT64 wedges from W<=0 vertices, fixed at dd>1; dd4 near-plane sheets are bad stream data the RDP paints too

Includes the work of the iteration that timed out at 06:18 (rc=124, nothing committed); its arms are in scratch/s6895 and folded here. Owner recipe (FPS60, 16:9, no logging env), autopilot flight, tools as s6894.

ORIGIN: RT64 rebuilds each RDP tri as three vertices and extrapolates the RDP's W plane to them (rt64_gbi_rdp.cpp). The RDP only evaluates W on rows it draws, so a rebuilt vertex can have W<=0. RT64 then emits clip w = 65536000/W, and the GPU projects that vertex to infinity away from the tri: a screen-wide flat wedge that no RDP ever paints. The value is legitimate RDP data; RT64's use of it as a clip w is the defect.

Same stream through angrylion (tools/angrylion_replay/frame_replay.c, capture ROGUESQ_G5B_FRAME, src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp): the flat frames do not exist on the RDP (docs/owner_sheet_s6895_wedge_vs_hardware.png). Offline model tools/g5b_negw_model.cpp predicts wedges per swap from the stream alone: f1 5 of 5 strong presented events, w0b 6 of 9, no strong event unexplained in either. That answers NEXT.md item 1: H-hw-paints for the sheets, see below; the flat frames are neither arm, they are an RT64-only wedge.

New ROGUESQ_W_CLAMP (lib/rt64 patch): default on at dd>1, off at dd1; =0 old, =1 on, =tog on in odd seconds (same-run A/B). Same-run arms, tog, 120 s after boot then 240 s capture, 120 ms band around each toggle excluded. These arms ran the first rule (clamp all mixed-sign tris, drop only over 20000 px area):

| arm | level | dd | strong T>=.08 on/off | T>=.04 on/off | small T .006-.04 on/off | sheets >=100k |

## Session 6896 (2026-11-05) — G5b: dd3/dd4 near-plane sheets are the map's last edge quad wrapping s16 in TriGen; fixed at dd>1, same-run 0 vs 112 and 0 vs 45

Unit from NEXT.md: why dd3 and dd4 emit near-plane sheets. Owner recipe (FPS60, 16:9, no logging env), autopilot flight, 120 s + 180 s, sheets >=100k px, one game at a time. Arms in scratch/s6896 (first batch in a1/).

ORIGIN: the writer is the game's own terrain stream, and the value is legitimate. TriGen takes a s16 vertex base and step (params 8 and 9) and the ucode adds them in 16-bit lanes (reference/gliden64/F5Rogue.cpp, TriGen02_BuildVtxData). Terrain bases are fixed map coordinates, not camera-relative: the same quad keeps the same words across swaps, and the observed range is -32768 to 32256, so the map appears to fill the s16 range. The last quad on the + edge has base 32256, step 512, far edge 32768, which wraps to -32768: one side of the quad lands a whole map away, a sheet through the near plane. At dd1 the far cutoff never reaches it on these flights (bases within +-18432). dd>1 meshes it from far away, which is why the onset followed draw distance.

New instrument ROGUESQ_G5B_TG=<file> (src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp, tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py, tools/g5b_tg_join.py): per swap TriGen count, base ranges, commands past s16, commands past half range (same-run control for the arithmetic), window, camera. W lines hold raw words of wrapping commands.

Failed first run: the probe skipped mode 2, which is ~95% of TriGen commands, so it saw only near terrain. Caught in the first rows, killed, fixed, rerun; that run is not used.

Before the fix, LEVEL=4:

| arm | setting | swaps past s16 | control past half range | sheets | sheet swaps with a wrap | sheet swaps without |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a4 | dd4 | 1930 | 5818 | 405 | 253 | 0 |
| e0 | dd4, DD_EDGE=0 | 1402 | 5899 | 389 | 256 | 0 |
| a2 | dd2 | 49 | 7119 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Every sampled wrapping command in a4 was mode 2, step 512, base exactly 32256 on one or both axes (11235 W lines, at most 6 per swap, so a sample). e0 refutes H-edge: without the off-map border the sheets are unchanged. Wrap without a sheet is common (1677 swaps in a4, 49 at dd2); presumably the quad is out of view, not measured.

Fix: rs64_g5b_tg_edge rewrites the base in DMEM to 32767 - step for mode 2 quads that would wrap, so the quad moves 1 unit and keeps its size. ROGUESQ_G5B_TG_FIX default on at dd>1, off at dd1; =0 old, =1 on, =tog on in odd seconds. The dd1 path is not entered. W lines still count wraps with the fix on, because the probe runs first.

Fix arms, tools/g5b_tg_tog.py, 120 ms band around toggles set aside:

| arm | level | dd | setting | sheets fix-on seconds | sheets fix-off seconds | in band | swaps past s16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t4 | 4 | 4 | tog | 0 | 112 | 16 | 2140 |
| t1 | 1 | 4 | tog | 0 | 45 | 0 | 1025 |
| f4 | 4 | 4 | default | 0 total | | | 1908 |
| d1 | 4 | 1 | default | 0 total | | | 0, control 4415 |

f4 is the first dd4 arm with 0 sheets; s6895's dd4 arms read 43-687. Off seconds in t4 and t1 are the same-run positive control that the census still sees sheets. Capture rate with logging: f4 40.5/s, t4 40.8/s, against s6895 dd4 38.3-39.5/s, so no slowdown; d1 59.6/s. Runs: 0 crash lines in t1, f4, d1 run logs, >250 ms gaps 0. These are ~300 s runs, one per arm, and sum_ files are empty as in s6895, so stall checking rests on the capture gaps.

Frames: docs/owner_sheet_s6896_edge_fix_on_off.png, t4, four largest off-second sheets above their on-second neighbours 0.8-1.1 s later. No bands or damage in the on row at sheet size, but the off row is not dramatic either, since the s6895 span rule already drops many sheets, and the views differ. Four frame pairs do not show the terrain looks right, only that nothing is obviously wrong. A dark stepped patch in off frame sw9776 is absent from its on neighbour; different view, not evidence. t1 had no sheet inside the capture picks, so no t1 sheet.

Not done: dd3 was not run on the fix (dd2 and dd4 were; dd2 has wraps, the fix ran but with no sheets to remove). Black steps not rechecked: s6895 saw sheets painted over that region, so this may clear them, untested. Whether the s6895 span rule is still needed is untested. Quads past the + edge (base wraps whole, drawn at the far - side) remain: they are not counted by wa/wb and are not fixed. Whether retail wraps with a camera close to the + edge is unknown; retail bases should wrap the same way if it gets there. 8074A380 and the dd1 small transients still open.

Conclusion: this selects H-wrap as the cause of the sheets, by a same-run A/B on two levels plus a default-path zero, and refutes H-edge, which is two lines of evidence for the sheets. It does not show the sheets are the owner's drops; G5b stays open until the owner flies it. Next discriminator: black steps in the post-MISSION FAILED scene with the fix =tog, where steps gone in on seconds tie them to this wrap.

## Session 6899 (2026-11-05) — G5b: dd4 cutscene ground loss is our window clamp ignoring the eye, fixed; same run near quads 287 vs 8, flight unchanged so the owner's in-flight drop stays open

The first s6899 iteration hit the runner timeout (rc=124) with the arms finished and unscored and the fix uncommitted. This entry scores them; no game was run in the second iteration. Binary: build/RogueSquadron64Recomp 11:35, arms d4, g4, e1 (LEVEL=4, FPS60, 16:9, owner recipe, 400 s). Earlier arms c4, e4, t1, t4, v1_e4 came from earlier builds and are not used.

ORIGIN: our own s6037/s6874/s6591 window clamp in binPolygonIntoTerrainGrid (funcs_9.c). A footprint wider than 64 cells is trimmed off-map cells first, then from the high end, with no reference to the eye, so the window stays anchored low. In the scene the eye sits at cell 78,79 (polygon point 0 = cam/2, median ratio 0.500) and the dd4 window is x,z 0..63, so the near cells are outside it. dd1's window there is x[51,101) z[79,103). This selects H-window's outcome (the visited cells do not include the eye's cell), by a different mechanism from the one NEXT named: the window is trimmed, and index wrap was not measured. H-budget and H-pool were not measured either; the fix restoring near quads with neither touched means they are not needed to explain the loss. The cells are never binned because our clamp cut them. The value is not corrupt: it is a legitimate footprint that our clamp trimmed on the wrong side.

Fix: tools/apply_s6899_eyewin.py, in RS64_REPLAY. After all trims, slide the window minimally, width unchanged, inside the pre-clamp bounds, so it holds eye +-26 cells, about what dd1 draws. A +-2 slide left a hard water edge (scratch/s6899/sheet_scene.png). ROGUESQ_DD_EYEWIN default on, =0 old, =tog odd mach seconds. The bound means it cannot slide unless the clamp trimmed, and a width at or under 64 stays inside the s6591 slot64 limit.

Results. Scene = eye within 6 of 157.35,159.2 and m2 >= 300.
- Same run, g4 =tog, 246 scene swaps (scratch/s6899/tog.py): slid 123, near p50 287, collapsed 2; not slid 123, near p50 8, collapsed 103. The 2 collapsed in the slid group are unexplained: the k/k-1 join may misfile swaps at a parity flip, but that was not checked.

- Default d4: 246 scene swaps, 0 collapsed, near p5/50/95 281/286/332. Positive control for the instrument: the not-slid half of g4 in the same run.
- Flight, g4 by parity, scene excluded, m2 >= 300 (par_all.py): off 5859 swaps, on 5759; near p50 278 vs 276; total quads p50 2347 vs 2327; near under 50: 2 vs 0, both at t 186.1-186.2, the scene's tail. So there is no measured far-terrain cost, and also NO in-flight effect. Eye outside the window off 154, on 7, but those sit in the pre-mission intro and the scene: 2 in flight. This closes the cutscene loss only. It says nothing for the owner's in-flight drops, and s6898 already showed the scene was not that drop in that run.

G3f's description is wrong, and that matters. "Camera slides 13 units sideways in 0.5 s while yaw lags ~3 s" read floats 9-11 of the ROGUESQ_G3F_CAM row as position. cam+0x2C is the inverse written by mat3x3InverseInto (retail store PCs 0x8001C7FC-980, from the s6791 trace), so that column is the view translation. World eye = -R^T t is smooth, ~3.8 s, and matches guest eye 0x800CD810 (-23.65,28.43,-3.01 settled). Yaw LEADS: the view turns ~90 deg in the first 0.6 s. tools/g3f_pan_cmp.py has the same misreading; its timing numbers are not position.

Camera facts, from funcs_28.c and a live word diff of 0x800CC000-0x800CE000 and 0x80130000-0x80132000 across a press: eye 0x800CD810, look point 0x800CD800, raw direction built at sp+0x28 by 0x800AD284 in updateHangarBayScene, then turned into angles. State byte 0x800CC3E4: 3 idle, 2 scroll, 3.83 s at FPS60, 3.93 s at 30 Hz. Cursor byte 0x800CD6E8 changes at the press and again on any press mid scroll (the game retargets). Destination = byte 0x800CC404[cursor], craft position list 0x800CDA5C + i*0x278 + 0xC. 0x800CD6E4 (bay index) only commits at pan end. Two dead hooks on the way, both caught by the log not appearing or by reading it: site 0x800ACA9C never runs for a scroll (the scroll uses 0x800AC67C, onto authored splines), and 0x800CD6E4 cannot name the destination at the press.

Measure (retail path): the next craft comes on screen ~1.6 s into the scroll at 40 deg off axis and 10 units away, then needs ~2 s to reach centre while the eye closes to 6.7 units. That fits the owner's "goes 1-2 s after it settles". Eye to craft settled is only 5.3-6.7 units.

Fix, tools/apply_s6907_aim.py (RS64_REPLAY after apply_s6904_fog): at 0x800AD284 turn the raw direction on the stack from its value at the press to eye->destination craft over ROGUESQ_G5G_TURN=1.6 s, then back onto raw over the last ROGUESQ_G5G_REL=0.9 s. Writes only that stack direction, so no game camera state changes and the authored eye path is retail. Default on, =0 retail, =tog flips every 2 scrolls. ORIGIN: retail's authored path, not a defect of ours; this is an owner-requested change from retail. G5G_LENS=<fovy> is an opt-in that eases fovy mid scroll (34 reached in the 21:9 arm, frames not judged).

## Session 6911 (2026-11-06) — G5h: dd4 floating horizon triangles are off-map coast cells reading past the level map in selectGridCellTileVariant; map index clamped at dd>1, same run bad quads 13.8 and 5.4 per swap vs 0, triangles gone in the same shot

HYPOTHESIS-ID: g5h-cutscene-bg. s6905_k30_h1d4 and h4d4 soak verdicts folded: rc=0, 0 CRASH lines in both logs. CURRENT-TRUTH under the Step 0 trigger, no maintenance. 7 runs (a4 b4 c4 d4 e4 f2 g1), all LEVEL=4 16:9 FPS60, 0 CRASH lines in all 7, owner save hash unchanged (37b93f3c6536, 3927d691e2ad). Harness scratch/s6911/arm.zsh.

ORIGIN: the junk heights are written by selectGridCellTileVariant (0x80046030), the game's own code, and the value is NOT legitimate for the cell. It indexes the level map with the cell's raw x,z (lh 0x18/0x1A, stride 0x80136DF8) while the cell's flags came from the clamped edge cell (clampGridCellLookup). A dd>1 window runs far past the map: LEVEL=4 map 94x94, window rows up to 143. So a flagged border cell reads past the map array, takes a junk tile index, and copies 25 junk height bytes into its pool slot. Witness, c4 log: `[s6911] off-map variant x=45 z=109 map 94x94 raw idx 10291`, z 102..109 in the first lines, x 45 every time. Why only that column: not measured; x=45 at the last map row is presumably the one flagged coast cell (the other cells in those rows take the preset tile pointer), which fits 1 bad column of 49 rows.

How it was found. a4 (s6909 binary + G5B_TRIS, W_CLAMP=tog, DD_FOG=tog): triangles reproduced, t 199.5-201. Same shapes with W_CLAMP on and off, so not the s6895 clamp or sheet drop. Rendering the triangle stream for swap 15042 puts them in the main terrain group (timg 8087E1F0): single terrain triangles spaced through the stream at far-ring depth, not an object mesh. That selects H-terrain and refutes H-mesh and H-lod as framed.
b4 (new ROGUESQ_G5B_TGCMD, DD_FOG=0): with fog off the triangles are stronger and water coloured (seen, crop only), so fog does not create them, it fades them. Adjacent quads should share corner heights. In swap 11790: 3429 quads, 98 edge mismatches, 49 each in columns a=-34 and a=-33 (the bad column and the neighbour that faces it); other columns clean.
My first reading, "heights over 0x8000 are the junk", was wrong as a test: negative heights are ordinary terrain, about 400 quads per swap in both parities. Only the edge mismatch count discriminates. Also cen.py's world column is off by a few cells (its origin drifts); the witness log is the reliable coordinate.

Fix: tools/apply_s6911_varclamp.py (in RS64_REPLAY after s6909) + rs64_s6911_mapidx, clamps x,z to the map. ROGUESQ_DD_VARCLAMP default on at dd>1 on levels 0..18, =0 old, =tog odd mach seconds, ROGUESQ_DD_VARCLAMP_LOG=1 witness.

Same run, =tog, edge mismatched quads per swap (par.py, every 5th swap, 0.15 s dropped at each second edge):
| arm | old: swaps, mean, p90, max | clamp on: swaps, mean, p90, max |
|---|---|---|
| c4 dd4 | 811, 13.8, 47, 99 | 826, 0.0, 0, 0 |
| d4 dd4 | 864, 5.4, 27, 66 | 838, 0.0, 0, 0 |
The old parity is the positive control: the instrument fires in the same run.
Pixels, e4 (=tog, scene t 186.3-192.3, the only pass of the three =tog runs to reach it): triangles present at t 186.51, 186.73, and at 186.94, which is a boundary frame carrying the old state; gone at 187.17 and 187.38 in the same shot, shore line still there. Dark slabs on the shore line go too. docs/owner_sheet_s6911_floating_triangles.png. One direction only: the shot leaves the horizon before the clamp turns off again. The quad table covers both directions.

Default path. f2 (dd2, default, 250 s): log on=1, fixed = seen, 0 mismatched quads in 1471 sampled swaps. No old arm at dd2 in that run, so this is not a before/after and says nothing about the s6910 dd2 smudge. g1 (dd1, 200 s): log on=0, fixed 0. dd1 also reaches this path: x=94 z=65 raw idx 6204, which wraps into the next map row. So retail code does this at dd1 too and stays as it is.

Audit, static only, nothing run: the same raw x + z*stride read is at 0x80046274 (buildGridCellLabel), 0x80048768, 0x80048DE4 (processGridCellByDistance), 0x80049844 (emitGridCellTileStrip) and 0x80049FE8 (Diagonal); the Adjacent variant has the same shape by count, not read. Whether they see raw off-map x,z is not established: processGridCellByDistance's cells come out with clean heights, so it may use clamped values. The strips feed normals, so this may be the ribbed dark border of docs/owner_sheet_s6905_window.png; unmeasured, next unit.

## Session 6912 (2026-11-06) — G5h: off-map raw map reads closed H-clean, clones are redirected to their on-map parent before label and strips, 0 off-map in about 1M hook calls with edge controls firing; ribbed border is not a junk read; s6911 clamp same run confirmed at dd2, dd3 and 21:9

HYPOTHESIS-ID: g5h-cutscene-bg. CURRENT-TRUTH under the Step 0 trigger, no maintenance. 7 runs (a1 b1 c4 d1 e4 f4 g4), 0 CRASH lines in all 7, owner save hash unchanged (37b93f3c6536, 3927d691e2ad). Harness scratch/s6912/arm.zsh.

Static read. Off-map border cells are clones: clampGridCellLookup (0x80048AF0) stores the raw x,z in a fresh cell and sets flag 0x20, with +8 holding the on-map parent. Per site:
| site | what it does | off-map x,z? |
|---|---|---|
| 0x80048768 (write to second map, +8) | only on flag 0x20 clear cells | no: those were made by the in-bounds path |
| 0x80048DE4 processGridCellByDistance | flag 0x20 branch reads the PARENT's x,z | no |
| 0x80046274 buildGridCellLabel | caller 0x8004B970: clone with 0x40 set returns early in label, clone with 0x40 clear goes to the parent path | no |
| 0x80049844, 0x80049BEC, 0x80049FE8 strips | same caller, strips get s0 = parent at 0x8004B9F0 and 0x8004CC88 | no |
Correction to my own mid-session reading: from the strip bodies alone I said label and strips see raw clone x,z. They would if called on a clone; the caller does not do that. Only selectGridCellTileVariant takes the clone itself. Second dispatcher 0x80045FC0 passes a scratch cell and another struct, not the level map, and was left out of the witness by address.

Witness, tools/apply_s6912_mapclamp.py + rs64_s6912_mapidx, built, measured, then REMOVED (git never carried it): per-site all/off-map/past/diff counts, plus ROGUESQ_DD_MAPCLAMP_TESTK=2 counting cells within 2 of the map edge as the control. a1 and b1 (lvl1) logged nothing: first build only printed on an off-map hit, then at 2^18 calls, so those two are no result. | d1 lvl1 dd4 all | 0 | 64491 | 8492 | 5637 | 60793 | 199531 | 0 |
| d1 edge control | 0 | 7305 | 3523 | 3520 | 6927 | 199531 | |

## Session 6918 (2026-11-06) — G5h far band: shot pairing, cutoff inputs and camera all match retail at the same pose, yet the near/far combiner split still differs, stable in two retail runs

What the two combiners are (decoded from the words, new): A 127E24:FFFFFFFF is TEX0 x SHADE, 1 cycle. B 127FFF:FFFFFE3F is the same in cycle 1, cycle 2 passes through, so B is the 2-cycle fog form. Near terrain is A, far terrain is B, and the game's switch is cutoff^2 at 0x8009DEB4, read in buildGridCellMeshForFace at 0x800434D8. Read of the code plus s6904; the mapping of chain to combiner was not traced.
Cutoff (read of 0x800455C8 computeGridLayerScrollOffset, its name is wrong): radius DEAC ramps between 0x80130C54 and C58 on eye y (cam +0x50) with thresholds C5C, C60; DEB4 = (0x80136FBC x K)^2 x radius^2. 0x80136FBC is set per level in setupCutsceneLevel. Tier table DE94..A0 is fixed.

Ran, same presses: retail oracle AT THE MOVIES 1227 s (scratch/s6918/oracle.zsh, xtrace at 0x800456D8 and 0x800455DC) and port at retail settings 953 s (new ROGUESQ_G5H_BAND=<file>, row per swap: A and B tri counts, the same guest words, 32 camera words). 0 crash. Result, H-slip REFUTED: shot indices were right. S ends at 79 only because the dump stopped at 945 s; durations line up index for index, and the 64-74 stretch differs only where retail's rate falls.
Result, H-select REFUTED: tools/g5h_band_pose.py, 75 retail vs 73 port pose segments: at matched eye position, scene scalar, radius and cutoff^2 agree in every segment with a match, 13 of 13 samples in most. Positive control in the same table: the values move 57-229 and 0.3 vs 0.9 scalar between scenes, and both arms follow. 3 segments had no pose match within 0.05. One median row (t=925, radius 20.86 vs 23.60, shot 65) is a median over a moving ramp; spot rows at 930, 935, 940 read equal, 16.000, 22.403, 24.000.
Result, H-input REFUTED for the camera: all 32 camera words at 5 spot poses (shots 65, 76-77 region) agree to 4 decimals, orientation included.
Split, same pose (scratch/s6918/tab.py, shots 67-76 pair cleanly, its 59-66 and 77 rows are mispaired and mean nothing): B/A retail vs port: 69 0.55 vs 1.88, 73 0.46 vs 0.78, 76 0.43 vs 0.78, all at cutoff^2 228.6. Same cutoff 228.6 matches on 67 (0.32/0.41), 68 (0.33/0.35), 70 (0.17/0.20). A+B stays equal to within 1-2%, so the same cells are drawn and only the near/far label moves.
Repeat: new retail dump vs s6792: shot 76 0.45 vs 0.44, 73 0.46, 69 0.55, 65 3.44 vs 3.46. Port s6918 vs s6915: 76 0.78 vs 0.79. Neither side is noisy, this is a stable difference. Retail frame counts also repeat (400 vs 399), so the oracle's slow shots are not random either.

What is left: the split is not decided by the threshold or the camera, so it sits in the cell list. buildGridCellMeshForFace takes the first node in list order under the cutoff as the chain start, so order or node d2 can move it. New hypotheses: H-order (list order differs, and it may carry history), H-dist (node d2 at +8 differs), H-emit (the cut is the same and the RDP label differs, combiner state inherited by tris). ## Session 6919 (2026-11-06) — G5h far band: our s6418 block overwrote the game's per-scene far cutoff at dd1; leaving it alone matches retail's near/far split on shots 67-76

HYPOTHESIS-ID: g5h-far-band, closed. No maintenance (35 KB). This session finished an iteration that timed out at the 1 hour limit (rc=124, runner killed at ~16:38 with all of s6919's code and arms uncommitted); the code, the retail run and the =tog run below are from that attempt, scored here.

ORIGIN: ours, s6418. The far clip block ran at every dd. It latched 0x8009DEB4 once (static org6418) and wrote that value back every frame, after computeGridLayerScrollOffset wrote the scene's value and before buildGridCellMeshForFace read it. So the game's per-scene cutoff never reached the near/far cut. The latched value depends on the route: 114.7 in AT THE MOVIES, 143.3 lvl1, 130.8 lvl4. The value is legitimate game data, the overwrite was the defect.

This selects the cutoff as the root cause of the shots 67-76 mismatch and closes H-order, H-dist and H-emit, which are no longer needed to explain those shots. It resolves s6918's question without the node walk: restoring the value alone moves the split onto retail's.

Why s6918 missed it: its rows sampled DEB4 at 0x800456D8, just after the game's write, so they read the game's value, not what the chain used. Sampled at the read, 0x800434F4 (retail spec scratch/s6919/oracle.zsh, port g_rs64_s6919 words on ROGUESQ_G5H_BAND rows, tools/g5h_cut_read.py), retail and port live agree and old stays at 114.7. s6918's "H-select REFUTED" and "cutoff inputs match" are superseded.

Fix: tools/apply_s6919_cutlive.py (RS64_REPLAY, after s6904 fog; idempotent re-run says already applied). ROGUESQ_CUT_LIVE default on, =0 old, =tog odd seconds: leaves the game's value alone wherever the dd scale is not active. dd>1 behaviour in flight unchanged by default. ROGUESQ_DD_CUT_LIVE=1|tog (default off): at dd>1 scale the game's value rather than the latch.

Result, same run, port =tog, AT THE MOVIES at retail settings, 0 crash, B/A at matched pose, retail vs live vs old (scratch/s6919/tab.py):
67 0.27 / 0.28 / 0.46; 68 0.32 / 0.32 / 0.39; 69 0.56 / 0.56 / 2.33; 70 0.17 / 0.17 / 0.19; 72 1.89 / 1.90 / 1.63; 73 0.54 / 0.54 / 0.71; 74 0.26 / 0.26 / 0.18; 75 0.44 / 0.41 / 0.39; 76 0.43 / 0.41 / 0.75.
Control in the same table: on shot 68 the old rows also read cutoff 228.61, and there live and old nearly agree (0.32 vs 0.39), which is what a split driven by the cutoff predicts. Why the old state read the game's value on that shot is not known. Shot 63 is 0 on all sides.
Second line of evidence: the read cutoff itself, retail vs port live, equal in every pose bucket from t=880 to 1144 with a live row (scene values 77.8 to 228.6), one small gap at ramps (115.3 vs 114.6, 199.3 vs 198.3); old 114.7 throughout except the t=958 bucket, 228.6, taken to be that shot 68 row.
Not matched: shots 59 (0.29 / 0.81 / 1.26) and 61 (0.19 / 1.62 / 5.62), though the cut read agrees there (209.96, 289.34). s6918 called 59-66 and 77 mispaired in this table, and live moved toward retail, but pairing was not fixed, so these two are unexplained, not explained. Shot 65 has no live rows.

Default build, lvl1 dd1 FPS60 16:9, no toggle, 220 s hold, 0 crash, 11108 terrain rows: read vs game gap p50 0, p99 0.11%, 1 row over 5% (30.6%, not looked at). Same check on old seconds of the =tog flight: p50 35%, 5222 of 5512 over 5%. Tail A 609, B 565. =tog flights dd1: lvl1 old A 461 B 755 vs live A 588 B 633; lvl4 old 339/828 vs live 458/615. So the fault also applied to mission flight, not only cutscenes. No retail flight read was taken. That means the earlier lvl1 retail flight match did not see this, or the two compared something else: not resolved. 344 of 2815 lvl4 odd-second rows read 130.8: inferred stale value after the toggle until the game next writes; the default arm has no such rows on lvl1, lvl4 default not run.

Can it be seen: barely, in the frames checked. docs/owner_sheet_s6919_cut_live.png, same run: shot 76 at same pose (d 0.009), B/A 0.75 vs 0.41, whole frame mean difference 0.28 and 0.14 of 255. ## Session 6936 (2026-11-07) — G1e: record_submit walkers merged per contiguous run on the wrap flush, same run windowed sync dd4 16:9 55.9 -> 59.6 tasks/s, sd_wall 14.02 -> 12.96 ms
HYPOTHESIS-ID: g1e-dd4-sync-rate. No owner report. No new soak verdicts since s6934 (folded in s6935).
Hypotheses: H-call (the walkers' cost is per call: the wrap flush ran record_submit once per DPC bump, 1M+ calls/s, each paying every walker's prologue; merging raises the rate in on blocks) / H-floor (no change: the cost is in the per-command decode or elsewhere) / H-split (a bump can end mid-command, so the per-bump walkers misread triangle body words as commands and merging changes decisions, not just speed).
Landed: ROGUESQ_G1E_WALK default on, =0 old, =tog 10 s blocks (src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp wrap-flush loop). With WRAP_MERGE on, rs64_dpc_record_submit runs once at wm_flush over [wm_lo, wm_hi) after every range of the run is restored from its shadow, instead of per range. The undo snapshot of each range is taken before its restore and record edits only restored bytes of disjoint ranges, so RT64 receives the same restored-then-edited bytes. G1D_PREWRAP_RECORD=1 forces the old order. ROGUESQ_G1E_WALK_STAT=1: a command cursor across contiguous ranges counts ranges starting inside a command; self-test (one 32-byte triangle bumped 4 x 8 + one 8-byte command) must read mid=3.
Run wt (scratch/s6936/w.zsh, windowed FPS60 dd4 16:9 sync, lvl index 1 keyed flight, WALK=tog + WALK_STAT=1), 240 s, alive, 0 crash: [s6936-walk] ranges=354418689 mid=0 tri_heads=40177747 bytes=9.56 GB selftest_mid=3. tools/g1e_tog_rate.py t>=100: off 55.9 tasks/s sd_wall 14.02 ms, on 59.6 / 12.96; skew 1: 55.7 / 14.18 vs 59.5 / 12.77. [g1d-edge]/[g1d-pillar] crop changes only at epoch 6/9/11 starts (swaps 447, 624, 1650), none at block flips. t165 frame: 16:9 flight, HUD at the screen edges, radar anchored.
Result: selects H-call: about 1.06 ms per task, more than the 0.9 ms the profile attributed to the walkers (the profile split by line, not counting call overhead). Rules out H-split: 0 mid-command starts in 354M ranges with a working control, so the ucode bumps DPC_END per whole command and the merge is equivalent on the command level. Single run for the rate (same-run toggle, so not cross-run noise). Behaviour change: the opt-in DD_SKYZ (default off) can now patch a SET_PRIM_DEPTH sent in an earlier range of the same run; before, it counted those as s_skyz_miss.
Queued: scratch/agent/soak_queue/s6936_locked_walk.sh, locked 60 Hz fullscreen sync dd4 16:9 defaults, the owner figure to compare with s6935's 47.3.
Not closed: locked on-glass figure; factor5_ucode self 4.5 ms; fence wait in fullSync; the other record_submit call sites (commit path is already merged; the direct path at the end of rsp_dpc_submit_impl is per submit).

## Session 6937 (2026-11-07) — G1e: the fullSync fence wait guards this task's own RDRAM readbacks every call (H-same), 1.0-1.1 ms per task in flight; s6936 locked soak void (human active), requeued

Soak folded: s6936_locked_walk rc=2, 0 s: human active (HIDIdleTime 7.5 s at session start). Requeued as scratch/agent/soak_queue/s6936_locked_walk_r2.sh.
Code read: in State::fullSync renderAndSynchronize, framebufferGraphicsWorker->execute() is immediately followed by wait() on the same RenderWorker fence (Metal: dispatch_semaphore signalled by that command buffer's completed handler). So the wait is always on work queued in the same call. The question left was whether that work carries data the CPU needs right after: the copyRenderTargetToNative readbacks consumed by the copyNativeToRAM writeback loop.
Instrument: ROGUESQ_G1E_FENCE_STAT=1 (lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp, off by default). It counts per call the readbacks queued (g1eNativeCopies), readbacks recorded then skipped (skipReadback sites), and wait ms. Per-second [g1e-fence] line.
Run fs (scratch/s6937/w.zsh, windowed FPS60 dd4 16:9 sync, lvl index 1 keyed flight, defaults + FENCE_STAT), 235 s, alive, 0 crash:
- t0-95 (boot, menus): 59.9 calls/s, none=9, 3.52 copies/call, skipped 0, wait 0.81 ms/call.
- t95-140 flight: 59.7 calls/s, none=0, 5.00 copies/call, skipped 0, wait 1.00 ms/call, max 1.80.
- t140-235 flight: 59.9 calls/s, none=0, 5.00 copies/call, skipped 0, wait 1.11 ms/call, max 1.83. sd_wall about 13.3 ms.
Positive control, same run: the none counter fired 9 times at boot, so the instrument can see a readback-free call.
Result: selects H-same. Every flight wait guards 5 readbacks that the writeback loop then copies into RDRAM. Rules out H-stale (no wait without data, no recorded-then-skipped readback), so a ROGUESQ_G1E_FENCE skip/defer toggle would be unsafe and was not built. The 1.1 ms (about 8% of the task) goes only with overlap (ROGUESQ_RDP_ASYNC) or with not reading back at all.
Not closed: whether those 5 writebacks per task are ever read (by the game CPU, or as a texture or VI source) before being overwritten (next unit, H-wb-dead); factor5_ucode self 4.5 ms; locked on-glass figure after WALK.

## Session 6938 (2026-11-07) — G1e: nothing in flight reads the depth writebacks, and the colour ones are read only by RT64's own hash checks (H-wb-dead); skipping the depth readback saves only 0.05 ms of the 1.1 ms fence wait, so the wait is GPU render time, not readback cost

Soak folded: s6936_locked_walk_r2 rc=2, 0 s, human active again (HIDIdleTime 10.5 s at session start). Requeued as s6936_locked_walk_r3.
Instrument: ROGUESQ_G1E_WBW=1 (src/main/main.cpp, off by default; hooks at the 4 copyNativeToRAM sites in lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp). After each colour/depth writeback the written 16 KB pages go PROT_NONE. The first touch of a page faults into wbw_try_handle_fault (chained first in the SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler), which records the host pc/lr (resolved offline with atos, slide logged) and ESR WnR, then unprotects. At the next writeback over the same range, the range scores live (read in between), dead (overwritten unread with every interior page still armed) or unk. rs64_wbw_self(1/0) wraps RT64's own self-check reads (hashTracking, checkRDRAM storeRAM/checkRAM): they count as "self" and their pages are re-armed afterwards, so a later game reader still faults. ROGUESQ_G1E_WBW_CTL=1 reads one byte of an armed range once a second (positive control, tagged kind 8).
Route: scratch/s6938/w.zsh (copy of s6937's, windowed FPS60 dd4 16:9 sync, keyed flight from t=95). Three runs, all alive, 0 crash.
- wb (no self-tagging): every flight read of a writeback came from FramebufferManager::hashTracking, which runs at the end of the same fullSync right after the writeback. That masks any later reader, hence arm ws.
- ws (self-tagged, re-armed): flight t>=95. Depth: 5371 writebacks, 0 read, 5273 dead, 98 unk (the 98 are exactly the ctl reads). Colour: 21484 writebacks, 5371 live, 16109 dead. Every live colour read is XXH3 called from State::updateScreen+2248, i.e. RT64 hashing the VI framebuffer once per frame to detect CPU drawing. No recompiled game function and no texture-load path touched any writeback in flight. Controls in the same run: ctl fired 100 times in flight with the right tag, and game-CPU faults were trapped and named at boot (rs_memset and buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial writes, drawSubtitleText and coalesceFreeHeapBlocks reads: heap reuse of old fb memory), so the trap does see the game thread. In boot, updateScreen+3964 also memcpys the VI fb (CPU-drawn frames).
- tz: ROGUESQ_G1E_WB_SKIPZ=tog (new, rt64_state.cpp, off by default; decided once per fullSync at the hashTracking site so both passes agree; 4 s blocks). Flight, 38 clean seconds per arm: copies/call 5.00 -> 4.00, wait/call 1.083 -> 1.036 ms, calls/s 54.2 vs 52.6 (windowed, within noise). Frames from both blocks render normally (scratch/s6938/tz_pair.png).
Result: selects H-wb-dead for depth (no reader at all) and for colour except RT64's own updateScreen hash. But the lever is worth only about 0.05 ms per task. The fence wait is the GPU executing the task's draws, not the readback copies, so skipping writebacks cannot buy the 1.1 ms. Skipping colour writeback would also need updateScreen's hash and storage checks made consistent, so it was not built.
Rules out: the readback copies as a meaningful part of the per-task cost. The remaining terms are GPU time per task (only overlap removes it: ASYNC) and factor5_ucode self 4.5 ms.
Not closed: one level (index 1) and about 100 s of flight. A level whose game code reads z (for example a sun flare test) would show as a non-self Z reader: rerun ws on other levels before ever defaulting SKIPZ. SKIPZ stays opt-in, diagnostic only.

## Session 6940 (2026-11-07) — G1e: the r128 "copy" cost was a stack-resident RSP register file forced by cold hook paths; lean gfx ucode arm cuts ~2 ms per task (13.58 -> 11.26 ms median, 9/9 block pairs), default on

Soak folded: s6936_locked_walk_r4 rc=0, locked 60 Hz fullscreen sync dd4 16:9, lvl index 1, defaults (G1E_WALK on): 51.1 fps, latency p50/p99 27.0/37.6 ms, 100% on glass, crash=0 (s6935: 47.3). Merged walk gain holds locked.
Read first (H-copy refuted): RSP::r128::operator=(__m128i) is `v128 = value`, a plain inline store; operator __m128i is a plain load. Disassembly at the top s6939 operator= leaf PCs (slide from base_x1.txt) shows `str q1,[x9,#0x70]` right after the sqxtn of a VMUDH, i.e. the sample is the result store (and the skid of the arithmetic before it), and every vector op loads its operands from and stores its result to the stack copy of rsp.vpu. Also seen: `bl rs64_vu_ring_push` blocks inline in the function body, ACC stores through a spilled pointer, constant shuffle masks stored to the stack.
Offline discriminator (no game run): compile the same fixed-up .c with the librecomp hook gate (rs64_rsp_hooks_on: VU ring, rs64_vld_note, SDV snapshot, m5 dmem store hooks) and the in-ucode probe gate (rs64_g1e_probes: M4 probes that take &rsp, dlw, inline probes) as constant 0. tools/g1e_fn_mix.py on factor5_ucode: main 47,789 insns, NEON 10,919, q loads 3,226, q stores 2,813, calls 1,908, (qld+qst)/NEON 0.55; probes-only 0: 47,156, same ratio 0.55; both 0: 21,047 insns, NEON 4,349, q loads 587, q stores 531, calls 236, ratio 0.26. So the header hooks (not the probes) keep the vector register file in memory; selects H-alias (in the sense: escaping/opaque cold paths), not H-real.
Landed: src/rsp/factor5_ucode_lean.cpp (same .c, RS64_RSP_HOOKS_GATE=0, RS64_G1E_PROBES_ON=0, RSP=RS64_RSP_LEAN, DMEM base dmem, same inline threshold; CMakeLists). librecomp rsp.hpp + rsp_vu_impl.hpp: `if (rs64_rsp_hooks_on` -> `if (RS64_RSP_HOOKS_GATE` (defaults to the flag; submodule-patches exported). tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py s6940 step: probe macros read RS64_G1E_PROBES_ON (defaults to rs64_g1e_probes), idempotent, applied to the live .c. main.cpp: per gfx task, factor5_ucode_lean iff ROGUESQ_G1E_LEAN (default 1) && !rs64_rsp_hooks_on && !rs64_g1e_probes && dmem base; ROGUESQ_G1E_LEAN_TOGGLE=<sec> flips with per-arm task counts in the [g1e-lean] line. Every soak with LOG_* or RSP hook env keeps the main TU automatically.
Equivalence, two lines: (1) tools/g1e_lean_equiv.py preprocesses both TUs with the build's compile line and maps main -> lean (type, function name, 36 hook gates and 51 probe gates -> 0, debug_file paths): 0 other diff lines besides one printf string; MUTANT=1 (one VMADN -> VMADH in lean) shows 2 diff lines, so the check bites. (2) The gated code is unreachable whenever the arm is chosen (dispatch condition = both runtime gates 0). Not run: an RDP byte compare between arms (the inputs never repeat across arms in a live run).
Run (tools/g1e_xt_flight.zsh lt 240 "ROGUESQ_G1E_LEAN_TOGGLE=10", OUT=scratch/s6940, windowed sync dd4 16:9 FPS60 keyed flight, lvl index 1): positive control, each [g1e-lean] flip line shows the arm ran 565-591 tasks in its block and the other 0. tools/g1e_logorder_tog.py (new: credits each [g1b] second to the last flip line by log order, drops 2 s after and 1 s before a flip), t>=100: lean off n=35 tasks/s 58.97 sd_wall med 13.58 ms; lean on n=35 59.71, 11.26 ms; adjacent block pairs sd_wall -2.01 +/- 0.27 ms (sd 0.82, 9 of 9 lower), tasks/s +0.44 +/- 0.25 (rate at the 60 cap both arms, so per-task time is the figure). So H-select (element select) and H-store (DMEM byte stores) are refuted as leading terms. The MAC family runs the x86 SSE algorithm through sse2neon: a 16-bit carry costs adds_epu16 + cmpeq + cmpeq, and the VMADN clamp costs 6 ops plus blendv (2).
Landed: librecomp rsp_vu_impl.hpp gains RS64_RSP_NEON_MAC (default 0), with native NEON bodies for VMUDN/VMUDM/VMUDH and VMADL/VMADN/VMADM/VMADH. The carry is one unsigned compare `sum < addend`. The clamp is `ACCH == ACCM>>15` (equivalent to SSE's shi&smd), with cval = ACCH >= 0 and a vbsl. The pack uses vzip + vqmovn/vqmovn_high. Submodule patches exported. src/rsp/factor5_ucode_nmac.cpp is the lean TU plus the macro (CMakeLists, RSP=RS64_RSP_NMAC). main.cpp takes it whenever the lean arm would run, under ROGUESQ_G1E_NMAC (default 1, =0 lean), with ROGUESQ_G1E_NMAC_TOGGLE=<sec> and a [g1e-nmac] flip line carrying per-arm task counts. ## Session 6954 (2026-11-07) — G1e: per-task ring splits the dd4 tail: task time scales with rsp_dpc_submit call count (~200 ns/call, flat per call), not RDP bytes; slow tasks are +19% calls for +2.7% bytes; H-submit (per-call) selected, H-ucode and H-rt64 refuted
HYPOTHESIS-ID: g1e-dd4-task-tail. No owner report; no new soak results since s6948 (folded). Only the built-in display attached (XG49V unit not runnable).
Hypotheses: H-ucode (slow tasks = more LLE interpreter work) / H-submit (per-call rsp_dpc_submit + task-end commit dominate, scale with call count) / H-rt64 (RT64 send_dl remainder grows).
Instrument (one build): ROGUESQ_G1E_AQ=3 (src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp) times every 16th rsp_dpc_submit call (x16 estimate; AQ=1's two clock reads per call cost more than the term) and the task-end commit (defer_end); ROGUESQ_G1E_TRING=<file> (src/main/main.cpp) writes one row per send_dl: wall, cpu (events.cpp hook rs64_g1e_tring_push after send_dl, lib/N64ModernRuntime, patch exported), ucode wall, submit, commit, calls, RDP bytes, phase, spin. tools/g1e_task_ring.py analyses.
Run: env OUT=scratch/s6954 zsh tools/g1e_xt_flight.zsh tr 360 "ROGUESQ_G1E_AQ=3 ROGUESQ_G1E_AQ_SPIN_NS=20 ROGUESQ_G1E_TRING=..." (windowed sync FPS60 dd4 16:9, lvl index 1 keyed flight), 360 s, alive, 0 crash. 19,189 task rows, flight (phase 7, t>=100 s) 13,334: 6,781 no-spin, 6,553 spin.
Control A: per-second ring mean sd_wall 8.502 vs [g1b] 8.504 over 316 matched seconds (ratio 0.9997, worst second 0.7%): the ring sees every task.
Control B (same run): SPIN_NS=20 on every submit call in alternate 10 s windows: sampled submit term +0.99 ms vs ~0.95 expected (calls x spin), sd_wall +0.77: the sampled submit estimate tracks a known injected cost.
Split, no-spin flight tasks (wall ms; ucx = ucode - submit; com = commit; rest = wall - ucode - commit):
- slow 10%: wall 11.44 = ucx 3.65 + submit 3.96 + commit 3.81 + rest 0.02; calls 58.4k, bytes 1.49 MB.
- mid 40-60%: wall 10.03 = 3.26 + 3.45 + 3.32 + 0.01; calls 48.9k, bytes 1.46 MB.
- fast 10%: wall 7.95 = 2.95 + 2.49 + 2.49 + 0.01; calls 31.7k, bytes 1.33 MB.
- slow - mid delta 1.40 ms: ucx +0.39 (28%), submit +0.51 (37%), commit +0.50 (35%); per-call cost flat (ucx 62/67, submit 68/70, commit 65/68 ns per call); calls +19%, bytes +2.7%, bytes per call 25.6 vs 29.7.
- OLS sd_wall = 101 ns/call + 2.4 ns/byte, R2 0.878; r(sd_wall, calls) 0.915, r(sd_wall, commit) 0.906, r(sd_wall, bytes) 0.465.
- The RT64 remainder outside ucode+commit is ~0.015 ms: RT64's own work runs inside the commit (defer_end), not after it.
=> H-submit selected in the per-call form: every term (interpreter, submit, commit) is a constant ~65 ns per DPC_END bump, so the tail is "more, smaller submits" (each ~3-4 RDP commands), not more RDP data or a costlier RT64 path. H-ucode refuted as a separate cause (its growth is per-call, not per-byte), H-rt64 refuted (remainder ~0). Single run, two controls; per-task grain.
Rules out: RDP data volume and RT64 draw-call build as the dd4 tail term.

## Session 6958 (2026-11-07) — G1e: repeat-load census in RT64 TMEM loads: 99.8% descriptor+content repeats, only 6.5% noops; H-partial selected, skip-identical-loads lever refuted

What ran: new opt-in diagnostic ROGUESQ_G1E_LOADREP=stat in lib/rt64 rt64_rdp.cpp (rs64LoadRepCensus wraps every loadToTMEMCommon). Per load
it records a descriptor key (kind, RGBA32, src, stride, tmem start/stride, words, rows, dxt), an XXH3 of the source bytes, an XXH3 of the 4 KB
TMEM before the load, and whether the load changed TMEM at all (noop = memcmp of the whole 4 KB before/after). A direct-mapped 4096-entry table
keyed by descriptor gives desc (descriptor seen), cont (also same source hash) and prior (also same TMEM-before). A noop load restores
g_rs64_tmem_gen, so the s6942 memo (ROGUESQ_G1E_TMEMMEMO=v, _STAT=1) counts the hash calls a skip would save and verifies them.

- 271k loads/s (~4.5k per task), 1,120 source bytes per load; 51.1% LoadBlock, 48.9% LoadTLUT, 0 LoadTile.

- noop 6.5% (TLUT 6.3 points, block 0.2): the rest rewrite TMEM. prior 36.5%.

- Positive control: load #1000 issued twice read bits 0xB = desc, cont and noop fired. My NEXT.md said 0xF; that was wrong, because prior compares
  against the TMEM state before the FIRST issue, which differs unless that issue was itself a noop. Message and comment corrected.

What it shows: the 4 KB TMEM is refilled with the same textures between draws (thrash). The loads repeat but TMEM before them differs.
