## Session 6959 (2026-11-07) — G1e: provenance-keyed upload hash census: 99.79% hit without the source hash but 802 wrong hashes in 105 s; with the source hash 99.97% hit, 0 wrong; key 60 ns vs hash 257 ns; H-prov selected, H-src live, H-prov-cost refuted

What ran: new opt-in diagnostic ROGUESQ_G1E_PROV=stat in lib/rt64 (submodule-patches/rt64.patch refreshed).
- Load side (rt64_rdp.cpp rs64ProvLoad, wraps loadToTMEMCommon): each of the 512 TMEM 8-byte words carries a tag. tagA = the load's
  descriptor key K (kind, RGBA32, src addr, src stride, tmem start/stride, words, rows, dxt). tagS = mix(K, XXH3 of the source rows) (exact).
  A word the load fully writes takes the tag; a partly written word chains mix(old, K) (0 such updates in this game). Which bytes a K writes
  comes from running the load on two scratch TMEMs filled 0x00 and 0xFF (written bytes agree in both), cached per K (4096 direct-mapped).
  Also counts srcchg = same K, different source hash than last time.
- Hash side (rt64_rdp_tmem.cpp rs64ProvCensus, after every TMEMHasher::hash in uploadTexture): key = tile params (tmem, line, siz, fmt,
  palette, width, height, tlut) + run-length walk of word tags over a SUPERSET of the bytes the hasher reads (texel span with wrap, the RGBA32
  upper half, the CI4 16-word palette or the whole CI8 upper half). Four arms, each a 4096 direct-mapped {key, real hash} table, every hit
  checked against the real hash: A = tagA, S = tagS, M1 = params only (mutant, the positive control), M2 = tagA without the TLUT span.
  Every 64th call times arm A's key and the real hash (mach ticks).
Run: env OUT=scratch/s6959 zsh tools/g1e_xt_flight.zsh r 240 "ROGUESQ_G1E_PROV=stat ROGUESQ_G1E_LOADREP=0" (windowed sync, FPS60 dd4 16:9,
lvl index 1 keyed flight). alive=1, 0 crash, tasks 60/s, sd_wall 9.70 ms with the census on. Summary: tools/g1e_prov_sum.py (new).

Results, flight t>=100 s (105 s, 113k hash calls/s, 96.4% CI4; loads 264k/s):
- arm A: hit 99.79%, bad 802 (0.007% of hits, 7.6/s).  arm S: hit 99.97%, bad 0.
- M1 (params only): bad on 93.7% of hits -> the verify arm discriminates.  M2 (no TLUT span): bad 802, same as A (palettes co-vary with
  index data here, so the palette tags add no safety in this scene; keep them anyway, they are a superset).
- key 60.5 ns vs real hash 257.4 ns per call (ratio 0.23); 2.0 runs and 273 words walked per call.
- srcchg 0.003% of loads (~8/s), the source of arm A's wrong hashes: a few textures are rewritten by the CPU under the same descriptor.
- maskmiss 0.37% of loads, partial-word updates 0.
- Boot (t<90 s) agrees: A 99.12% hit / 365 bad, S 99.50% / 0 bad, ratio 0.24.
What it shows: the provenance key is a near-perfect proxy for the hashed TMEM bytes AND cheap (H-prov selected, H-prov-cost refuted), but
only with the source content in it: without it, ~8 wrong hashes per second would show wrong textures (H-src live). Same-run positive control
(M1) and an exact reference arm (S). Single run.
Budget: hashing is ~113k x 257 ns = 29 ms per wall second (~0.48 ms/task). An S-keyed cache saves that minus the key (~7 ms/s) and a per-load
source XXH3 (~1.1 KB per load, ~10 ms/s at 264k loads/s): expect about -0.2 ms/task; RDRAM dirty-page tracking instead of the source hash
would take it to about -0.35. Modest: commit is ~3.4 ms/task, so this is a step, not the whole commit term.
Ruled out: a provenance key without source content (wrong textures), and "key costs as much as the hash".
Next: build the S-keyed cache (skip TMEMHasher::hash on a hit), =tog same-run timing, =v verify. NEXT.md.
Verdict line: s6959 selects H-prov with H-src (cache must key the source), refutes H-prov-cost.

(texel spans, palette entries, the 6 trailing param fields) is appended to an 8 KB stack buffer, the TLUT index scan runs once over the texel span,
and the digest is one XXH3_64bits call instead of reset + N streaming updates + digest. Same value by construction (XXH3 streaming == one-shot over
the concatenation; the TLUT bitset is an OR); overflow past 8 KB flushes into the streaming state. ROGUESQ_G1E_HGATHER default 1, =0 old, =tog 10 s
blocks, =c check (gather hash used, streaming recomputed every call and compared; mutant control streaming with width+1 every 16th check must
differ), =s stat. Latched per wrap flush like LBFAST. [g1e-hgather] per second. TRING gains a 17th column; tools/g1e_batch_arms.py --arm hgather.
Offline second line: tools/g1e_hgather_equiv.cpp includes the real header: 400,000 random (TMEM, siz/fmt/line/tmem/palette, w up to 1024, h up to 256,
tlut 0-3, NEON scan on/off, byte loop on 1/8): bad=0, 67,701 took the overflow path, byte-flip control changed the hash 25,000/25,000, width+1 mutant
equal 0 times.
Run c (in-game check, 210 s): alive=1 crash=0. chk=12,532,224 bad=0; mutant mchk=783,264 msame=0. Census: segs/hash 1.013, 2,047 bytes/hash, over=0.
So the texel span is almost always ONE segment: the gain cannot come from texel call overhead; it comes from the palette and param tails (CI4 palette
entries hashed 8 bytes per streaming update when the bitset is partial, plus 6 tiny param updates and the reset/digest).

  thread; its sleep_until(next - 2 ms) wakes up to ~7.4 ms after target under timer leeway, past the s6456 2 ms spin. The game is
  VI-locked (kicks at VI+0.12 ms), so a late VI edge is a late frame.

  a 0.5 ms spin (ROGUESQ_VI_RT_SPIN_US); =2 QoS USER_INTERACTIVE only; ROGUESQ_VI_RT_AT=<s> one-way flip. DEFAULT ON; =0 restores the old
  thread. Same run, flip at 150 s in flight: a1 (RT) VI p90 3.88 -> 0.00 ms, >2 ms 22% -> 0%, >=19 ms intervals 8.65/s -> 0; a2 (QoS
  only) 5.09 -> 1.51, 43% -> 0%, 13.1/s -> 0 (QoS still ~1 ms late, past the 0.5 ms spin; RT kept). r1/r2 (20 s toggle): the first
  20 s before any RT p90 4.1-4.9 (= t2 all run), 0.0 in every window after t=20, INCLUDING the THREAD_STANDARD_POLICY off blocks -> the
  revert is sticky, so the toggle's off blocks are not an arm (documented; use _AT). Spin cost 2 -> 0.5 ms per VI.
- Present side (not closed): late presents 0.07-0.25/s in no-RT runs vs 0-0.1/s with RT (cross-run only; the same-run before windows had
  0-0.02/s, too few to compare). The level still forms with RT: r2 (no drain) at level 54-84% acq>5, lat 38.5, its 7 onsets with EVEN
  cadence (dqmax 16.73 ms = baseline), and a2's level (lat 45.7) survived the flip. So hitch onsets are gone, and an even-cadence path
  remains: H-vsync-phase (our VI clock and the display's vsync are two free 60 Hz clocks; the phase drifts until a present misses its

## Session 6979 (2026-11-08) — G1e: the 21:9 Gfx-thread "preemptions" are its own blocking stderr write()s; async stderr lands default on (same-run 12.9 -> 0 write-blocks/min, gaps >3 ms 4.3 -> 0/min)

Work unit (NEXT.md g1e-gfx-preemptor): name what preempts the USER_INTERACTIVE Gfx thread at 21:9 late presents.
Hypotheses: H-intra (our threads saturate the P cores), H-extern (other processes), H-ecore (migration), plus H-block added
this session (the thread is not preempted at all but blocked).

Instrument (lib/N64ModernRuntime events.cpp namespace g1et, ROGUESQ_G1E_THREADS=<file>, opt-in): a USER_INTERACTIVE 1 kHz
sampler (task_threads + THREAD_EXTENDED_INFO: cumulative CPU ns, run_state, curpri, name), per-CPU host ticks every 10 ms, task
TASK_EVENTS_INFO faults/pageins every 10 ms, and whenever the Gfx thread is WAITING or UNINTERRUPTIBLE: suspend, read
PC/LR/FP chain + ARM exception state (ESR/FAR), resume (no allocation while suspended), dladdr names. Cost ~5-8% of one core.
Positive control: the Gfx thread shows "ran" in 0.78-0.80 of 1 ms samples in normal send_dl windows (cpu ~8.2 of ~9.7 ms), and
its WAITING stacks resolve (19384 samples in RT64 State::fullSync semaphore wait = the GPU sync, as expected).

Runs (21:9 dd4 FPS60 VI_LOCK=1 GFX_QOS=1, s6977 Q0 recipe, scratch/s6979/, all 0 crash, each 330 s): T1, T2, T3 (census), T4 (fix A/B).

Results.
- CPUs are NOT saturated at late instants: per-CPU busy over the 20-30 ms tick window <=0.5 on 14-15 of 15 CPUs; our other threads
  0.33-0.52 cores. H-intra and H-extern (CPU saturation) refuted, two runs (T1 5 lates, T2 3 lates).
- In 6/8 late windows (T1+T2) and 2/3 (T3) the Gfx thread spends 2-5 consecutive 1 ms samples in TH_STATE_UNINTERRUPTIBLE mid
  send_dl; normal windows ~0.00 per window. Stacks (T3, every U sample in any send_dl window: 9 late + 54 normal): ALL in
  __write_nocancel (ESR 0x56000080 = SVC, no page-ins: 0 in every late window, 2.5/s run-wide) from fprintf(stderr) in
  rsp_dpc_submit_impl (factor5_ucode_nmac), RT64::State::updateScreen and FramebufferRenderer::submitRasterScene.
  The remaining late wall-cpu is "runnable but no CPU" samples (0.2-0.5 of the window); one late per run had no U at all
  (T1 660530: rRrRrrr, T2 661020 = H-rsp-work).
- ORIGIN ours: the default build writes ~190 KB/s of diagnostic stderr (log_T3 62 MB/330 s; [s5855] 18.8 MB, [s5901], [si-thr],
  [vi-mode-table], [dpc-fwd], [present-1024], ...) and stderr is unbuffered, so each line is a write() syscall on the calling
  thread; writes to the log file block for ms (host 33 GB into swap, Terminal.app holding 26 GB compressed - very likely game
  stderr scrollback from Terminal-launched runs).
- FIX (src/main/main.cpp s6979se, ROGUESQ_STDERR_ASYNC DEFAULT ON, =0 old): fd 2 -> pipe; USER_INTERACTIVE reader into memory
  (cap 256 MB, then counted drops), UTILITY writer to the original fd. ROGUESQ_STDERR_ASYNC_AT=<s> = same-run switch;
  rs64_stderr_async_restore() (crash handler, SIGABRT handler, atexit, at_quick_exit) drains <=300 ms and restores fd 2.
  Crash positive control ROGUESQ_TEST_CRASH_AT=12: 5009 pre-crash lines drained, then the full [CRASH] dump in the log.
- Same-run A/B T4 (ASYNC_AT=180, tools/g1e_stderr_async_ab.py, windows from 95 s): before 18 U samples (12.9/min, all write()),
  wall-cpu >3 ms 6 (4.3/min), max 6.59 ms; after (2.51 min) 0 U, 0 gaps >3 ms (expected ~10 at the before rate), max 2.54 ms,
  p999 2.72 -> 1.96. Sham control T3 (no switch, split at 257 s): U 18.9 vs 12.3/min, gaps >3 ms 4.3 vs 3.3/min - both halves
  stay non-zero, so the T4 drop is the switch, not time. T4 itself had 0 late presents in both halves (late rate is 0-5 per run),
  so the late-present effect is not yet measured: whole-run replicas s6979_219_async_r1/r2 queued (pre-registered vs 1.04/min).
Rules out: CPU saturation (in-process or external) as the cause of the 21:9 H-rsp-host lates; page-in/memory compression stalls.

control); refutes H-intra and H-extern (no CPU saturation at late instants, 3 runs) and H-ecore/page-in (0 page-ins, the wall-cpu

## Session 6985 (2026-11-08) — G1e: late present fence wait = present thread waking late (H-cpu-wait); ROGUESQ_PRESENT_QOS=1 opt-in cuts lates ~1/3

Work unit (NEXT.md s6984, slug g1e-late-present): split the late present pass's executeCommandLists+fence wait (gpu_ms
1.5-1.9 vs 0.36 ms on lates, s6984) into GPU queue wait (H-gpuq), slow GPU execution (H-gpuclk) and CPU wake (H-cpu-wait).

Instrument (lib/rt64, exported to submodule-patches/rt64*.patch): plume_metal.cpp executeCommandLists, when the present
thread arms it (rs64_present_stamp_arm, only while ROGUESQ_PRESENT_RING is on), retains the wait-semaphore buffer and adds a
completed handler (registered before the fence signal) storing both buffers' GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime (host mach seconds,
same base as rs64_pring_now). Every other fenced buffer folds max(GPUEnd-GPUStart) and max(GPUStart-commit) into atomics read
and cleared per Q row. Q row gains ws (wait buf start - commit), wx (wait buf span = acquire semaphore), gs (main start - wait
end), ge (main span), hw (fence-wait return - main GPU end), oge/ogs/on (other buffers), qos (qos_class_self). New opt-in

of present() in the handler. tools/g1e_late_leg.py parses S rows (keys qc sc sp pgs pge cg, cg = on-glass - commit). New
tools/g1e_commit_phase.py: commit phase vs the on-glass vsync grid (P at), late vs normal, and vsyncs commit->glass.

- **Writer named (ROGUESQ_MATWATCH=1, new tools/apply_s6992_matwatch.py, in the fixup apply list after s6591; s5798 per-store hook).** Material pool = rs_malloc(0x3000) at boot, 512 x 0x18 nodes at 0x8015FDE0 (positive control: [matw] base publish + [matw-own] buildMaterialFreeList link stores fired). Foreign writers: allocateDisplayListBuffer +0x14 and emitMaterialRenderStateDL +0x0E (legit field users, every frame), and **hudDisplayUpdateWorker pc 0x800496A8** (its own thread, phase 9) writing 8 words of palette (0x2B5D1A57...) into node 327 at 0x80161C88. That worker (misnamed; it is the terrain-cell texture streamer) PI-DMAs 0x820 bytes into getTextureDataByMaterialId(desc+4), then copies the 32-byte TLUT at +0x800 to getTextureTlutEntry(desc+6) = ((u32*)*0x80128EFC)[id].
- **Why the destination is the pool:** [matw-tlut]: desc 0x80B1CB4C, data_id 367, **tlut_id 4184, table count 2000 (40 used)**; entry address 0x80161C70 lies past the 8000-byte table inside the material pool and holds a node pointer (0x80161C88), so the copy lands on a node. [descw2] (fixed watch on the deterministic desc): loadLevelTextureCache pc 0x8004836C writes +6 = getTextureAttrBySlot(data_id) = record+0xE for all 4 cache entries (0x1058 each). [matw-rec]: that record is the named buffer "ltex_cache_5" (+8 = 64x64, +0xC = 0x0820, **+0xE = 0x1058**, data 0x80796500). loadTextureToMemory sets +0xE to a fresh TLUT slot only when the caller passes TLUT 0xFFFF; otherwise it keeps the old +0xE, and initTextureLUTAndAllocBuffers zeroes only +0 of each record. So +0xE is stale (H-stale) or set by a path not yet watched.

HYPOTHESIS-ID: l15-219-tlut-oob (closed).
- **Static read first (no instrument build needed).** loadLevelTextureCache (0x800482xx) rs_mallocs a header per "ltex_cache_N" with +0x20 = hdr+0x1058 (the TLUT data), then registerHmtTextureInTable -> parseHmtMaterials -> loadTextureToMemory(slot, tlut=hdr+0x20 word, ...). loadTextureToMemory 0x8001FC20: `if ((tlut & 0xFF000000) != 0x80000000) record+0xE = tlut` (treat it as a TLUT slot id), else pack the palette and store the allocated slot. Record +0xC is the data size (0x820 = 64x64 4bpp + 0x20), not an id. So +0xE = 0x1058 = low half of the pointer 0x81001058: the header landed at 0x81000000, the dd>1 spill base (OSMEM_MB=12 layout, s6587/s6858/s6893).
- **H-stale and H-path refuted, H-layout refuted:** the value is written, by the retail store at 0x8001FD10, from our heap address. The 2000-slot table count was a post-corruption read (fixed 21:9 run: 2048, like 4:3/16:9).
- **Idiom-class audit (RecompiledFuncs, all funcs_*.c):** 14 `lui 0xFF00`; 7 are the pointer test (relocateSndPointer 0x800925FC, allocTextureTlutBlock 0x8001E5DC, loadTextureToMemory 0x8001FC20 + 0x8001FD50, loadAndDecodeTexture 0x80023164, 0x8002340C (texture-attr helper after getTextureAttrBySlot), texPackTlutSlotOrAlloc 0x80023570); 7 are 0xFF00FF00 fill masks (isStructUninitialized, initActorRenderDescriptorIfUninit, executeActorType1Effect, cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag). The 0xF0000000 tests (musyxInitVoiceFromSample, loadSpeechFile) already accept 0x81. No `>> 24 == 0x80` game sites. The s6862 HEAP-ADDR-AUDIT covered host patches only, which is why this class was missed.
- **Fix (default on):** tools/apply_s6993_ptrmask.py (in the fixup list after s6963) replaces the 7 mask loads with rs64_s6993_mask(pc, v) (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp): 0xF0000000, or retail 0xFF000000 with ROGUESQ_PTRMASK=0; logs [s6993] for the first 16 values whose verdict the masks disagree on. Non-pointer values at these sites are 16-bit slot ids / small offsets; 0xB0 ROM addresses still pass relocateSndPointer's second test.
- **Arms, one build, L15 dd4 FPS60 VI_LOCK QOS_ALL MATWATCH, 200 s hold, cursorMask 0x8000 all (scratch/s6993/arms.sh, data scratch/s6993q):** 21:9 PTRMASK=0 (control): [s6993] v=81000298..810020A8 then v=81001058 x10 "slot id", [tlutw] oob=1 x12, tlut_cnt 2000 after corruption, `[CRASH] signal 10` (reproduces s6991). 21:9 fixed: alive at 200 s, oob 0, 0 crash, [s6993] same pointers "pointer (fixed)", tlut ids 70 of 2048. 16:9 fixed: alive 200 s, oob 0, 6 [s6993] lines — so 16:9 dd>1 also passed spill pointers as slot ids before (silent wrong palette slots, no crash). Two lines of evidence: static code path + same-binary control/fix pair with the exact predicted value 0x81001058.

## Session 6998 (2026-11-08) — G5a open question closed: RT64 copyNativeToRAM writebacks land only in the colour image's own heap block or the non-heap top-of-RAM framebuffers; 0 stale, 0 foreign-live, 0 header hits at dd4 16:9 and dd1 4:3 (positive control passes)
HYPOTHESIS-ID: g5a-copynative-live. Question from s6893: at dd4 16:9 RT64 copyNativeToRAM wrote pixels on the watched word
8074A380/8074AC60. Is the guest block under it live (H-stale: image address freed and reused; H-span: copy runs past the
image into the next block) or the game's own colour image (H-fb)?
Instrument (new, opt-in, default off): ROGUESQ_G5A_WBLIVE=1, src/main/upstream_compat.cpp rs64_g5a_wblive, called from the
existing rs64_g1d_blk_dma("rt64wb") hook inside Framebuffer::copyNativeToRAM (no lib/ edit). Each writeback walks the
rs_malloc arenas (heads 0x8010FEFC/FF00/FF18; header hw+0 1 free / 2 alloc / 8 terminator, +4 size, next = h+0x10+size,
read from rs_malloc 0x80001BB4-0x80001C50) and classifies the written range against the block holding the image address F:
own / stale (F's block free) / nonheap / foreign (another allocated block overlapped); hdr = any block header inside the range.
[g5a-wbl-d] logs each distinct (F, lo, hi, class, block) once (cap 600); foreign/hdr lines uncapped to 300.
Positive control, same run, every arm: [g5a-wbl-ctl] on synthetic ranges in the live heap: range inside allocated block A
-> own, A into the next allocated block B -> foreign, inside a free block -> stale. All three as wanted.
Arms, one binary, LEVEL=4 (Gerrard V) forced route, FPS60, owner save read-only (md5 f8b29b66... unchanged), screen unlocked:

| d4w2 | 4 | 16:9 | 177 | 1 | >=32768 | 12923 | 19845 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| d1c | 1 | 4:3 | 178 | 1 | >=32768 | 13327 | 19441 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
(counts at the n=32768 line; foreign/stale lines would print unconditionally and none did over the whole run.)

## Session 7001 (2026-11-08) — G5b ring-7 "diagonal" dips are the opposite: armed outer-ring dips sit on axis headings (0 of ~5300 near-diagonal swaps), where the 64-cell window's forward edge hovers on the ring-7 boundary; extra terrain, not a loss; item closed

HYPOTHESIS-ID: g5b-ring7-diagonal. Offline only, no game run (traces scratch/s6901/{tg,g3e}_{f4,fw,f2,l1,l5}, scratch/s7000/*_d4). No new soak verdicts. CURRENT-TRUTH 14.7 KB, no maintenance.

Question from NEXT: s6901 saw ring-7 dips rise armed (f4 47->107, l1 31->79) and guessed square-window diagonals (H-diag) vs H-edge (window on the pre-clamp bound) vs H-noise (thin ring near threshold).
New tool tools/g5b_ring7_discrim.py (seamless parity split as g5b_fwdwin_seamless.py; per dip: distance of heading to the nearest diagonal dg, window w/h, window edge on site-13 bound, ring ref; baseline = all swaps of that parity; thresholds 60 and 120). scratch/s7001/band.py: per heading class, forward reach and ring 6/7 counts dip vs non-dip.

| arm | armed dips dg<15 / 15-30 / 30-45 (of swaps) | off dips same bins | armed edge>0 dip vs all | armed ring7 p50 vs off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f4 L4 dd4 16:9 | 0/1070, 29/1273, 204/1407 | 10/1270, 20/1542, 59/1624 | 0.42 vs 0.83 | 512 vs 0 |
| fw L4 dd4 21:9 | 1/949, 73/951, 110/1145 | 9, 29, 30 | 0.33 vs 0.65 | 296 vs 0 |
| l1 L1 dd4 | 0/1014, 29/830, 249/1261 | 11, 7, 43 | 0.29 vs 0.83 | 512 vs 0 |
| l5 L5 dd4 | 1/634, 3/1222, 120/1681 | 5, 21, 80 | 0.46 vs 0.69 | 512 vs 0 |
| d4 L7 dd4 | 3/1610, 5/1804, 63/1689 | 10, 18, 43 | 0.17 vs 0.70 | 445 vs 0 |
| f2 L4 dd2 | 2 dips total (ring 7 barely reached, ref>=60 on 1% of swaps) | 2 | - | 0 vs 0 |

Positive control: the off arm's dips fire in the dg<15 bin on every dd4 arm (9-11), so the detector is not blind at diagonals; the armed zero there is a measurement.
H-diag REFUTED (inverted): armed dips sit on axis headings, none on diagonals. H-edge refuted: dips touch the pre-clamp bound LESS often than the average swap (0.17-0.46 vs 0.65-0.83). H-noise partly: threshold 120 keeps most dips (211 of 233 f4), so it is not count noise, it is geometry.
Mechanism (band.py): ring = Chebyshev distance / 8 cells, ring 7 = 56-63 cells. Along an axis the FWDWIN window (64 wide, centre eye+26) ends at ~58 cells, so the forward edge sits on the ring-7 boundary: axis non-dip swaps have reach p50 52-61 and ring7 p50 0-285, dip swaps reach 51-55 and ring7 0, ring 6 still 353-662. Near a diagonal the corner reaches 63 and ring 7 is full (512). So a dip is the edge stepping one cell row across 56 as the eye crosses cell boundaries: the normal stepping of a window edge, at a radius the off arm (ring7 p50 0) and dd1 (reach 28-34) never draw at all. Total-quad dips < 0.8 stay 0 armed in every arm.
ORIGIN: no defect; the armed rise counts flicker of extra terrain the old clamp did not draw. Not a mitigation, nothing landed in the game.
Rules out: diagonal corner geometry and map-edge clamping as the cause of the s6901 ring-7 rise. Does NOT show how this band looks on screen; it is beyond the dd1 radius and inside the dd fog range (G5e), so the owner's dd4 flight judges it like the rest of G5b.

## Session 7017 (2026-11-08) — tog-parity-bias: the s7010 odd-second split is biased by the harness autopilot's 2 s press cycle; new xor8 split (rs64_tog_odd) passes A/A null (rsp +0.08 ms vs parity +0.73 same frames) and positive control (WIDEWIN=tog L1 21:9 dd4 rsp +3.50, fps 60.0/59.6)

What ran. Step 1 offline on the s7016 A/A rings (N1 GLUE_TOG=3, G1, F1), new tools/g5e_parity_spectrum.py + scratch/s7017/fold.py:
per-1 s rsp buckets are strongly autocorrelated (lag1 +0.79..+0.82, slow decay: scene drift), and the detrended rsp has a
4 s Fourier component of 0.37-0.87 ms in all 8 rings checked (s7014 k3/k4, s7015 L1/L15/L4w169, s7016 F1/G1/N1) plus a 2 s
component 0.23-0.65 ms in the non-toggling runs. Folding on game frame count (mod 60/120) gives nothing (<=0.4). Source named:
the flight autopilot schedule in g1_level_coverage_common.zsh presses a, sl, a, sr every 2 s (1.8 s hold, SDL_GetTicks clock):
an 8 s cycle with fire every 4 s, i.e. a load at harmonics of 0.125 Hz. A plain 1 s parity split (a 0.5 Hz square wave) projects
onto the 0.5 Hz harmonic -> the A/A bias. Its phase is set by the SDL clock origin, so it agrees within one batch (s7016 3/3) and
differs across batches (s7014 k3 vs k4): that is why it looked "phase-locked". H-tool (anchor mapping) refuted: the injected-effect
control below recovers effects, and the bias follows the autopilot harmonics. H-thread not needed.
Fix: split = (sec ^ sec>>3) & 1 ("xor8"): alternates every second, inverts every 8 s, so any 8 s-periodic load cancels exactly
over 16 s. Offline on N1/G1/F1, shifts 0/500/1000/3000/5000/8000 ms: xor8 |rsp delta| <= 0.11 everywhere; parity +-0.55..0.81;
splitmix hash 0.2-0.66 (unbiased in expectation but ~6x noisier with this autocorrelation, so rejected). Estimator control:
--inject-ms 0.5 / 1.0 on N1 xor8 -> +0.42 / +0.92 (null -0.08).
Step 2 code: src/main/upstream_compat.cpp rs64_tog_odd(mt) / rs64_tog_xor8() / rs64_tog_anchor(mt) (one [s7010-clk] line, now
with split=xor8|parity); used at WIDEWIN=tog, DD_LODMUL_TOG, GLUE_TOG (dpc_bridge record_submit), CULL_SPIKE=tog. tog3 stays sec%3.
ROGUESQ_TOG_SPLIT=parity restores the old split. tools/g5e_cost_by_parity.py reads split= from the anchor (absent = parity), adds
--split parity|xor8|hash and --inject-ms. Other older tog sites (MELT, SKYZ, LETTERBOX, CUT_LIVE ...) still use plain parity: they
are look toggles, not cost splits.
Same-build runs (scratch/s7017/all.zsh, L1 21:9 dd4 MELT CULL=1 OWNER_TIMING, 320 s holds, 0 crashes, 0 VI stalls):
N2 A/A (WIDEWIN=1 GLUE_TOG=3): xor8 rsp +0.08 (shift 500 +0.06, 3000 +0.08); the same frames under parity +0.73 / -0.32 / -0.73.
P2 positive control WIDEWIN=tog: off/on fps 60.0/59.6, rsp 8.95 -> 12.45 (+3.50), run +1.13, P(>=2VI) 0.00/0.00; shift 500 +0.20;
shift 3000 -0.83 = xor8's own lag-3 correlation (-0.25) x 3.50 -> -0.88 expected; parity-misread +0.18 (orthogonal, as designed).
So s7015's L1 21:9 "+4.21 ms, 60.0 -> 58.1 fps" overstated it: same level/aspect now +3.50 ms and -0.4 fps (single run each).
Rules out: H-tool, a game-side 120-VI workload. Remaining caveat: the split only cancels loads periodic in 8 s; another schedule
period (e.g. the EARLY 4 s list, which ends before skip 130 s) would need checking with the A/A null again.
Next: resume G5e / gfx host-glue cost work with the de-biased split (re-measure s7016 GLUE_TOG=1/2 walk deltas), NEXT.md.
Note: s7017 tl rings (gitignored) were deleted after analysis; numbers above are the record.
Verdict: this selects H-periodic (an autopilot-driven 8 s load cycle, not a 120-VI game workload) and refutes H-tool (anchor mapping: injected
effects are recovered exactly) and H-thread (not needed: the bias sits at the autopilot harmonics and cancels under xor8). It closes the
tog-parity-bias thread. Next discriminator (NEXT.md, slug gfx-host-glue): GLUE_TOG=1/2 on the xor8 split; a walk delta >= 1 ms selects
H-glue-big, < 0.3 ms selects H-glue-small.

## Session 7033 (2026-11-09) — G1c off-map height gate: image-neutral at all frozen poses but it disarms the cull (42 of 5444 cells/frame still culled, rsp +0.01 ms vs -7.96 ungated, same run): H-costgone, height lever closed
HYPOTHESIS-ID: g1c-offmap-cells.
Units, from the binary: the stream's span test (streamTerrainGridCellsByDistance 0x80042D6C..DA8) processes a cell iff span_max(0x80130DB0) >= rec[3] and
span_min(0x80131DB0) <= rec[4], rec = *(0x80136DC4) + (hm[z*w+x] & 0x1FFF) * 30, hm = *(0x80136DC0) (row clamped at 0x80042C28..C80, so off-map cells reuse the
edge cell's record = the "plateau"). Span bytes = trunc(plane-solved y * f22) in scanConvertTriangleToSpanTable (0x80042614..0x80042694), f22 = C/H from
binPolygonIntoTerrainGrid 0x800428A8 (C = *(0x8003A4F8), H = *(0x80136DD0)); measured sc = 40.0. So cell byte heights and eye y * 40 share units.
Change (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp, host only, no regen): rs64_s7033_frame (called from rs64_s7030_begin) latches eye byte height and "up" from the eye's own
clamped cell (eye above its ground); rs64_s7032_cell then culls an off-map cell past R only if (top - eye)*up > margin, top = the clamped edge cell's highest byte.
ROGUESQ_DD_OFFMAPCULL_H=<margin> (default 1, gate on whenever OFFMAPCULL is set), =off fixed R (s7031), =tog gate in tog3 phase 1 only. Per-phase keep/pass counters in [s7033].
Calibration check: up = -1 on every frame (upc 0/16811): y is down-negative, eye bytes -35 .. -155, eye-cell ranges e.g. 63..86 or -56..-56 (eye always above).
Run 1, frozen poses (scratch/s7033/run_L1h.zsh, tools/g3_optin_pose_arms.sh, L1 21:9 dd6 FPS60 DD_UNSAFE MELT WIDEWIN cap 10240 CULL_SPIKE=1 FAST=1 PROBES=0, PIN=1,
7 freezes; arms offA, r2h = OFFMAPCULL=2 + gate, r2 = OFFMAPCULL=2 _H=off, k03 = FOGCULL=0.3). Mean |dLum| vs offA, poses 0..6 (tools/s7032_pose_cull_score.py):
 intra 0.00; k03 3.04 1.48 0.54 0.94 0.50 3.64 3.97 (control responds); r2 0.20 0.13 0.16 0.30 0.51 10.60 39.00 (= s7032 to 2 decimals: deterministic,
 the positive control for the void); r2h 0.00 at all 7 poses. Sheet docs/owner_sheet_s7033_heightgate.jpg (offA | r2h | r2 | diffs). 0 crashes x4.
Run 2, cost, same run (scratch/s7033/run_cost.zsh, tog3 R=-1,2,2 with _H=tog, L1 owner path, 289 s flight, 0 crashes, 0 VI stalls; g5e_cost_by_parity --phases 3):
 p0 (no cull) fps 53.3 rsp 14.19; p1 (R=2 + gate) 55.2 / 14.20 (rsp +0.01); p2 (R=2 ungated) 59.8 / 6.23 (rsp -7.96, reproduces s7031's -9.75 in direction).

  and fits the file-to-ring clock offset: 0.23 s, +-3 s controls score 0 (python monotonic = the TL steady clock).
  Positive control: normal seconds are 99% `osRecvMesg` waits (waitForPostSwapAck 174k, submitGfxFrame 29k samples), on-CPU 4.8k.

  `runVideoFrameTick -> musyxNoopStub -> waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone -> yield_self_1ms` holds 85-104 samples (113-138 ms at
  1.33 ms/sample); plus shutdownMusyXVoices 51-59 (2 gaps) and waitForAnyAudioSlot 20 (1 gap, = s7064's 25-66 ms drain).
  On-CPU guest work in the gaps is small. H-compute refuted (no compute burst); H-tokenwait refuted (the blocked frames are our

  waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone seeds to 16 is decremented by s3 = the number of 0xC0 (192-sample) mix chunks produced that synth frame
  (16-entry chunk ring at 0x80149988 index, per-frame chunk cap at -0x68B2). So the wait = 16 x 192 = 3072 output samples; at the
  game's 22047 Hz AI rate = 139.3 ms = 8.37 VI (1.91 chunks per VI), which predicts both the 133-150 ms stretch and its 8-or-9-VI

  game's own constants and the AI rate, not by our scheduler, so retail pays the same ~139 ms (inference from the code; the oracle
  cannot drive these transitions, so no retail timing measurement). Gap = 139 ms countdown + 25-66 ms slot drain (s7064) + an

## Session 7081 (2026-11-10) — N64Recomp self-branch miscompile fixed: 16 resampler helper exits return-and-dispatch into the caller tail, differential test against the retail bytes passes 2400/2400, old path crashes on every exit
HYPOTHESIS-ID: n64recomp-selfbranch-fix. Soaks: none new (SOAK-RESULTS tail unchanged since s7062). Owner reports: none new.
Census (new tools/scan_selfbranch.py over the live tree): 18 gotos leave their function. 16 are the s6871 set, 4 per helper (interpolatePointTableSamplesToPackedWord 800927B0, interpolateLutSamplesToPackedWord 80092A54, interpolateConstantSamplesToPackedWord 80092CF0, packFourLutResampledSamples 80092F94). Each one jumps into its caller's code just before the helper (80092758/60/68/6C, 800929FC/A04/A0C/A10, 80092C6C/C7C/C8C/C9C, 80092F10/F20/F30/F40). Worse than s6871 said: N64Recomp prints out-of-range labels at the first instruction >= label, so the four labels are spread over the helper's first four instructions (L_80092768 sits at 800927B8), not all at the entry. The other 2 are data_gap_800CC3D4 and data_gap_80045024, both decoded data, and are left alone.
Retail semantics (read from the ELF): the helper is a leaf with no frame, called by jal. On a finished one-shot sample ($s3 == 0) it branches into the caller's tail: shift and store the last packed word, zero-fill the rest of the output, then the caller's epilogue, which returns to the caller's caller.
Change (H-dup/H-tail hybrid, the smallest correct form): new tools/fixup_selfbranch.py. Each bad `goto L_T` becomes `if (g_rs64_sbx_on) { g_rs64_sbx_target = T; return; } goto L_T;`. Every call to the helper in the caller is followed by a dispatch: take the target, log it with rs64_sbx_hit, then `switch` to a new label rs64_sbx_T placed at T's instruction inside the caller (unknown target -> __builtin_trap). Pairs are found generically: the target must lie in a function that calls the helper. The script is idempotent, checks it found 16, and is wired at the end of tools/fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py. Runtime: new src/main/rs64_selfbranch.cpp (thread-local target, `ROGUESQ_SELFBRANCH_FIX=0` keeps the old path, startup line `[s7081 selfbranch] fix on|OFF`, the first 16 hits logged, then powers of two). Added to CMakeLists. Applied to the live tree; afterwards the live funcs_24.c is byte-equal to the file the test ran on.
ORIGIN: the writer of the wrong control flow is N64Recomp recompilation.cpp (print_branch warns, then emits `goto L_T` and the label prints at the first vram >= T). The value is legitimate: the retail branch target is real code in the caller. This repairs the miscompile at its source in the generated text. It is not a guard.
Differential test (new tools/s7081_selfbranch_test/): mips_ref.py is a small big-endian MIPS III interpreter. It executes the retail .entry+.text bytes from ../rogue_squadron64/build/roguesquadron.elf and raises on any opcode it does not implement, so it shares nothing with N64Recomp. run_test.py builds a harness from the patched funcs_24.c (its preamble plus the 4 callers and 4 helpers, with the same flags and include order as the RecompiledFuncs target), runs random voice states in forked children, and compares all GPRs plus the a0/a1/output/stack regions against the reference. Seed 7081, 300 cases per caller per kind:
  exit (s3 = 0), fix arm: 300/300 match on every caller. Cases where an exit fired: 155 / 173 / 279 / 265. All 16 targets were hit.
  exit, old arm (ROGUESQ_SELFBRANCH_FIX=0 path): crashed in exactly those 155 / 173 / 279 / 265 cases and matched the rest. The restarted helper rereads samples from $t1 = $s3 = 0. So if the miscompile had ever run in the game it would have crashed, not silently corrupted.
  loop (s3 != 0, the positive control where N64Recomp was already right): both arms match, 300 / 300 / 53 / 300. The reference skipped 247 Constant-loop cases because random states sent the wrapped pointer out of RAM (it raises; these are not counted as passes).
  Harness bug fixed on the way: the first build lacked data stubs for the preamble's hook flags (dyld abort, every case read as a crash). Also, PointTable never reached its end compare until s2 was set to the last sample's address (t1 == s2 is an equality test on even addresses).

The resampler functions are absent from 114 host stack samples, so live reach is still not shown in this run. Preempt fixup still reports 6.

  variable shifts masked &31/&63, sltiu compared unsigned). The 177 addu that feed jump tables use the s7083 `jr_addend_` form.
  Negative control: one mult mutated S64(S32 -> U64(U32 in memory is flagged (+1). Positive control: the 0x800464F4 div in
  loadGridCellTilesByDistance is enumerated and classified guarded (break 7 + break 6).

  value (lo=0) only matters where retail already dies. The 3 unguarded 32-bit divides use constant divisors (_Ldtob /100000,
  computeNoteRatePairFromTableA/B divu by 0x300). The 2 unguarded **ddivu** are u64DivU64 0x80007500 (divisor is 64-bit data

  lo=0, hi=a. The R4300 gives lo=0xFFFF...FFFF, hi=a. I did not prove whether a zero divisor can reach these sites in play

  woken by the first send keeps the token, and the second send hands out another (two mutex holders).
  Fix: the rule now prepends only one-line needles. Checked on the pristine s7082 pass: 1 call each, and the block

## Session 7093 (2026-11-10) — RSPRecomp scalar-unit lowering census CLOSED: 0 live differences; one latent template defect (sltiu with $zero and a negative immediate) FIXED in RSPRecomp

Work unit (NEXT.md, slug rsp-su-lowering-census): does RSPRecomp lower every SCALAR RSP instruction in the 3 compiled
TUs (main gfx ucode, audio ucode B, boot) the way the RSP executes it? New tool `tools/s7093_su_census.py --controls`
(exit 0; report scratch/s7093/census.txt). It does not trust rabbitizer or RSPRecomp's templates: every top-level record
of a fresh pristine pass (`zsh tools/ucode_regen.sh verify`) gets a vram by counting (every L_ label agrees, record
count == text_size/4), its retail word is read from the ROM and decoded by the tool's own decoder.
Results:
- A decode: comment mnemonic and fields == ROM word on every record of all 3 TUs (1,777 records; 0 mismatches).
- B control flow: every branch/j/jal/jr goto == target computed from the word; delay slot == the next ROM word, emitted
  inside the taken path before the goto and again as the following top-level record; no branch in a delay slot; every
  jal emits `r31 = 0x{pc+8}`. One target differs and is already owned: main 0x1FF0 `bgez` runs past the IMEM end (the
  hardware PC wraps to 0x000 = IMEM 0x1000) and RSPRecomp emits `goto L_0000`; the live fixup "L_0000 self-restart"
  (PORTING-STATE s5428-s5455) handles it. Allowlisted only while the live file carries that tag.
- C cop0/cop2: every mfc0/mtc0 action matches the decoded register (DPC_* go to the bridge macros; SP_STATUS, DMA_FULL,
  DMA_BUSY, SEMAPHORE read 0 by design); mfc2/mtc2 carry the decoded element, cfc2 the decoded rd (only rd 1 = VCC used).
- D semantics: the 1,083 distinct live scalar lines (1,845 records; ALU, shifts, slt*, loads, stores, branch
  conditions) compiled into host functions with the live rsp.hpp DMEM block + RSP_ADD32/SUB32/SIGNED and run against a
  Python reference of the decoded word (wrap, sign/zero extension, sign-extended immediates, unaligned and wrapping DMEM
  bytes, shift masks), fast DMEM path and byte loops: 94,060 cases, 0 bad. Plus 1,090 SYNTHETIC lines produced by the
  real RSPRecomp binary from assembled boundary instructions (imm 0/0x7FFF/0x8000/0xFFFF/..., rs = $zero and a
  register, every shift amount, wrap/unaligned memory offsets): 91,360 cases, 0 bad after the fix below.
- E cop2 moves: rsp.MFC2/MTC2 all 16 e, CTC2->CFC2 rd 0..3 x 65,536 values + per-lane flags vs a byte-level cxd4 su.c
  reference: 3,473,408 cases, 0 bad.
- F jal link: RSPRecomp stores 0x1000|(pc+8), hardware stores (pc+8)&0xFFF. All 11 non-jr readers of $31 are pure
  save -> restore -> jr chains ($30/$7/$8 copies, DMEM 0x16A and 0x50($18) halfwords, and audio ucode B lane 6 of $v31
  via mtc2/mfc2: every vector op on $v31 in ucode B uses e=8..13, lanes 0-5, and $v31 is never stored), and the
  indirect dispatch masks (jump_target|0x1000)&0x1FFF, so the bit-12 difference never reaches data. The ucode itself
  loads 0x1xxx return addresses (`ori $ra, $zero, 0x1088`). Harmless.
DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (latent, 0 live sites): RSPRecomp lowered `sltiu rt, $zero, -imm` to `rt = 0 < -0X8000 ? 1 : 0`.
r0 prints as the int literal 0, so the compare is SIGNED and gives 0 where the RSP gives 1 (2,000 bad synthetic cases).
With rs = a register the uint32_t operand forces an unsigned compare, so only the $zero form was wrong. Fix in
../N64Recomp/RSPRecomp/src/rsp_recomp.cpp (commit 85c6156 in that repo; mirror submodule-patches/n64recomp-rsprecomp-sltiu.patch):
a negative immediate is emitted as U32(-0X...). Non-negative immediates print as before, so the 12 live ucode TUs
regenerate byte-identical (`tools/ucode_regen.sh verify` 12/12 SAME; the only 2 sltiu sites use $10 with imm 3). No game
binary change, so no boot run was needed (nothing to test at runtime).
Controls (all fire): one corrupted ROM bit -> check A flags it; mutant shapes (sltiu signed, lb zero-extended, sra
logical, beq->bne, sllv &15) flagged on 35/35 distinct live lines; the pre-fix sltiu template gives 2,000 bad; MFC2
without its e+1 wrap gives 32,636 bad.
Rules out: RSPRecomp scalar lowering as a source of any RSP misbehaviour in this game. With s7091 (fixups) and s7092 (VU
memory + divide), the recompiled-RSP layer is audited end to end except the runtime DMA / cop0 model (next).

DISCRIMINATION: selects H-su-ok for every live site (0 diffs over 94,060 live cases, controls firing) and refutes

sites, fixed in RSPRecomp). Next discriminator: rsp-dma-cop0-model, H-dma-ok vs H-dma-shape vs H-cop0 (NEXT.md).

Unit (NEXT.md, slug rsp-dma-cop0-model): compare the runtime the recompiled RSP code calls (librecomp rsp.hpp
dma_rdram_to_dmem / dma_dmem_to_rdram, SET_DMA_*/DO_DMA_* macros, RSPRecomp's constant cop0 reads) with hardware.
Three lines of evidence:
1. Host differential tools/s7094_dma_test (`zsh run.sh`): the LIVE rsp.hpp DMA functions (hooks stubbed) vs cxd4 su.c
   MT_DMA_* + SP_DMA_READ/WRITE extracted verbatim, 20,000 random cases per class x rd/wr x fast/slow = 560,000 compares.
   CANON shape (mem&7=0, raw&7=7, raw<0x1000, fits the 4 KB bank, DRAM<8 MB): 0 bad of 80,000. DRAM low-3-bit class:
   0 bad (both mask &0xFFFFF8). Every other hardware feature the runtime does not model differs on ~all cases:
   mem low 3 bits, raw&7 != 7 (hardware rounds to 8 inside the 8-byte copy loop), count/skip rows, skip bits alone
   (runtime takes them as length), DMEM wrap at 0x1000 (runtime clips). Controls: len2 mutant (runtime copies raw+2)
   fails CANON 65,835/80,000 (rc 1); norel mutant (drop cxd4's |7 in mtc0) changes nothing, which shows the rounding
   lives in cxd4's 8-byte loop, not the mtc0 store (scratch/s7094/control_*.txt).
2. Static census tools/s7094_dma_census.py: SP_RD_LEN sites 6 / SP_WR_LEN 2 across the 3 compiled TUs (count control
   = s7093's C sections, pass); 28 DMA-routine call sites (10 gfx, 17 audio, 1 boot) listed with their literal mem/len; every literal length ends
   in 7/F (0xF, 0x3F, 0x4F, 0x7F, 0xFF, 0x17F, 0x197, 0x2FF, 0xFFF ...), the dynamic ones are masked (&0xFFF,
   &0xFF0 - 1, &0x3FF, lhu-1).
3. Live census (new passive instrument src/rsp/s7094_dma_shape.cpp, one gated call at the top of both rsp.hpp DMA
   functions, ROGUESQ_S7094_DMASHAPE=1; startup self-test 10/10 pass; same-run positive control
   ctl_count_mask7ff fires on every live raw >= 0x800; IMEM flag fires on overlay loads): L6 4:3 dd1 boot to flight,
   83 M DMAs, 290 distinct shapes. On the DMEM bank: mem_lo3 0, count 0, skip 0, wrap 0, raw==-1 0. len_not7 hits only
   IMEM overlay loads (skipped by design, the ucode is recompiled) plus ONE DMEM shape:
   rd bank=aud mem=0x0000 len=0x800 dram=0x800A4E00 (19,869 times) = run_task's audio ucode_data staging.
ORIGIN: the writer is lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/src/rsp.cpp run_task. It passed ucode_data_dma_size (the declared
0x800 image size, or the legacy 0xF80) to dma_rdram_to_dmem, whose argument is the hardware SP_RD_LEN value
(bytes - 1). So every audio task copied 0x801 bytes: one byte from RDRAM ucode_data+0x800 into DMEM 0x800, which
rspboot (passes ucode_data_size - 1) never writes. Upstream used 0xF80 - 1; main.cpp's gfx staging uses size - 1;
the s-era M5 rewrite that introduced declared_size dropped the -1 against its own comment ("declare a 0x800-byte image").
Not a legitimate value. FIX: pass size - 1 (ROGUESQ_S7094_UCODE_DATA_OFF1=1 restores the old copy for an A/B).
Qualification (two runs, same recipe scratch/s7094/run.zsh): before L6 flight 305 s, 0 crash, 0 VI stall, defect
shapes 1; after: flight 310 s, 0 crash, 0 VI stall, audio tasks live (2.14 M aud reads, 125,805 aud writes), the shape
is now len=0x7FF, census defect shapes 0 (rc 0). Whether the stray byte was ever read before being written by the audio
ucode is NOT measured; the fix is hardware-exact either way.
cop0 (H-cop0), code-read, single-source: RSPRecomp lowers mfc0 SP_STATUS / SEMAPHORE / DMA_FULL / DMA_BUSY to 0.
DMA is synchronous, so FULL/BUSY 0 is exact. The only SP_STATUS consumer is the gfx task-start yield test (andi 0x80,
SIG0); 0 = "no yield requested", consistent with sp.cpp's completion-wins osSpTaskYielded (returns 0). SP_STATUS
writes (0x2800 clear SIG1/SIG2 at start, 0x4000 set SIG2 before break) are dropped; the CPU side gets task completion
from the runtime, not from those bits. Semaphore: no CPU-side SP_SEMAPHORE literal found in the recompiled C, so a 0
read is what hardware returns. DPC_* reads go through the DPC bridge (RSP_DPC_STATUS_READ), not audited here.
DISCRIMINATION: this selects H-dma-shape for exactly one live site (audio ucode_data staging, fixed); H-dma-ok holds for
every DMA the 3 ucode TUs themselves issue (0 defect shapes in 83 M + 136 M DMAs, controls firing); this refutes H-cop0 by
code-read (single-source). Rules out the RSP DMA model as a source of DMEM corruption. Next: DPC register model (NEXT.md).

## Session 7095 (2026-11-10) — RSP-side DPC register model vs hardware CLOSED: 0 live branch-relevant differences (15/15 ROM sites, 92 M live reads shadowed)
HYPOTHESIS-ID: rsp-dpc-reg-model. Hypotheses: H-dpc-ok (every DPC value the ucode branches on gives the same branch
outcome as hardware with an instantly consuming RDP) vs H-dpc-shape (a polled status bit, or a CURRENT value reported too
early, changes a wait loop or the ring-wrap / task-entry resume decision) vs H-dpc-xbus (the ucode sets XBUS and the bridge
drops the write).
1. Offline, tools/s7095_dpc_census.py (exit 0): decodes the ROM words (s7093 decoder, independent of RSPRecomp) for every
   mfc0/mtc0 on cop0 8-15. main 12 sites (3 in delay slots, which RSPRecomp emits twice, so 15 macro uses; live 15), ucode_b
   2/2, boot 1/1; overlay TUs 6 or 15 uses (resident copies, s7091). The STATUS bits tested are only 0x1 XBUS (0x1E14, b
   0x1080), 0x100 DMA_BUSY (b 0x1098, boot 0x107C) and 0x400 START_VALID (0x114C, 0x1E48). An idle RDP that consumes
   instantly, with XBUS cleared, reports 0 for all three, and our RSP_DPC_STATUS_READ() is a constant 0. The only STATUS
   write is 0x1E58 value 0x1 (clear XBUS), so XBUS is never set: H-dpc-xbus refuted. The audio ucode (src/rsp/aspMain.cpp)
   has no DPC access. Positive controls flagged: mask mutated to 0x80 (CBUF_READY, hardware 1) and write mutated to 0x2.
2. Live, new passive instrument src/rsp/s7095_dpc_model.cpp (ROGUESQ_S7095_DPC=1; hooks in include/rsp_dpc_macros.h
   and in dpc_bridge.cpp rs64_dpc_current_read / rs64_dpc_reset; startup self-test 4/4 pass, crafted sequences fire both
   wait predicates and the escape fires 2 times in 130 polls). It keeps a hardware shadow: START sets START_VALID and leaves
   CURRENT alone; END loads CURRENT from START, then consumes to END; nothing resets between tasks. It compares every read
   with ours. Run: L6 dd1 4:3, boot to flight (scratch/s7095/run.zsh), flight 309 s, 0 crash, 0 VI stall. Over 22,041 tasks,
   92.27 M END writes, 92.30 M CURRENT reads, 92.31 M STATUS reads and 23,429 ring wraps (no laps, max chunk 0x160):
   - CURRENT differs from the shadow in only two contexts. 'entry' (22,039, which is tasks-2): our per-task reset gives 0
     where the shadow has the previous END. 'pend' (23,429, which equals wraps): we snap CURRENT to the new START, where the
     shadow keeps the old END. In 'other' it differs 0 times.
   - Shadow wait predicates: L_115C (spin while CURRENT == new START) 0, L_116C (spin while CURRENT is in (START,
     START+len]) 0, so the hardware value exits both wrap waits on the first poll, as ours does. START_VALID pending at a
     STATUS read 0, START_VALID pending at task start 0, XBUS differs 0.
   - Task-entry decision (0x1DB0..0x1E44): the shadow has CURRENT == END at every entry (hw_cur_ne_end_at_entry 0), so
     hardware takes branch 4 (CURRENT == END) or branch 2 (buffer start above END). Ours takes branch 2 (END 0). Both go to
     L_1E48 for a fresh ring start. The resume path (branch 5) needs CURRENT != END, so it is unreachable with an instant
     RDP under either model.
   - Bounded-poll escape (rs64_dpc_current_read returns v+8 after 64 identical polls): 0 fires in 92.3 M reads. It is dead
     in live play, and the shadow shows that hardware would never spin there either. It stays as a deadlock guard.
DISCRIMINATION: H-dpc-ok is selected on two lines (ROM decode plus the live shadow). H-dpc-shape is refuted: every
divergence is in a context where both values give the same branch. H-dpc-xbus is refuted (the only write clears XBUS). This
closes the RSP side end to end (s7091-s7095). No fix needed. Next: the bridge's RDP forwarding coverage, i.e. whether every
byte hardware would consume in [CURRENT, END) reaches RT64 exactly once (NEXT.md, slug rdp-submit-coverage).

## Session 7096 (2026-11-10) — DPC bridge forwarding coverage CLOSED: RT64 receives exactly the hardware-consumed byte stream (0 missing / 0 duplicate / 0 out-of-order over 34.1 GB, 3 runs); every late content change is one of our own record_submit edits
HYPOTHESIS-ID: rdp-submit-coverage. Hypotheses: H-fwd-exact (bytes forwarded to RT64 == the [CURRENT, END) stream an
instantly consuming hardware RDP reads, each once, in order) vs H-fwd-drop (ranges lost at wraps / task ends / defer:

Instrument: new src/rsp/s7096_fwd_cover.cpp (ROGUESQ_S7096_FWD=1|ctl). The HW stream comes from hooks in
include/rsp_dpc_macros.h RSP_DPC_START/END: hardware model, CURRENT=START if START_VALID else the previous END, persists
across tasks, plus a byte snapshot taken at the END write. The FWD stream: every ultramodern::submit_rdp_range goes through
rs64_rt_submit, which now takes a site id (live/merged/wrap/commit/synth/forcefs). Every deliberate bridge drop records its
range with a reason (pipe/synthrep/cimg/oob/wrapdrop/noflush/eqlast/uj). An online per-task matcher reports matched / out
of order / duplicate / foreign / missing, attributes missing bytes to recorded drops, and compares content at the handoff.
A pre-compare at the top of rs64_dpc_record_submit (before the bridge's edit walkers) splits late writes from our edits.
Controls: an init self-test on 8 crafted streams passes 8/8. The ctl arm mutates 1 task in 1000 in the matcher's input
(inside the first call of >= 64 B: drop 8 B, duplicate 8 B, swap two 8 B chunks, flip 1 snapshot byte). v1 mutated "call
#2-#5" and never fired, because a task makes ONE merged RT64 call (plus wrap flushes), so that run counts as a datum only.
Runs (scratch/s7096/run.zsh + arm c/d, L6, FPS60, owner-style route, flight 308-309 s each, 0 crash, 0 VI stall):
| arm | tasks | HW bytes = FWD bytes | missing / dup / order / foreign | drops recorded | content diff | ctl flagged |
| A dd1 4:3 | 21,776 | 2,824,708,824 | 0/0/0/0 | 0 | 0 | 21/21 (all 4 classes) |
| B dd4 16:9 | 22,124 | 15,068,792,088 | 0/0/0/0 | 0 | 417,532 | 22/22 bad, 20/22 all 4 |
| D dd4 16:9 | 21,805 | 16,604,129,200 | 0/0/0/0 | 0 | 399,098; pre-edit 0 over pre_bytes = 16,604,129,200 | 21/21 bad, 20/21 all 4 |
(C = D without pre_bytes, same picture: 9.64 GB, content 354,589, pre 0.) Site split at dd4: merged commit 2.5-2.7 GB, wrap
flush 7.1-12.4 GB, live 0, synth/forcefs 0 (no synthetic FULL_SYNCs in flight). Not one deliberate-drop path fired (pipe,

The two ctl tasks that missed "all 4" are ring-lap tasks. There the greedy forward search finds the mutated address in a
later lap, so the matcher classes a mutation as order/dup rather than missing. It is still flagged (tasks_bad), and in the

## Session 7098 (2026-11-10) — RT64 vs angrylion on the same dd4 stream: big presented terrain drops are already in the RDP stream (H-stream); they are an FPS60 near-wall flicker, not a draw-distance effect

Work unit from NEXT.md (slug rt64-vs-angrylion-stream). Owner recipe L6 dd4 16:9 FPS60, no logging env, scratch/s7098/arm.zsh (copy of s6895's).

Capture a6: one run, ROGUESQ_G5B_FRAME (RAM every 20 swaps) plus g5b_capture of the window (384x216, 11,473 frames, 158.8 s,
74 g5b_drops transients). The stream file reached its 22 GB cap 154 s into the 159 s presented window. The flight part
(mach <= 20949200000000, then mission over and menus) holds 316 swaps that carry their own RAM snapshot. a6.cap (23 GB) was
deleted after replay. The replayed frames stay in scratch/s7098/al and altr.

Tool defect found: frame_replay SIGSEGVs on these frames. ASan on a source build: global-buffer-overflow in fbfill_16, because the
g3_angrylion core is built with RDRAM_MAX_SIZE 0x800000 and rdp/rdram.c sizes static rdram_hidden[] from it. At dd4 16:9 the colour
image is at 0x98AA00 (796 wide), above 8 MB. New tools/angrylion_replay/build16.sh builds a patched 16 MB copy. Any earlier replay
of a dd>1 frame with an image above 8 MB was invalid. The s6895 frames worked, so their images were presumably below 8 MB.

Results:
1. Sampled frames (tools/s7098_rt64_vs_al.py): 48x27 block diff after lag calibration (15 ms). Median 0.043, MAD 0.009,
   threshold 0.099; 1/316 frames flagged (11902, 0.10). Positive control: a KILL_AREA=3000 replay of 16 of the swaps is flagged
   16/16 (smallest kill effect 0.09 -> 0.12 over threshold).
2. Every presented transient (tools/s7098_transients.py, 70 in flight): all swaps within 100 ms before each of x, a=x-1 and b=x+k
   were replayed (257 swaps), and the best-matching swap was scored. 53 are H-stream (some swap's hardware render matches x as well
   as it matches the neighbours), 7 are unmatched (neighbours above 0.10) and 10 were scored H-rt64. Those 10 are the large ones,
   T 0.12-0.71. By eye (scratch/s7098/rt64_a.png, rt64_b.png: a | x | b | angrylion(sx)), each angrylion render shows the same
   picture as the presented transient. The score gap is the HUD radar sitting further left in the replay; that HUD 16:9 anchor is
   applied in RT64, not in the stream. So all 10 are H-stream, and H-rt64 is refuted for every large drop in this run.
3. What the large drops are: in every one the near canyon wall that fills the view vanishes for 1-3 frames while the camera hugs or
   enters it, and sky and far terrain show through.
4. Arms, one run each, L6, tools/s7098_wall_flicker.py (events: T >= 0.12 after a wall-hug frame; episodes: events more than 1 s apart):
   | arm | setting | wall-hug s | events | episodes |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | a6 | dd4 FPS60 | 121 | 16 | 6 |
   | t6 | dd4 FPS60 CULL_SPIKE=tog | 131 | 26 | 4 (1 in cull-on seconds, 3 in cull-off) |
   | n6 | dd4 FPS60=0 | 130 | 0 | 0 |
   | d6 | dd1 FPS60 | 118 | 18 | 2 |
   t6 refutes the spike cull, since episodes occur in both parities. The d6 events are the same picture (scratch/s7098/d6_ev.png):
   the eye alternates between inside and outside the wall, and when it is inside the wall is not drawn. n6 still has 39 small
   transients, so the detector was running, but n6 is a cross-run arm with no same-run positive control. Its 0 is single-source.

Conclusion: RT64 renders the stream faithfully on every large drop in this capture. The drops visible at the owner recipe on L6 are
game-side. They follow FPS60 (the game ticks at 60 Hz with dt 1/60) and not dd: dd1 shows them too. This does not explain the owner's
report that dd1 is clean and dd2/dd4 drop. Either the owner's dd1 flight did not hug walls, or there is a second, dd-dependent class
this route did not show.
Rules out: H-rt64 (for the large drops), the spike cull as their source, and dd as the trigger of the near-wall class.
Left open: the camera term (H-osc spring/push-out tuned for dt 1/30, H-par parity-gated routine, H-ret retail also enters the wall).
Next: same-run split using ROGUESQ_G1E_LIMIT=1 ROGUESQ_G1E_WIN=600 with FPS60=0 (60 fps in alternate windows), plus a camera eye log.

## Session 7105 (2026-11-10) — FPS60 near-wall flicker: every near-eye terrain cell the stream keeps is emitted as an F5 TRI_GEN on every frame of all 4 episodes, with an unchanged LOD byte and command word (H-emit-skip and H-lodswap refuted, single run); the loss is in the RSP/ucode or the wall is not grid terrain
HYPOTHESIS-ID: fps60-wall-mesh-emit
Static read (s7105). buildGridCellMeshForFace 0x8004317C walks the distance list (a0 head, via node+4): per node a LOD tier from node+8 dist^2 vs the
table 0x8009DE94 (0x800431E0..0x80043294) gives the lod byte elem+0x10 (elem = *(node+0x14)+0x20; 0 = 25-height mode-0 mesh, 2 = flat 4-corner
path; far cells are lod 2), morph shorts elem+0x16..0x1E, then buildGridCellMesh 0x8004B930 and the elem+0/+4 chain link; the chain is cut at the
far cutoff 0x8009DEB4 and that element is returned (s5). A post pass 0x80043528..0x80043770 forces lod 1 on neighbours of lod-2 cells.
The emit is renderFlatMeshFaceGroup 0x8001108C: s0 = *(s1+0x20), loop L_800113F0..0x800119A4 (s0 = *(s0+0)); EVERY element writes one 0x28-byte
TRI_GEN (0x05) command: height path L_80011714 (w0 = 05 | size<<16 | (t0&F)<<12 | (+0x2E&1)<<8 | lod; w1..: the colour bytes, +0x24 height ptr,
+0x28 colour ptr) or the flat path (lod 2, inline corner heights). There is no per-cell cull in this CPU loop. renderUnlitMeshFaces 0x80011C9C is
the same walk but emits only elements with +0x2E bit 1 (it never fired in this run, uv=0).
New tools/apply_s7105_emit.py (fixup list after s7104, needs it): ROGUESQ_S7105_EMIT=1 + S7104_CELL=1 + the CHASE file write one `ce` line per
buildGridCellMeshForFace call: list length, renderer calls and visits, whole-list lod histogram, and per cell in the 7x7 around the eye: list dup
count, lod byte, on-the-s5-chain bit, emit visits, plus the emitted w0 of the 9 ring<=1 cells. Measurement only.
New tools/s7105_emit.py (push.txt drops.csv split.txt; episode alignment as s7104_cellcull.py).
Run (scratch/s7099/arm.zsh 6 4 s7105a, L6 dd4 16:9 FPS60, G1E_LIMIT=1 600-VI windows, CELL=1 EMIT=1): 0 crashes, 9247 gens, 4 episodes (lim1 2 /
3812 ticks, lim2 2 / 2291; fewer than s7104's 8). scratch/s7105/emit_a.txt, split_a.txt.
- Controls: the renderer runs 2 calls per gen, one starting at the s5 chain start, and visits exactly the list length in 9214/9247 gens (the 33 others
  are gens with no render call, rc=0). Lod histogram over the whole list 0: 51 k, 1: 9.5 M, 2: 23.2 M; lod 0 is 35% of ring-0 cells, 15% of ring-3
  cells and 0.15% of the list, so the tier test fires and grades by distance. The s5 chain bit is not the render path (the renderer walks the whole
  list, rv == nl), kept only as a side count.

  listed-not-emitted cells are the 33 no-render gens. Across each episode the near 3x3 lod bytes and the eye cell's w0 stay constant

## Session 7106 (2026-11-10) — FPS60 near-wall flicker: per-command RDP triangle census in the F5 ucode; the 9 near-eye cells' TRI_GENs keep producing screen-covering triangles through 8 of 10 episodes (H-clip refuted as the general cause, single run); the ucode DMEM parse matches the bridge triangle count on 8505/8505 swaps
HYPOTHESIS-ID: fps60-wall-rsp-clip
CURRENT-TRUTH 58119 B, under the Step 0 trigger, no maintenance. No new soak verdicts since s7103_camfix_r1/r2 (already folded).
Static read. The main gfx ucode appends RDP commands to a DMEM output buffer at 0xD60 with fill pointer r16; the flush routine L_112C
(r10 = r16 - 0xD60) DMAs [0xD60, r16) to the RDRAM FIFO, kicks DPC_END and resets r16 = 0xD60. The dispatch loop L_1090 fetches the
command words at DMEM r17. So the RDP bytes command k produces are DMEM [r16 at fetch k, r16 at fetch k+1), split by any flush between.
The overlay files build/factor5_ucode/*ovl*.c are not compiled (CMake builds only the main, _b and boot TUs; overlay code is spliced
into the main file), so one TU covers it.
New instrument (one build):
- src/rsp/s7106_rsptri.cpp (ROGUESQ_S7106_RSPTRI=<file>): rs64_s7106_fetch at every L_1090 fetch (placed before the s6896 TG edge fix,
  so p8/p9 are as the CPU wrote them) and rs64_s7106_flush at the L_112C flush entry parse [pos, r16) with the RDP length table and
  give the triangles to the command being processed. One `rt` line per swap: TRI_GEN count, their tris, all tris, bridge tris, per
  class (w0 mode/sub) cmds/tris/zero-tri/min/max/modal count, and per near cell (3x3 around the eye) seen/tris/zero/degenerate/bbox.
- tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py block "s7106 rsptri" (idempotent; tools/ucode_fixed patch refreshed with ucode_regen.sh snapshot,
  verify = 0 DIFF, census 0 unexplained).
- tools/apply_s7106_rsptri.py (fixup list after s7105): s7105_visit publishes w0 + words 8/9 (+0x20/+0x24) of the last TRI_GEN
  emitted for each ring<=1 cell into g_s7106_kw/k8/k9; a fetched TRI_GEN matching (w0, p8, p9) is attributed to that cell.
- dpc_bridge.cpp rs64_spike_scan calls rs64_s7106_btri per forwarded triangle: the independent per-swap count (tbr).
- tools/s7106_rsptri.py (rt.txt drops.csv split.txt; episode alignment as s7105_emit.py).
Run: scratch/s7099/arm.zsh 6 4 s7106a (L6 dd4 16:9 FPS60, G1E_LIMIT=1 600-VI windows, CELL=1 EMIT=1 RSPTRI), 0 CRASH lines, capture
15563 frames 61.5/s, 10 episodes (lim1 6, lim2 4). scratch/s7106/rt_a.txt, rsptri_a.txt, split_a.txt.
Controls (positive, same run):
- Mark everything: over 8505 TRI_GEN swaps the DMEM parse total equals the bridge's forwarded-triangle total on every swap (41,324,051
  both, |diff| p90 0), 0 parse overruns. So the attribution sees every RDP triangle exactly once. TRI_GENs carry 90.3% of all tris.
- Key match: 9 (6917 swaps) or 8 (723) of the 9 near keys published; each matched cell is seen about once per swap (seen=1), so the
  keys are unique per cell. Classes: mode0 sub1 (the 05050001 cells, 3x3 grid) modal 8 tris when unclipped, max 15; mode 2 quads 2,
  max 5; zero-tri commands 45-66% (off-screen cells rejected), so the counter moves both ways.
Result. Eye cell (slot 4): flight 2.41 tris/cmd with 62% zero-tri commands (the camera is high, the ground under it out of view);
episode 4.31 tris/cmd with 8% zero. At the swap nearest each event the eye cell emits 2-8 tris whose bbox covers most of the screen
(e.g. -199..995 x -112..559 px) in 8 of 10 episodes, with no change across the event (t=124.3: 2 tris every swap, t=131.1: 2-4). The
other two: t=211.2 (eye cell is a lod-0 05050000 cell giving 0-1 tris on all 12 swaps, before and after the event, slot 7 gives 4-5)

## Session 7108 (2026-11-10) — FPS60 near-wall flicker: the push-out corner width does not cause the eye-cell near clip (CAMWIDE=tog no change), and the clip happens at the 30 fps rate too (H-aspect, H-neardist, H-tick refuted)

Ran: one L6 dd4 16:9 owner-recipe run (scratch/s7099/arm.zsh 6 4 s7108a, ROGUESQ_G1E_WIN=600 G3C_LOG=1, S7101_CHASE, S7104_CELL,

Code-read of applyPlayerVehicleStateUpdate 0x8004CD00 (constants read from the ROM at 0x8003A8D0-0x8003A8F0): the corner vector is
x = w*0.5*240/h, y = 120, z = 120/tan((fovy+2)/2 deg), scaled by f20 = 2*near. The camera struct s2 = 0x80138D18 + i*0x144 is the
setupCameraMatrices camera (cam = s2+8), so s2+0x18/0x1C are the viewport w/h that s6112 VPW widens (w 796 at 16:9), s2+0x28 the
fovy and s2+0x2C the near. setupCameraMatrices gives guPerspective aspect = (w/h) * (vs_w / vi_w) * f(0x8011A840) * ASPECT_SCALE.
New tools/apply_s7108_camwide.py (fixup list after s7107): records the final guPerspective fovy/aspect/near per camera struct and
prints them beside the corner half-tans once per 600 push-out calls ([s7108] lines); ROGUESQ_S7108_CAMWIDE=1|tog scales the corner x
by max(1, k) so the corners cover the projection with the retail 2-degree margin (tog: odd absolute mach seconds). Default off.
New tools/s7108_split.py (presented episodes + losscan rows split by tog state, --shift control).
Numbers (10 [s7108] lines, constant): w 796 h 448, fov 65 = pfov 65, near 30 = pnear 30, corner horizontal half-tan hx 1.176 vs
projection px 1.368, vertical 0.662 vs 0.637, k 1.208. The 1.208 is the pixel-aspect term (2.1469 / (796/448)); with w 512 the
same ratio holds at 4:3, so the narrow corners are retail, not a 16:9 artefact. Near distances agree, so H-neardist is refuted.
Split (scratch/s7108/split_a.txt, losscan_a.txt): eye-cell near-z stream losses (ref painter c+0+0, drop minz < 0x100) 27 with

remove the clip, so H-aspect is refuted as the cause (single run). Positive control: losscan flagged 328 swaps with >= 300 lost cells,

FPS60=0, ROGUESQ_G5B_FRAME_EVERY=1 FROM=5000 MAX_MB=12000 (env order: the extra env follows EVERY=20 in XENV_EXTRA, later wins; confirmed by 741/741
swaps carrying RAM). Stream swaps 5000..5740 (24.7 s of flight, 12.0 GB, deleted after replay), window capture 10942 frames 320x240. 0 crash.
Tool bug found by reading frame_replay.c before replaying: rs64_g5b_frame writes 'SWAP' then that swap's 'RAM ' then 'RNG ' records. frame_replay
started the frame on the SWAP tag from the snapshot it already held (the previous one, EVERY swaps old) and the following RAM tag hit the
"keep frame's own view" branch, so a swap's own snapshot was NEVER used; at EVERY=1 the first swap errored "no snapshot before". Fixed: a frame
that has run no range takes its own snapshot (LEGACY_SNAP=1 restores the old behaviour); new SNAP_FROM=<swap> forces one older snapshot for every
replayed swap (the H-tool control). Rebuilt scratch/s7124/al16/frame_replay16 with tools/angrylion_replay/build16.sh. New tools/s7124_capidx.py
indexes a stream (swap mach hasram nranges bytes).

   (3rd rotation column, M+0x8/+0x14/+0x20). So the gate is "pitch > 60 deg: skip the clear". There is no on-screen test in NDC, so
   NEXT's H-vis43 had the wrong mechanism. Other rodata: 0x8003AE38 = pi/360 (fov deg -> half rad), fov at cam 0x80138D20+0x20 = 65.

## Session 7142 (2026-11-11) — G3 hangar RT64 vs angrylion at 21:9 and 16:9: RT64 drew 2D texrects 1.33x wide (aspectRatioScale on Rectangle draws), fixed default-on (ROGUESQ_RECT_ASPECT=0 restores)
HYPOTHESIS-ID: g3-fidelity-hangar-219
Work unit from NEXT.md (H-equal / H-wide-menu / H-hangar-cam). New tools/s7142_arm.zsh: s6995 first-entry hangar route (owner save
read-only, NO_SAVE_WRITE, no SAVE_FROM), owner recipe FPS60 dd4 + ROGUESQ_ASPECT=21:9|16:9, G5B_FRAME EVERY=3 from swap FROM, MAX_MB 12000,
g5b_capture 504x216 alongside; scored with tools/s7141_post.zsh (unchanged). Painted-square control PASS on all 5 replays; 0 crash all runs.
H1 (FROM=1900): the first ~300 swaps paired with frames from before the window recorder started (DL=38 s): harness artefact, so FROM=2250 afterwards.
Steady hangar: centre frac>40 median 0.08 vs side 0.007. Sheet + zoom: angrylion text is ~1.3x narrower than RT64's at the same height; 3D ship
matches; rect registration sweep gains nothing (best 7.35 vs 7.38). G5B recorder runs after every bridge walker (s7125), so the bytes are equal:
cause is inside RT64.
ORIGIN: RT64 framebuffer_renderer: aspectRatioScale = target/source when the fb-pair scissor ratio is within 10% of the VI fb ratio. The port
hands RT64 a Manual target (21:9 -> "1024:448" = 2.286; 16:9 -> 16:9) while the game itself renders the wide fb (VI fbSize 1024x336 = 3.048 /
796x336). Rectangle and fill draws then get invRatioScale = 3.048/2.286 = 1.333 about fbWidth/2; LLE triangles take the RawTriangles path, which
never applies it. So text/2D was 1.33x wider than the stream asked and inconsistent with the 3D. Not a guest value: legitimately-designed RT64
behaviour for HLE games that render 4:3 and get expanded, wrong for this LLE wide-fb port. In flight the scissor ratio differs, so flight was unaffected (s7141 H-equal).
Fix: lib/rt64 rt64_framebuffer_renderer.cpp aspectRatioScale = 1 unless ROGUESQ_RECT_ASPECT=0 (exported to submodule-patches/rt64.patch).

## Session 7179 (2026-11-11) — UNBLOCK: "2 iterations ended WORKING" was the runner watchdog killing live sessions (fixed, reproduced)
Block (iterations 66+67, 18:14-18:33): STATUS stayed WORKING, no commit, empty runner output, BLOCKED.md guessed "unit too
large / out of turns". Route taken: refute and fix locally (route 1 -> 2). Not a turn or size problem.
- Evidence (session transcript c3eaf533, iteration 67): 02:24:20Z the agent ran `echo WORKING > scratch/agent/STATUS`, launched
  `s7141_arm.zsh 17 L17r ... 60`, then sat in a blocking 575 s wait loop. runner.sh's hung-claude watchdog (2026-10-17) fires when
  STATUS is newer than ITER_START_MARK and has not changed for DONE_GRACE=480 s. It checked mtime, not content, so WORKING counted
  as "finished". claude was killed at 02:32:32Z (= 02:24:20 + 480 + one 15 s poll; tool result "Exit code 137"), so there was no
  JSON and rc=0. Both contract retries were then killed on their first 15 s poll because STATUS was already >480 s stale. That is
  why the whole iteration was 9m17s with 3 empty outputs. Iteration 66 matched it (9m17s, same shape).
- Second trap: `scratch/s7141/sum_L*r.txt` is 0 bytes on EVERY level (L10-L17), so a wait on `[ -s sum_*.txt ]` never succeeds and
  always runs to its cap. Wait on `! pgrep -f s7141_arm.zsh` plus a non-empty arm_*.out instead.
- Fix: tools/agent/runner.sh watchdog also requires STATUS content to be DONE or BLOCKED. Sandbox test with a fake `claude` (sleep
  50 s, DONE_GRACE=10). Old runner + WORKING: killed at 21 s ("watchdog ... hung=1"), so the mechanism is reproduced. New runner +
  WORKING: runs the full 50 s and returns its JSON. New runner + DONE: still killed at 20 s (positive control, so the hang guard is
  kept). Nothing was disabled. The RUNNER_MAX_SECS 3600 cap is unchanged.
- The L17 retail capture from iteration 67 completed and is still on disk: scratch/s7141/L17r.cap (12.6 GB) + L17r.raw (2.5 GB),
  cap_L17r.txt window (225,46,1062,828) frames 10970 fails 0. It was never post-processed. NEXT.md resumes from it.

shift, AL-lit pixels 248 -> 235 instead of 218. Forward binning by AL luma also has a regression-to-mean bias (reverse binning shows
AL darker in RT64's top bin).
Step 3, one run F1 = s7181 M1 route (tools/s7146_arm.zsh RDIR=s7182 ASP=4:3 FROM=0 EVERY=5 SECS=70 DL=5 DU=60, FPS60=0 dd1) with the

wall control +0.6, best shift (0,0); p99 RT64 249 vs AL 243 (brighter); lit>192 px -21%.

RGB 253/253/188 vs 248/248/189 (hardware RGBA5551 ceiling 248 vs RT64 8-bit); edge pixels -26.9/-33.5; 83%/85% of loss pixels lie on an
AL luma step. (2) Loss map docs/owner_sheet_s7182_ring_edges.png (AL | RT64 | red = AL brighter by >40): red only on segment outlines and
seams, interiors grey. Angrylion's edges are hard staircases fully lit up to the boundary; RT64 at high internal resolution draws the

high-res edge rendering is the expected look. No fix. s7155's 16:9 "animated holo" residual is this edge class too (not re-measured).
Lesson for scorers: check the rect against raw height (242 > 240 raw rows) and prefer full-res captures for thin geometry.
