## Session 7191 (2026-11-12) — M6 boot freeze: static census of video-ack queue 0x80128CF0 / vflag 0x80037808 (every live receiver clean, mode-2 flag leak is dead code); passive per-thread wait table + CF0 event ring land in [stall-dump], positive control PASS
HYPOTHESIS-ID: m6-boot-freeze-loop
Soak fold: s7190_bootloop_b and _c ran 14 boots each, all `crash=0 OK` (fs 1949-2078, origin 0xA12B00/0xA7CF00). Their rc=2 is a
recipe defect, not a freeze: the loop runs recipes under bash and line 11 used a zsh glob qualifier `(N)` (syntax error after
the hunter returned 0). Fixed in the still-queued _d (bash shebang, plain ls). Running total in the s6993 owner env: 41 boots
clean (13 s7190 + 28), 0 freezes.
Static census (offline, recompiled C + MIPS comments in ../N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs funcs_4/funcs_5):
- One sender: viRetraceHandlerThread 0x80019B50, `if (lbu 0x80037808) osSendMesg(CF0, 0, BLOCK)`, after the 0x80128D10 unlock
  (0x80019B30, NOBLOCK). CF0 is created with msgCount 1 (0x8001xxxx osCreateMesgQueue(CF0, 0x80128D08, 1), funcs_4:39634).
- Four receive sites, all `vflag=1 (delay slot); osRecvMesg(CF0, BLOCK); vflag=0; osYieldThread`: waitOnVideoQueue (BE9C/BEAC),
  acquireFreeBufferSlot (C0E8/C0F8), waitForPostSwapAck (C2B0 + clear), bufferArbiterAllocSlot mode 0 (BFF4/C004).
  bufferArbiterAllocSlot mode 2 (C018-C054) DOES leave vflag=1 when it returns after a recv (no clear on the found-slot exit),
  but every caller passes 0 or 1 (submitGfxFrame 1, initVideoSubsystem 0, postSwapRdpReset 1), so that window is dead code.
- Callers: waitOnVideoQueue <- advanceVideoFrame x2, bufferArbiterProducerScanWait, initVideoSubsystem, selectAndApplyViMode;
  waitForPostSwapAck <- waitForPrevFrameDone; acquireFreeBufferSlot <- ensureHeapInitialized. vflag is ONE shared byte for
  receivers on at least two guest threads.
- Runtime: ultramodern do_send/do_recv are libultra-faithful (a recv pops one blocked sender, a send pops one blocked receiver).
  osYieldThread_recomp is a host std::this_thread::yield() (upstream_compat.cpp:738) and never yields to another guest thread.
- Re-read of the original frozen log (scratch/s6993s/log_L4.txt.zst, both dumps VI 896/1496): CF0 mtq=0 fullq=8011CD28
  valid=1 count=1, vflag=0; D10 and VI queue 0x80114388 valid=1 no waiter; slot states 5,4.
Derivation: the dump state (retrace on the full-send list, no receiver, flag 0) needs a CF0 receiver that took a message and
then lost the CPU for >=2 VIs inside osRecvMesg (check_running_queue after do_recv) before its guest `vflag=0`. Retrace posts a
stale message on VI n and blocks on VI n+1. On its own that state heals: any later CF0 recv pops retrace. So the freeze
also needs that receiver to then block somewhere OTHER than CF0. Static code cannot name that second wait, which leaves
H-consumer as the leading form (single-source: static read + one frozen dump).
Instrument (built, default on, ROGUESQ_WAITTAB=0 off; src/main/upstream_compat.cpp Rs64WaitScope in osSendMesg_recomp /
osRecvMesg_recomp, printed from the rt64_render_context.cpp [stall-dump] via rs64_waittab_dump):
`[stall-wait]` = per guest thread id, its current (IN) or last blocking send/recv: mq + recompiled caller (dladdr of the host
return address; ctx->r31 is 0 in recompiled calls, so a first build printed ra=0 and was replaced). `[stall-cf0]` = the last 48
CF0 send/recv enter (S/R) and return (s/r) events with tid, caller, validCount, vflag, fullq, mtq, age in ms.
tools/boot_freeze_hunt.sh echoes both on FROZEN.
Positive control (scratch/s7191/ctl2.log, retail boot, ROGUESQ_STALL_DUMP_TEST=300): rows for tids 0-4 (tid 0
viRetraceHandlerThread last R 0x80128D10, tid 3 IN submitGfxFrame+0x1dc on 0x8011A818, tids 1/2/4 recvServiceMessage),
and 48 CF0 events in the healthy pattern (tid 0 S/s at viRetraceHandlerThread+0x205c every 16.7 ms with vflag=1, tid 3
waitForPostSwapAck R/r). In healthy boot frames the receiver is the gfx thread (tid 3) only.
VERDICT: refutes H-lost-post in its game-code form. No live receive path leaves vflag set without a waiter: mode 2 is dead,
the other four sites are balanced. Selects "delayed-clear receiver + second wait elsewhere" (H-consumer) as the only static
route to the dumped state (single-source). The next freeze names that receiver and its second wait from [stall-wait] /
[stall-cf0] in any run, soak or owner, without needing the sampler.
ORIGIN: no mitigation; instrument only.
Rules out: the bufferArbiterAllocSlot mode-2 vflag leak (dead code); a dump byte-order misread of vflag (dump uses ^3,
verified in source).

## Session 7192 (2026-11-12) — M6 boot freeze forced-state arm: ROGUESQ_CF0_DELAY_TEST reproduces the s6993 pre-state on demand (retrace blocked on full CF0, vflag 1) and it heals 10/10 -> H-stale-heals; the freeze needs a second wait
- **Fold:** s7190_bootloop_d rc=0, 14/14 owner-env (HUNT_OWNER) boots OK, 0 FROZEN. Owner-env total now 55 clean (0 freezes).
- **Instrument (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp, Rs64Cf0Delay, default off):** `ROGUESQ_CF0_DELAY_TEST=<k>[:<ms>]`. On the k-th
  blocking recv on CF0 (0x80128CF0) that returns a message, as the last thing before guest code runs again (an RAII object
  declared first in osRecvMesg_recomp, so before the receiver's vflag clear), it blocks that guest thread cooperatively on a
  private queue fed by osSetTimer. Prints `[cf0-delay] begin/end` (waited ms, CF0 events during the hold, valid, vflag,
  fullq) plus the full [stall-wait]/[stall-cf0] tables.
- **v1 was an instrument artifact (scratch/s7192_v1artifact):** scratch at 0x9FF00000 is above rs64_ram_top, so
  mesgqueue_guard refused the queue (`[mesgqueue-guard] osCreateMesgQueue refused mq_=0x9FF00000`), the recv returned in 0.0 ms,
  and every delay boot froze at fs~600, 10/10 (ctl 5/5 clean). Those dumps show retrace waiting on the VI queue 80114388, not on
  CF0: a different state. The likely mechanism is the timer's message to a refused queue being requeued forever by
  dequeue_external_messages (do_send returns false on a refused mq). This is a latent runtime hazard, but no game path is
  known to post to an out-of-range mq. Not fixed, noted. v2 puts the scratch 0x200 below the receiver's guest sp.
- **v2 arms, one build, owner env (HUNT_OWNER=1), 5 boots x 34 s each (scratch/s7192/arms.zsh, arms.out):** k=600:40 5/5 OK
  fs~1948; k=600:100 5/5 OK fs~1947; control k=0 5/5 OK fs~1951. 0 crash, 0 FROZEN.
- **Positive control PASS (full-log boots, scratch/s7192/full_d40.log, full_d100.log):** receiver tid 3
  (waitForPostSwapAck+0x2ec) held 44.2 ms and 103.5 ms. During the hold, retrace (tid 0, viRetraceHandlerThread+0x205c) posted
  CF0 (valid 0->1), then posted again with valid=1 and blocked: at end `valid=1 vflag=1 fullq=8011CD28`. That is exactly the
  s6993 dump's queue state (retrace on CF0's full-send list). Both boots then ran on to fs~1691 at 30 s.
- **Result: H-stale-heals.** The s6993 pre-state forms readily under a delayed receiver and heals as soon as the receiver
  returns to CF0. So the frozen state (vflag 0, retrace on fullq, no receiver) needs the receiver to block on a second queue
  whose producer depends on the retrace thread, which is a dependency cycle. Refuted: H-stale-freezes (a delay alone does not
  freeze, 10/10 heal at 40 and 100 ms). H-no-form is also refuted (the state forms on demand).
- **Next lead (single-source, from the v1 artifact dumps):** tid 3's other blocking wait is submitGfxFrame+0xc70 on 8011A7E8
  (the gfx task-done queue). If the RDP/SP done message for that queue is gated on VI/present pacing (VI_LOCK=1 is in the owner
  env) or on the retrace thread, then delay + retrace blocked on CF0 closes a cycle. NEXT.md: list the producers of every queue
  tid 3 blocks on and check each for a retrace/VI dependency; then one forced arm that holds the 8011A7E8 delivery while
  retrace sits on CF0's fullq.

## Session 7193 (2026-11-12) — M6 boot freeze retrace-dependency census: 120 forced retrace holds over the boot window always park tid 3 back on CF0 (waitForPostSwapAck), never on a second retrace-fed queue -> H-cycle-7e8 refuted; remaining lead is the host scheduler (yield) losing tid 3
HYPOTHESIS-ID: m6-boot-freeze-loop
- **Static (step 1 of NEXT.md), read from RecompiledFuncs:**
  - 0x8011A7E8 (gfx DP-done) has ONE producer: dpInterruptHandlerThread (0x8001C328) recvs the host OS_EVENT_DP queue 0x8011A408 and
    sends NOBLOCK to 7E8 only if gate byte 0x8011A89D != 0. Host DP event = events.cpp dp_complete(), raised right after
    renderer_context->send_dl returns on the gfx thread. send_dl can stall only on RT64's 4-slot workload ring, whose thread waits
    for presents ALREADY issued (workload.presentId), so the host DP path does not need the guest retrace thread.
  - Gate 0x8011A89D is set by submitGfxFrame (0x8000C254, before its NOBLOCK task send to scheduler 0x8011A420, cap 8) and by
    postSwapRdpReset (0x8001C218), cleared by advanceVideoFrame (0x80017EAC, unconditional) and by the two flag-checked 7E8 waiters
    (bufferArbiterProducerScanWait 0x8000BFD4, 0x80018244). submitGfxFrame's sync recv (s1!=0, 0x8000C2B8/0x8000C4A8) is unconditional.
  - viRetraceHandlerThread per VI: osViSwapBuffer -> postSwapRdpReset (if 0x8011A8C8: clears it, sets 89D, submits RDP task NOBLOCK
    to 0x8011A420) -> NOBLOCK send 0x80128D10 -> if vflag: BLOCKING send CF0.
  - waitForPostSwapAck (0x8001C260): if C9 && C8: loop { vflag=1; recv CF0; vflag=0; osYieldThread } while C8; C9=0. C8 is cleared
    by the RETRACE thread's postSwapRdpReset, which runs before its CF0 post on the same VI. So a receiver delayed >=2 VIs between recv
    and vflag clear leaves the loop with retrace parked on CF0's full-send list and vflag 0: the s6993 state is the ordinary
    exit of this loop, which matches s7192 (it heals once tid 3 next comes back to CF0).
- **Instrument (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp Rs64RetraceHold, default off):** `ROGUESQ_RETRACE_HOLD_TEST=<start>:<period>:<ms>:<count>`
  holds tid 0 (retrace) BEFORE its per-VI NOBLOCK send to 0x80128D10 (fires every VI regardless of vflag, so the hold lands at an
  arbitrary point of tid 3's frame), cooperatively on a private timer queue 0x200 below its sp, then prints [rt-hold] (CF0 valid,
  fullq, mtq, vflag, C8, C9, 89D) and [rt-hold-w] for every guest thread (IN/last, mq, recompiled caller, blocking calls during hold).
- **Run (scratch/s7193/arms.zsh, hold1-3.log):** owner env (s6993 recipe), 3 boots x 36 s, HOLD=120:37:60:40 (VI 120..1563, period
  prime vs the 2-VI frame; covers the s6993 freeze point fs~273). 120/120 holds fired (waited ~60 ms), 0 crash, 0 stall, fs~1877.
- **Result:** at all 120 hold ends: tid 3 IN R CF0 caller waitForPostSwapAck, calls_during 0, cf0 valid 0, mtq=tid 3, vflag 1, C8 0,
  C9 1, 89D 1. tid 1/2/5 IN recvServiceMessage (801548C0/80154CF0/802CCA30), tid 4 recvServiceMessage 8018FAC0 (IN 15, last 105).
  Positive control: the instrument fires every hold and shows threads blocked on retrace-fed waits (tid 3 IN CF0 at each).
  Whatever the phase, a retrace-absent tid 3 runs its frame to completion and parks on CF0, which heals the moment retrace posts.
  **H-cycle-7e8 refuted** (tid 3 was never IN 8011A7E8 or any non-CF0 queue at a hold end; 7E8's producer chain has no retrace
  edge, static). H-other-wait refuted for the boot window sampled. Caveat: 40 phases/boot x 3 boots, not exhaustive.
- **H-host-yield refuted statically, same session:** the yield after the vflag clear is osYieldThread_recomp
  (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp:738) = host std::this_thread::yield(), with no guest-scheduler state, so it cannot lose tid 3.
- **State of the thread:** both guest-side explanations are now refuted (s7191 receivers balanced, s7192 pre-state heals, s7193 no
  second retrace-fed wait at any sampled phase), and so is the yield. The second wait is unknown and is NOT reproducible by forcing.
  Go passive: [stall-wait]/[stall-cf0] plus the host `sample` ride along in every run and name it on the next recurrence (0/73 since s7190).
  Pivot (NEXT.md) to the one concrete runtime defect this thread found: s7192's latent hazard, where an external message to a
  queue that mesgqueue_guard refused is requeued forever by dequeue_external_messages. It froze 10/10 boots under the v1 artifact.
ORIGIN: no mitigation; instrument only.
Discrimination summary (s7193): the 120-hold census refutes H-cycle-7e8 and H-other-wait for the sampled boot window (tid 3 ends IN CF0
at every hold end, never on 8011A7E8 or another retrace-fed queue). The osYieldThread_recomp source refutes H-host-yield (it is a
host-only yield). Next discriminator, passive: on the next real freeze the [stall-wait] row for tid 3 (IN <mq> vs last) selects
between a guest wait and a host-side loss. Active next unit (NEXT.md): the refused-mq requeue A/B, where arm a (old requeue, must
freeze) vs arm b (drop, must heal) on the v1 recipe selects H-requeue-freeze or H-other.

## Session 7194 (2026-11-12) — refused-mq requeue fix: external messages to a mesgqueue_guard-refused queue are now dropped (logged once per mq) instead of requeued forever; v1 positive control freezes 5/5 with the old path and heals 5/5 with the fix, owner-env control 5/5 clean
- **Change (lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/mesgqueue.cpp, patch exported):** new `external_requeue_ok()` guards all three
  requeue sites (dequeue_external_messages, wait_for_external_message, wait_for_external_message_timed). If the target mq, or its
  msg buffer, is outside 0x80000000..rs64_ram_top, do_send can never succeed, so the message is dropped and logged
  `[mesgqueue-guard] dropped undeliverable external msg mq=.. msg=.. src=.. dropped_total=..` (once per mq, up to 64 mqs).
  A genuinely full in-range queue still requeues as before. `ROGUESQ_REFUSED_REQUEUE=1` restores the old requeue-forever path (A/B arm).
- **Test hook (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp Rs64Cf0Delay):** `ROGUESQ_CF0_DELAY_TEST=<k>:<ms>:v1` puts the delay scratch back at
  0x9FF00000 (the s7192 v1 artifact) as a test that can reproduce the refused-mq case on demand.
- **Arms, one build, owner env (HUNT_OWNER=1), 5 boots x 34 s (scratch/s7194/arms.zsh, arms.out):**
  a) v1 + REFUSED_REQUEUE=1: **5/5 FROZEN** at fs 614-651 (positive control, matches s7192 v1 10/10);
  b) v1 + fix: **5/5 OK** fs 1950-2078; c) k=0 + fix: **5/5 OK** fs 1950-2079.
  Full-log boot of arm b (scratch/s7194/full_b.log): `osCreateMesgQueue refused mq_=0x9FF00000`, `[cf0-delay] begin k=600`,
  `end waited_ms=0.0`, then `dropped undeliverable external msg mq=0x9FF00000 msg=0x00007192 src=0 dropped_total=1`, fs=1949.
  So the v1 path really ran in the fixed arm, and the drop is what let it heal (two lines: arm split + the drop line in the same boot).
- **Selects H-requeue-freeze:** the v1 freeze was the timer message to the refused queue cycling through the external queue forever.
  H-other refuted for v1 (with only the requeue changed, the same delay heals). Fix lands default-on.
- **Scope note:** this does NOT explain the rare real s6993 boot freeze (no refused-mq line in that dump; its CF0 is in range).
  That thread stays passive ([stall-wait]/[stall-cf0] on recurrence).
ORIGIN: the writer is the runtime's own timer/event path: osSetTimer posts via enqueue_external_message_src (src 0 = timer, requeue on)
to an mq that mesgqueue_guard rejected. The value is legitimate (a real timer message); the queue is not deliverable, so dropping is
the correct behaviour, not a mitigation of a corrupted value. The game itself never targets a refused mq in 15 logged boots here.
Discrimination summary: arm a (old requeue) 5/5 FROZEN vs arm b (drop) 5/5 OK on the identical v1 recipe selects H-requeue-freeze;
control c 5/5 OK shows the fix is harmless on the normal path. Next (NEXT.md): class audit of every mesgqueue_guard refusal return
path for other retry-forever / spin shapes (guard-refusal livelock class).

## Session 7195 (2026-11-12) — guard-refusal livelock class closed: a BLOCK osRecvMesg on a refused mq returned -1 at once and the guest receive loop spun without yielding, freezing every other guest thread; it now parks the thread (old path 3/3 FROZEN, fix 3/3 OK, control 3/3 OK)

Work unit: CURRENT-TRUTH item 1 / NEXT.md (HYPOTHESIS-ID guard-refusal-livelock-class), H-one (s7194 was the only
livelock) vs H-more.

Static table, every refusal return in lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src (grep `refuse` / `rs64_ram_top`: mesgqueue.cpp
is the only file with refusal returns; events.cpp / timer.cpp / extensions.cpp post through enqueue_external_message_src):
| site | what the caller sees | verdict |
| osCreateMesgQueue | returns, mq untouched; every later op on it is refused too | SAFE |
| osSendMesg / osJamMesg (any flag) | -1. BLOCK callers ignore it and move on; NOBLOCK = retail "full" semantics | SAFE |
| do_send / do_send:msg | false -> osSendMesg -1, or external drain (dropped since s7194) | SAFE (s7194) |
| events (VI/SP/DP/AI/SI) + osSetTimer to a refused mq | one external msg per event, refused by do_send, dropped not requeued | SAFE, bounded (s7194) |
| wait_for_external_message(_timed) | same drop path | SAFE (s7194) |
| vi-deq | logging only | SAFE |
| do_recv (mq) | osRecvMesg checks the same bound first | DEAD |
| osRecvMesg NOBLOCK | -1 = retail "empty" semantics | SAFE |
| **osRecvMesg BLOCK** | -1 at once, no yield, no external drain; `for(;;) osRecvMesg(BLOCK)` re-enters forever | **LIVELOCK** |
| **do_recv:msg, msg_!=NULL, BLOCK** | false without consuming, validCount stays >0, so the next BLOCK recv returns at once | **LIVELOCK (same shape)** |
| do_recv:msg, msg_==NULL | consumes the slot without reading the buffer | SAFE |

Fix (mesgqueue.cpp, default on): both LIVELOCK rows call s7195_refused_block_recv, which parks the thread the way
osStopThread(self) does (run_next_thread_and_wait in a loop, logged `[mesgqueue-guard] ... parking thread`, first 8).
A queue that can never deliver blocks forever, which is the only OS-legal meaning of BLOCK. ROGUESQ_REFUSED_RECV_SPIN=1 =
old path. Forced arm ROGUESQ_REFUSED_RECV_TEST=<mqhex>:<nth>: from the nth BLOCK recv on <mq>, that mq is seen as refused
(0x7FF00000); a reporter prints `[s7195-rr] t= spin= park= recv_other=` at 1/3/6/10/15 s.

Two-arm qualification, one build, scratch/s7195/arms.zsh (boot_freeze_hunt owner env, 34 s, target 0x8018FAC0 = tid 4's
recvServiceMessage queue, which blocks once per boot in normal play, s7191 ctl):
- a_oldspin (TEST + SPIN=1): **3/3 FROZEN** at fs=41; [stall-wait] tid=4 blocking_calls 167748-174788; reporter
  spin=489764-511446 by 15 s with recv_other=0 (no other guest thread received one message: total starvation).
- b_park (TEST): **3/3 OK** (fs 1950-2079, same as control). Full-log boot scratch/s7195/b_full.log: TEST armed, park=1,
  spin=0, recv_other 1362 -> 31242 by 15 s (other threads keep running).
- c_ctl: 3/3 OK, no s7195 lines.
The do_recv:msg row has no forced arm (forcing it means corrupting a live mq's msg field); it uses the same helper.

ORIGIN: no writer. A refusal has never fired outside a forced arm: 49 soak_results logs + every scratch/s7*/ log hold one
osCreateMesgQueue refusal and one s7194 drop, both from the s7194 forced run. So this is a correctness fix of our own
guard's semantics (it turned a corrupt pointer into a whole-game spin), not a mitigation of an observed corruption, and it
does not explain the 1-in-65 boot freeze (whose dumps show tid 3 parked on a real queue, not a spinner).

This refutes H-one and selects H-more: a second livelock existed (old 3/3 FROZEN vs fix 3/3 OK, same build). It closes the guard-refusal class: every refusal row is SAFE, DEAD or fixed.
Next: guest-side NOBLOCK busy-poll audit (NEXT.md): retry loops that on real hardware are rescued by preemption but on
this cooperative scheduler never let the producer run.

## Session 7196 (2026-11-12) — cooperative-scheduler busy-poll class closed: no guest-produced NOBLOCK poll exists; one runtime hazard fixed (a PI DMA to an unknown region never posted its completion: forced arm old 3/3 FROZEN, fix 3/3 OK, control 3/3 OK)
HYPOTHESIS-ID: coop-sched-busy-poll-class (closed)
What ran (offline census first, then a two-arm qualification). Full table in docs/COOP-SCHED-POLL-CENSUS.md.
- scratch/s7196/census.py: 99 os{Recv,Send,Jam}Mesg sites in RecompiledFuncs.
  - Only 3 NOBLOCK receives: peek/tryRecvServiceMessage and serviceStreamingVoice. Each is a single poll inside a
    loop that makes progress. mainEventQueueWorker goes back to a BLOCK recv when idle.
  - No NOBLOCK send is retried until it succeeds.
- osYieldThread_recomp is a host std::this_thread::yield(): it never switches guest thread and never drains external
  messages. 29 yield sites were classified:
  - Most are `recv BLOCK; yield`, which is SAFE.
  - Two real spins:
    - waitForSerialIdle waits on 0x80110741, which siServiceThread (pri 0x76) owns.
    - submitDmaSlot / waitDmaSlotComplete / pollDmaSlotStep spin while dispatchPendingPiDmaToWorker()==1. With busy
      0x801126B8 set, that dispatch returns 1 without any OS call. The producer is piDmaWorker (pri 0x78).
  - Both producers have higher priority than the spinner. Neither blocks inside its flag window, because do_dma and
    osContStartReadData enqueue their completions synchronously.
  - Priorities were read statically from the osCreateThread / registerServiceWorker arguments.
- Hazard found: librecomp pi.cpp do_dma's "read from / write to unknown region" paths only printed [WARN] and posted
  NO completion. Hardware still raises the PI interrupt.
  - ORIGIN: the writer is our runtime (do_dma skipped the enqueue). This is not guest data, and the value is
    illegitimate (hardware always completes).
  - Fix, default on: post the completion. ROGUESQ_PI_UNK_COMPLETE=0 restores the old drop.
  - Forced arm ROGUESQ_PI_UNK_TEST=N: the Nth ROM read still copies, but its completion goes through that path.
Arms (scratch/s7196/arms.zsh, boot_freeze_hunt owner env, 3 boots each, 34 s):
- a_old (TEST=400, COMPLETE=0): **3/3 FROZEN at fs=444**. [stall-wait] tid=1 IN recv mq=80111290 caller=piDmaWorker+0x844,
  and the forced hit was logged on that same mq. This is the positive control: a lost PI completion freezes the game.
- b_fix (TEST=400): 3/3 OK (fs 1951-2078). The hunter keeps only log tails, so a separate full-log boot was run. It shows
  `[s7196-pi-unk] TEST rom-read ... mq=0x80111290 complete=1` and reaches fs=1694.
- c_ctl (TEST=0): 3/3 OK.
Rules out: H-poll (no guest busy-poll can starve its producer, given the priority table). The lost-PI-completion path
was never seen outside the forced arm, so it does not explain the 1-in-65 boot freeze, which stays passive.
lib/ edited, so submodule-patches exported. Next: the host completion-delivery class (SP/DP/SI/AI/VI/timer paths that
can return without posting).
Discrimination: the census **refutes H-poll and selects H-none** for guest-produced busy-polls. The forced arm
**selects H-lost-completion** as a real freeze mechanism: old 3/3 FROZEN, fix 3/3 OK. The fix is engineering, not
diagnostic: pi.cpp now posts the completion on the unknown-region read and write paths.
Next discriminator: the host completion-delivery table (NEXT.md, HYPOTHESIS-ID host-completion-delivery-class). Every
SP/DP/SI/AI/VI/timer return path that skips its post is classified DEAD/SAFE/HAZARD. A HAZARD row selects H-lost as a
boot-freeze candidate; an all-DEAD/SAFE table selects H-none.

## Session 7197 (2026-11-12) — host completion-delivery class closed: one HAZARD found and fixed (the default AI drain thread never posts once the SDL device stops pulling, so guest audio tasks stop for good: old arm audio-task rows 2 after the stall, fix 578, control 0 fallback fires)
HYPOTHESIS-ID: host-completion-delivery-class (closed)
What ran (offline census first, then a two-arm qualification). Full table in docs/HOST-COMPLETION-CENSUS.md.
- Every producer of an external message was enumerated: SP and DP (task thread and gfx thread), the osSpTaskStartGo
  override, DL extension events, VI, the 3 AI paths, timer, SI (osContStart*), EEPROM, PI do_dma, flash. The delivery layer
  was also covered: drop-on-full for VI/AI/PI, the s7194 refused-mq drop, NULL mq.
- Classes: DEAD (cannot happen), SAFE (hardware posts nothing too, or the failure is loud: QUICK_EXIT/throw/assert), HAZARD.
  Drop-on-full is SAFE, because libultra's exception handler and __osDevMgrMain post with NOBLOCK.
- **HAZARD (1): the AI drain thread** (default since s5672, ROGUESQ_AI_EVENT_DRAIN=2048) posts AI only when SDL's queue
  is at or below thr bytes. Hardware raises AI from the DAC clock, so it always completes. A device that exists but stops
  pulling never drains: SDL2 stops calling the queue callback when a device is paused or its output disconnects
  (HDMI TV off, Bluetooth headset gone). Once that happens, AI is never posted again. Close/reopen is fine:
  audio_device==0 reports 0 bytes.
  - ORIGIN: the writer is our runtime (the drain thread substitutes queue drain for the DAC clock). The skipped post is
    illegitimate, since hardware completes.
  - Fix, default on: after ROGUESQ_AI_STALL_POST_MS (100) without a post, post anyway and log `[s7197-ai-stall]
    fallback post`. =0 restores the old drain-only path.
  - Forced arm ROGUESQ_AI_STALL_TEST=<sec> (main.cpp get_frames_remaining): calls SDL_PauseAudioDevice(dev,1) from <sec>
    on, and re-pauses after a reopen.
- Near-hazard made visible: the osSpTaskStartGo override returns without submitting (so no SP/DP post) on an invalid OSTask
  pointer. It is DEAD in practice, but it was silent. It now logs `[s7197-sp-drop]`. 0 hits in all runs below.
Arms (scratch/s7197/arms.zsh, boot_freeze_hunt owner env, 3 boots x 45 s, pause at 15 s), plus full-log single boots:
- Hunter: a_old 3/3 OK, b_fix 3/3 OK, c_ctl 3/3 OK. No arm froze: fs reached about 2576 in every boot, so rendering
  survives a lost AI completion.
- Full logs (scratch/s7197/full_{old,fix,ctl}.log):
  - Positive control `TEST paused device=2 at 15.0 s` appears in both old and fix.
  - old: guest audio-task rows `[s3299-t2]` (type-2 task successor) stop right after the pause. There are 2 rows after
    the pause (the last one is 24 lines past it), against about 100/s before. 0 fallback posts. Guest audio is dead for
    good, and video carries on.
  - fix: 578 audio-task rows after the pause (about 10 tasks/s, the 100 ms fallback cadence). Fallback posts start at
    remaining=2597 and climb by 768 B each.
  - ctl (60 s, rebuilt binary): 0 fallback posts, 0 sp-drop, 6187 audio-task rows, fs=3405. The fallback never fires in
    normal play.
Discrimination: the census selects H-lost for exactly one path (AI drain) and H-none for every other producer. The forced
arm shows what a lost AI completion does: permanent silent guest-audio death, not a game freeze. So it does not explain
the 1-in-65 boot freeze, which stays passive.
Caveat (single-source, untested): while the device is stuck, the queue grows by about 768 B per fallback post, and the guest
audio clock runs at the fallback cadence. Recovery after the device resumes, and the latency the backlog adds, were not
measured. That is the next unit.
lib/ edited: submodule-patches exported.

## Session 7201 (2026-11-12) — pad hot-plug: removing the open pad left input dead with a second pad present (H-pad-orphan confirmed, H-pad-latch refuted); remaining pad now adopted, default on

What ran: code read of src/main/main.cpp poll_input/get_n64_input, then one build with a forced arm
ROGUESQ_PAD_HOTPLUG_TEST=<sec>: attaches two SDL virtual gamepads (SDL_JoystickAttachVirtualEx, type GAMECONTROLLER;
P1 holds A + left stick right, P2 holds X = N64 B + left stick up), detaches P1 at <sec>, and logs the pad word handed to
the guest once per wall second ([pad-hp] word). Arms scratch/s7201/arms.zsh, 40 s boots, same binary: new (default),
old (ROGUESQ_PAD_HOTPLUG=0), ctl (no detach).

Code read: get_n64_input reads live SDL state each call, so nothing can latch; but a pad opened only on its own ADDED
while none was open, and REMOVED only closed ours. A second pad connected at boot (its ADDED arrives while pad 1 is
open) was never adopted.

Result (seconds per pad word):
- ctl: 39 s btn=0x8000 x=1.00 (positive control: virtual P1 state reaches the guest).
- old: 14 s 0x8000 x=1; detach at 15.0 s, removed ours=1; then 24 s btn=0x0000 x=0 y=0 pad=none. Input dead for good
  with P2 still connected. Goes to zero, so H-pad-latch refuted (no stuck turn/fire), H-pad-orphan confirmed.
- new: 14 s 0x8000 x=1; at the removal `[pad-hp] adopt idx=0 id=1`; then 24 s btn=0x4000 y=1.00 = P2's state. Fixed.
  (The adopt line prints "RS64 virtual P1" as the name of id 1: sdl2-compat name lookup on virtual pads; the word proves
  it is P2.) 0 crash lines in all arms.

legitimate for the old code's design, which simply never rescanned.

Fix, default on (ROGUESQ_PAD_HOTPLUG=0 = old): on REMOVED of ours, rs64_pad_adopt() opens the first remaining game
controller (skipping the removed id); also each poll, if ours reports !SDL_GameControllerGetAttached without an event,
close and adopt (not exercised by this test). New witnesses: [pad-hp] added/removed/adopt lines (always), and
[g1f] display changed / display event lines in the event watch for the next unit (display hot-plug).
This selects H-pad-orphan and refutes H-pad-latch (same-run old/new/ctl arms); the fix resolves the root cause in the host

  unchanged; plume is built with PLUME_APPLE_RETINA_ENABLED OFF), so RT64 renders a 1360x764 image into the top-left of a

  chain size (resize() puts it back). Exported to submodule-patches/rt64-plume.patch.
- src/main/main.cpp rs64_display_hotplug_tick (update_gfx, main thread): on a display removal while fullscreen, leave
  fullscreen at +0.3 s and re-enter desktop fullscreen + raise at +1.5 s, so macOS builds the Space on a live display.

screen, so the new check does not fire in normal play. 0 CRASH in all 8 runs.

into the new drawable (16:9 game on a 16:10 panel = small bars). Not changed (game-side width cannot change live).
Side finding for the next unit: bi shows SDL drawable 2720x1528 at create but RT64's swap chain runs at the 1360x764 point
size, so on any 2x display (built-in Retina, a 4K TV at "looks like 1080p") the game is rendered at half the panel's
resolution and upscaled by CoreAnimation. That is G1f item (4) "internal resolution follows the window", unmeasured until now.
Discrimination: fullscreen arm SELECTS H-display-dead and REFUTES H-display-follow for fullscreen (hidden Space, 0 on-screen
frames); windowed arm SELECTS H-display-follow for position but adds H-layer-stale (2x drawable vs point-size swap chain).
H-aspect-stale is confirmed by construction and left as is. Next discriminator: RETINA=0/1 arms on the built-in panel

(NEXT.md, HYPOTHESIS-ID retina-render-scale).

## Session 7206 (2026-11-12) — interlaced still screens: RT64 resolved the fb one row early (B517C8), presents ran 20/s or through a stale VI; fixed, now 60/s through the current VI
Unit from NEXT (HYPOTHESIS-ID retina-nonflight-present). Offline first, on the s7204 rings: the B517C8 screen also appears at boot
t=11-28 in all 8 s7204/s7205 arms, at 20/s with no extra presents. The mid-run window (L6 autopilot backdrop cycle) gave
vi=B51E00 60/s presents in R0 2/2 (L6r0 205-213, L6r0b 193-201) and in R1 0/1 (L6r1b never reached it). Rows: in R0 every
B517C8 present is skip=1 (stale-queue drop, writeCursor moved on) and the shown presents are vi=B51E00 fb=B51E00, one per
workload (W fbs=B51E00 60/s); in R1 B517C8 is presented (fb=B51E00) at 20/s. [threadPresent] viW=1592 origin B517C8 drawn B51E00.
Mechanism (code read, rt64_state.cpp early present + rt64_vi.cpp): the screen is an interlaced double-stride VI (width reg 1592,
fb 796 cols at B51E00, origin reg B52438 = fb + one 796-col row, serrate 1). VI::fbAddress() subtracts a row computed from the raw
width 1592, not the halved stride fbSize().x = 796, so the current VI resolves to B517C8, which no colour image matches: early
present never fires through the current VI, and the screen is presented only on VI changes (20/s). Early present can still match
a LEFTOVER entry of the 3-slot VI history whose estimate lands on B51E00 (the [pe-stale] log names it: w=640 org B52300 ys 0x612
v=51-51, a zero-height VI from before the screen), and then the fb is presented 60/s through that obsolete VI while the real VI
presents are dropped. Whether that entry is still in history is timing; Retina does not enter the path (H-retina not selected:
the s7204 R0/R1 split is history content, not the setting).
Fix, both default on, lib/rt64 (submodule-patches/rt64.patch refreshed):
- ROGUESQ_VI_ILACE_ADDR (=0 old): fbAddress() uses fbSize().x as the row width when serrate halves it -> B51E00.
- ROGUESQ_PE_STALEFIX (=0 old): early present only through history entries compatibleWith() the current top VI; [pe-stale] logs
  rejects (first 4, then every 600th).
Run (tools/g1e_owner_quiet_arms.zsh, L6 owner recipe FPS60 dd4 16:9 fullscreen, HOLD 222, shots 13,20,26,194..212, quiet host
idle > 27700 s, one game at a time), data scratch/s7206:
  f0 (both =0): boot 11-28 B517C8 20/s; stale state REPRODUCED at 189-197 (B51E00 60/s shown, B517C8 skip=1 20/s): 3/3 R0 runs.
  f1 (fixed):   boot 10-28 B51E00 skip=0 60.1/s (plus 59.8/s superseded duplicates); 0 B517C8 rows anywhere; [pe-stale] fired
                (positive control that the stale entry exists in this run and is now refused).
  Picture: f0 vs f1 shots c1-c3 (boot title stills, same seconds) inside the 4:3 box: mean diff 0.00 at shift 0, 1.37-1.72 at
  +-1 row, so the image is pixel-identical; only the present rate and the VI it goes through change. Shot c4 (t=194) is a
  cross-fade wipe between two backdrop stills (hangar / Hoth).
  Flight control (from 95 s): Q 59.8/s, shown 59.3/s in both arms; gaps > 250 ms 0/0; 0 crashes.
ORIGIN: RT64's fbAddress() row estimate (upstream heuristic) uses the raw VI width register on double-stride interlaced modes; the
stale match is RT64's 3-slot history keeping entries across a VI mode change. Not game data, not a guest corruption.
NOT shown: that the 60 workloads/s on these stills are 60 distinct images (static title is identical across shots, so the gain
there is nil; the wipe may gain motion); 4:3 retail interlaced screens (Elite Rogues 512x448) not re-scored against angrylion
with the new address; RETINA=1 arm not re-run with the fix.
Verdict: root cause named and fixed; H-retina not selected, H-phase-like history timing explains the R0/R1 split; H-retail
(retail VI scans the fb every refresh, so 60/s through the current VI is the faithful behaviour) is consistent but single-source.
Next: distinct-frame count on the boot title/wipe windows (f0 vs f1) and a 4:3 G3 re-score of the interlaced menus.

ORIGIN: RT64 workload_queue sets each target's resolutionScale from the workload that draws into it (fixedResScale = aspectTarget/aspectSource

getViewportAndScissor) applied that x/y ratio to a DIFFERENT, newer VI fbSize at a mode switch, so the box took the old VI's shape. Not the
game, not our walkers.
Fix (lib/rt64, default on, ROGUESQ_PRESENT_SHAPEFIX=0 = old): when the target's rs.x/rs.y differs >3% from aspectTarget/aspectSource of the
present VI (Manual: userConfig.aspectTarget; Expand: max(swapW/swapH, src); Original: src), RenderParams.shapeScale = {rs.y*want, rs.y} is used
for the viewport/scissor only; sampling (videoResolution) keeps the target's own rs. RDRAM-upload (scratch) targets are excluded: a first build
stretched the genuine 4:3 320x224 boot logo to full width (Y21 run, caught by the vishape log), fixed before the arms below. [s7213-shape] logs

  removed at ~35 s; arms RETINA=1 / RETINA=0. Positive control: vd ndisp 1->2->1, `[s7199-hotplug] added=3`, `[g1f] display

  - REMOVAL of the added display (window NOT on it): `[g1f] display removed fullscreen=1` -> our s7202 handler did
    `hotplug: leave fullscreen` + re-enter: 2 resizes, Z rows 3024x1724 -> 3024x1898, on-screen 19/20/17 per s for 3 s
    (no gap >250 ms). H-churn, caused by our handler, not macOS.

  for the s7221 case (window's display removed) and never checked which display went.

  if no current display has those bounds. ROGUESQ_HOTPLUG_ANY=1 restores the old behaviour. Log line now carries
  own_display / still_present / any.

  | m | window ON removed vd (s7221 path) | still_present=0, leave + re-enter on display 0 | 6 | 6 | 30/s from +2 s | 0 |

  still recovers (3024x1898 on the built-in; pre-removal P at=0 on the vd as in s7221). Screenshot g_rm5 shows the game
  fullscreen on the built-in. 0 crashes in 5 runs.

  x (both signs); one cell near; dist2 exactly at the threshold; material mismatch; non-flat partner; flagged (0x40000000) group; height overflow

## Session 7254 (2026-11-12) — loop soak phase waits (bounded) for host idle instead of skipping idle-gated soaks at the boundary
What ran: no game run. At 23:22 the host was on AC (pmset 'AC Power', 100%) but the owner was active (HID idle 89 s, then 0 s); loop.log shows
iteration 18's soak phase skipped all three queued recipes (s7248_fixed_fps_b, s7250_slowhost, s7251_dd6r_ac: needs 180 s, idle 60 s). All three
are SOAK_NEEDS_IDLE=180 and the boundary check is a single instant, so an evening of owner activity skips them every iteration while paid
iterations run without the measurement they wait on.
Change (engineering, tools/agent/loop.sh): run_soak_queue = run_soak_pass + a bounded wait. When a pass ran nothing and skipped >=1 idle-gated
recipe, the loop polls every SOAK_IDLE_POLL (30) s for up to SOAK_IDLE_WAIT (1800) s for the smallest requested idle, then runs one more pass;
on expiry it logs 'idle wait expired' and starts the iteration. SOAK_IDLE_WAIT=0 restores the old one-check behaviour. No wait when any recipe ran.
Test: tools/agent/test_soak_idle_gate.sh 13/13 (4 new: expiry keeps the recipe queued and takes >= the wait; host going idle mid-wait runs the
recipe and ends the wait early; an ungated recipe that ran suppresses the wait (control); WAIT=0 = old path). The expiry check fails on the
pre-s7254 code (it returns at once), so it is the negative control.

submits per frame would be a lever; if the GPU timeslices fairly, fps does not depend on the foreign buffer length.

the window-to-window spread 11.6-12.5). Two lines: the dose-response shape (sublinear, not k*cb) and the direct A/B. The GPU shares

work is coalesced; not pursued.

logs and loop.log carry no record of which game processes were alive when a recipe started (no hit for "games alive"/"still
alive"/"foreign"), so whether a soak ever ran beside a leftover game cannot be answered from history. Landed the guard instead,
so the question is answered going forward (every kill is written into the SOAK-RESULTS verdict line).

Change (tools/agent/loop.sh): `soak_kill_games` (pgrep -x the game name, SOAK_GAME_NAME overrides it for tests; SIGKILL all,
print the pids). Called (1) at the start of run_soak_queue, whether or not anything is queued: an iteration's leftover game
gets a `<ts> | loop | leftover game alive after the iteration, SIGKILLed: pids ...` line; (2) before each recipe: the verdict
line gains ` | foreign game killed before start: pids ...`; (3) after each recipe's process-group kill: ` | own game outlived
the recipe, SIGKILLed: pids ...` (a game that escaped the group via setpgrp/setsid). The iteration has ended whenever these run,
so any live game is a leftover; killing it is safe. ORIGIN: the s7312 stale-frame datum (s7313: a leftover game's window
captured by `pgrep|head -1`); the writer of the leftover is whichever iteration/soak arm failed to reap its game, and now each
occurrence is named by pid in the ledger feed instead of silently doubling host load.

Test (tools/agent/test_soak_idle_gate.sh, fake game = C sleeper renamed rs64fake7314): control "no game alive -> no note";
leftover before start -> killed and named (recipe itself asserts it sees no game, exit 7 otherwise); recipe spawning a game in
its own process group -> reaped and logged; empty queue -> iteration leftover reaped with the loop line. 19/19 PASS. Same test
against HEAD's loop.sh: the 3 kill checks FAIL (positive control that the test discriminates). Pid class audit: tools/ has no
remaining `pgrep ... | head` pid pick outside the helper/its test (s7313 covered the users). Rules out nothing about the game;
closes harness item 12.

## Session 7315 (2026-11-14) — retail RAM-size/upper-bound idiom class closed: new tools/s7315_retail_bound_census.py finds 86 sites in retail code, 0 fixed heap bounds; the only size dependence is 4 MB vs more

HYPOTHESIS-ID: retail-ram-bound-idiom (closed).
- Unit: NEXT s7315 step 1 found no leftover/foreign/outlived kill line in SOAK-RESULTS, and the last 15 session titles are not sweep
  titles, so this is not a REVISIT. Paired idiom-class audit chosen per iron rule 14: retail-side RAM-size constants. s6992 showed
  the s6862 HEAP-ADDR-AUDIT reads host-patch C literals only. Retail builds bounds in registers (`lui`+`ori`, `sltu`), and its
  0xFF000000 pointer mask was missed that way. Hypotheses: H-bound (some retail code compares heap pointers with a constant top,
  e.g. 0x80800000, so spill/OSMEM>8 pointers get rejected like s6992) vs H-none (only mode/size reads, no pointer bounds).
- New tool tools/s7315_retail_bound_census.py: reads the original-instruction comments in RecompiledFuncs, lists every lui of a
  RAM-size high half (0x3F/0x40/0x7F/0x80/0xFF) or a KSEG0 top (0x8040..0x8100) plus every osMemSize (0x80000318) load, names the
  completing ori/addiu and the first consumer, and checks a verdict table (exit 1 = unclassified). Positive control `--selftest`:
  a fake `lui $at,0x8080; sltu` + `lw 0x318` function comes back 2/2 unclassified, rc=1. The count cross-checks with an independent
  grep: 84 lui PCs + 2 lw PCs = 86, same as the tool.
- Result: 86 sites, 0 unclassified -> H-none. partitionFramebufferMemory: FB top = 0x80400000 in 4 MB mode
  (*0x8010FCB0+0x44 & 0x2000), else 0x80000000|osMemSize. getUsableRdramSize 0x80002664 returns 4 MB or osMemSize.
  resetGameSettingsAndMissionStats/initIdleDemoTimersAndSave store settings 0x80130B63 = (usable > 4 MB), which is 1 at both 8
  and 12 MB. Two 0x80808081 are divide-by-255 magic. The other 70 are flag bits, MusyX 16.16 volume/pitch values and field masks.
  No retail code branches on 8 MB vs more, so OSMEM_MB=12 moves the framebuffers and changes nothing else in retail code.
- Evidence: single-source, static. Method limit: a bound loaded from a data word or taken from a heap-end variable is not caught.
  Dynamic side, already on record: the s6992 mask class and the dd>1 OSMEM_MB=12 300 s holds (s7294/s7298) are clean.
- Docs: docs/HEAP-ADDR-AUDIT.md gains the s7315 section. CURRENT-TRUTH Next steps 13 = this class (closed), 14 = fallback.
- No game run (static audit, no build change). Rules out the retail fixed-top pointer-bound class as a source of dd>1/OSMEM defects.

over ~740M DMAs here and in s7324). ROGUESQ_RSP_DMA25_CTL=1 compares the 24-bit and 25-bit images per bit-24 read.

| off | 0xFFFFF8  | 0 | 49152+ (direct_spill 51655) | 49152/49152 | 204/204 |

  4-7 tasks until the mixer moves on. No wait edge within 0.5 s. -> **H-next-task.** Same in retail settings -> not dd/aspect/FPS60.
- **Class 2 (b only, 3 hits):** bulk=0 rs_free of 0x80171570+0x1E30 and 0x80175870+0x298 inside waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone (entry

  in flight across the free. The wait's countdown 0x8014998A is decremented by musyxSynthFrame at build time, not at SP completion
  (s7065), so the guest frees as soon as the last chunk is built. Code-structure race; the host RSP task is ~0.1 ms, hardware longer.
- Overlap: every hit classed freed means no live host-map block contained the address at DMA time, so in both runs no allocation
  reused the buffers in the window: 0 corrupting reads/writes.

ORIGIN: the reads/writes are issued by the MusyX audio ucode on command lists the guest synth (musyxSynthFrame) builds into buffers the
guest itself freed (class 1: retail bulk free coalesceFreeHeapBlocks of untagged mixer buffers at boot; class 2: retail rs_free in

Rules out: H-wait-noop for class 1 (no wait involved, every task post-dates the free); a dd/spill/aspect cause (retail-settings arm

command line kills its own watchdog (cmdline match); use a script file or kill by pid (tools/rs64_game_pid.zsh).
Verdict: this selects H-next-task for the boot class (every hit task submitted after the bulk free, both arms) and refutes

## Session 7352 (2026-11-14) — class AC signed 32-bit add/sub/negate overflow closed: 407 sites + 178 blind-spot rows, 0 open, no defect (census s7352_signed_census.py with controls; VRCP/VRSQ INT_MIN guard UBSan control PASS)
HYPOTHESIS-ID: host-signed-overflow. Work unit from NEXT.md (s7351): idiom-class audit, class AC.
Hypotheses: H-safe (operands narrow / unsigned / 64-bit / float, so no signed-32 sum can leave int range), H-diag (the only
full-range sums sit in gated probes), H-ub (a default-on int32 sum of two full-range guest words: fix with uint32 or int64).
Generated code first (largest volume of guest arithmetic): N64Recomp ADD32/SUB32 (recomp.h:96-100) add two `gpr` = uint64_t and
then truncate, so no signed overflow. RecompiledFuncs has 0 S32()/SIGNED() +/- (one `(int32_t)((a & ~Nu) + ...)` casts an
unsigned sum). Its Sll32 form is `S32(x << n)`, a uint64 shift. The F5 ucode C files have 0 signed +/- too. Their `S32(rN) << k`
(213 sites) is signed left shift, but the ucode files are compiled LANGUAGE CXX under CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20 (CMakeLists.txt:9, :301),
where it is defined as modular. Not a defect.
Host census: new tools/s7352_signed_census.py on the s7343 scope (183 files, 96k lines). It reuses s7338 sites() C/P/G/D, s7343
ln_fn/body_gated/hand, s7344 decl/CORE and s7348 lhs_of/rhs_of. Site = binary + / - / += / -=, unary -, or abs() whose arithmetic is
signed 32. That means at least one operand is declared or cast int/int32_t/s32, and no operand is unsigned 32, 64-bit or float.
Classes: NAR (known widths fit in 31 bits), HOST (no guest-derived operand within one assignment level), H, PTR, U, W64 (hand
corrections), FIX, B.
Controls (same run, `--controls`): planted `(int32_t)task->a + (int32_t)task->b` -> '?', int16/masked twin NAR, gated twin G,
uint32 twin counted U, int64 twin counted W64: PASS.
Result: 4826 +/- sites seen. Not signed 32: U 2549, W64 844, FLT 618. Untyped (an operand's type unresolved) 2095. Signed-32 sites:
407 = HOST 146, G 76, NAR 69, D 62, H 33, U 11, PTR 8, W64 1, P 1. 0 '?' / B.
The 22 first-pass '?' were pointer + int (rdram / g_rdram_for_submit / diag dumps), uint32 + int32 that the usual conversions make
unsigned (overlays `rom_addr - rom + ram_addr`), or bounded counts (n += bool over 8 compares, rows <= 512, palette 0xF80 + idx<<3).
HAND also moves the guest-derived-but-narrow families the one-level HOST rule had mislabelled into NAR/H with reasons: rt64 tile
coords (uint16 12-bit), rect/scissor coords + extended-GBI offsets, x/yScroll vs int(texcoord), the floor-texel diag sampler
(returns without ROGUESQ_LOG_FLOOR), RSP VU VCL/VMACQ/VMULQ, and terrain cell indices.
Blind spot made explicit: 178 default-on +/- with a guest-derived operand of unresolved type, all classed: U 150 (120 are RSP
LWC2/SWC2 address maths, where rs is RSP::r32 = uint32_t (rsp_vu.hpp:66); the rest are u-suffixed literals or GBI p0/p1 uint32
bitfields), PTR 9, NAR 9, HOST 7, H 3. The census exits 1 on any unclassified blind-spot row.
Only interesting default-on candidate: RSP VRCP/VRSQ `data = input ^ mask; data -= mask` with a guest double-precision input
(DIVIN << 16 | low). At input = INT_MIN (DIVIN 0x8000, low 0) the step would compute INT_MAX - (-1). The real code runs the `-=` only
under `if (input > -32768)`, so INT_MIN never reaches it.
Control tools/s7352_signed_ctl.cpp (clang -O1 -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow -fno-sanitize-recover): the guarded step (verbatim)
runs 16,777,481 inputs clean, including every 16-bit input, the INT_MIN / INT_MAX edges and a 0x101-stride sweep of all 32-bit
values. The unguarded twin aborts: "2147483647 - -1 cannot be represented in type 's32'". PASS. The census also checks the guard is
still in the header (2 copies).
No code fix, so no game run (NEXT.md: runtime only if a B site is fixed). Second line of evidence: the UBSan control covers the one
non-trivial default-on site only. The other 406 rest on static review: single-source.
Conclusion: H-safe selected for all 407 signed-32 sites and 178 blind-spot rows. H-ub refuted: no default-on full-range int32 guest
sum exists in host code. H-diag is not needed to explain it. Rules out: signed add/sub overflow UB as a live defect source.

## Session 7353 (2026-11-14) — class AD invalid bool / enum values from guest bytes closed: 19 sites, 0 open, no defect (census s7353_boolenum_census.py with controls; UBSan bool,enum control PASS)
HYPOTHESIS-ID: host-bool-enum-load. Work unit from NEXT.md (s7352): idiom-class audit, class AD.
Language facts the classes rest on (C++17 [dcl.enum]/[expr.static.cast]): a scoped enum (`enum class`) always has a fixed underlying
type (int if none is written), so any int value is defined; an unscoped enum with `: T` likewise. Only unscoped enums WITHOUT a fixed
type have the narrow bitmask range, and clang exploits it only under -fstrict-enums (no CMakeLists in the tree sets it). A bool is
different: every bool load carries !range [0,2), so a guest byte memcpy'd into a bool or read through a bool* is the real hazard.
`bool b = guest;` is a conversion, not a load. NEXT.md's H-safe wording ("enum class without a fixed type" as risky) was wrong on
that point and the census uses the corrected rule.
New tools/s7353_boolenum_census.py (reuses s7338 sites() C/P/G/D, s7343 ln_fn/args_of/body_gated/hand, s7344 decl/CORE). Enum and
struct tables come from the scope plus src/, include/, lib/rt64/src, lib/N64ModernRuntime headers (test/gtest/rabbitizer excluded),
with `using X = E;` / typedef aliases. Site kinds: E (static_cast<E>, (E)x, E(x)), BP (cast to bool*), BS (memcpy/memmove/fread or
cast whose destination is a bool or a struct with a direct bool member: 203 such structs).
Blind spot fixed during the run: the first pass found only 11 enum casts, because the RT64 combiner/blender decoders live in
lib/rt64/src/shared/*.h (compiled into the host under HLSL_CPU), which s7343 files_in_scope() does not cover. The census adds them
(EXTRA_SCOPE) and they produced the only unscoped-unfixed casts.
Controls (same run, `--controls`): planted `static_cast<Mode>(task->a)` with unscoped unfixed `enum Mode {A, B}` -> '?', enum class
twin FIXED, `: uint32_t` twin FIXED, `& 1` twin RC, gated twin G, `bool b = task->a` not a site, `memcpy(&flag, rdram + task->a, 1)`
into a bool -> '?' (BS): PASS.
Result: 19 sites, 212 files: FIXED 10 (mods RelocType : uint8_t, ReplacementFlags, PatchActionType, RT64 user-config enums Antialiasing /
ReplacementShift / ReplacementOperation / VisualizationMode / UpscaleMode / QualityMode, Blender Approximation), RC 8 (rt64_blender.h
decodeInputP/M/A/B: `(blenderInputs >> k) & 0x3` into 2-bit unscoped InputPM/InputA/InputB; 4 lines x 2 casts), HOST 1 (rt64
application window SDL userdata cast to ApplicationWindow*, a bool-carrying struct, but the pointer is the host `this`). 0 bool*
casts on guest data (the two `(bool)` hits are conversions), 0 copies into a bool or bool struct. 196 non-bool copies; 11 of them have a
guest source and an unresolved destination type (9 D, 2 G): all hand-resolved (BLIND_HAND) to uint8_t / uint32_t / uint64_t /
int32_t buffers. ColorCombiner ColorInput/AlphaInput (unscoped, unfixed) are only produced by switch returns of enumerators
(colorInputA..D), never cast from a field. Census exits 0; it exits 1 on any '?', B or unresolved blind-spot row.
Second line: tools/s7353_boolenum_ctl.cpp, clang++ -std=c++17 -O1 -fsanitize=bool,enum, worst-case guest word 0xFFFFFFFF and byte
0x5A. UBSan reports exactly two errors: "load of value 4294967295, which is not a valid value for type 'Mode'" (planted unscoped cast)
and "load of value 90, which is not a valid value for type 'bool'" (byte memcpy'd into a bool). No report for the enum class, the
`: uint32_t` twin, the masked twin, the verbatim rt64 decodeInputP shape (both cycles) or the `bool b = g` conversion. PASS: the
checker agrees with every class rule the census applies.
No code fix, so no game run (NEXT.md: runtime only if a B site is fixed).
Conclusion: H-safe selected for class AD: every enum cast is FIXED or range-masked, and no guest byte reaches a bool object. H-ub
refuted; H-diag not needed. Rules out: invalid bool / enum loads as a live defect source in host code.
Next: class AE, data races on non-atomic host globals shared between host threads (CURRENT-TRUTH 27s, NEXT.md).
Discrimination: census + UBSan control select H-safe and refute H-ub for class AD.

main; the generated C (RecompiledFuncs, factor5_ucode) is not instrumented, so guest-RAM traffic is untraced). Build took ~2 min.

repairs it, and build_tsan.sh now does that at the end. New tools/s7354_tsan_report.py groups TSan reports by (kind, top frame
pair), prints location / threads / frames and applies a HAND class table (exit 1 on '?' or B).
Positive control (same run, every run): ROGUESQ_S7354_RACE_CTL=1 (main.cpp s7354_race_ctl_start) plants two detached threads
incrementing a plain static; TSan reported s7354_race_ctl_var in all 6 run logs.
Runs (owner-style recipe FPS60 dd8 21:9 forced L1 route, BUILD=build_tsan, owner save COPIED into build_tsan/saves, read-only):
run1 (pre-fix, 2 attempts) + run1 attempt 3 / run2 / run3 (post-fix). Datum: under TSan the game stalls in early boot every time,
pre- and post-fix: VI keeps ticking (17856 VIs) but RDP frames stop at rdpFs=39 at origin 0xA6F000 and initMission never comes
(run3: nomission after WAITN=90). So TSan's runtime coverage is boot / intro threads only (game, VI, gfx, task, AI drain,
present, workload, Metal). Not root-caused; ASan builds reach missions, so it is TSan slowdown or a TSan-specific interaction.
Findings (groups) and classes:
- B -> FIXED: `events_context` (ultramodern events.cpp). vi_thread_func called `events_context.vi.update_vi()` with NO lock; it
  reads next_state, then `cur_state ^= 1; *get_next_state() = *get_cur_state();`. osViSwapBuffer / osViSetMode /
  osViSetSpecialFeatures / osViSetEvent write next_state under message_mutex on game threads. TSan: VI-thread read at the update
  vs writes at osViSwapBuffer, osViSetMode, osViSetSpecialFeatures, plus osViSetEvent read vs VI write. Failure shape: a swap
  whose store follows the flip lands in the new CURRENT state and the copy then discards it from next, so the next VI shows
  the old framebuffer (lost swap = held frame) until the game swaps again; osViGetNextFramebuffer also reads a mid-flip index.
  ORIGIN: writer = vi_thread_func's unlocked update_vi (upstream N64ModernRuntime shape); values legitimate, ordering not.
  Fix: update_vi, set_dummy_vi (pre-game dummy mode) and osViGetNextFramebuffer / osViGetCurrentFramebuffer take message_mutex.
  Nothing called from update_vi takes message_mutex (its lockers: osSetEventMesg, osViSetEvent, sp/dp_complete, osVi*, the two
  AI drain threads); no caller of osViGet*Framebuffer holds it. Not measured: how often the lost swap actually fired in normal
  play (ns window); latent-to-rare, not tied to any owner symptom.
- B -> FIXED: `sample_rate` (audio.cpp): written by init_audio / set_audio_frequency (game thread), read by the AI drain thread via
  get_audio_frequency -> std::atomic<uint32_t>.
- SEM (TSan blind spot): guest mq / OSThread fields in RDRAM read in osRecvMesg / osSendMesg_recomp / osRecvMesg_recomp / the new
  thread after osCreateThread, writers guest threads; and the gfx thread signalling the init semaphore on T13's stack. All are
  handoffs through moodycamel::LightweightSemaphore, which on macOS is a mach semaphore_t that TSan does not intercept.
  Control tools/s7354_sem_ctl.cpp (clang++ -fsanitize=thread, maxSpins 0 so it blocks in semaphore_wait): `sem` arm (correctly
  synchronised handoff) 1 report, `mutex` arm 0, `none` (real race) 1 -> TSan cannot see this happens-before; these rows are FP.
- BENIGN: g_recomp_rdram_for_wp_raw (one aligned 8-byte publish of the rdram base before guest code, read by diag poll threads);
  RT64 sharedResources->swapChainRate (aligned u32 pacing hint written on the present thread under its mutex on window move,
  read unlocked by RT64Context::get_display_framerate).
- EXT: plume_metal.cpp completion-handler block + vptr (copied on the present thread, run on Metal's internal queue).
- D: osViSwapBuffer_recomp ROGUESQ_FB_HASH (the m6 harness sets it) hashes the guest framebuffer while RT64 fullSync writes it.
- No lock-order-inversion, deadlock, use-after-free or signal-unsafe reports (2845 data race + 31 vptr reports total, all grouped).
Before/after (same recipe, same boot window, per TSan log): events_context rows 4/4/0/0/0, sample_rate 1/1/0/0/0 (2 pre-fix
logs, 3 post-fix logs with >500 reports each); control present in all.
Smoke on build/ (normal build, fix in): `env SECS=260 zsh scratch/s7326/run.zsh s7354_dd8 ''` (hangar -> mission -> abort cycles,
dd8 21:9 FPS60): crash=0 resets=14 late=0 arenafull=0, 6 initMission, 259 update_screen rows; same reset count as earlier
smokes on this route.
lib/ edited (events.cpp, audio.cpp): ./submodule-patches/export.sh run, N64ModernRuntime.patch refreshed in this commit.
Rules out: a default-on unsynchronised global between game / VI / gfx / AI threads in the boot path other than the two fixed.
Does not rule out: races that only occur in mission phases (TSan never got there); races inside the uninstrumented generated C.
Conclusion: the TSan table selects H-race for the VI state (events_context) and sample_rate globals (fixed, 0 rows after) and
refutes H-safe; every other row selects H-diag / blind-spot (SEM, BENIGN, EXT, D). Next discriminator: class AF signal-handler census.

Boring thing first (the macros): librecomp reserves 4 GB PROT_NONE behind rdram (addresses.hpp allocation_size) with 512 MB RW.
MEM_x(off, base) = rdram + ((base+off) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000). For ANY sign-extended 32-bit base the host offset is in [0, 4 GB):
guest RAM or a deterministic fault, never host memory. TO_PTR masks & 0x1FFFFFF. N64Recomp ctx->rN are always sign-extended.
So a null/junk guest pointer arg to the 57 live exports (cont/pak/eep/sp/ai/vi/pi/ultra_translation/upstream_compat) can not
corrupt host memory -> H-safe for the arg class as framed; H-trust moot.

## Session 7367 (2026-11-14) — guest video-ack deadlock named and FIXED: retrace parks on a duplicate ack into full cap-1 CF0 while MAIN waits on 0x8011A818 (cycle through the scheduler); duplicate-ack drop default on; TSan arm old 5/5 deadlock -> fix past it (to the old 0x8000e29c material crash); VI_HZ 60/20 deadlock, 10 clean
HYPOTHESIS-ID: host-container-race (closing the TSan-deadlock sub-thread; next slug tsan-arm-material-crash)
- **Instrument (lib/N64ModernRuntime ultramodern events.cpp):** `ROGUESQ_VI_HZ=<1..240>` (default 60, diag only, prints `[s7367] VI_HZ n`)
  replaces the fixed 60 in the VI deadline and VI count. Run script scratch/s7367/arms.zsh (TSan arm via scratch/s7366/tsan_run.zsh,
  autopilot times scaled by 60/hz, ROGUESQ_S4259=1 + G1E_TL). Classifier `tools/s7367_vi_deadlock.py <tl> <run.log>`: reads the first
  [stall-dump]'s [stall-cf0] ring + [stall-wait] table (s7191 passive instruments) -> CLEAN / H-sem / H-flag / H-cycle.
- **VI_HZ arms (dd8 21:9 FPS60, TSan build):** v60 deadlock fs=39 t=43 s; v20 deadlock fs=266 t=109 s; v10 CLEAN 600 s (fs=1649) although
  its timeline shows 22 double-send windows (each healed). Slower VI delays/thins the deadlock, does not remove its precondition.
- **Mechanism, two sources.** (1) Runtime ring, 5/5 stalls (s7366 t2/t3/t4, s7367 v60/v20/ab_old) identical: MAIN (tid 3) blocked in
  waitForPostSwapAck's CF0 recv; retrace posts (S/s, wakes MAIN) but MAIN does not run for ~80-120 ms (TSan starvation); retrace, one VI
  later or replaying its pending VI message, posts AGAIN into the still-full capacity-1 queue and parks (S without s, vflag 1). MAIN's recv
  then consumes one, retrace's retry lands, and retrace posts once more and parks again; MAIN returns (r: valid 1, fullq = retrace
  0x8011CD28), clears vflag, sees C8 already cleared by that retrace pass and LEAVES the ack loop. It next blocks on 0x8011A818
  (advanceVideoFrame+0x474 or bufferArbiterProducerScanWait+0x164) instead of returning to CF0. Every S row has vflag 1 (H-flag
  refuted); every r after the final S still lists the sender, and earlier recvs resume parked senders normally (H-sem refuted).
  (2) Static: 0x8011A818's only senders are in spTaskSchedulerThread (0x80019C54, 0x80019EF8), which is parked on 0x8011A420, whose
  producers are submitGfxFrame (MAIN, blocked) and the retrace thread's postSwapRdpReset / per-VI task posts (parked) -> closed cycle.
  This is exactly the s6993 owner-env boot freeze signature (retrace on CF0 fullq, vflag 0 at dump, no receiver) and the s6814/s6834
  title-boot freeze at fs=39; s7193's 120 forced holds never reached it because a held RETRACE lets MAIN return to CF0 - the cycle
  needs a starved MAIN, not a held retrace. s7192's "pre-state heals" is right only when MAIN's next wait is CF0.
- **ORIGIN:** the writer is the retail retrace thread (viRetraceHandlerThread 0x80019B50: osSendMesg(0x80128CF0, BLOCK) every VI while
  vflag 0x80037808 is set; return value ignored, next op osYieldThread). The second message is a legitimate duplicate ack; it is the
  BLOCK on a full queue that turns MAIN's >=1 VI starvation into a permanent cycle. Retail hardware preempts on interrupt, so MAIN is
  rarely starved that long; our host scheduler (TSan, host load, slow host wake) starves it.
- **FIX (default on, ROGUESQ_CF0_DUPDROP=0 = retail BLOCK), mesgqueue.cpp osSendMesg:** a BLOCK, non-jam send to 0x80128CF0 that finds
  the queue FULL is dropped (returns -1, check_running_queue, `[s7367] cf0 dup ack dropped n=` first 8 + powers of 2, TL code 17).
  Safe: a full queue already holds an ack, so the receiver cannot starve; only the park is removed.
- **A/B, same TSan build, VI 60 (scratch/s7367/fix_ab.zsh):** ab_old (DUPDROP=0) H-cycle deadlock fs=39 t=46 s (5th of 5); ab_fix
  drops 64+, no CF0 cycle, front end advances to fs=331 (two slow-progress stall-dumps with MAIN running, fs 105 -> 150 -> 331), then
  SIGBUS at t~65 s: allocateDisplayListBuffer+4792 <- allocOrEvictMaterialNode <- findOrCreateMaterial <- emitMaterialTexturedDL,
  far = rdram_base + 0x80000000 (guest NULL), last guest PC 0x8000E29C = the "material noise" family filed 2x in s605-s607 and never
  chased. Unknown whether it is TSan-timing-only; it is the next unit (NEXT.md).
- **Normal build smoke (build/, fix in):** `env SECS=260 zsh scratch/s7326/run.zsh s7367_dd8 ''` crash 0, resets 14, arenafull 0,
  6 initMission, 258 update_screen (= s7366), stall 0, **drops 1**: the duplicate-ack precondition occurs in normal play too.
- **Queued soaks:** s7367_bootload_old / s7367_bootload_fix (6 title boots each under hw.ncpu `yes` load, boot_freeze_hunt with
  HUNT_CONTROL): does host load reproduce the fs=39 freeze on the old path, and does the fix arm hold.
Conclusion (s7367): ring (5/5) + static producer chain select H-cycle (starved MAIN leaves the ack loop while retrace is parked on a
duplicate ack); the ring refutes H-sem and H-flag; VI_HZ 20 still deadlocking refutes "VI rate alone" (H-slow in its pure form).

  SPSC ring (own index relaxed, peer index acquire, publish release = correct), the sp.cpp site table (under its spin lock), or
  env-gated diagnostics (M5/FLZ/vtx fault probes: pending fields ARE published by a release store of pending_n; crash-snapshot
  fields; G1d/inline/trigen probes). Static volatiles: breadcrumbs / log tags / probe state; g_rs64_dd_scene is game-thread only
  (s6903 cinegate guest patch writes, s6904 fog / s6911 mapidx guest hooks read). Diag-only defect left as-is: the M5 VI-commit
  probe does its release store of latest_sequence BEFORE the field stores (wrong order, but env-gated, log only).
- The defect: FramebufferRenderer (workload thread) writes g_rs64_last_drawn_fb (exchange), then _width, then _siz, all relaxed;
  the present thread in follow-draw mode 3 (the default since s23) loads the three separately with no lock, then decides
  sane-width / REGISTERs fbManager.get(drawn, siz, drawnW, h). A read between the writes pairs the new address with the old width.
- Fix (lib/rt64, default on): the writer also stores the whole tuple as one 64-bit word g_rs64_last_drawn_packed (addr | width<<32
  | siz<<56) with release; mode 3 and the 1024-phase diag read it via rs64_last_drawn_snapshot (one load-acquire).
  ROGUESQ_S7383_FBPACK=0 = old separate loads. Instrument: every snapshot also loads the separate fields and checks them a read later
  against the width the packed word finally holds for that address (tear counter), plus a writer-side width-change counter;
  ROGUESQ_S7383_LOG=1 prints `[s7383] reads= tear= wchg= pack=` every 600 reads. Control ROGUESQ_S7383_TEAR_CTL=1: the writer stores
  width+8 for 200 us after moving the address. First control try (plain 200 us delay) gave tear=0 over 7800 reads: successive
  targets share a width, so a torn read looks the same as a good one. The planted wrong width fixed that.
- Runs (dd8 21:9 FPS60 hangar->mission->abort route, `env SECS=200 zsh scratch/s7326/run.zsh <name> '<env>'`, one at a time):
  | arm | reads | tear | wchg | [vi-follow-skip] wild-w | crash |
  | ctl, packed (TEAR_CTL=1) | 7200 | 3377 | 5 | 0 | 0 |
  | ctl, old (TEAR_CTL=1 FBPACK=0) | 7200 | 1580 | 6 | 53 | 0 |
  | default smoke (packed) | 21000 | 0 | 6 | 0 | 0 |
  The detector fires (positive control). With the planted tear, the old path let 53 torn widths reach the mode-3 decision and the
  packed path let 0 through. Default play saw 0 natural tears and only 6 width changes in 200 s, so the defect is real but latent
  (the 0 is single-source). Control arms ran fewer presents (7200 vs 21000) because the 200 us writer sleep slows the workload thread.
  Packed control arm logged 3 mode-3 REGISTER lines, the others 0; not followed up (control-only, correct widths).
- TSan arm not run: the change is atomics only (TSan does not report atomic-vs-atomic ordering), and no lock or plain-data access
  changed. Submodule patch refreshed (submodule-patches/rt64.patch).
Rules out: any other relaxed/volatile handoff of non-atomic data on a default path in the audited scope (H-relaxed-publish beyond
this tuple, and H-volatile).
Next: class AZ, non-atomic static / file-scope mutable state written from more than one host thread (NEXT.md).
Conclusion: this selects H-relaxed-publish for the RT64 last-drawn tuple only (root cause: three relaxed fields read unlocked by
default follow-draw mode 3; fixed and checked against the planted-tear control, old 53 vs new 0) and refutes H-volatile and
H-relaxed-publish everywhere else in scope. Next discriminator: the AZ thread-root census of non-atomic shared statics (NEXT.md).

**Verdict.** H-none MEASURED (0 foreign takes in 40 held windows, 4 retail-path runs, both settings arms; control PASS), but H-race
is structurally live: five guest thread ids use this mutex and a foreign guest thread ran inside 1/11 windows in both RETAIL=1 runs
(two independent lines: static window + per-thread recv census + xwin). H-port-timing refuted as a source: the port enters the
window no more than retail would (no yield in it; the one foreign call is a thread already runnable). ORIGIN: the free token is
written by retail code, buildHeapFreeList's re-seed post at 0x80001fe8 while its rs_malloc caller holds the mutex; not a port writer.

**Fix (default on, ROGUESQ_S7394_HOLDFIX=0 = retail).** namespace s7394fix tracks the 8010FEE0 holder (tid of the last successful

Code read of ultramodern timer.cpp found a latent defect: osSetTimer writes t->timestamp/interval/mq/msg on the CALLING guest
thread, while t may still be in the timer thread's std::set whose comparator reads t->timestamp. Re-arming a live non-head
timer mutates a set key in place (and races the comparator): the set holds the struct twice / out of order, erase() by key
can miss it (an interval timer keeps firing after osStopTimer), and a timer that sorts behind a stale entry can be starved.
Fix (ROGUESQ_S7397_TIMERFIX default ON, =0 old path): osSetTimer only enqueues the values; the timer thread erases any live
entry for the struct by pointer, writes the fields, re-inserts; osStopTimer falls back to a pointer erase when the keyed
erase misses. ORIGIN: upstream N64ModernRuntime timer.cpp design (guest-thread write of the set key), not game data.

Runtime: ROGUESQ_S7397_TM=1 logs [s7397-tm] set (live flag = already in set) / stop / fire rows; ROGUESQ_S7397_TM_CTL=1 plants

## Session 7413 (2026-11-15) — class BW aligned load/store macros closed (H-equal): 58,654 emitted forms of 15 ops vs a byte-wise big-endian model, 0 mismatches and 0 stray writes, mutant control PASS x8, KSEG1 not aliased but has 0 RDRAM constants

HYPOTHESIS-ID: aligned-load-store-macro-semantics. Work unit from NEXT.md s7413 (M3 idiom-class audit, item 3).

**Instrument (new):** `tools/s7413_aligned_ldst.py [K]` (rc 0 = H-equal + CONTROL PASS, ~25 s). It harvests every
lb lbu lh lhu lw lwu ld sb sh sw sd lwc1 ldc1 swc1 sdc1 site in ../N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs and takes the lowering line
that carries the op's macro. It skips only pass-through prefixes: the `g_rs64_last_guest_pc` stamp, `CHECK_FR`, and every
`if (__builtin_expect(g_rs64_store_diag, 0))` observer, which can span several lines. It requires the statement's base,
offset and dest/source to match the disasm operands; 0 operand mismatches. It compiles each distinct form VERBATIM against
the real build header (-DRS64_BYTE_WATCH as CMakeLists sets it, -include include/rsp_dpc_macros.h, -O2), with
RS64_S5798_ST and rs64_s4307_synth_read stubbed as no-op observers. Each form runs K=40 cases against a byte-wise VR4300
big-endian model driven by the disasm operands: random GPR/FPR file and f_odd array, a random 72-byte image around the
target, every legal alignment of the op, and a KSEG0 base.
- Loads: the dest must equal the sign- or zero-extended BE value, and every other register must be unchanged.
- Stores: exactly the op's width is written, and the whole 128 KB image is compared after each form.

**Result.** 101,169 pure sites, 58,654 forms, 2.35e6 cases: 0 MISM and 0 stray for every op. Rows: lb 9.8k, lbu 89k,
lh 17k, lhu 69k, lw 226k, lwu 80, ld 200, sb 173k, sh 157k, sw 882k, sd 6.2k, lwc1 315k, ldc1 16k, swc1 336k, sdc1 50k
cases. The plain (non-BYTE_WATCH) MEM_B arm on all lb/sb forms also gave 0.

**Positive control, same run.** Each mutant header was run on up to 400 forms per op, and each flagged only its own ops:
- MEM_B ^3->^1 (both defs): lb/sb 6455
- MEM_BU ^3->^1: lbu 3980
- MEM_H ^2->^0: lh/sh 8000
- MEM_HU zext->sext: lhu 1996
- MEM_W sext->zext: lw 1992
- MEM_WU (force header) zext->sext: lwu 11
- SD hi/lo swap: sd/sdc1 5230
- LD hi/lo swap: ld/ldc1 4050

Other ops: 0 in all 8. CONTROL PASS.

**Dead ends in this session.** The first run printed no rows and still said VERDICT H-equal: a false null. The harness had
died with SIGSEGV because the harvest took a line inside the s3285 freelist guard block (`ctx->r31 = MEM_W(ctx->r29,
0X10)`) as the lowering of `lw $v1,0($v0)`. Fixes: (1) a harness death now aborts the tool; (2) any non-prefix line before
the macro line marks the site as guarded; (3) the operand check against the disasm. The second run dropped every store
because the multi-line store-diag observers were not skipped; fixed. Lesson: a verdict needs non-empty rows.

**Skipped sites.** 1,738 guarded/gated sites (lw 1398, sw 260, sb 52, sh 15, others <=5) are owned by earlier guard
audits: s6287 ppcount, s6826 fps60, s4307 synth joins, alloc/freelist/cache guards, s6883 spancell. They are not
re-tested here.

**KSEG1.** The macros subtract 0xFFFFFFFF80000000 only, so guest 0xA0010000 maps to host rdram+0x20010000. That is the
PROT_NONE part of librecomp's 4 GB reservation, NOT an alias of physical 0x10000 as on hardware (measured by address
arithmetic in the harness). The lui census shows this cannot be reached through a constant:
- 0 sites in 0xA000-0xA07F (KSEG1 RDRAM) and 0 in KSEG1 MMIO.
- The 0xA8/0xAA hi-halves are rand LCG and divide-by-3 magic (rand_recomp, MusyX).
- 0xB0 x9 are PI ROM addresses passed to DMA (loadOverlay, initDmaSlots, mainBootstrapWorker, relocateSndPointer), which
  pi.cpp handles.
- 0xB4-0xBF are DL opcode words.

A computed K0_TO_K1 would fault loudly (SIGSEGV in rdram+0x2000xxxx), never corrupt silently, and 19-level soaks show 0
such crashes. **Two lines for KSEG1: static census + crash-free soaks.** The macro equality itself is single-source: the
model is written from the VR4300 manual.

**$zero-base sites.** 206, all in data_gap_800CC3D4 (180), data_gap_80024A0C (24) and data_gap_800FA248 (2). Each has 0
callers (the only references are its definition and the funcs.h prototype); this is data decoded as code, as s7412 found
for 800CC3D4.

Rules out: H-ext (sign/zero extension), H-swz (lane per alignment), H-width (neighbour bytes touched) for every pure
emitted aligned load/store. Class BW closed, no code change. Next: class BX, FP compare emission (NEXT.md s7414).

**Conclusion: selects H-equal, refutes H-ext, H-swz and H-width** for all 101,169 pure aligned load/store sites. It also
refutes H-kseg1-live: 0 KSEG1-RDRAM constants, so the non-aliased mapping has no static site. That last point rests on a
static census plus 0 crash in the soaks. **Next discriminator:** class BX, FP compare emission under NaN/inf/denormal
operands vs the MIPS cond table, with mutant control (NEXT.md s7414; H-equal / H-nan / H-fmt / H-stale).

**Work unit:** class BZ, offline. New `tools/s7416_ctrl_flow.py` (rc 0, ~3 s, output scratch/agent/s7416_ctrl_flow.out).
It tokenizes every function in ../N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs, strips the pass-through prefixes (PC stamps, CHECK_FR), and checks:
- S1, conditional branches (beq/bne/blez/bgtz/bltz/bgez + likely, bltzal/bgezal, bc1x): the emitted `if (COND) {` text is exactly
  the expected one for that op and those registers (full 64-bit gpr, SIGNED() for the sign tests, `0` for $zero). The condition
  comes before the slot, so MIPS order (evaluate first, then the slot) holds by construction, including when the slot writes the
  branch's own source register. Also checked: goto target == disasm target, label defined in the function, the slot copy inside
  the if is identical to the fall-through copy, and likely <=> `goto skip_N;` with the skip label after the fall-through copy.
  18,674 ok. 48 non-ok, each one a deliberate fixup PATCH block or a data_gap.
- S2 jal: 14,225 call the function whose first instruction is the target (ELF symtab for the `_recomp` libultra names), 251 are
  `LOOKUP_FUNC(0xT)` overlay calls with the constant == target, and the slot always comes before the call. S3 j/b: 5,296 goto a
  defined label or tail-call the function at T. 7 are `pause_self` idle self-loops; 74 emit `do_break(pc)` (preamble/invalid,
  traps loudly if ever reached, never runs silently wrong). S4 jr $ra: 2,527 `slot; return;`.
- S5 jump tables: all 177 `switch (jr_addend_A >> 2)` case lists equal the words of the ELF table named in switch_error, read
  from the ELF segment whose word at A is the jr encoding (overlays share a vaddr). 0 mismatched, 0 undefined labels; jr_addend
  is captured at the table-base addu from the index register (177/177).
- S6: the 634 distinct condition texts (18 shapes) compiled verbatim against recomp.h and run on 16 64-bit edge values per
  operand (INT32 edges with non-canonical upper words, INT64 min/max) vs a MIPS model: 111,154 cases, 0 MISM. Mutants: 32-bit
  compare, sign-extend-32, signed<->unsigned and operator flip each flag 632-634/634 forms (the 2 unflagged are the `SIGNED(0)`
  constant forms, which no operand mutation can change). CONTROL PASS.
- S7 structural positive control: 11 synthetic emissions (good bne/bnel/blez, plus each defect: slot moved before the
  condition, likely without skip, non-likely with skip, wrong target, diverging slot copy, 32-bit cond, unsigned blez, swapped
  regs). 11/11 classified correctly. PASS.
- Hazards: the jr/jalr emission runs the slot BEFORE `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->rS)`. MIPS reads rS before the slot, so a slot that
  writes rS would jump to the wrong place: a LATENT generator defect. The detector found exactly 2 such sites (organic positive
