## Session 7429 (2026-11-15) — class CL save durability on quit: copy-based finalize left a 0-byte save on a mid-copy kill (236-259/2000 kills) and the loader never fell back to the whole .bak; fixed (fsync + atomic rename, short-file .bak fallback, flush before SDL_QUIT quick_exit)

Soak fold: s7428_audio_route_arms rc=2 VOID again (1/5, re-queued by the loop; arm C "injected Return not seen").

Offline read (librecomp files.cpp / pi.cpp): update_save_file writes <save>.temp, then finalize copies final -> .bak
(final stays whole) and copy_file(temp -> final, overwrite_existing), which truncates final before copying. The loader
open_input_file_with_backup falls back to .bak only when final fails to OPEN, so a short final is read and zero-filled
(s7357 path) = the profile is lost while a whole .bak sits beside it. Separately, the saving thread writes only after 10 ms
with no new save_write (coalescing up to 128), and SDL_QUIT -> std::quick_exit (main.cpp poll_input) never joins it.

Measurement: tools/s7429_save_quit/harness.cpp #includes the real files.cpp, forks a writer doing the exact
update_save_file sequence with alternating whole 512-byte saves A/B, SIGKILLs it at a random 50-3000 us, then loads as
read_save_file does. Same binary, two arms: ROGUESQ_S7429_OLD_FINALIZE=1 (old copy) -> 259/2000 and 236/2000 bad loads
(all short, got=0, none mixed); new finalize -> 0/4000 twice (A/B split ~50/50, so the kills land throughout the cycle).
H-window SELECTED for the finalize; H-durable holds after the fix.

Fix (lib/N64ModernRuntime, patch exported): finalize fsyncs the temp and std::filesystem::rename()s it over final (atomic on
POSIX; the old copy is kept behind ROGUESQ_S7429_OLD_FINALIZE=1). read_save_file: when final is short and the .bak is whole,
load the .bak ([s7429-io] line). pi.cpp counts buffer writes (write_gen) vs the last written generation; new
ultramodern::flush_save_file() writes the buffer if it is behind (serialised with the saving thread by a file mutex; keeps
the ROGUESQ_NO_SAVE_WRITE gate; ROGUESQ_S7429_NO_QUIT_FLUSH=1 skips it); main.cpp SDL_QUIT calls it before quick_exit and
logs [s7429-quit] save flush=N.

Runtime (tools/s7429_save_quit.sh, copied folder /tmp/rs64_s7429, never build/saves): R1 0-byte final + whole .bak ->
"[s7429-io] ... loaded the complete .bak" (1 line); control R1c 0-byte final, no .bak -> [s7357-io] zero-fill (1 line).
R2 unforced write run (NO_SAVE_WRITE unset in the copy, FORCE_UNLOCK + FORCE_SAVE_MISSION=3, 40 s): the game wrote NO save
(mtime unchanged), so the game itself never ran the rename path: harness evidence only. The quit flush is code reading
only (single-source): no injected quit reaches the game (s7428 VOID). Script exit 0 = VERDICT H-durable. Owner save
build/saves untouched (mtime 2026-11-08, md5 f8b29b66...).
Rules out: the .bak ever protecting against a mid-finalize kill in the old code (it could not: the loader never reached it).
Open: runtime proof of the quit flush needs a real SDL_QUIT (owner Cmd+Q, or a working key/quit injector).
Next: class CM, unbounded default-on file growth in build/.
Conclusion: the kill harness selects H-window for the old copy-based finalize (236-259/2000 0-byte loads) and refutes
H-window for the fsync + rename finalize (0/4000), which closes the finalize half of class CL as the root cause of
quit-time save loss. H-stale (the 10 ms coalescing window dropped at quick_exit) is fixed but unverified; next
discriminator: a real SDL_QUIT right after a save write, two arms ROGUESQ_S7429_NO_QUIT_FLUSH=1 vs default, comparing
the save bytes after reload.

- REAL: plume_metal.cpp:3906 "load of value 190, not a valid value for type bool" = MetalRenderState::dynamicDepthBiasEnabled.
  ORIGIN: the writer is the MetalGraphicsPipeline ctor: it sets the field + 3 bias floats only when the desc has dynamic or
  static bias; a no-bias pipeline (most of them) leaves them uninitialized (the struct has no default). 190 = 0xBE = ASan's
  malloc fill byte, so the value is not legitimate. MetalCommandList's depth-bias apply reads them for every bound pipeline,
  so an unbiased draw could get a heap-garbage (or the last dynamic) depth bias. Fix: else branch initializes to no-bias.
- FP-compiler x6: rt64_rdp.cpp:3423/3424/3455-3458 left shift of negative int32 (TexRect s/t fixed point; rt64 TU is C++17,
  clang emits shl, defined in C++20).
- FP-idiom x3: mesgqueue.cpp:626/709/729 GET_MEMBER = offsetof via ((type*)nullptr)->member, never dereferenced.
- FP-tagged-ptr x3: plume_metal.cpp:1429 MetalShader dtor functionName->release() (+ NSObject.hpp:112) on an ObjC tagged
  NSString (address 0x9dd9e565f1b2183b).
  All in tools/s7467_san_reviewed.tsv.

## Session 7472 (2026-11-16) — class EB opened: host-side guest-heap chain walker (ROGUESQ_S7472_HEAPCHK), L4/L7/L12 dd4 16:9 + L15 dd8 21:9 0 bad headers, plant PASS (H-heap-clean, pre-mission control only)

Class EB = the guest-code blind spot of class EA (ASan cannot see a guest overrun into a neighbouring rs_malloc block).
- **Instrument (src/main/upstream_compat.cpp `s7472_check`, env ROGUESQ_S7472_HEAPCHK=1, default off, C++ only, no regen):**
  runs on the guest thread from the existing rs_malloc-exit (`rs64_s6063_malloc`) and rs_free-entry (`rs64_s6063_free`) hooks,
  at most every ROGUESQ_S7472_HEAPCHK_MS=250 ms, so the chain is never read mid-update. Walks the three arena heads
  0x8010FEFC/FF00/FF18 (deduped); header u16 flags, u16 tag, u32 size, 16 B, next = h+0x10+size (linear first-fit, rs_malloc
  0x80001ACC; no free-list links exist). Checks flags valid, size 16-aligned, next > h and < rs64_ram_top, terminator reached.
  Logs `[s7472] heap-bad why= arena= blk= field= val= prev_ok= idx= gpc=` once per distinct header, `[s7472] chk` summaries,
  and a flag histogram at the first check (layout self-test). Plant ROGUESQ_S7472_HEAPCHK_PLANT=<s>: <s> s after the first
  check, set the largest free block's flags to 0x0010; the next check must report it, then the word is restored.
- **Run 1 = H-walker-wrong, fixed in-session:** every check reported `field=flags w0=00060000` on one huge block at the top of
  the arena (e.g. 80A23DF0 size 163A00). Flags 0x0006 = used + bit 4, the top-down allocation flag (rs_malloc tests a1&4 at
  0x80001B18); legitimate. The walker stopped at that block, so the plant (then 0x0004, colliding with the real bit) never
  armed. Valid set now {1,2,6} (+8 end), plant bit 0x0010. Without the first-check histogram this would have read as 398 hits.
- **Run 2 (tools/s7472_heapchk_recipe.zsh, normal build, owner recipe, HOLD=220) rc=0 score=0:** l4 (plant) / l7 / l12 dd4 16:9,
  l15 dd8 21:9 all alive_at_end=1, crashlines=0, vi_stalls30s=0, initMission 2/1/1/1, 561-721 checks per arm, 110-239 blocks per
  walk in flight, terminator reached every walk, heap_bad_nonplant=0 on all four. Control: `plant SET blk=800C4C90` t=60.1 ->
  `heap-bad ... PLANT` -> `plant DETECTED after 0.000 s; restored`. The flag histogram matched the layout on all arms.
- Caveat (iron rule 3): the plant fired at log line 28750, before initMission#1 (line 32668) = front-end heap phase, so the
  in-flight null is controlled by the same walker but not in the same phase. Queued scratch/agent/soak_queue/
  s7472_heapchk_inflight.sh (PLANT_S=150, same arms) to place the control in flight.
- Rules out (header level only): a guest overrun across a block boundary that reaches the next header's flags/size in these
  4 levels. Does not rule out writes inside a block's data or a corrupted header restored before the next check (250 ms).
- **Verdict:** run 2 selects H-heap-clean and refutes H-heap-hit for L4/L7/L12/L15 at header level (0 non-plant bad headers
  over 2524 in-flight-spanning walks, plant detected in the same build); refutes H-walker-wrong after the 0x6 fix (flag histogram
  {1,2,6,8} only, other=0, every arm). Next discriminator: the in-flight plant (s7472_heapchk_inflight, PLANT_S=150) — detected
  = the in-flight null stands; not detected = the walker is blind in the mission phase and run 2 says nothing about flight.

- **Class EC: the passive `[s4279-BAD]` burst.** An offline pass (/tmp/s4279cls.py over all 23 EB arm logs) found that every
  arm prints exactly 40 rows, all bad=10 (bit 8 out-of-region plus bit 2 chain-end-not-head), at n~8870-9040. All rows have
  head/tail in 0x80192xxx, and every row short enough to verify from the logged fields (5 per arm) is a consistent
  doubly-linked list. Cause: tools/apply_s4279_nodeinvariant.py hard-coded the node region 0x801F9C00..0x801FB400, but in that
  front-end phase the game runs the sample-stream LRU list from a 60-node pool at 0x80192C40. The walker stopped at the first
  node, and poollen=0 was the same artifact.
  **ORIGIN:** the instrument (our s4279 walker), not the game; the list values are legitimate.
- **Fix (tools/apply_s4279_nodeinvariant.py, idempotent upgrade of the already-patched funcs_24.c):** any aligned KSEG0
  pointer below 0x81000000 is accepted, and leaving the primary region sets a new `offreg=1` field instead of bad. Added a positive
  control, ROGUESQ_S7474_LRU_PLANT=<n>: at entry call n the walker sees the first node's next word XOR 1 (a host-side read
  only; guest memory is untouched).
  Side effect handled: the script chains apply_s4278 -> apply_s4222_storewatch, which re-added a `rs64_m5_writer_parity`
  store watch to 49 funcs files that the current tree (the last build) did not carry. Those 49 insertions were stripped again
  by exact-line match, so the build differs from the last one only by the s4279 change. A full regen chain behaves as before.
- **Same-run check (scratch/s7474_lruwalk, g1e_owner_quiet_arms, L4 plant n=8890 / L12 plant n=3000, dd4, HOLD=60):** both
  arms alive, vi_stalls30s=0. Each arm had exactly ONE [s4279-BAD] row, at the planted n (bad=1, offreg=0, len=236 / 35), and
  135 offreg=1 chk rows with bad=0 (len 3-13, len+poollen=60, a full walk). The front-end burst is gone and detection still
  fires. initMission=0 in 60 s, so this check covers the front end only; in-flight rows in the 23 EB logs were already bad=0.
- **Verdict:** EC H-walker-wrong selected by two lines: (1) the offline consistency of the 40-row bursts, and (2) the fixed
  walker's full off-region walks staying bad=0 while the same-run plant fires. Rules out an LRU inconsistency in that phase.
- **Discrimination:** this selects H-walker-wrong for EC and refutes H-lru-corrupt; the root cause is the walker's hard-coded

## Session 7482 (2026-11-16) — s6202 G1d retarget pool reserved by the game's own span: ORIGIN named (partitionFramebufferMemory returns $v1 = ec as the heap boundary), fix default on, same-build A/B loc_S 151 -> 0, H-collide refuted (latent)

HYPOTHESIS-ID: g1d-retarget-unreserved-pool. Work unit from NEXT s7482 (CURRENT-TRUTH item 1a).

ORIGIN (read from the binary, funcs_0.c 0x80000DD4..0x80001080 + both callers 0x80001180/0x800013F0): partitionFramebufferMemory
places F0/F4/E8/F8/EC either upward from the bump cursor $a0 or downward from $v1; at the end it stores $v1 (lowest descending
block) to *(t6) (a0==0 path, returns 0) or *(t5) with size a0-v1 (returns 1), and the callers pass that to heap init 0x80002150
(a3 = *(sp+0x48) or the 0x8010D200 hole struct). So $v1 = ec is the heap's reserved-span boundary. The s6202 retarget writes
E8 = base = ec - t2, BELOW ec, and never lowered $v1, so the heap re-init owned [base, ec): that is why the s7481 locator found the
live pool inside the big free block 0x8023E7F0 (data end 0x809B85F0, next data = task out = ec). The writer is our patch; the
retail value is not involved.

Fix: tools/apply_s6031_far.py apply_s7482_reserve (live script __main__ + fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py funcs_0 block, right after
s6202): the ok branch records base/ec; at L_80001060 (before both out stores and the a0-v1 size), if ROGUESQ_RETARGET_RESERVE != 0
and $v1 == ec, $v1 = base. Logs `[s7482] reserve applied|skipped v1= -> pool= a0= on=`. Default ON (port bug fix); =0 restores the
old span. Detector: upstream_compat.cpp s7482_check at every rs_malloc exit (rs64_s6063_malloc -> s7475_malloc, unconditional):
[ptr, ptr+req) vs the live span published through g_rs64_s7482_base/_ec (cleared on every call that does not take "ok"), logs
`[s7482] pool-collide`; ROGUESQ_S7482_CTL=1 reports the first live-span malloc as a CONTROL line. Recipe tools/s7480_uaf_recipe.zsh:
LV entries take an optional third field of per-arm env (`7:4:ENV+ENV`, tag l<lvl>x<k>), prints s7482_reserve_applied/skipped,
s7482_pool_collide, s7482_collide_ctl, and scores rc 1 on any collision or on frame_span_S>0 in an arm whose reserve applied.

Runs (one build, screen unlocked, HID idle >52000 s):
- s7482_reserve_ab (L7 dd4 16:9, HOLD=220): RESERVE=0 arm never reached the "ok" scene (no mission restart; 4 retarget lines, all
  reject/skip) -> void for the A/B; RESERVE=1 arm did (initMission=2): reserve applied v1 0x809B8600 -> 0x8096D600 (a0=0 path),
  CONTROL fired, pool_collide=0, loc_S=0, loc_F=0, controls PASS, alive.
- s7482_reserve_ab2 (same, HOLD=300, both arms initMission=2, both reached "ok"): RESERVE=0: reserve skipped, frame_span_S=151

(31-37 per run). Who wrote that RAM? Hypotheses: H-ez-cover (another image's RT64 writeback) / H-ez-cpu (guest stores) / H-ez-dma
(RSP/PI DMA) / H-ez-hash (hash moved with no real change).

Instrument, ONE build (ROGUESQ_S7501_EZ=1, ROGUESQ_S7501_CTL=1; rides S7475_CANARY+STORE_DIAG store bitmap):
- lib/rt64 rt64_framebuffer_manager.cpp: checkRAM -> rs64_s7501_chk (every fb, every pass), hashTracking + rt64_state.cpp s7387 skip ->
  rs64_s7501_hash, uploadRAM -> rs64_s7501_up with the byte bbox of words differing from nativeSwappedRAM (before the refresh). Patch exported.
- main.cpp s7501_*: one time-stamped writer ring: RT64 writebacks (exact base via rs64_s7493_base: wbself / wbo), host DMA writes
  (upstream_compat rs64_s7486_hostread kinds 6-8 -> sp_gfx / sp_aud / pi, filtered to ranges overlapping a tracked fb), guest stores
  (every tracked fb's bytes marked in the s7475 bitmap; rs64_s7475_store hands them over first -> cpu / zmem / os, with pc and fn).
  Upload class = newest ring event in the window overlapping the bbox; hash = 0 words differ; none / trunc otherwise.
- Control: from t>=30 s the host XORs one word in the middle of a just-uploaded fb; the next upload covering the word must carry ctl.

Run 1 (same build minus two fixes): L15 ctl DETECTED, **L4 ctl MISSED**: the upload at t=67.1 s had bbox exactly the poked word but the
window started at the fb's last re-hash (0.47 s), after the poke (58.8 s). hashTracking / overlapping draws re-hash RAM without refreshing
RT64's native copy, so the window must start at the fb's previous upload (native copy == RAM). Also 99M-187M sp_gfx events/run wrapped the
1M ring in ~2 s. Fixed in-session: window = since previous upload (else first sighting); DMA events kept only when they overlap a tracked
fb; ring 2M. Instrument defect, not a result.

| L4 dd1 | 38 | 14 | 18 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 4 | 1 | 0 |
| L15 dd8 21:9 | 32 | 13 | 9 | 2 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 1 |

## Session 7507 (2026-11-16) — class FD: RSPRecomp control-flow emission audit, 0 defects in the generator output (12 files) and 0 in the compiled live composite (9 spliced overlay streams, 68 overlay routes); 8/8 mutation controls PASS

Step 0: CURRENT-TRUTH 48,697 B, no maintenance. Work unit = NEXT.md FD (BZ/s7416 for the RSP side). No game run (H-live not selected).
Tool: tools/s7507_rsp_ctrl_flow.py. It decodes every ucode image itself from the toml ROM bytes (big-endian words, not the C comments)
and walks the emitted C one instruction at a time. Each step is gated by alignment: a control op must sit under a comment with the same
mnemonic, and a non-control op under a non-control comment.
 R1 cond branches: the branch segment holds only `if (COND) {`, so COND runs before the slot. COND must equal the expected text (beq/bne on
    uint32_t rN, RSP_SIGNED for bgez/bltz/bgtz/blez). The copy target must equal the decoded target, and the slot copy must equal the linear slot.
 R2 jal: `r31 = 0xV+8` comes before the slot, and every return address has a switch case that reaches its label.
 R3 jr/jalr: jump_target is latched before the slot. The 2 slot-writes-rS sites per gfx image (10C4/10D4 `jr $2; negu/ori $2`) read the
    latch, which is correct. 0 jalr. jr sites by register are listed per file.
 R4 0 control ops in a delay slot. 0 resume labels (no file is built with has_overlays). One mtc0 SP_RD_LEN sits in a slot in ucode B,
    which has no overlays, so the DMA runs in both copies.
 R5 COND forms were compiled with rsp.hpp's RSP_SIGNED and checked over 81 edge pairs: 0 mismatches. Mutants were flagged 36/15/36.
 R6 controls on the live main composite, each giving +defects > 0: slot before cond, wrong copy target, diverging copy, unsigned bgez,
    jr latch after the slot, wrong jal ra, dropped `case 0x1090`, splice goto redirected to base. 8/8 PASS.
Result (scratch/s7507_fd.txt):

  Totals: main cond 59 / j 27 / jal 18 / jr 15. B cond 55, plus one `b` (beq $0,$0, emitted as unconditional: correct) / jal 45 / jr 19.
- Live compiled files (CMakeLists: main, B and boot only): 0 defects. The main composite has 133 cond / 57 j / 57 jal / 23 jr across the
  base stream plus 9 spliced streams (CLIP, OVL10/12/14/18/1C/20/24/2C), 86 switch cases and 68 overlay routes.
  The tool classifies (not counts) these deliberate fixups:
  (a) The IMEM-wrap `bgez $2, L_0000` at 1FF0 goes to RS64_UCODE_ENTRY (the old self-restart fixup).
  (b) 6 OVL20 `jal 0x1ED4` go to OVL1C_1ED4, and the byte-0x20 routes to OVL1C_1ED4/1F04 do too. Overlay 0x20's DMA covers only 0x12A0..0x13F7

Boring checks first: (1) the recompiled game code (N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs, 24,264 lui) has 0 `lui 0xA4xx`, so the game never

both halves and queues exactly nbytes at vaddr: equal to hardware iff nbytes&7 == 0 (carry and flag then key on the same sum),
addr 8-aligned, len < 0x40000.

Code read (two sources: ultramodern input.cpp/cont.cpp vs mupen64plus-core game_controller.c in rs64-oracle, and the game's own loads):
- Status: ultramodern writes type 0x0005, status 0x00, errno 0 on port 0; errno 8 and nothing else on ports 1-3 (= libultra
  __osContGetInitData). mupen/hardware report status 0x02 (PAK_CHANGED) with no pak. Game loads of the status array: errno (+3) in
  pollControllerInputs 0x80003048, initMemoryPack 0x80005A48, writeSave* 0x80005CD8/0x80006048, rumble 0x80002CB8/0x80002D7C; type&1 at
  0x8000305C; no load of +2 anywhere -> H-dead, not changed (would be a lib/ edit for a byte nobody reads).

  0x800BF0D0: x / 75.0f (ROM 0x800A622C), y / 80.0f (0x800A6230), clamp to [-1, 1] (0x800A6220/24), dead zone 0.015 (0x800A6228);

## Session 7519 (2026-11-17) — class FP: D-cache store side (write-back + write-allocate dirty lines vs PI DMA); 0 dirty lines under a cart->RDRAM DMA, 0 dirty discards and 0 live rows outside a planted missing writeback on L4 dd1 / L15 dd8 21:9 (~0.9 / 1.3 billion tracked stores), the planted miss is caught (3 dirty-over-DMA rows) and then resolved dead by the game's invalidate-after; FO levels closed

**FO levels fold.** s7518_fo_levels score=0 (L1 dd8 21:9, L7/L10/L12 dd4: stale_load only in ctl, 4/4 alive) -> FO CLOSED 6 levels.
**Question.** On a VR4300 a guest store dirties a 16 B D-cache line that reaches RAM only on writeback / eviction / index op; the port
writes RAM at once. Port and hardware differ if a dirty line meets a PI DMA into the same line (eviction or writeback later puts the
CPU's copy over the DMA bytes, or a load returns it), or if an interior osInvalDCache Hit_Invalidate discards a dirty line (hardware
loses the store). Hypotheses: H-canon (every DMA'd line the CPU stored to is written back before the DMA: wb -> DMA -> inv idiom),
H-dead (dirty-at-DMA lines exist but the invalidate-after discards them before anything reads or evicts them), H-live (a dirty line
survives a DMA, or a discarded store is later read).
**Instrument (one build, logging only; src/main/upstream_compat.cpp s7519 block + librecomp ultra_translation.cpp hook).** Per tracked
16 B line (the s7518 bitmap; wb'd lines now marked too) dirty state 0 clean / 1 D / 2 X dirty-over-DMA / 3 L lost, driven by guest stores
(s5798 store hook, ROGUESQ_STORE_DIAG=1, routed exclusively to s7519_store under ROGUESQ_S7518_STALEWATCH=1), osWritebackDCache /
osWritebackDCacheAll (rs64_s7519_wbev), osInvalDCache (edge lines Hit_Writeback_Invalidate, interior Hit_Invalidate, n >= 8192 index
writeback-invalidate) and PI DMA. Rows: dma_over_dirty, discard, live_wb, live_load, live_lost, st_on_S; [s7519-sum] counters.
Ctl ROGUESQ_CACHE_SHAPE_CTL_WB=<k>: the first wb at/after the k-th that starts at a past DMA address and covers a dirty line is dropped.
Scorer tools/s7519_store_side.py --controls --ctl (7 synthetic PASS).
**Dead ends (recorded).** Run 1: the store hook returned 0, so the s5798 dispatcher fell through into its fixed table with a marked
address -> SIGSEGV in rs64_s5798_st (loadTxtFile), both arms (same failure as s7475 v1); fixed by returning 1 always. Run 2
(scratch/s7519_fp): ctl dropped wb k=600 at 0x8018FB70 (a CPU-written buffer no DMA follows) -> 0 rows, ctl unproven; the ctl was
then restricted to wbs of past DMA slots.
**Run 3** (scratch/s7519_fp3, g1e_owner_quiet_arms HOLD=120, both alive, 0 VI stalls): L4 dd1 st_seen=905.7M, wb_clean=26.6M,
L15 dd8 21:9 st_seen=1312.0M, wb_clean=39.8M; outside ctl dma_over_dirty=0, discard=0, live_wb=live_load=live_lost=0, st_on_S=0,
pending_over_dma=0, pending_lost=0 (pending_dirty 641 / 23,604 = ordinary dirty data). Ctl (both arms landed on slot 0x801B4ED0+0x104,
k=783 / 773): exactly 3 dma_over_dirty rows, all ctl=1, stores from zmemcpy (0x80018F30) and rs_free (0x80001D3C); all 3 then
dd_inv_ok (the interior Hit_Invalidate after the DMA discards the cache copy, so the DMA bytes win as in the port) = positive control
PASS and evidence that even a missed wb is dead in this idiom unless the dirty line is an unaligned edge.
DISCRIMINATION: selects H-canon (every DMA slot the CPU stores to is written back first; 0 dirty-over-DMA outside ctl), with the idiom
also H-dead-robust (inv-after discards a dirty-over-DMA line, ctl). Refutes H-live for stores (0 live rows, 0 discards; the MusyX stream
ring takes no CPU stores after its allocation invalidate). Gaps (stated): stores to a line before its first marking are unseen; no
eviction model; 120 s per arm. FO+FP close the libultra replaced-function surface (s7518 census). Levels soak queued (s7519_fp_levels).

## Session 7520 (2026-11-17) — class FQ: executed CPU code bytes vs the recompiled image; regen ELF == ROM over every recompiled function extent, and at run time 0 code words differ from the ROM, 0 overlay calls into non-resident bytes and 0 stale func_map dispatches on L4 dd1 / L15 dd8 21:9 (planted code flips caught on both arms); FP levels closed
HYPOTHESIS-ID: executed-code-bytes-census.
**FP levels fold.** s7519_fp_levels rc=0 score=0 (L1 dd8 21:9, L7/L10/L12 dd4, 4/4 alive, ctl ok) -> FP CLOSED 6 levels.
**Question.** A static recompile runs the code the ROM held at regen time; a VR4300 runs whatever bytes sit in RAM when the I-cache
fetches them. Port and hardware differ if the game writes code at run time (patching, self-modifying code, decompressed code), if an
overlay's RAM text differs from the ROM image N64Recomp compiled, or if the port dispatches into an overlay whose bytes are not
resident (the 3 overlays mission/menu/cinematic share 0x800A5130). Hypotheses: H-canon (RAM text == ROM wherever code runs), H-dead
(differences only in words never executed), H-live (the port runs different instructions than hardware).
**Offline line (tools/s7520_elf_vs_rom.py, new, rc 0).** Every FuncEntry extent of recomp_overlays.inl (5 sections, 2542 funcs,
304,259 words): regen ELF bytes == build/rogue_squadron.z64 bytes. Ctl: one byte flipped per section -> exactly 1 DIFF each (5/5).
**Runtime instrument (one build; librecomp overlays.cpp s7520 block, patch exported).** ROGUESQ_S7520_CODEWATCH=1: at every
osViSwapBuffer, osInvalICache and overlay registration, compare the RAM words of every FuncEntry extent of the main sections and of
each overlay section with the ROM; log every address entering/leaving the differing set ([s7520-w]); overlay state vs the section
registered last; every get_function into 0x800A5130-0x8010B6D0 checked against the registered section's func_map (gf_stale /
gf_funcdiff) and the called function's bytes vs ROM (exec_diff); every PI DMA into main code (dma_main) or the overlay window
([s7520-odma], does the ROM offset equal some section's own image at its link address?). Ctl ROGUESQ_S7520_CTL=1: swap 600 flips one
byte of a main code word (0x800599C4), restored at 660; after swap 900 the first overlay call flips a byte inside the called function
(0x800B3654), restored once caught. Scorer tools/s7520_code_bytes.py --controls --ctl (9 synthetic PASS): changed words classified
DATA (ELF OBJECT symbol, data_gap_* / renamed data gap, or a non-code splat subsegment in roguesquadron.yaml) vs CODE.
**Dead ends (recorded).** v1 (scratch/s7520_fq) logged only state transitions: main was "bad" from swap 2 (17 words, first rngSeed
0x80003470, an OBJECT inside setRngSeed's 0x20 extent) so the main ctl was invisible; v2 logs the per-address set. The first v2 scoring
called 82 / 65 words CODE because the ELF sizes audioCompandS16 (0x8009DD7C, 29,620 B) and __OSGlobalIntMask (0x80039110, 19,984 B)

**Run** (scratch/s7520_fq2, g1e_owner_quiet_arms HOLD=120, both alive, 0 VI stalls): L4 dd1 / L15 dd8 21:9 6,902 checks each; changed
words 269 / 283, all DATA (rngSeed, main .data under audioCompandS16 / __OSGlobalIntMask, data_gap_800CC3D4 menu, fake_func_800AF6A8 =
data_gap cinematic), 0 CODE outside ctl; overlay get_function 428,183 / 360,939, each byte-checked: exec_diff 0 outside ctl,
gf_stale 0, gf_funcdiff 0; dma_main 0; 55 overlay-window DMAs each = a section's own ROM image (mission 27 incl. the boot worker's
0x80000D04 preload of the mission tail ROM 0x101000 -> 0x80100400 n=0xCE00 before the only osInvalICache, menu 22, cinematic 6).

no overlay dispatch into non-resident bytes); refutes H-live; the data-in-text words are H-dead by type (data symbols / data
subsegments; recompiled code never executes them). Gaps (stated): load_overlay overwrites func_map entries but never erases a replaced
overlay's leftovers (0 calls reached one here, gf_stale 0); main code direct calls are covered by the per-swap byte compare, not per call;

## Session 7521 (2026-11-17) — class FR: executed RSP code bytes vs the RSPRecomp images; 2 task tuples, boot/text 0 diff bytes, every IMEM DMA a ROM image that a compiled composite or hand route covers; overlay 0 runs 8 bytes lower on hardware than the boot copy main compiled, but the one instruction whose meaning changes (path A `j 0x1E5C`) is never taken; FQ levels closed

**Fold.** s7520_fq_levels score 0 (L1 dd8 21:9, L7/L10/L12 dd4; 0 exec_diff / gf_stale / dma_main, both ctls caught, 4/4 alive) -> FQ CLOSED 6 levels.

**Question.** The port selects RSP code by task TYPE only (main.cpp get_rsp_microcode / rs64_run_lle_gfx) and skips every IMEM DMA
(rsp.hpp). A real RSP runs whatever the task's ucode_boot / ucode / ucode_data and the ucode's own IMEM DMAs bring from RDRAM.
Hypotheses: H-canon (all those bytes == ROM images RSPRecomp compiled), H-dead (some differ only where the compiled path never looks),
H-live (game patches ucode, a second ucode, or an IMEM image no toml compiled).

**Instrument** (one build): src/rsp/s7521_ucode_watch.cpp, ROGUESQ_S7521_UCODEWATCH=1. Per SP task (hooks: librecomp rsp.cpp run_task
= audio; main.cpp rs64_run_lle_gfx = gfx; **gfx tasks never pass run_task**, first run saw gfx=0): distinct tuple rows; boot/text/data
RDRAM vs ROM (main segment ROM 0x1000..0xA5D30 <- 0x80000400; ranges past the segment end compared on the ROM-backed prefix, TAIL row).
Per IMEM DMA (rsp.hpp skip branch): source bytes vs ROM, distinct (mem, dram, len). Hardware window model: gfx task start = boot image;
DMA into 0x1DB0 = that image; at every L_1DB0 entry (rs64_e9prov_l1db0_reset) and branch (rs64_inline_probe_trigen_branch, 0..5) count
by resident image (needs ROGUESQ_G1E_PROBES=1 so the probe TU runs). Ctl ROGUESQ_S7521_CTL=1: gfx task 600 flips boot+0x10 / text+0x100 /
data+0x40 around the compare; first IMEM DMA after gfx 900 flips a source byte; after gfx 700 one forced "RDP busy" DPC_CURRENT read
(dpc_bridge rs64_dpc_current_read) inside L_1DB0 must produce path A. Scorer tools/s7521_ucode_bytes.py --controls --ctl (static check +
7/7 synthetic).

**Static.** The factor5_rsp / factor5b / boot toml text images == ROM at 0x25610 / 0x9ABE0 / 0x831D0 = the task ucode addresses.

**Run** (scratch/s7521_fr, g1e_owner_quiet_arms HOLD=120, both alive, 0 VI stalls; L4 dd1, L15 dd8 21:9): score 0 both arms.
- 2 tuples only: gfx boot 800825D0/D0 ucode 80024A10/1000 data 80038D00/800; audio same boot, ucode 80099FE0/1000 data 800A4E00/800.
  Type-only dispatch is sound.
- boot + text: 0 differing bytes in ~6.3k gfx + ~5.7k audio tasks per arm.
- ucode_data: differing bytes are CPU-written fields (gfx DMEM 0x33F, 0x404..0x40F; audio 0x320.. = rodata main/A5D20). Same RDRAM on
  hardware; none in the DMEM dispatch tables the tomls baked as extra_indirect_branch_targets. Audio declares 0x800 but only 0x330 is
  main segment; the rest is the overlay window at 0x800A5130 (hardware reads the same bytes).
- IMEM DMAs: 3.77M (L4) / 24.9M (L15), all ROM bytes, 12 distinct images, each == a compiled composite (main text, ovl4/10/12/14/18/
  1C/2C at 0x1DB0, ovl20/24 at 0x12A0) except two: overlay 0x28 (ROM 0x27348, 7 words: addiu $17,32; restore-DMA main text+0x220 ->
  0x12A0 len 0x330; j 0x122C with ra 0x10D8) = the fixup 6c hand route, and **overlay 0** (ROM 0x26348, 0xD4 bytes, table DMEM 0x7C).
- **Overlay 0 placement.** The boot text DMA puts ROM 0x26340 at 0x1DB0 (two nops, then the init code); overlay 0 puts ROM 0x26348
  there, so the same code sits 8 bytes lower. Relative branches agree; resident j/jal targets agree; the absolute `j 0x1E5C` (path A:
  DPC idle-check passes but DPC_CURRENT != DPC_END, i.e. RDP still busy) lands past mtc0 DPC_START/END in the overlay copy and on them
  in the boot copy. main.c compiled the boot copy (L_1E5C = mtc0s) and the port routes DMEM 0x153 == 0 to it. Window model: **all
  6288 / 6329 L_1DB0 entries ran with overlay 0 resident**, so hardware always runs the shifted copy. But path A (b5) was taken 0 times:
  every entry took b3 (DPC_CURRENT == 0: rs64_dpc_reset zeroes it per task), going L_1E48 -> mtc0s in both copies. H-dead. The forced
  ctl took path A once per arm (seen as win=ovl0 ev=5), the game stayed alive: the port's extra START=END=$4 submits an empty range.
  Not changed: honouring hardware's skip would leave g_rsp_dpc_start at the previous task's start and the port's submit(start,end)
  would resubmit it; it only matters if the DPC model ever reports a busy RDP at task start.
- All 5 ctls caught on both arms (text 1, boot 1, data rows, imem 1, l1db0 1).

**Rules out:** a second ucode / patched ucode text / boot (H-live text), uncompiled IMEM images in the 0x1DB0 and 0x12A0 windows,
dispatch-table drift in ucode_data. **Gap:** the 0x12A0 window (ovl20, ovl24, ovl28's restore) is not modelled at port dispatch time
(FD audited the routes statically). Levels soak queued: scratch/agent/soak_queue/s7521_fr_levels.sh (L1 dd8 21:9, L7/L10/L12 dd4).

## Session 7522 (2026-11-17) — class FS: hardware IMEM residency vs the port's overlay route at every RSP dispatch; 179M (L4 dd1) / 377M (L15 dd8 21:9) dispatches all run the resident code except FR's known L_1DB0-under-overlay-0 case, planted 8-byte model shift caught on both arms; FR levels closed after a scorer fix

**Fold s7521_fr_levels (rc=1).** The one LIVE row was `log_l10.txt: no l1db0 window rows`. The rows are there: an `[s2020-svc]`
entry/exit pair from another thread landed between the last `[s7521-sum]` and the three `[s7521-l1db0]` window rows, and the
scorer read a fixed `L[si+1:si+4]` slice. tools/s7521_ucode_bytes.py now takes the first row per window in the 200 lines after the
sum (2 new synthetic cases: interleaved clean = 0, interleaved path A = 1; 9/9 pass). Re-score: L1/L7/L10/L12 live=0, ctl 5/5 each,
ovl0 b5 = 0 everywhere -> **FR CLOSED 6 levels.** Side datum: L10 does ~4 IMEM DMAs per task against ~3.4k on L1/L7/L12 (bytes
checked 0.2 G vs 15-19 G). L10 is the cloud level with no terrain grid (CURRENT-TRUTH run recipes), so this is benign.

**FS hypotheses.** H-canon: the code the port routes to equals the code hardware has resident at every dispatch. H-dead: mismatches
only where the bytes are equal. H-live: the port runs another overlay's code. The port picks overlay code by DMEM 0x153 in the
do_indirect_jump switch, while hardware runs whatever the last IMEM DMA left. Windows can overlap partially: ovl20 (0x158 bytes)
is longer than ovl24 (0xE4) at 0x12A0, so a per-window model would miss leftovers. The model is per word.

**Instrument** (one build). src/rsp/s7521_ucode_watch.cpp: `isrc[1024]` = RDRAM source of every gfx IMEM word, reset per gfx task
and updated in the IMEM-DMA hook before FR's ctl branch. `rs64_s7522_disp(target, 0x153)` counts (target, 0x153, isrc[target],
ctl). `rs64_s7522_ovl28(src)` models the restore DMA the ovl28 hand route skips. ovl28 decoded from ROM: `addiu r17,0x20; lw r2,0x10(r1);
ori r3,0x12A0; ori r4,0x32F; addiu r2,0x220; j 0x122C; ori r31,0x10D8` = 0x330 bytes into 0x12A0. tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py block
"s7522 imem residency" inserts both calls, gated on rs64_s7521_on. Rows dump at each sum, before FR's rows. Ctl (ROGUESQ_S7521_CTL=1):
after gfx task 800, the next real overlay DMA into 0x1DB0 (not ovl0) is modelled 8 bytes off until the next 0x1DB0 DMA.
Scorer tools/s7522_imem_residency.py --controls (7/7 synthetic). It parses the generated switch (86 cases, 74 0x153 rules, brace and
brace-less forms, OVL2C mode 0, 0x28 hand route) into the compiled composite each (target, 0x153) runs. It byte-compares that image
with ROM at the modelled source, from the target to the end of the resident DMA extent.

**Result** (L4 dd1 + L15 dd8 21:9, HOLD 120, both alive, 0 stalls). L4: 178.9M dispatches, 254 keys. L15: 376.6M, 252 keys. Every
key is canon except L_1DB0 with overlay 0 resident (6,285 / 6,309), which is FR's placement case, H-dead by FR's path-A count.
0x12A0-window dispatches: 57M / 134M. These include 0x153=0x28 routed to main (60M / 120M; resident bytes = main after the
modelled restore, src28 always 0x024C30) and 0x153=0x04 routed into the ovl24/ovl20 composites (canon: the 0x12A0 window still holds
that overlay while ovl4 sits at 0x1DB0). 0 rs64_clip_stray, 0 unhandled, 0 unmodelled. Ctl: perturbed ovl4 DMA (0x025820) at gfx
1639/1643 -> 92 live dispatches on each arm -> caught. FR scorer on the same logs: live=0, ctl 5/5, after a second fix. The FR
ovl28 known_route string match broke because the s7522 call now sits inside the route, so the scorer strips that call before
matching. **FS H-canon on L4/L15.**
**Discrimination:** selects H-canon, refutes H-live (0 non-resident dispatches in 555M with the planted shift caught) and leaves H-dead
only for the FR L_1DB0 case. Next discriminator: the FS levels soak, then class FT (DPC/SP status read model, NEXT.md).
**Rules out:** the port running a stale or other overlay at any dispatch, ovl20 leftovers under the ovl24 route, a wrong ovl28 restore
source. **Gaps:** a later partial DMA inside a resident run is not re-split (the compare assumes the run is contiguous from the
target). Direct (non-dispatch) entries into a window are covered only for L_1DB0 (FR).
Levels soak queued: scratch/agent/soak_queue/s7522_fs_levels.sh (L1 dd8 21:9, L7/L10/L12 dd4; score = max(FS, FR)).

## Session 7523 (2026-11-17) — class FT: finite-rate RDP model for the RSP DPC registers; path A and every ring wait run live, forwarding stays exact, control flow H-dead; same-task ring late-rewrite found, writer open
HYPOTHESIS-ID: rsp-dpc-register-model.
Fold: s7522_fs_levels score 0 (L1 dd8 21:9, L7/L10/L12 dd4; FS canon, FR live 0, ctl 92 live per arm, 4/4 alive) -> FS CLOSED 6 levels.
Unit (NEXT.md class FT). Boring-first check: s7094/s7095 had already closed the RSP cop0 + DPC register model, but only against an
INSTANT RDP (s7095 shadow: END loads CURRENT then consumes at once). The open part is a finite-rate RDP: a task that starts while the
previous list still drains (CURRENT != END), which makes the L_1DB0 resume path (b5, j L_1E5C) and the wait loops L_114C (START_VALID),
L_115C, L_116C (CURRENT inside the next chunk) and L_1E48 live. Hypotheses: H-canon (same branches), H-dead (branches differ, output
identical), H-live (a wait is skipped or the RDP would read different bytes than RT64 got).
Instrument (one build): opt-in ROGUESQ_S7523_SLOWRDP=<bytes per DPC poll>[,<bytes per task gap>] (new src/rsp/s7523_slow_rdp.cpp;
hooks in include/rsp_dpc_macros.h END/STATUS reads + START/END writes, dpc_bridge.cpp rs64_dpc_current_read + rs64_dpc_reset).
Every DPC read is served by a queue model of the RDP (ranges per END write; START binds a new list; STATUS = CBUF_READY | DMA/CMD_BUSY
while queued | START_VALID while a bound START is not yet begun); END persists across tasks. Each queued range is snapshotted after
the bridge submit; when the model consumes it, bytes are compared (OVERWRITE = what a slow hardware RDP would read differently from
RT64). Ctl: every 997th range gets one planted snapshot flip. A mutex was needed: ucode B on the RSP task thread also reads
DPC_STATUS (first run aborted, "pointer being freed was not allocated" in consume, concurrent with the gfx thread).
Second gate (DP-gated arm): the port raises DP at FULL_SYNC forward time; hardware only once the RDP consumes it, so the gated model
drains at each forwarded FULL_SYNC (rs64_dpc_get_cumulative_fullsyncs) at the next END or task reset.
Runs (tools/g1e_owner_quiet_arms.zsh, HOLD 120, + ROGUESQ_S7096_FWD=c, S7521_UCODEWATCH, G1E_PROBES; scratch/s7523_ft/):
| arm | alive | entry busy | b5 path A | busy polls | escapes | s7096 MAIN missing/dup/order | over bytes (same/next task) | ctl |
| L4 dd1 8 B/poll ungated | 120 s | 6631/6795 | 2 (b2 6309) | 190M | 0 | 0/0/0 of 1.50 GB | 12.0M / 11.1M | 45159/45160 |
| L15 dd8 21:9 64+4096 ungated | 120 s | 1929/6356 | 0 (b4 2) | 68M | 0 | 0/0/0 of 2.37 GB | 109k / 17k | 50465/50465 |
| L4 gated | 120 s | 0/6788 | 0 | 86M | 0 | 0/0/0 of 1.49 GB | 22.7M / 0 | 45037/45041 |
| L15 gated | 120 s | 0/6355 | 0 | 67M | 0 | 0/0/0 of 2.38 GB | 103k / 0 | 50525/50525 |
s7096 CTL caught 6/6 (L4) and 5/6 (L15: one ctl task lacked one mutation kind; s7096's own ctl, not this instrument).
Readings: (1) every wait loop exits on model progress (0 deadlock escapes in 330M+ busy polls), so the ucode's DPC protocol is
satisfied under a slow RDP as compiled; (2) the resume path is structurally near-unreachable on this game: b2 (END below the task's
buffer start) sends ~every task to the fresh path whatever the timing, path A ran 2 times in the most pessimistic arm and those tasks
forwarded exactly (tasks_bad 0); (3) under DP gating the RDP is idle at every task entry, which is what the port's per-task
DPC reset reports. Ungated cross-task overwrites were SET_SCISSOR (0xED) commands at fixed ring addresses rewritten by the next task
(snap ED000000 02C70700 -> ED238000 02A38700): an artifact of an RDP lagging past the CPU's completion signal, gone under gating.
OPEN (single-source, not yet explained): same-task late rewrites persist under gating (L4 8 B/poll 1.5% of consumed bytes, L15
64 B/poll 0.004%; strongly rate-dependent; e.g. L4 0x7344C8.. triangle coefficient bytes zeroed, L15 0x714BE0.. 46/56 bytes changed).
The writer is unnamed: the RSP later in the same task (ring overwrite the ucode's wait should forbid), the concurrent CPU thread, or a
bridge commit. The port never shows it (it forwards at END time), so it is only a would-be divergence for a much slower RDP.
DISCRIMINATION: this selects H-dead and refutes H-live for task-entry control flow and wait-loop termination and for forwarding coverage (two lines: ungated/gated arms x 2 levels,
s7096 exact + l1db0 branch counts); for ring content nothing is selected yet (writer open). Next discriminator: re-compare queued ranges at RSP task end vs next task start (changed at task end selects H-rsp-race; changed only after it selects H-cpu/H-bridge). No fix; instrument default off.
Next: NEXT.md (split the late-rewrite writer: re-snapshot every queued range at the RSP task end and at the next task start).

## Session 7524 (2026-11-17) — class FT writer named: the gfx ucode's own ring DMA, because the port's osSpTaskLoad skips retail _VirtualToPhysicalTask (KSEG0 pointers in DMEM kill the L_116C/L_115C wrap waits); opt-in ROGUESQ_S7524_V2P=1 removes every late rewrite under the slow-RDP model

Work unit: name the writer of s7523's same-task ring late-rewrites under ROGUESQ_S7523_SLOWRDP (DP-gated). Hypotheses: H-rsp-race
(gfx ucode overwrites queued ring bytes later in the task), H-cpu (concurrent CPU thread), H-bridge (dpc_bridge commit/edit after submit).
Instrument (one build, src/rsp/s7523_slow_rdp.cpp, same env): queue kept as merged segments; every RSP DMEM->RDRAM DMA (s7094 hook,
src/rsp/s7094_dma_shape.cpp now also armed by ROGUESQ_S7523_SLOWRDP) marks the queued not-yet-consumed bytes it overwrites (tch 1 gfx /
2 audio); each consume-time mismatch byte is attributed rsp_gfx / rsp_aud / resid; every 256th END the whole queue is scanned before and
after rsp_dpc_submit (include/rsp_dpc_macros.h rs64_s7523_pre_submit) so new untouched mismatches inside submit = bridge. Positive
controls: DMA coverage (every pushed ring byte must have been written by a gfx RSP DMA since its last push), the s7523 planted flips.
Run A (L4 dd1, SLOWRDP=8,0, S7096_FWD, 120 s, scratch/s7524_ft): alive, over_bytes 22,307,211 in 1.52 GB (as s7523), **att_rsp_gfx
22,307,211 = 100%, att_rsp_aud 0, att_resid 0**, bridge 0 hits in 176,533 pre/post pairs; ctl cov 1.0000 (1.52 GB), planted 45,319/45,321.
-> H-rsp-race selected, H-cpu and H-bridge refuted. Example: ring wrapped to 0x720000, old lap 0x7344C8-0x73FF60 still queued,
CURRENT read 0x7344C8, ucode then DMAs 176 B at 0x734448 (CURRENT inside the write) after ONE CURRENT read. The L_116C predicate
(build/factor5_ucode/factor5_ucode_recompiled.c: proceed if dest-CURRENT >= 0, spin while CURRENT in (dest,dest+len]) should spin there.
Run B (60 s, + raw DMA address): dma_gfx_hi8 = 11,098,663 / 11,098,663 -> every gfx ring DMA address carries KSEG0 bits, so
dest(0x80xxxxxx) - CURRENT(24-bit) is always a positive int32 and the wait never spins (L_115C beq CURRENT==base never matches either;
s7523's "b2 routes every task fresh" is the same: the task buffer start is KSEG0, END is 24-bit).

N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_8.c: ucode, ucode_data, dram_stack, output_buff, output_buff_size, data_ptr, yield_data_ptr); the port
replaces it with osSpTaskLoad_recomp -> rs64_m5_port_task_load and rs64_run_lle_gfx pokes the raw KSEG0 fields into DMEM 0xFC0.
The value is not legitimate on hardware (retail DMEM sees physical pointers). Fix (opt-in, default unchanged): ROGUESQ_S7524_V2P=1 in
rs64_run_lle_gfx converts the same 7 fields (only 0x80000000-0xBFFFFFFF) in the DMEM copy, guest task untouched.

sections 2/3/4 all link at 0x800A5130 (sizes 0x665A0 / 0x283F0 / 0xB810). load_overlay only inserted the new section's func_map keys and
emplace_back'd loaded_sections, so every function start of the previous overlay that is not also a start in the new one stayed live (a call
there would run the old overlay's C instead of failing) and loaded_sections grew one duplicate per swap.

this game's chunked-DMA route through pi.cpp never calls). Values are legitimate function pointers of a non-resident overlay, not corruption.
Fix (overlays.cpp rs64_s7528_pre_load/post_load, patch exported): before registering, unload every loaded section whose [ram, ram+size)
overlaps the new one, same body as unload_overlays (erase each func key, reset section_addresses, erase loaded_sections). Default on;
ROGUESQ_S7528_EVICT=0 = old. Census per load: [s7528] pre (evicted_secs/funcs) + post (stale_window_entries, loaded_sections);

## Session 7543 (2026-11-17) — class GD CLOSED: no port yield splits two dependent guest-struct stores (49 replacement functions, 1 guest critical section, 13 cop0 Status writes, 51 injected yields; tools/s7543_gd_census.py exit 0, controls 9/9)

Soak fold: nothing new to score. s7540_rwait_cost voided again (3/5, human/lock/sleep), still queued; fold rule unchanged (NEXT.md s7542).

Question (from s7542 GC): guest threads run one at a time, so the remaining exposure is atomicity. Does any yield the port makes
fall between two dependent guest-struct stores, so another guest thread sees a half-updated OSMesgQueue / OSThread / OSTimer /
OSIoMesg / cont buffer that hardware never shows? Hypotheses: H-atomic (no yield between dependent stores), H-yield-safe (a yield,
but the struct is consistent there), H-torn (a real split).

Boring check first: `__osDisableInt_recomp` / `__osRestoreInt_recomp` are no-ops (ultra_translation.cpp:193-204), so the port
never models interrupt masking. Hardware only switches threads inside an OS call (block / wake a higher priority) or at an interrupt,
and interrupts cannot land inside a DisableInt region. So the census needs three sections, not one.

Tool: tools/s7543_gd_census.py (reuses the GB/GC/FZ engines; the GC H-guest-thread set + every runtime function calling a yield primitive).
- A, 49 runtime functions: guest-struct stores (S) and yields (Y) in body order, one level of callee followed (a call to a yielding
  or storing runtime function counts as Y/S). 36 H-atomic (no yield, or tail yields only). 6 H-yield-safe, each with a named span
  and invariant: do_send blocks in `while (MQ_IS_FULL(mq))` (only the sender is queued, slot/first/validCount untouched, re-read after
  resume); do_recv `while (MQ_IS_EMPTY)` + the s7195 park, which never returns; _thread_func (first park precedes guest work; the exit
  store runs only while it still owns the OSThread and holds the token, because a destroyed thread's context is cleared before its wake
  signal and the dying host thread only reads); osStopThread_recomp (self-stop branch returns at once); osStartThread (branch split:
  the state store is the init else-branch); osSendMesg (dup-drop yields and returns -1; the later on_result store is the host-side
  s4260 Ent table). 7 H-def hand-off primitives (run_next_thread(_and_wait), resume_thread_tagged/_and_wait, wait_for_resumed,
  swap_to_thread, check_running_queue): nothing touches guest RAM between `running.signal()` and the caller's `running.wait()`, so the
  outgoing host thread cannot overlap the incoming one.
- B, generated code (../N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_*.c): exactly one DisableInt..RestoreInt region (funcs_24.c:7835-7869,
  musyxSynthFrame_s4562_impl), no call inside. All 13 cop0_status_write sites (7 math functions in funcs_4.c, 0x80018860-0x800196B4)
  resolve by a backward constant resolver to SR|0x04000000 or SR&~0x04000000: the FR FPU-mode toggle, not IE/EXL.
- C, 51 yields the port injected into guest code (yield_self*, rs64_preempt_point, check_running_queue, osYieldThread_recomp ... in
  31 functions: audio waits, video thread, SI service, menus, JPEG decoder) all lie outside every B region, so each is a point where
  hardware could also switch threads (by interrupt).

Controls (--controls 9/9): planted rs64_preempt_point between do_send's slot store and validCount++ -> do_send H-torn-OPEN; planted
swap_to_thread after osSetThreadPri's priority store (callee followed) -> OPEN; do_send rule deleted -> OPEN; planted guest read before
wait_for_resumed's running.wait() -> FAIL-check; fixture with a call inside a DisableInt region -> B OPEN; fixture IE-bit Status write
(resolved ('SR',1,0)) -> B OPEN; fixture yield inside the region -> C OPEN and after it -> H-int-enabled; rule-less A -> all 6
yield-safe rows OPEN; live 49/14/51 rows, all 7 hand-off primitives present, 0 OPEN/FAIL.
First live run had 4 B OPEN rows: the clear side builds ~FR via `nor` of a register loaded earlier, which the first 14-line window
missed. The resolver now follows straight-line register assignments within the function, and all 13 resolve. Two controls also
failed at first (the mutation hit osCreateThread's priority store; wait_for_resumed was not in the row set). Both are fixed and

- **Arm A** owner recipe L4 dd4 16:9 FPS60 HOLD 600 (g1e_owner_quiet_arms, a4): footprint 999 MB @60 s -> 1214 @121 -> 1748 @546,
  linear ~1.25 MB/s in steady flight; malloc'd 449 MB @200 s -> 894 MB @560 s. leaks: only the plant. So the growth is REACHABLE
  (H-cache), not orphaned. tag alive 1, crash 0, vi_stalls30s 0.

  crash 0): malloc'd 623 MB @300 s -> 1013 MB @600 s (~1.3 MB/s) — the same per-second rate as steady flight, so it tracks time,
  not mission loads (H-leak per load not separable yet; masked by this growth).
- **Arm C** (naming): same recipe as A, HOLD 360, MallocStackLogging=lite (heap then labels blocks by allocating function), `heap -s`
  at 120 s and 330 s, diffed by tools/s7585_heapdiff.py: +253 MB in 210 s, of which 153,584 AGXG17XFamilyCommandBuffer (+ its
  _impl and ResourceGroupUsage, same count) = 260 MB, ~731/s. Everything else < 4 MB.
- **Writer:** lib/rt64/src/contrib/plume/plume_metal.cpp MetalCommandQueue::executeCommandLists creates one autoreleased
  `commandBufferWithUnretainedReferences()` "Wait Command Buffer" per call (ROGUESQ_MTL_SKIP_EMPTY_WAIT is off by default, so on
  every call) on a long-lived RT64 thread with no autorelease pool: the thread's implicit pool never drains, so every buffer stays
  alive forever. Legitimate object, never released. ORIGIN: plume upstream code path (no pool in this function), not an rs64 edit.
- **Fix:** NS::AutoreleasePool around the function body, default on; ROGUESQ_MTL_WAITPOOL=0 restores the old behaviour. Exported
  (submodule-patches/rt64-plume.patch). cmake --build build OK.

  `mach_thread_self()` in g_g1b_thread_port[k] for every guest thread and never released it. mach_thread_self adds a user ref to the
  thread's port; when the host thread exits (several guest threads per mission load), libpthread drops its own ref and ours turns
  into a dead name. Not a legitimate long-lived reference: the only reader ([g1b-gt], events.cpp) skips a slot when thread_info fails,

  is bounded at 64 names, about 7 load cycles).

  leaked uref per ms on its own thread. It now caches the port once. submodule-patches/N64ModernRuntime.patch refreshed.

**Boring first.** Plumbing already existed: ultramodern __osMotorAccess -> input_callbacks.set_rumble, which was

s7516 (class FM) had already shown with ROGUESQ_PAK_SHAPE_CTL=1 that reporting a Rumble Pak makes the game pulse ~30 Hz and
that osPfs* (Controller Pak saves) is only reached on save device 2, never on our EEPROM device 1 -> reporting a pak is save-safe.

get_connected_device_info reports RumblePak unless ROGUESQ_RUMBLE=0. set_rumble(ch 0) records on/off edges (mutex, 512 cap).
rs64_rumble_tick() runs at the end of poll_input (the thread that owns `controller`, so no open/close race and no extra thread;
a guest that stops polling lets the last 150 ms call expire): duty = on-fraction of the last 100 ms, s = (0.25+0.75*duty)*
ROGUESQ_RUMBLE_SCALE (0..2, clamp 1), SDL_GameControllerRumble(lo=s, hi=0.6 s, 150 ms) on a >2% change or every 50 ms, (0,0,0)

L12 -> no game rumble event there; the round-1 build had no injection, so its zero vpad count was not yet a result.

## Session 7635 (2026-11-19) — walker fusion landed (default on): spike + region bodies in one walk, equivalence proven same-run (0 live late writes / 703M commands, injected 21/21), saving only ~0.8 ms/s
- Change: src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp. rs64_spike_scan / rs64_region_scan loops split into per-command `body(a) -> len` lambdas
  (continue/break -> return len/0); rs64_spike_scan takes an optional region-body callback run after its own body on each
  command; rs64_region_scan(lo, hi, fused) runs its prologue then drives the spike walk with its body. Dispatch in
  rs64_dpc_record_submit_impl: ROGUESQ_S7634_FUSE default 1; 0 = old two walks; tog = old on odd GLUE_TOG=3 seconds; chk/inj =

  or G5B_FRAME_EARLY=1 (recorder sits between the two walks).

  a, looks ahead only at op bytes and 0x2F words (skyish), and writes command a or late the w1 of an earlier 0x2E (DD_SKYZ put).
  Runtime check covers the late-write half.

## Session 7640 (2026-11-19) — class AT (AppKit thread affinity) audit: Main Thread Checker + static census, 1 live off-main call (RT64 NFD_Init on Gfx Thread), fixed default on

NEXT.md: no owner report, so a new host-side idiom-class audit. Class AT = Objective-C/AppKit calls reached off the main
thread (s7639 ST covered SDL only). Hypotheses: H-clean (every AppKit use is main-only or guarded) vs H-defect (>=1 live
off-main AppKit call).

Ground truth not from our runtime: Apple's Main Thread Checker (Xcode libMainThreadChecker.dylib via DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES;
reports every AppKit API on a background thread with a backtrace). Runner scratch/s7640/run.zsh: boot with
ROGUESQ_BIND_PANEL_TEST=1 until the F6 panel draws (~50 s), +10 s, SIGKILL. One game at a time.
Pre-fix run (existing binary): exactly 1 report, `-[NSApplication activationPolicy]`, Thread name: Gfx Thread, backtrace
NFD_Init <- RT64::Application::Application <- recomp::RT64Context ctor <- create_render_context <- gfx_thread_func.
RT64's FileDialog::initialize calls nativefiledialog's NFD_Init (nfd_cocoa.m: [NSApplication sharedApplication],
activationPolicy, setActivationPolicy if Prohibited) from the Application ctor, which ultramodern runs on the Gfx Thread.

ORIGIN: writer = upstream RT64 (Application ctor -> FileDialog::initialize), not game data. The call is legitimate on
Windows/Linux; on macOS it is an AppKit read (and potential policy write) on the wrong thread: a race on NSApplication state,
no observed crash. NFD_Quit (Application dtor, same thread) is an AppKit setter with the same problem at teardown.
Fix (lib/rt64 src/gui/rt64_file_dialog.cpp, default on; ROGUESQ_S7640_AT=0 = old direct calls): when off the main thread,

Issuer: guest thread id 1 carries ~99% of PI DMAs and every dd4 overlap (tid 2: 0; tid 0: a few). The ra field read 0 on every

Example: DL 0x1B04D8 reads 0x110 B at 0x1950A0 while a 256-B ROM chunk (0x4AED20) lands at 0x195190.

What it shows: the s7645 overlap is not port timing on retail settings. At dd1 the game never refills bytes the current or
previous gfx task read, although PI DMAs still land mid-task as often; at dd4 it refills them thousands of times per 120 s,
and in ~40-100% of stale cases the same task reads both the old and the new bytes. Rules out H-live as stated (timing alone)
and H-retail (dd4 has no retail). New hypothesis H-slot-recycle: the level-data chunk cache filled by thread 1 is sized for the
retail cell window; the dd>1 window references more chunks than it holds, so slots are evicted and refilled while a display
list still uses them -> wrong geometry for a frame = G5b candidate. Single-instrument (one hook family), two levels.
ORIGIN: not a mitigation; no behaviour change (instrument default off).

  setupResolveFramebuffer (texture/resolvedTexture .get()), RenderFramebufferStorage::setup (colorTarget->texture.get()),
  or the framebuffer_manager tile copy. Writer still unnamed; s5383 breadcrumb `[plume-null-color-attachment]` stays armed.

## Session 7690 (2026-11-19) — G6c pair-partner loss root-caused: STANDINS=frame starved the game's two-frame view-test slice; fixed (ROGUESQ_S7690_PARITY)

No new crash reports (crash_reports FOLDED=27 new=0). Work unit: NEXT g6c-pair-partner-cull (H-variant / H-coloc / H-viewexit).

Offline first: the s7689 logs already showed the never-added partner is always odd=1 (index parity) with every held call
si_novt (no view test ran), so addNpcToVisibilityBucket rejects it before the view test. Code read of 0x80057C8C (funcs_12.c):
the view test is sliced over two frames. lui 0x8014 / lw -0x7764 = *0x8013889C (game frame counter) & 1: odd -> an instance whose
inst+8 has 0x80 jumps to L_80057E74 and reuses the cached 0x200 visible bit; even -> one with 0x100 does. An unassigned instance
(0x180 == 0) is put in the smaller group by comparing counters 0x801394E2 / 0x801394E4 and tested at once. Consecutive stand-ins
therefore alternate groups, and the starting balance (which depends on the real objects already assigned) decides which partner
gets which -> the per-run flip. STANDINS=frame calls only on alternate submit calls (one game-frame parity), so one group was
tested once at its first call and then always read its stale cached bit. All three NEXT hypotheses were wrong: not the item data,
not co-location, not a view exit, but a view test that never ran (H-slice). It matches s7689's "H-phase refuted": STANDINS=1 calls
every frame, so both groups are tested.

Fix (src/main/rs64_standins.cpp): in frame mode, before our bucket call, if inst+8 & 0x180 is the group that skips this frame,
regroup it to the one that is tested (odd -> 0x100, even -> 0x80); counters untouched. ROGUESQ_S7690_PARITY=0 = old (mismatches
still counted). New log: [s7690-par] per stand-in at 120 tries (grp, mism, fix, adds) and [s7690-pt] run totals per second, under
STANDINS_LOG; tools/s7690_par_tally.py tallies them.

Run 1 (wrong address, kept in scratch/s7690_wrongaddr/): my first build read 0x80137764 (bad arithmetic for -0x7764), so the
"fix" moved every stand-in INTO the skip group: new arm 0 adds in 82 windows vs old 3435. Not a result for the fix, but a causal
positive control for the mechanism: forcing the skip group alone removes every stand-in draw.

Run 2 (0x8013889C, scratch/s7690_parity_ab.sh, L1 dd2 STANDINS=frame HOLD 150, same binary, new vs PARITY=0): 2/2 alive, 0 crash,
vi_stalls30s=0, flicker synthetic control PASS both, sheet control PASS both.
  - adds total 6816 vs 3425; never added before spawn 13/34 vs 21/34; old arm skip-group items mism=119/120 (tested once).
  - sub 0x14 pairs: CEB08/CEBC4 207/208 vs 197/0 adds, CEC80/CED3C 228/220 vs 216/0.
  - flicker window 1 680.6 vs 454.0 px/triplet (window-2 off controls 44.6/44.4).
  - cluster sheet med_fpx 175 vs 0; top crops show the far bunker on stand-in frames only (magenta), old arm crops land on
    near-ground specks. docs/owner_sheet_s7690_frame_parity.jpg.
Two lines (per-item add log + pixels). ORIGIN: the cached-cull state is written by the game's own slice assignment
(0x80057D54/0x80057DD8 sh flags | 0x80 / 0x100 into inst+8) on our stand-in instance; legitimate for an object drawn every
frame, wrong for our alternate-frame calls. Owner impact: STANDINS=1 never affected; frame-mode proofs/sheets (s7628, s7688,
s7689) under-reported stand-ins by about half. The s7688 "L1 dd2 med_fpx 0" regression is explained, not a regression.
Rules out: H-variant, H-coloc, H-viewexit, and any s7672-s7687 handover cause for the bunker.

## Session 7725 (2026-11-20) — RT64 Present SIGTRAP root-caused: plume MetalBufferFormattedView over-released a +0 textureBufferDescriptor (103 NSZombies at boot -> 0); s7587's "debug-env artifact" reading refuted

Work unit (NEXT s7725, M6 secondary): the FOLDED .ips RogueSquadron64Recomp-2026-11-18-014353 (EXC_BREAKPOINT SIGTRAP, thread
"RT64 Present", object_getClassName <- AutoreleasePoolPage::autoreleaseNoPage <- objc_autoreleasePoolPush <- -[NSAutoreleasePool
init] <- plume::MetalDescriptorSetLayout ctor <- FramebufferReadChangesDescriptorBufferSet <- NativeTarget::copyFromRAM).
`tools/crash_reports.py --since 2026-11-13`: FOLDED=27 new=0.
- Attribution: the process ran 01:43:48.95-01:43:50.08, inside the s7587 run-A `own1` arm window (scratch/s7587/A/arms.log 01:43:45-
  01:46:20; env ROGUESQ_MTL_OWN=1 + OBJC_DEBUG_MISSING_POOLS=YES + ROGUESQ_S7587_PLANT=1). s7587 called it an instrument artifact.
- Disassembly (lldb, this macOS libobjc): object_getClassName+48 is `brk #0xc472`, the isa pointer-auth failure (autda on the
  object's isa). objc_autoreleasePoolPush+72 calls autoreleaseNoPage(x1) where x1 = the TLS deferred-autorelease slot
  (TPIDRRO_EL0+0x160, bit1 set): the push first flushes a pending +0 return value. So the trapping object was a pending
  autoreleased object whose memory was already freed and reused (bad isa), not POOL_BOUNDARY.
- Offline witness tools/s7725_pool_trap_repro.sh (rc 0, CONTROL PASS): a pool-less pthread's first push exits 0 with and without
  OBJC_DEBUG_MISSING_POOLS (the env alone does NOT trap -> refutes the artifact reading); an MRC caller releasing an
  objc_autoreleaseReturnValue object and then pushing segfaults even with no env (rc 139, positive control). Two lines of evidence
  that the defect is a freed pending object; the debug env only selects the reporter branch that reads its isa.
- Game run 1 (pre-fix binary, boot 30 s, OBJC_DEBUG_MISSING_POOLS=YES + NSZombieEnabled=YES, ROGUESQ_NO_SAVE_WRITE=1): alive (zombie
  isa is valid, so the reporter prints instead of trapping), 7784 MISSING POOLS lines of which 103 name
  `_NSZombie_MTLTextureDescriptorInternal` (3 threads: 89/12/2), 0 other zombie classes -> the freed object is a texture descriptor.
- Writer: plume_metal.cpp MetalBufferFormattedView ctor: `MTL::TextureDescriptor::textureBufferDescriptor(...)` is a +0 class
  factory, then upstream `descriptor->release()`. The s7587 census missed it because its +0 regex listed only a few getters.
  ORIGIN: plume upstream ownership bug (MRC TU, +0 factory released by the caller); the value is legitimately created by Metal and
  wrongly freed by us. In normal play it stays latent: without the debug env the flush stores the dangling pointer in the
  never-drained implicit pool (s7588), so it would only be messaged on thread exit or an outer pool pop.
- Fix (lib/rt64, rt64-plume.patch exported): under ROGUESQ_MTL_OWN (default on) the descriptor is built inside Rs64OwnPool and not
  released by us; ROGUESQ_MTL_OWN=0 restores the upstream release. Census widened: PLUS0 now matches any
  `MTL|NS|CA::Class::lowerFactory(` (not alloc), and `if (!rs64MtlOwn()) x->release()` counts as OLD-only (gated() read it
  backwards). Census: OLD {OK 63, NEEDS-POOL 9, OVERRELEASE 7, LEAK 7}, NEW {OK 82, NEEDS-POOL 4 (3 boot-once singletons
  sharedCaptureManager/processInfo + s7587's preferredDeviceNameNS)}, rc 0; before the fix the widened census rc 1 on line 1318.
- Game run 2, same rebuilt binary, both boot 30 s with OBJC_DEBUG_MISSING_POOLS=YES + NSZombieEnabled=YES: default arm 0 zombies
  (7619 MISSING POOLS, all live objects), ROGUESQ_MTL_OWN=0 control arm 103 `_NSZombie_MTLTextureDescriptorInternal`, 0 others;
  both alive 30 s. The control fired with the same count as the pre-fix run.
- Queued scratch/agent/soak_queue/s7725_texdesc_L4.sh (owner recipe L4 16:9 dd4 FPS60 STANDINS=1, 300 s, SOAK_NEEDS_IDLE=300).
Verdict line: selects H-overrelease (a new name for NEXT's H-nopool: a pool-less thread plus a freed pending object), refutes

rsp_dpc_submit appends every raw ucode RDP byte (before cull/merge/RT64); POSE_FREEZE writes the completed slots after its sleep.
New tool: tools/s7751_cxd4_task/ (replay.c compiles the rs64-oracle cxd4 sources in, scalar C VU; hardware boot =
_VirtualToPhysicalTask + rspboot to IMEM 0; RDP instant; re-kicks on cxd4's SP_STATUS poll-timeout halts until BREAK). Two
harness bugs fixed on the way: macOS SIGBUS on the PROT_NONE guard (cxd4's size probe traps SIGSEGV only) and stopping at 64
re-kicks (a task needs ~3,900-4,500). New tools/s7751_rdp_compare.py: splits both streams, lists |W|<=0.01 textured tris.

(717,576 of 1,719,776 bytes, byte-identical); the live run uses the dd>1 policy cap 1048576 (main.cpp setenv). With it, cap_fires=0.

| task | offline TG_FIX=1 vs live | offline TG_FIX=0 vs cxd4 | tg_hits | residual tg0 vs cxd4 (cmds) |
| f0 s4054 | byte-identical (1,719,776) | same length 1,716,608, 75,671 cmds aligned | 100 | 31 differ |
| f0 s4053 | byte-identical (1,768,976) | same length 1,765,456, 83,440 aligned | 101 | 31 |
| d s4056 | byte-identical (1,721,520) | same length 1,718,528, 75,682 aligned | 100 | 33 |

- H-fixup SELECTED for residual (b) port-only 0F tris and (c) the 846-command texture-load block order: both vanish with
  ROGUESQ_G5B_TG_FIX=0 (s6896 TriGen s16 edge clamp, default on at dd>1). Two lines: the TG_FIX=0 stream is length-exact with
  cxd4 and every insert/delete run is gone; the TG_FIX=1 stream is byte-identical to live with tg_hits=100 per task.
- Residual (a) = 31-33 replaced commands, two shapes: edge slope words whose port high half is 0xFE33 (DxMDy @28 on tris with
  yh==ym, i.e. an edge spanning zero scanlines, plus 2 @12/@24 cases) and texture/Z coefficient words on W~16384 near-saturated
  tris (@96-@172, values 0x8000/0x7FFF-adjacent). Rendered impact (angrylion, same snapshot): colour image 12,659 px (s4054) /

- Side result (new second source for G5b): render TG_FIX=1 vs TG_FIX=0 on s4054/s4056: 340,734 / 339,736 colour px differ,

New tools (engineering):
- tools/s7815_vu_ops/run.sh + harness.cpp: live librecomp rsp_vu*.hpp copied each run; cxd4 vu/*.c compiled UNMODIFIED as a
  separate C unit (scalar path, or CX_SSE=1 = its ARCH_MIN_SSE2 path through sse2neon); element broadcast from the RSP manual; the

  from cen64 rsp/vfunctions.c. 7 mutants (madh_carry, mulf_round, addc_vco, lt_cmp, cl_vce, mrg_sel, madn_clamp).
- tools/s7815_vu_ops/patch_cxd4.sh: copies cxd4 to a scratch dir and fixes its 5 VU defects (FIXES= subset for ablation; the
  rs64-oracle tree is never modified). VCH is replaced by a scalar transcription of CEN64 rsp_vch.
- tools/s7815_vu_gate.py (sweep row S7815_VU, ~31 s): ours vs patched cxd4 (all ops) + CEN64, both flavours; controls = stock cxd4
  must show exactly the known six-op signature, madn_clamp mutant must fire both references. Run: GREEN, CONTROLS PASS.

Results:
| comparison (595,200 compares per flavour) | live ops differing |
| ours vs stock cxd4 (scalar, and CX_SSE=1 identical) | VMADL 6297, VMADN 2022, VABS 2726, VCH 2758, VCR 14620, VMRG 19200 (+ dead VMACU 1228) |
| ours vs CEN64 on those six | 0 / 19,200 each, NEON_MAC 0 and 1 |
| ours vs patched cxd4 | 0 live (dead VMACU only) |
Aliasing is not a factor (bad counts equal across the 4 alias classes). The cxd4 defects, each read in its source:
1. VCR (select.c do_cr): merge() computes fail + cmp*diff and needs cmp in {0,1}; do_cr passes sn in {0,-1} (do_ch converts with
   >>15). Example vs=0x8000 vt=0x79A2: cxd4 0x79A3 = 2*vs - ~vt, hardware ~vt = 0x865D. Wrong whenever signs differ and ge != le.
2. VCH (do_ch "cch" hack): keeps -(-32768) at 0x7FFF and threads that into eq/le; CEN64 and ours wrap to 0x8000.
3. VABS: subtracts the corner-case 1 from ACCL as well as vd and also when vs>0; CEN64 comment: "acc_lo will be 0x8000 but vd 0x7FFF".
4. VMRG: leaves VCO; CEN64 RSP_VMRG writes zero to VCO hi/lo.
5. VMADN/VMADL SIGNED_CLAMP_AL: "clamped ACCM != raw ACCM" misses out-of-range lanes whose raw ACCM is already 0x7FFF/0x8000;
   CEN64 rsp_uclamp_acc clamps on ACCH != sign(ACCM). cxd4's SSE path shares defects 1-4 (it calls the same scalar helpers) and gave
   identical counts for 5.
Reachability: live. `vcr $v0,$v0,$v31[6]` (factor5_ucode_recompiled.c:1857, one per ucode TU, 10 sites) feeds $v0 into VMADM and two
SSV stores; $v31 = LQV DMEM 0x40, lane 6 = 0x0002 in both retained snaps, so it clamps to [-3,2] and cxd4 returns 2*vs+3 for lanes <= -3.
End to end (2 retained s7751 snaps, offline, our ucode at ROGUESQ_G5B_TG_FIX=0 UCODE_CAP=1048576 via tools/s7752_port_task/harness):
| task | stock cxd4 vs ours | patched cxd4 vs ours | fix1 | fix2 VCR | fix3 | fix4 | fix5 VCH | fix2+5 |
| s4054 (1,716,608 B) | 561 B, 31 cmds | BYTE-IDENTICAL | 31 | 25 | 31 | 31 | 7 | 0 B |
| s4056 (1,718,528 B) | 627 B, 33 cmds | BYTE-IDENTICAL | 33 | 25 | 33 | 33 | 9 | 0 B |
So s7752 residual (a) (edge-slope words 0xFE33 on yh==ym tris + coefficient words near 0x8000/0x7FFF, called "<=1 LSB precision")
is cxd4's VCH + VCR defects, and our LLE is byte-exact vs an independent RSP on whole real gfx tasks. Superseded entry added.
Discrimination: selects H-differ-live with OURS correct (two lines: CEN64 executed equality on all six ops; patched cxd4 equality on
every op and on 3.4 MB of real RDP output), refutes H-equal and H-differ-dead. No change to our code.
Side finding (affects past evidence, not the port): every angrylion "retail oracle" run loads the stock cxd4 dylib (g3_ai_gap_pair,
g3_menu_pair, g3_showroom_pair, g3f_retail_pan, oracle/run_m4_retail_pcs), so those frames carry these defects (s7752 measured
<=1 LSB on ~12k px per task). NEXT s7816 builds a patched oracle plugin and re-scores one retail pair.

read (n64-systemtest not used). cxd4's bundled SSE2NEON.h is too old to build its SSE path: run.sh shims it to the maintained sse2neon.

## Session 7825 (2026-11-22) — logo quarter-pixel residual is a systematic size-scaled input difference (port logo slightly smaller, 0.707 inward, controls PASS), not FPU rounding: 0 fused multiply-adds in generated game float math, FCSR only switched in guPerspectiveF; thread closed single-source-plus-audit
Work unit (NEXT s7825, HYPOTHESIS-ID g3-logo-quarter-pixel). Pre-checks: crash_reports new=0, no new SOAK-RESULTS lines, no owner answers.
Instead of the two-sided RDRAM alignment (expensive, the fallback clause allowed closing), two independent offline lines:
- Line 1, CPU-semantics audit of the port (boring thing first). RecompiledFuncs is built -O2 with Apple clang (default
  -ffp-contract=on), so FMA fusion was the obvious host/MIPS divergence (VR4300 has no fused madd). Census of every fused
  op (fmadd/fmsub/fnmadd/fnmsub) in the 3 build objects dirs: RecompiledFuncs 201 (11 objects), PatchesLib 0, main 131. Mapped
  to source lines via llvm-objdump -l: 201/201 are on our injected PATCH host-C lines (s6907 lens, G5g hangar vectors, s7103,
  s5897 dist, drawSubtitleText aspect patch, ...), 0 on generated MUL_S/ADD_S statements (one op per C statement, so on-mode
  contraction cannot fuse them). FCSR: the only cfc1/ctc1 in the whole game is libultra guPerspectiveF's RZ cvt.w.d idiom
  (perspNorm), emitted correctly (set_cop1_cs -> fesetround); round.w.* (lroundf, half-away vs MIPS half-even) has 0 sites;
  cvt.w 15 sites (lrint, mode-aware), trunc.w 1199 ((int) casts). So the port's float math is IEEE-identical to MIPS for these
  ops, except FS flush-to-zero of denormals (irrelevant at logo magnitudes).
- Line 2, shape of the residual (new tools/s7825_tri_shift_bias.py, same-run planted controls): per missed retail tri vs the
  nearest port tri, each pure-X edge-word shift classed inward/outward against the frame centroid. Retail 2720:2986 vs port
  (offset 795:804): inward 4004, outward 1658, inward fraction 0.707 (sign-random noise would be ~0.5; p astronomically small).
  Controls on the same frames: A planted one-LSB inward shifts on 10% of tris -> 1.000; B random sign -> 0.493; PASS.
  Flip rate per 30-frame bin falls as the logo shrinks: 0.33, 0.26, 0.21, 0.13, 0.06, 0.06, 0.02, 0.03, 0.02, and the
  inward bias vanishes in the last bins (0/0, 24/24, 22/12 = noise floor once the error drops below the LSB). An error that
  scales with the object's on-screen size and has one sign is a relative input difference (the port's logo transform is
  slightly smaller/further along), with rough size ~1e-3 relative (flip rate x 0.25 px / typical 60 px offset; inference,
  the per-frame spread metric was too noisy to measure it directly). A 1-ULP float difference (6e-8) would flip ~1e-4 of
  words with random sign.
- Reading: H-cpu (recompiled FPU semantics) and H-oracle-cpu (mupen FPU rounding) are both disfavoured: neither predicts a
  one-signed, size-scaled ~1e-3 error. H-input-time is favoured: the logo zoom is time-driven (like the s7821 hangar bob) and
  the port samples its animation clock at a slightly different sub-frame phase than the VI-clocked det oracle. Not a port
  defect; 1/4 px, invisible. Not proven: the animation-clock read was not named (no logo-zoom function identified; the obvious
  symbol names do not contain it).
- Rules out: FMA contraction in game code (0 sites), a mishandled rounding mode, round-half-even divergence (0 sites) as the
  cause of this or any other port/retail float residual.
- Verdict: selects H-input-time (single-source on the residual shape, plus the independent FPU audit); refutes H-cpu as an
  FPU-semantics cause (fusion/rounding-mode/round-half audited clean) and disfavours H-oracle-cpu (ULP noise cannot be one-signed
  and size-scaled). Next discriminator if ever reopened: a guest-RAM read of the logo zoom parameter per VI in both arms
  (oracle --det watch vs port dump) shows a constant sub-frame phase offset under H-input-time. Thread closed; NEXT resumes
  g3-det-menu-pair at the first mission frames.

9DE900/A62B80 and test H-retail vs H-port-load vs H-present.

   43.384, then 125 ms with no present, 6 presents repeating one frozen workload (wl=2553, gen unchanged), 71 ms gap, resume: the

Verdict: H-retail selected (two lines: oracle VI holds with PC attribution + port host stack on the same wait). Port hold at hangar
entry 275-295 ms = 16.5-17.7 VIs vs retail 17 VIs on the same musyxNoopStub wait; retail then shows one static frame a further
123 VIs during the hangar load, which the port does not (port is faster there). The same holds for the port's TRANSITION holds at
58.6/66.8 s (282-392 ms) vs retail 15-19 VIs at the same waits. Rules out H-port-load (no port-only synchronous cost at this
transition: the port is <= retail) and H-present. G5c: the in-flight bar was met (s7920) and the only in-scene pre-flight hold is
retail-shaped -> G5c CLOSED on measurement; owner judges feel.
Side check: the 17.3 s TRANSITION "hold" at ring t=11-28 s is the single-buffered title (B51E00, 1592 wide): gen advances on 1015 of
1018 presents, so the picture animates; retail's title also sits on one buffer (0x790400/0x790800). Not a freeze; tool label only.
Caveat (single-source for the absolute ms): oracle VIs are emulated time (mupen interpreter cycle model); the 17-VI equality is a
VI-count match, and the wait's own length (8-9 VIs) is fixed by the audio countdown, not by CPU speed.
